### This blog post is all about the best coffee shops to work from in New York City.

**What Makes Great Laptop-Friendly Coffee Shops to Work or Study From in NYC?**

There are thousands of cafes in New York, but not all of them are ideal for setting up shop with a laptop.

Here’s what I look for when searching for the best WiFi coffee shops in Manhattan and Brooklyn:

- **Reliable and fast WiFi**
- **Comfortable seating and outlets**
- **Relaxed atmosphere**
- **Great coffee and snacks**
- **Laptop-friendly policies**

Whether you’re a night owl who works best in the evening or someone who likes to start their day with a 9am cold brew, there’s a spot for you.

**I recently spent three weeks in New York as a digital nomad, staying at SharedEasy apartments in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. You can see a lot of these coffee shops to work from in New York in my YouTube vlogs during my most recent trip to New York:**

Let’s dive into my favourite coffee shops to work from in New York City.

**Coffee Shops to Work From in New York: Manhattan**

Below are my favourite coffee shops to work from in New York City.

These coffee shops have been tried and tested by yours truly, so you can know for sure that these are great places to set up shop with your laptop for the day.

No matter if you need a coffee shop to study from or to get some work done, this list of coffee shops to work from in New York will have exactly what you need.

**1. Bibliotheque – SoHo**

**Address:** 54 King Street, New York, NY 10014

An ideal pick for anyone searching for NYC coffee shops with WiFi and ambiance.

Set among bookshelves and bathed in warm lighting, it’s one of my favourites for a quiet and stylish work session.

I sat at the bar area to work when I visited which had plug sockets underneath.

Almost everyone there was working on a laptop, but you can browse some books before you leave too or grab a glass of wine.

Just note, laptops are banned after 5pm!

**2. Housing Works Bookstore – SoHo**

**Address:** 126 Crosby Street, New York, NY 10012

This one is a true gem. A café with a purpose, Housing Works supports programs for the homeless and people living with HIV/AIDS.

It’s one of the best coffee shops to work from in New York for remote work thanks to its welcoming space and reliable WiFi.

However, when I visited they didn’t have any plug outlets if you needed to charge your laptop.

**3. Cafe Urbana – Chelsea**

**Address:** 225 West 23rd Street, New York, NY 10011

A green oasis in the heart of Chelsea and one of the best coffee shops to work from in New York City.

This plant-filled café is vibrant and peaceful. Perfect for freelancers looking for a fresh, focused vibe.

**4. The Marlton Hotel – West Village**

**Address:** 5 West 8th Street, New York, NY 10011

If hotel lobbies are your vibe, this is a dream.

With vintage furniture, roaring fires in the winter, and soft music, it’s the perfect retreat when you’re tired of cramped cafés.

The Marlton Hotel is my favourite place to work remotely on a wet, rainy day in New York.

Their tomato soup is also the perfect winter warmer.

**5. Stumptown Coffee Roasters – West Village**

**Address:** 30 West 8th Street, New York, NY 10011

A consistent favourite among remote workers.

With its great WiFi, even better coffee, and community feel, it’s an excellent choice for anyone wondering where to work remotely in NYC.

Just know that it doesn’t have as much seating as other options on this list.

However, it’s just across the street from the Marlton Hotel if you need a back-up.

**6. Amano – West Village**

**Address:** 172 West 4th Street, New York, NY 10014

Minimalist and quiet, Amano is one of my go-to coffee shops to work from in New York City when I need to be super productive.

The clean interiors and fast internet help me focus for hours.

It’s best to go here during the week when it’s quieter as it’s not the largest coffee shop ever, but if you can grab a seat, you’re in luck!

**7. The Drama Book Shop – Midtown**

**Address:** 266 West 39th Street, New York, NY 10018

Not many people think of Midtown when looking for a peaceful work spot, but this bookstore café is a game-changer.

With low noise levels and comfortable seating, it’s great for focused work time.

If you need to find a coffee shop to work from in Midtown, New York, this is the spot!

**8. Capital One Café – Midtown**

**Address:** 853 Broadway, New York, NY 10003

A surprising yet fantastic option for digital nomads in NYC. If you’re a Capital One cardholder, enjoy half-price drinks while working from co-working rooms with free WiFi.

For those that aren’t Capital One customers (like me), you can still make use of their free WiFi and work for the day.

They’ve got many breakfast options and lots of plug outlets too. A great spot near Central Park to get some work done.

**9. The Clock Coffee Shop – Midtown**

**Address:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166

Inside the MetLife Building, this café caters to the city’s corporate crowd.

But for freelancers and remote workers, it offers strong coffee, a professional vibe, and solid WiFi.

**10. Bluestockings Cooperative – Lower East Side**

**Address:** 116 Suffolk Street, New York, NY 10002

A peaceful and socially conscious café in the LES, ideal for writers and deep-thinkers.

One of the best NYC coffee shops with WiFi if you’re after something with soul.

*If you’re planning a trip to New York City, make sure to check out my **140+ page travel guide eBook** which you can **download here** to help you plan!*

**11. Georgie’s – Lower East Side**

**Address:** 175 Delancey Street, New York, NY 10002

A new find for us and one I’d definitely go back to!

Massive and full of light, Georgie’s is a fantastic option if you’re looking for spacious coffee shops to work from in New York City.

Just bring a full battery, as plugs are limited.

**12. P&T Knitwear – Lower East Side**

**Address:** 180 Orchard Street, New York, NY 10002

Need a podcast studio and a WiFi café in one? You’ve found it. While seating is limited, it’s a fun spot with excellent coffee and creative energy.

This is probably my top spot that I always love to work from.

You’re in the middle of a bookstore, it’s never too busy and you’ll always find a seat to work from.

Plus, they have a great coffee shop inside too with soft drinks.

And even better, you’re on Orchard Street. My personal favourite street in all of New York.

**13. Black Cat LES – Lower East Side**

**Address:** 172 Rivington Street, New York, NY 10002

You’ll find Black Cat on every list of coffee shops to work from in New York City.

It’s extremely popular with freelancers and students, so be sure to arrive early.

If it’s packed, Rex is just around the corner!

**14. Rex – Lower East Side**

**Address:** 151 Essex Street, New York, NY 10002

Perfect for late-night creatives, Rex stays open until 10pm on weekdays and 1am on weekends!

We worked here on a few occasions as it was always quiet enough to grab a table in, great stable WiFi and lots of plug outlets too.

One of the few coffee shops to work from in New York that opens late.

**Coffee Shops to Work From in New York: Brooklyn**

Below are the best coffee shops to work from in New York, located in Brooklyn.

I recently spent **three weeks living in Brooklyn in December and January**, so tried my fair share of coffee shops in the area for remote work!

Let me take you through the best coffee shops to work from in New York that I came across.

*And if you want to see an extended list, you can  read this blog post of the 30 Best Coffee Shops to Work From in Brooklyn here.*

**15. Brooklyn Roasting Company – Williamsburg**

**Address:** 25 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

Whether you’re writing blog posts or editing a YouTube video like me, this place delivers on all fronts: strong WiFi, comfy seats and fantastic coffee.

A solid pick for digital nomads working in Brooklyn.

**16. Think Coffee – Williamsburg**

**Address:** 10 Devoe Street, Brooklyn, NY 11211

Laid-back, community-driven, and filled with remote workers.

Easily one of the best coffee shops in NYC for remote work, especially if you’re based in Brooklyn.

**17. The Hoxton Hotel – Williamsburg**

**Address:** 97 Wythe Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11249

Another stylish hotel lobby café that’s ideal for winter work sessions.

A great setting for client calls, focused work, or just sipping coffee and planning your next project.

One of the best coffee shops to work from in New York if you want to treat yourself.

*If you’re planning a trip to New York City, make sure to check out my **140+ page travel guide eBook** which you can **download here** to help you plan!*

**18. Devoción – Williamsburg**

**Address:** 69 Grand Street, Brooklyn, NY 11249

This one might be the most beautiful coffee shop I’ve ever worked in. The lush greenery, huge skylights, and high-quality Colombian coffee make it a must-visit.

Just note that it’s very popular (for its amazing coffee) so you might struggle to find a table if you don’t get there at a good time.

**19. Nyla Café – Williamsburg**

**Address:** 65 Irving Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11237

If you need a brunch break between Zoom calls, head here. Nyla is a well-rounded café with strong WiFi, good food, and a friendly vibe.

This was our local spot near to where we were living for the three weeks and we always managed to grab a table.

It’s a spot where you’ll quickly feel like a local – we loved it!

**20. Sweetleaf Coffee Roasters – Greenpoint**

**Address:** 159 Freeman Street, Brooklyn, NY 11222

Arguably the top spot in Brooklyn for freelancers. It’s spacious, well-lit, and filled with digital nomads and remote workers.

Plug in, grab a flat white, and get to work.

I would move to Greenpoint just so I could work from here every day. The best of the best coffee shops to work from in New York.

**21. Principles GI Coffee House – Gowanus**

**Address:** 139 9th Street, Brooklyn, NY 11215

Set in a converted warehouse, this large café stands out not only for its vibe but also its ethics – they pay their staff a liveable wage, and tipping isn’t expected.

A great pick if you want to work somewhere with purpose and happen to be in Gowanus.

**The Best Coffee Shops to Work From in New York**

Finding the right coffee shops to work from in New York City isn’t hard.

It’s narrowing them down that’s the real challenge.

Whether you need all-day comfort, late-night hours, or just great coffee and solid WiFi, the city has something for everyone.

Here are my personal top picks of the best coffee shops to work from in New York for digital nomads:

- **Most beautiful space:**- **Devoción, Williamsburg**
- **Best all-rounder:**- **Sweetleaf Coffee Roasters, Greenpoint**
- **Best for brunch and work:**- **Nyla Café, Williamsburg**
- **Most atmospheric:**- **The Marlton Hotel, West Village**
- **Best Midtown hidden gem:**- **The Drama Book Shop**

Wherever you go, bring your charger, grab a good coffee, and make the most of one of the world’s greatest cities to work remotely in.

title: The 11 Best New York City Coffee Shops For Freelancers - Keep Calm and Chiffon
author: Austen Tosone
text:
# The 11 Best New York City Coffee Shops For Freelancers

I’m so excited to be bringing you all this *highly* requested blog post.

As I’m sure many of you know, I’m currently freelancing and I often work out of coffee shops when I have to get stuff done, but not every coffee shop is ideal for laptop dwellers.

In fact I’ve even gone through a truly awkward scenario where I purchased food and a coffee and as it was being prepared I tried to log on to the shop’s WiFi…only to realize that they didn’t have any!

So I decided it was time, once and for all to put together a list of some of the best places to work in NYC if you’re a freelancer or blogger because I tried Googling it and I couldn’t find any posts about the best coffee shops to work in in NYC.

These are all coffee shops tried and tested by yours truly.

I mostly stick to Brooklyn and Manhattan and I’m sure I haven’t found every single amazing spot for freelancers to work out of (and if you have any, please leave them in the comments!) but every one of these has been great to me.

Each spot on this list has WiFi, a bathroom and friendly employees who work there.

Some spots I’ve worked at for two hours at a time and some I’ve camped out at all day.

I hope that no matter how long you’re there that this post saves you a few minutes either scrolling through Yelp reviews trying to get some answers or time that you would have spent scoping these shops out in person.

If you’re looking for the best cafes to work in in NYC, you’ve come to the right place.

## Brooklyn

**Breukelen Coffee House – Crown Heights
**764 Franklin Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238

Not only does this place have all of the essentials, but it really feels like a place where people are encouraged to come and camp out all day.

Their matcha latte was delicious and they also have food (I’d definitely recommend the bacon, egg, and cheese croissant) and it felt like a community of other freelancers who could spread out and get shit done with outlets galore.

**Woops! – Williamsburg
**548 Driggs Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11211

If you have a love of hard work and a sweet tooth, you’ll love spending the day working at Woops!

Located right of the Bedford Ave L, this coffee shop is such a splendid place to post up for a while and get things done.

You can grab a table or some of the seating by the window and nibble on macarons as you work.

**Hungry Ghost – Williamsburg
**721 Metropolitan Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11211

I’ve been loving the newest location of this coffee chain. It’s clean, the staff are friendly, and there are a ton of places to plop yourself as you get work done.

If you want an outlet, make sure to claim a spot with a stool against the wall you don’t run out of juice.

Ironically I actually don’t love their coffee but they make a mean matcha.

**Devoición – Williamsburg
**69 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11249

I would say that Devoción makes the best coffee on this list, because who can resist that Colombian blend?

Other than that, this is a great spot to bring your laptop to and grab a small bite as you work.

Just as a heads up, they don’t offer WiFi on weekends (specifically to deter laptop-dwellers)

**Sey Coffee – Bushwick
**18 Grattan St, Brooklyn, NY 11206

This is probably one of my favorite spots to get some work done.

This Bushwick coffee shop is bright and filled with plants and feels like a place that welcomes everyone whether you want to meet up with a friend for a cold brew or get some work done solo.

You may have to move around a bit to get a seat by an outlet but it’s not impossible if you’re patient.

**Odd Fox – Greenpoint
**984 Manhattan Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11222

This is my most recent and most delightful discovery when it comes to places to work in Brooklyn. Odd Fox GETS IT.

Every table has a sign on it that says “this is a shared table and no bags on chairs,” which makes it super freelancer friendly. Plus, there’s an adorable garden out back where you can sit and work.

I would just recommend bug spray if you go outside because a mosquito found me and would not leave me alone.

**Rose Wolf Coffee – East Williamsburg
**867 Metropolitan Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11211

This spot is a recent addition to my neighborhood and I’ve only been once but I am already in love.

The seating area is separate from the coffee counter so you can really get shit done.

They’ve got great coffee as well as some vegan and gluten-free pastries to snack on too. Plus, it’s women-owned, which I love.

# Manhattan

**Spreadhouse – Lower East Side
**116 Suffolk St, New York, NY 10002

Is there anything more satisfying than a coffee house with tons of rugs, lots of random places to plop and excellent lattes? Literally no, so look no further than Spreadhosue.

They have food and tables and it’s a shop that I return to over and over again for the good vibes and good coffee.

**Cha Cha Matcha (Broome St + Chelsea)
**373 Broome St, New York, NY 10013

During the weekend this pink and green paradise is packed with tourists, but throughout the week it’s a great place to work.

The Flatiron location is newer and definitely has more outlets than the SoHo location but you can still make it work in SoHo.

Don’t order your average coffee—get the pink drink, the divine drink, or the matcha lemonade to spice it up a bit.

The music can be loud but if you have headphones you’re fine. *The Nolita location doesn’t have WiFi or a bathroom!!*

**Joe & the Juice (any location but if I had to choose go to the SoHo one)
**67 Spring St, New York, NY 10012

Every trendy New Yorker will at some point in their lives get a beverage from Joe & the Juice.

This Copenhagen-born chain has pretty reliable shops when it comes to outlets, WiFi and high-energy employees.

I definitely recommend the SoHo location off of Spring Street since sometimes models like to hang out there and it can be fun to people watch. The music here can be extremely loud so just keep that in mind.

**Max Caffe – Harlem
**1262 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY 10027

One of the few reasons I’ll ever trek back uptown to Columbia territory is to get some work done at Max Caffe.

Max Caffe knows what’s up. There are tons of couches and tables, a reasonable amount of outlets, and this place has food, coffee and even wine!

If you find that yourself there past 5PM order yourself a glass of the house wine and stay a while as Max transforms from workspace to cozy date spot.

Also if it’s nice out, grab a seat outside!

Do you have a favorite coffee shop to work at? Leave it in the comments!

yours,

Austen

title: Top 7 Work Cafes NYC for Remote Workers (2026 Guide)
author: Remotetribelife; Andrew Williams
text:
For remote workers and digital nomads in New York City, finding the perfect cafe is about more than just a good caffeine hit; it’s about discovering a third space that genuinely supports productivity. The ideal spot requires a delicate balance of reliable Wi-Fi, accessible power outlets, comfortable seating, and an atmosphere that allows for deep focus. But with thousands of cafes scattered across the five boroughs, the search can be overwhelming. Too often, a promising work session turns into a frustrating hunt for a better location because of unwritten rules, packed tables, or nonexistent outlets.

This guide cuts through the noise. We’ve compiled a detailed list of the best **work cafes NYC** has to offer, specifically for those who need to get things done. We move beyond simple recommendations and provide the practical details you need to make a confident choice. For each cafe, we break down:

- **Wi-Fi Reliability & Power Outlets:**The non-negotiables for any remote worker.
- **Seating & Noise Level:**Find a spot that matches your workflow, from quiet corners to social hubs.
- **Food, Drink, & Pricing:**Know what to expect for your coffee and lunch budget. To truly appreciate your work cafe experience, understanding the wide array of beverages available can be insightful. Explore the nuances of various brews and find your perfect cup by checking out this guide on different types of coffee.
- **Location & Transit:**Practical details like address, hours, and nearby subway lines.

Whether you’re a long-time New Yorker tired of your usual spots or a digital nomad just touching down, this curated list will help you find your next favorite cafe office. Let’s dive in.

## 1. Think Coffee

Think Coffee stands as a cornerstone for remote workers, earning its spot as a top-tier work cafe in NYC through sheer reliability and a welcoming atmosphere for laptop users. This local chain has strategically placed its multiple locations across Manhattan and in Williamsburg, making it a go-to hub whether you’re near Union Square, in the Flatiron District, or across the bridge. Its spaces are intentionally designed with work in mind, offering a mix of two-top tables perfect for a laptop and a notebook, communal tables for collaborative energy, and comfy sofas for more casual sessions.

What makes Think Coffee special is its consistent “laptop culture.” You’ll never feel out of place opening your computer, as you’ll be surrounded by fellow professionals, students, and freelancers doing the same. This creates a focused, library-like buzz that is productive without being silent. The menu is another significant advantage, featuring a full coffee and tea program alongside substantial food options like sandwiches, salads, and pastries, including many vegan choices. This breadth means you can comfortably settle in for several hours without needing to leave for a meal, a key factor for deep work sessions.

### Practical Details & Pro Tips

While the Wi-Fi is generally steady, outlet availability can be inconsistent, so arriving with a full battery is a smart move. Locations near universities, such as the one on Mercer Street near NYU, can get particularly crowded during peak academic times and midday. For a more relaxed experience, aim for mid-morning or later in the afternoon on weekdays.

| Feature | Details | 
|---|---|
| Address | Multiple locations including: 248 Mercer St (Greenwich Village), 123 4th Ave (Union Square), 73 8th Ave (West Village), 180 Wythe Ave (Williamsburg). | 
| Hours | Vary by location, but typically open from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM. | 
| Wi-Fi & Outlets | Wi-Fi:Free and generally reliable.Outlets:Limited and vary by location; not available at every table. | 
| Noise Level | Moderate to high, with a constant background hum of conversation and keyboard clicks. | 
| Pricing | Coffee:~$4.00 – $6.00.Sandwiches/Salads:~$10.00 – $14.00. | 
| Best For | Deep work sessions, casual client meetings, and social co-working. | 

If you find that the dynamic cafe environment isn’t structured enough for your needs, you might explore more formal options. To see how these cafes compare to dedicated workspaces, check out this guide to some of the best coworking spaces in New York.

**Website:** https://thinkcoffee.com

## 2. Coffee Project NY

For those who prioritise the quality of their coffee as much as the reliability of their Wi-Fi, Coffee Project NY is a standout choice. This speciality coffee roaster has earned its place among the best work cafes in NYC by blending an award-winning coffee program with a clear, professional-friendly laptop policy. With several locations, including a notable presence in the East Village, Chelsea, and Long Island City, it provides a sophisticated setting for focused work, especially for those who appreciate the craft behind their caffeine fix. The spaces are clean, modern, and designed with intention, though seating can be limited.

What truly sets Coffee Project NY apart is its transparency. Each location explicitly states its rules regarding laptop use, which eliminates the guesswork and potential awkwardness of setting up shop. While some locations restrict laptops on busy weekends and holidays to accommodate all guests, their weekday policies are generally welcoming. This clarity creates a respectful environment where everyone knows the expectations. The menu is a major draw, featuring meticulously prepared espresso drinks, creative signature beverages like their deconstructed latte, and a selection of high-quality pastries. The focus on education, with some sites offering public classes and cuppings, adds another layer of appeal for true coffee aficionados.

### Practical Details & Pro Tips

The biggest advantage is knowing the rules before you go; always check the website for the specific laptop policy of the location you plan to visit. The quality of the coffee means these spots are popular, so the smaller cafes can fill up quickly, especially during the morning rush. Arriving early or during off-peak hours (like mid-afternoon) is your best bet for securing a table. Since outlets aren’t guaranteed at every seat, come with a fully charged device.

| Feature | Details | 
|---|---|
| Address | Multiple locations, including 23 E 10th St (East Village), 155 7th Ave S (Chelsea), and 21-10 51st Ave (Long Island City). | 
| Hours | Varies, but typically open from around 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM. | 
| Wi-Fi & Outlets | Wi-Fi:Free and available on weekdays.Outlets:Very limited; do not expect an outlet at your table. | 
| Noise Level | Low to moderate. The atmosphere is generally focused and respectful, with less ambient chatter than larger cafes. | 
| Pricing | Coffee:~$4.50 – $7.00.Pastries:~$4.00 – $6.00. | 
| Best For | Coffee connoisseurs, solo work sessions, and quiet, focused tasks on weekdays. | 

The exceptional quality found at places like Coffee Project NY is a global trend, and you can find out about other unique places by reading up on some of the cool co-working spaces in the world to work from.

**Website:** https://coffeeprojectny.com

## 3. Devoción

Devoción elevates the concept of a work cafe by blending stunning, biophilic design with high-quality, farm-to-cup Colombian coffee. Its most notable locations, particularly in Williamsburg and the Flatiron District, feel less like coffee shops and more like urban oases, filled with natural light, living green walls, and ample space. This inspiring atmosphere makes Devoción an exceptional choice for remote workers who thrive in aesthetically pleasing environments, making it one of the most sought-after work cafes in NYC. The intentional layout in their larger cafes provides a variety of seating, from leather couches for casual brainstorming to dedicated tables ideal for focused work sessions.


What truly sets Devoción apart is its commitment to both ambiance and functionality. You'll find that the larger spaces are generally well-equipped for productivity, with strong Wi-Fi and a surprising number of power outlets thoughtfully placed near seating areas. This removes the "outlet anxiety" common in other cafes. The focus on single-origin Colombian coffee ensures a premium beverage experience, perfect for fueling long work sprints. While the food menu is more limited to pastries and light bites compared to full-service cafes, the quality is high, providing enough sustenance to keep you going. This combination of inspiring design and practical amenities makes it a top-tier destination for both deep work and impressive client meetings.

### Practical Details & Pro Tips

Due to its immense popularity, Devoción can get very crowded, especially during peak morning hours and on weekends. To secure a good spot with an outlet, arriving early on a weekday is your best strategy. Be aware that some locations may have informal time limits or restrict laptop use in certain areas during their busiest periods to manage turnover. Always be prepared to order a second drink if you plan on staying for an extended time. Understanding the nuances of the remote work lifestyle can make your cafe sessions more productive; for a deeper dive, you can explore the pros and cons of remote working to optimize your approach.

| Feature | Details | 
|---|---|
| Address | Williamsburg (69 Grand St), Flatiron (25 E 20th St), Downtown Brooklyn (276 Livingston St), and several others across NYC. | 
| Hours | Vary by location. Williamsburg: 7 AM–7 PM. Flatiron: Mon-Fri 7 AM–7 PM, Sat-Sun 8 AM–7 PM. | 
| Wi-Fi & Outlets | Wi-Fi:Free and typically fast.Outlets:Plentiful in the larger Williamsburg and Flatiron locations, but less common in smaller outposts. | 
| Noise Level | Moderate to high. The large, open spaces can amplify background chatter and music, so noise-canceling headphones are recommended for focused work. | 
| Pricing | Coffee:~$4.50 – $7.00.Pastries:~$4.00 – $6.00. | 
| Best For | Creative work, impressing a client, and solo work sessions in an inspiring setting. | 

**Website:** https://www.devocion.com/pages/cafes

## 4. Variety Coffee Roasters

Variety Coffee Roasters has firmly established itself as a Brooklyn-born favorite that successfully crossed the bridge into Manhattan, offering some of the best work cafes in NYC for discerning coffee lovers. Known for its high-quality, house-roasted beans and minimalist-chic interiors, Variety provides a productive yet relaxed environment. The spaces often feature large windows that flood the rooms with natural light, alongside a thoughtful layout of individual tables and communal benches that cater directly to the laptop crowd.


What makes Variety a standout choice is its commitment to both excellent coffee and a work-friendly atmosphere, especially on weekdays. Unlike some specialty shops that can feel unwelcoming to remote workers, Variety strikes a great balance. You'll find a steady hum of keyboard clicks and quiet conversation, creating an ideal background noise for focused tasks. The Park Slope location, in particular, is a gem for its ample seating and reliable Wi-Fi, making it perfect for settling in for a few hours of coding or writing. The menu is coffee-forward, but you can find a solid selection of pastries to keep you fueled.

### Practical Details & Pro Tips

While Wi-Fi is consistently strong across their locations, power outlets can be a bit of a treasure hunt; they aren’t available at every seat, so it's wise to come with your devices fully charged. Weekends and late afternoons get noticeably more social and crowded, so for heads-down work, aim for a weekday morning. The quality of the coffee itself is a major draw, so take a moment to enjoy a pour-over or their excellent single-origin espresso.

| Feature | Details | 
|---|---|
| Address | Multiple locations including: 368 Graham Ave (Williamsburg), 146 Wyckoff Ave (Bushwick), 261 7th Ave (Chelsea), 126 W 23rd St (Chelsea). | 
| Hours | Generally 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM, though hours can vary slightly by location. | 
| Wi-Fi & Outlets | Wi-Fi:Free and typically fast.Outlets:Limited and strategically placed, but not guaranteed for every seat. | 
| Noise Level | Low to moderate during weekday mornings, increasing to a social buzz in the afternoons and on weekends. | 
| Pricing | Coffee:~$4.50 – $6.50.Pastries:~$4.00 – $6.00. | 
| Best For | Coffee aficionados, focused morning work sessions, and a neighborhood co-working feel. | 

Finding the right cafe can make all the difference, but so can your personal workspace. For tips on creating a productive environment wherever you are, explore this guide to the best work-from-home office setup.

**Website:** https://varietycoffeeroasters.com

## 5. Ground Central Coffee Company

Ground Central Coffee Company carves out its niche by masterfully blending the focused energy of a library with the warmth of a classic coffee bar. Its various locations, primarily clustered in Midtown and other key Manhattan business districts, make it an incredibly convenient choice for commuters or anyone needing a reliable work spot between client meetings. The interiors are intentionally cozy and bookish, often lined with shelves of actual books, creating an atmosphere that encourages solo work and quiet concentration.


What truly sets Ground Central apart is its dependable presence in areas where quiet, work-friendly cafes can be surprisingly scarce. While many Midtown spots are grab-and-go by nature, Ground Central invites you to settle in. This makes it one of the most reliable work cafes in NYC when you need a predictable environment near a client’s office or a major transit hub like Grand Central Terminal. The menu supports longer stays with solid espresso drinks, a variety of teas, and a good selection of pastries and grab-and-go food like sandwiches and salads. You’ll feel perfectly comfortable pulling out a laptop here, as the ambiance strikes a great balance between productive buzz and peaceful study hall.

### Practical Details & Pro Tips

While the book-lined walls promote focus, be aware that locations can get quite busy during the pre-office morning rush (8-9:30 AM) and the post-work wind-down period. Seating can become competitive during these times. Not every location is ideal for taking video calls due to the ambient chatter, so it’s best for tasks requiring deep focus rather than lots of conversation. If you’re a coffee aficionado and often on the move, you might be interested in creating your own quality brew anywhere; explore options with this review of the 9 best portable espresso machines.

| Feature | Details | 
|---|---|
| Address | Multiple in Manhattan including: 888 8th Ave (Midtown West), 155 E 52nd St (Midtown East), 25 W 56th St (Midtown). | 
| Hours | Varies by location, but most are open weekdays from around 6:30 AM to 6:00 PM. Weekend hours are often shorter. | 
| Wi-Fi & Outlets | Wi-Fi:Free and generally stable for work.Outlets:Can be a bit of a treasure hunt; some locations have them along banquettes or specific walls, but not at every seat. | 
| Noise Level | Low to moderate. The "library" vibe keeps it quieter than many cafes, but it's not silent. | 
| Pricing | Coffee:~$4.50 – $6.50.Food:~$9.00 – $15.00 for sandwiches and salads. | 
| Best For | Solo work sessions, pre- or post-meeting work blocks, and focused reading or writing. | 

**Website:** https://www.groundcentral.com

## 6. Partners Coffee — Café & Roastery

Partners Coffee, especially its flagship Williamsburg location, is a magnet for remote workers who appreciate exceptional coffee as much as a productive environment. This roastery-cafe hybrid offers a unique experience, allowing you to work amidst the aroma of freshly roasted beans. The space is expansive and thoughtfully arranged, with a generous number of individual and communal tables that create a dynamic yet work-friendly atmosphere, solidifying its reputation as a top work cafe in NYC. The constant, quiet hum of activity makes it an ideal spot for those who thrive on ambient energy.


What truly sets Partners apart is the direct connection to its roastery. The quality of the coffee is outstanding, from their signature blends to seasonal single-origin pour-overs, providing the perfect fuel for a long work session. Unlike smaller cafes, the large footprint means you can usually find a spot without feeling cramped, particularly on weekdays. The crowd is a mix of freelancers, creatives, and professionals, fostering a community feel where settling in with a laptop is the norm. The menu includes pastries and light bites that pair perfectly with their coffee offerings, ensuring you can stay productive for hours.

### Practical Details & Pro Tips

The Wi-Fi is known for being dependable, which is a major draw for remote workers. However, power outlets are a coveted resource and are not available at every seat, so it's best to come with a fully charged device. The cafe is busiest on weekends and during the late afternoon rush on weekdays when locals stop by for their coffee fix. For the best chance at securing a prime spot with an outlet, aim to arrive mid-morning. Its proximity to the Bedford Ave L train stop also makes it an easily accessible option for those commuting from Manhattan.

| Feature | Details | 
|---|---|
| Address | Flagship roastery at 125 N 6th St (Williamsburg), with other locations in the West Village (44 Charles St), Long Island City (2-21 51st Ave), and Midtown. | 
| Hours | Williamsburg: Typically 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily. Other locations may vary. | 
| Wi-Fi & Outlets | Wi-Fi:Free and consistently reliable.Outlets:Limited; not guaranteed at every table. It's wise to charge up beforehand. | 
| Noise Level | Moderate, with a steady buzz of conversation, espresso machine sounds, and keyboard clicks. Earphones are recommended for deep focus. | 
| Pricing | Coffee:~$4.50 – $6.50.Pastries:~$4.00 – $7.00. | 
| Best For | High-quality coffee enthusiasts, creative work, and solo work sessions. | 

**Website:** https://www.partnerscoffee.com

## 7. Poetica Coffee

Poetica Coffee offers a refreshing, community-focused alternative to the more corporate cafe chains, establishing itself as a beloved neighborhood spot for remote work, especially in Brooklyn. With several locations, each possessing a unique, bright, and comfortable design, it has cultivated a reputation for being genuinely laptop-friendly on weekdays. The atmosphere feels less like a transient office and more like a local gathering place, making it an excellent choice for those who prefer a relaxed, less intense work environment to settle in for a few hours.


What distinguishes Poetica is its successful blend of quality coffee and a welcoming stance toward laptop users without sacrificing its neighborhood charm. Unlike some cafes that can feel overly transactional, Poetica encourages a more leisurely stay, with a mix of comfortable seating and, in some locations, larger back areas perfect for finding a quiet corner. You’ll find a steady stream of locals, freelancers, and students, creating a low-key, productive buzz. The menu supports longer work sessions with excellent specialty coffee, a solid selection of pastries, and tasty food items like breakfast burritos and toasts, meaning you can easily fuel your morning and afternoon work sprints.

### Practical Details & Pro Tips

While Poetica is generally work-friendly, amenities can differ significantly between locations. The Prospect Park West and Park Slope branches are often cited for having more space, but it's always wise to have a backup plan. Outlets are not guaranteed at every seat, so arriving with a charged device is a good strategy. The cafes can get busy during weekend brunch, so for the best work experience, aim for weekday mornings or mid-afternoons when the rush subsides and the atmosphere becomes more conducive to focus.

| Address | Multiple in Brooklyn including: 200 Smith St (Cobble Hill), 110-112 S 3rd St (Williamsburg), 321 7th Ave (Park Slope), 1128 Bedford Ave (Bed-Stuy). |

Drawback: peak-hour crowding; outlets vary |

Drawback: popularity → noise and seat scarcity | 
| Variety Coffee Roasters | Low–Medium — roomy, laptop-accommodating shops (Park Slope highlighted) | Stable Wi‑Fi, longer hours at some locations; outlet availability varies | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ — Reliable for long writing/coding blocks 📊 | Extended focused work, neighborhood remote days | Advantage: consistent, roaster-owned quality. Drawback: crowded evenings/weekends; outlets vary |

Drawback: limited outlets at some seats; weekend crowding | 
| Poetica Coffee | Low–Medium — bright, comfortable cafés with relaxed laptop-friendly weekdays | Good pastries and food; amenities and outlets differ by location | ⭐⭐⭐ — Suitable for a few hours of work; community vibe aids focus 📊 | Neighborhood work sessions, casual meetings, relaxed focus time | Advantage: community-oriented, less corporate feel. Drawback: inconsistent amenities; noise for calls at some sites | 

## Making the City Your Office: Final Thoughts and Next Steps

You’ve just toured some of the most dynamic and productive **work cafes NYC** has to offer. From the expansive, community-focused vibe of **Think Coffee** to the artisanal dedication at **Devoción** and **Coffee Project NY**, it’s clear that New York City provides a rich backdrop for any remote professional. The key takeaway is that the “perfect” work cafe is not a one-size-fits-all destination; it’s a personal match for your specific workflow, mood, and daily objectives.

This guide provides a solid foundation, equipping you with details on everything from Wi-Fi reliability and outlet availability to the specific roast profiles and seating arrangements at top spots like **Variety Coffee Roasters** and **Poetica Coffee**. Your ideal spot for deep focus might be a quiet corner at **Ground Central Coffee Company**, while a collaborative project could thrive in the brighter, more social atmosphere of **Partners Coffee**. The city’s cafe scene is your flexible, extended office.

### Building Your Personal Cafe Toolkit

As you continue to explore, think of yourself as a connoisseur of workspaces. The most successful remote workers in a city like New York are adaptable. They build a personal roster of go-to locations for different tasks. Use the criteria from this article as your own evaluation checklist for any new cafe you discover.

**Your Quick-Check System for New Cafes:**

- **The Power & Wi-Fi Scan:**Is there a strong, stable connection and are outlets within reach of comfortable seats? This is your non-negotiable foundation.
- **The Vibe Check:**What’s the noise level? Is the music distracting or energizing? Is the general atmosphere conducive to focus or better for casual tasks?
- **The Seating Situation:**Are there dedicated laptop tables, communal areas, or just small two-tops? Seating dictates how long you can comfortably work.
- **The Policy & Etiquette:**Look for signs about laptop-free zones or time limits. Observe how other patrons are working to understand the unwritten rules.


Key Insight:Don’t limit yourself to just one cafe. Curate a personal list: a “deep work” spot, a “client meeting” spot, a “light admin and social” spot, and a “weekend work” spot. This approach gives you the flexibility to match your environment to your daily professional needs.

### From Finding a Seat to Finding Your Next Role

Mastering the art of working from cafes is a significant step in building a sustainable remote career. Once you’ve found your ideal work environment in NYC, the next logical step is often to find remote jobs that match your skills and support your location-independent lifestyle. With a comfortable and productive workspace secured, you can focus your energy on landing a role that offers the freedom you’re looking for.

Ultimately, turning New York City into your office is about more than just finding good coffee and free Wi-Fi. It’s about integrating your work life into the fabric of this incredible city, drawing energy from its streets, and finding community in unexpected places. The cafes we’ve highlighted are just the beginning of your journey. Be curious, be respectful, and enjoy the freedom of designing a workday that truly inspires you.

title: The Best NYC Coffee Shops With Wifi For Getting Work Done - New York - The Infatuation
author: Sonal Shah; Molly Fitzpatrick; Will Hartman; Bryan Kim; Willa Moore
text:
#### Sonal Shah

NYC Editor

A journalist since 2005, Sonal spent many years in India before returning to New York. She still prefers kebabs to hot dogs.

NYCGuide

photo credit: Emily Schindler

Apartments in the city are increasingly cramped, the wifi is increasingly terrible, and your roommates sit on the couch all day watching *Love Is Blind*. That’s where coffee shops come in. But you can’t work at just any coffee shop. Your workspace needs to have a strong internet connection, a bathroom, and preferably some food (because loitering for a few hours in a place with outlets and free wifi requires adequate sustenance). Here are some of your best options around NYC, grouped by borough.

Unrated: Restaurants we want to re-visit before assigning a rating. We only rate spots where you can eat a full meal. We won’t rate a coffee shop, bar that only serves peanuts, or dessert shop.

To get inside this tea room, you have to buzz into an unmarked door on Bowery and head up an industrial staircase to a room full of Togo couches and neon gramophones. There’s also a small room with vinyl records that you can listen to on headphones, and twice a day, a DJ comes in to blast something like Boards of Canada. Contrary to what you might think, the ambient music actually makes it easy to concentrate. Do your best to ignore the person recording a TikTok in the corner, and settle in with a Japanese tea and a pastry from Paloma in Greenpoint.

Between the couches and spread-out tables with green lamps on them, this coffee shop in the bottom of a FiDi residential building feels like an old-fashioned bank or reading room (it's actually the former set for an __immersive show__). It's a good place to spend several hours using the outlets and wifi, and drinking decent coffee. They also serve substantial snacks like loaded brioche toasts, and there’s a full bar for when you wrap up for the day. Or, you know, don't wrap up the day.

Conwell Coffee Hall

Asano is a budding coffee shop enterprise that takes over restaurants during the day, and one of those restaurants is __Sandro’s__ on the Upper East Side. It’s a little weird to sit in a proper dining room, at a table that’s usually covered by a white cloth, and listen in to someone speculating about Anna Wintour’s hair on a “work Zoom,” but the drinks are good, as are the pastries (from __Colson Patisserie__, and occasionally guest bakers). There aren’t a ton of outlets, but you can sit here for hours after paying your $16 coffee-and-pastry tax, and no one will bother you.

Sonal Shah

The Bar Room At The Beekman is not a coffee shop, but it serves coffee, has wifi, and is so beautiful that it will make you want to write a novel or something, even if the longest piece of creative writing you’ve ever done was a four-sentence text. This lavish FiDi __hotel bar__ fills up at night with people who drink two more espresso martinis than you thought possible, but it’s easy to snag an armchair during the day. Start with a coffee, and then move on to a martini once the post-work crowd begins to arrive (usually around 4pm).

The Beekman, a Thompson Hotel

Enoch’s is probably the least corporate hangout within five blocks of Hudson Yards. Originally a bike repair shop, it’s now run by the former owner’s son and channels a grungy ’90s coffee shop (sofas, neighborhood open mics) with a sprinkling of contemporary glitter (matcha lattes with fruity syrups, a carousel unicorn hanging out on the stage). It’s got wifi and an artistic bent, with paintings on the walls, evening figure drawing events, and a __documentary__ in post-production. Forget The FRIENDS™ Experience and just come here.

Sonal Shah

Everything at this East Harlem spot is geared towards getting work done and fostering community. Head past the faux-old-timey coffee bar with bulbs on ropes to a bigger working space in the back. There’s a communal table as well as smaller ones, and even a printer. They have pastries and brunchy foods if you need to refuel, plus alcohol, in case an innocent “What are you working on?” turns into “Want to get a drink?”

Sonal Shah

Just a few blocks from 103rd and Lexington, Townhouse Cafe checks the boxes for a useful neighborhood coffee shop, with plenty of charm. Besides wifi and seats with access to outlets, there’s a heated back patio with a couple of tables too. They serve coffee and tea from Austrian brand Julius Meinl, and make many of their own pastries. Check out the case stuffed with baklava, banana bread, and teddy bear financiers.

Sonal Shah

If the words Coke Studio evoke anything for you, you’re going to love Kaafi. At the Harlem chai and coffee shop, a framed TV plays music from the beloved, long-running Pakistani show. Even if you’ve never heard of it (ask a South Asian friend), it’s worth stopping by Kaafi for a cup of coffee or one of their four chai varieties. The place gets crowded around lunchtime, so come early if you just want to use the wifi, an outlet, and nibble on some homemade rusk. Or late—this spot is open from 7am-10pm.

Sonal Shah

Buunni is a coffee shop that specializes in small-batch coffee beans from Ethiopia (where the owners are from). They have several locations in Washington Heights and Inwood: the one in Pinehurst has a communal table and a few counter seats inside, but the Inwood location is the largest. So if you’re looking for a calming space with plenty of seating and lots of natural light, come here. The coffee is truly special, and they have snacks, including Ethiopian wraps. They also often host evening events, in case you need to unwind after a long day.

Maribel Acosta

Caffe Reggio looks more like a curio shop than a place to fire off emails. It opened in 1927, the ceiling is caving in, and it’s cramped with iron-backed chairs and tiny mismatched tables. But the lingering ghosts of other Greenwich Village strivers (and the opera soundtrack) are strangely soothing. Even more soothing: the coffee comes in heavy ceramic cups, and it’s available until 3 or 4am every night.

Sonal Shah

NBHD Brûlée is a great long-haul coffee shop in Harlem. There are tables and outlets inside, as well as a wraparound enclosed porch area when you need a change of scene. The sandwiches and snacks are better than they need to be for a workday breakfast or lunch break. Get the Cajun shrimp and grits and, when you’re ready to unwind and close the laptop, hit the wine section of the menu.

Come to this coffee shop inside of Harlem's Mushtari Hardware & Garden to get out of a rut, contemplate a fresh-baked cookie or a new plant, and chat about your project with a stranger. Mushtari Cafe only has metal stools for seats, but the wifi is good and the playlists are killer—particularly if Youseph is behind the counter.

Alex Staniloff

Have you ever wanted to answer emails in the middle of a rich person’s greenhouse? Hanging out at Remi43, which has two locations in Midtown, feels like that. It’s so lush and luxurious, your coworkers will probably ask where you are when you sign on for that quick daily meeting.

Carina Finn

Slate feels like it should be in Brooklyn or Tribeca, not a few blocks from Murray Hill. So if you find yourself in the neighborhood, make the most of it. Spend a few hours here, and maybe get a sandwich or some s’mores dip (exactly what it sounds like). And feel free to transition from coffee to rosé as the day goes on.

Bring sunglasses if you’re stopping at Cafe Calaca, because this Bed-Stuy spot has a great backyard—and the wifi extends all the way to the back of it. Located right by the Franklin Ave. subway stop, it’s a nice spot to hang out all day, and you can even take a meeting from that yard without catching too much glare. If you get hungry, they have a pretty good breakfast burrito.

Will Hartman

This horror-centric bookstore and cafe in Williamsburg is a great place to channel your inner Stephen King and get some writing (or other work) done, ideally while sipping a cappuccino out of a ceramic skull from an armchair by the fireplace. There’s also plenty of room for laptops around the cafe counter, or you could head out back to enjoy the graveyard mural along the patio. Spooky novelty drinks here include the Mary Shelley, a pandan latte in an appropriate shade of Frankenstein green.

Molly Fitzpatrick

Sweet Sundays keeps East Flatbush locals supplied with chaga matcha lattes, espresso-spiked arnold palmers, and two-tone butterfly pea lemonade. If you need a quick bite, they also make solid sandwiches, including a chicken pesto panini and a BEC with fluffy eggs mounded over a pile of thick-cut bacon. Order at the counter, then grab a seat in the adjoining sitting area where you can catch some natural light, use the wifi, and listen to coffee shop staple Hall & Oates.

Bryan Kim

A cavernous space that looks like an Anthropologie warehouse, this Greenpoint nonalcoholic bar is a great place to get work done during the day. They open at 8am and serve coffee, drinks with alleged wellness benefits, and pastries. Call a friend over for some mocktails once you've knocked off your daily word count.

Ciera Velarde

Not only is Cordelia in Crown Heights a cafe, wine bar, and bookstore, but it's also the unofficial co-working space for anyone with a 11238 zip code. It’s a great cozy place to get some work done, and you’ll be in like-minded company if you swing by during the day. There’s a small cafe menu of pastries from 8am to 3pm, and at 5pm they switch over to wine and a few small snacks. Two things to note: They close from 4pm to 5pm every day, and host lots of events during the week, so check the Instagram before heading over if that’s not the kind of mood you’re in.

Tiffany Yannetta

Everyone is on their laptop at Lazy Suzy in Bushwick, an airy coffee shop with plenty of room for seating, strong wifi, and classic rock playing at a phone-call-appropriate volume. While their food selection isn’t fully worthy of a dedicated lunch, they do have a good selection of pastries, including some vegan options like pumpkin and zucchini bread.

Will Hartman

Dumbo has a lot of crowded coffee shops where you’ll pay around $8.50 for a mediocre latte, but Fontainhas is different. The Goan all-day spot on Jay Street is generally quiet and sunny, which makes it a good place to get some work done alongside a royal chai topped with sea salt cream and a sprinkle of saffron. Sometimes a few very well-informed tourists find Fontainhas, and drink a bottle of wine in the middle of the day because they can. Lucky them.

Willa Moore

This all-day cafe in The Refinery at Domino by the Williamsburg waterfront is large and pleasant, if slightly corporate. Try a baked good, like a strawberry cheesecake danish or a churro croissant. When those sell out, not to worry. The Italian dip, a cross between a French dip and an Italian beef, will make up for it.

Natalie Black

Devoción roasts their own beans, and they have an exceedingly nice coffee shop in Williamsburg with exposed brick, a skylight, and repurposed pipes. So stop by and grab a table by a chest on a rug near a leather sofa that would look nice in an office of your own.

This is another cafe that turns into a super casual bar in the evening. Sensing a theme here? We could make a whole separate list for the work hard, play harder types among us, but for now, you should know that they have everything from lattes and sandwiches, to chaga (mushroom) coffee, natural wine, and cocktails. During the day, sit with your laptop at a table or the long counter with plenty of outlets up front. When they turn the lights purple, you know it’s time for that wine.

Noah Devereaux

With its open floor plan and excessive foliage, K’Far is kind of like an upgraded WeWork. The Israeli restaurant spans the entire hotel lobby at the Hoxton in Williamsburg, with a coffee cart and bar on one side, and a dining room on the other. Start your day on the coffee side, which has a ton of comfy chairs and some outlets. It turns into quite the scene by 10am, but if you don't mind some chatter, it’s a fun place to hunker down with a Yemeni latte and breakfast sandwich. You won’t get any free beer when you’re done, but you should definitely hit the bar for a martini.

Emily Schindler

There’s just something about the Park Slope outpost of Variety roasters that makes the coffee taste better than at their other locations. The cafe is big and sunny, with ample seating and fast wifi. It’s also close to Prospect Park, so you can take a walk if you need to clear your head in the middle of getting work done. But Variety's other locations around town are pretty good too.

Kate Previte

Odd Fox is such a pleasant place to hang out with your laptop that we actually suggest taking a “fake commute” here if you’re a remote worker who doesn’t live in Greenpoint. They brew Parlor beans, so the coffee is well above average, and there’s wifi as well as ample indoor and outdoor seating.

Alex Staniloff

Classy cane Jeanneret chairs and big front windows make this Tibetan cafe a pleasant place to spend a couple of hours eating a morning glory muffin, or getting some work done (with good wifi and a few outlets). There’s the obligatory cool-cafe cloud matcha, and drinks like a Berry Tsampa Boost (with barley), but we usually go for a mug of their Tibetan butter tea or coffee. The coffee in particular has a creamy, bitter-and-salty flavor that’s more complex than the usual latte. When you need a break, go browse the shelves stocked with Tibetan tchotchkes, books, and posters.

Sonal Shah

At Nhà Minh in Ridgewood, you can sit down with your laptop, bang out a few hours of work fueled by excellent Vietnamese iced coffee, pandan snickerdoodles and bánh mì, and leave with a painting from the wall (they’re all made by local artists). You might also see one of the owners' kids making use of a new pack of crayons while hanging out in the cafe, which is open nearly all day. They also regularly host events, like mahjong parties, with neighboring concert hall Trans-Pecos.

Kate Previte

In addition to fast wifi, this charming Long Island City coffee shop has conveniently located outlets, a folky soundtrack of Noah Kahan and Bon Iver, and pastries to snack on as you procrastinate. There’s even a designated play area for kids in the back of the cafe.

Molly Fitzpatrick

This neighborhood cafe in Astoria is well worth a trip for their iced matcha einspanner. And while you’re at it, you might as well hang at a table and eat an egg sando to take a break from building decks or whatever it is you do for money. There’s not much happening by the way of decor, but who needs design flair when you’ve got wifi and good matcha?

Anne Cruz

If you live in Ridgewood, this should be your go-to spot for laptop loitering. Milk & Pull has some hanging plants and hardwood floors that you’ll wish you had in your own apartment, and a nice amount of space, including a big communal table that you can use for a group hang. Go sit there and work with a friend, while you eat a donut or a bagel sandwich.

If you’re a coffee snob who lives in Astoria, you should be working from Kinship. This sleek modern cafe has their own line of single origin beans, and they actually have a robot-type machine that makes pour overs, so you don’t have to worry about pesky human errors ruining your perfect cup. There’s also a bathroom, strong wifi, and tons of seating both inside and outside.

Alex Staniloff

There’s a very long list of enjoyable things to do on Arthur Avenue in the Bronx. Getting work done isn’t on it. But with more than 50 coffee drinks, and 7am-11pm hours every day, Prince Coffee House makes working about as pleasant as possible. It’s also right at the entrance to one of Little Italy’s most concentrated strips of great shops and restaurants, so when you need a break, you’re not far from a bakery, cheese shop, or massive botanical garden.

Emily Schindler

Whether you’re looking for the city’s best beans or its best spots to linger with a warm mug, these are our favorite places to get something caffeinated.

NYC Editor

A journalist since 2005, Sonal spent many years in India before returning to New York. She still prefers kebabs to hot dogs.

Senior Staff Writer, NYC

Molly is a writer and reporter from New Jersey who now lives in Queens. She is clinically incapable of shutting up about either place.

Staff Writer, NYC

Will is passionate about bagels and being disappointed by The Mets. He has been writing for The Infatuation since 2023.

Editorial Lead, NYC

Bryan joined The Infatuation in 2016. By his own estimate, he’s been to more NYC restaurants than everyone but the health inspector.

Staff Writer, NYC

Willa was raised in Brooklyn and now lives in Brooklyn, which means her favorite bagel place hasn't changed since birth.

title: 20 Best Coffee Shops in NYC For Working [2026 Guide] | Bel Around The World
author: Www Facebook Com; Belaroundtheworld; Isabel Leong
text:
Have you ever dreamt about what it’d be like to earn a living while having the freedom to travel around the world?


Many people have turned that dream into reality. In the US alone, the number of digital nomads from 2019 increased by 49% in 2020. This data suggests that millions of people have come to realize that they actually can work from anywhere around the world – further debunking the myth of having to work in an office to earn a sustainable income.


The pandemic has normalized flexible work setups across different industries, giving workers the independence to work from anywhere they choose, whether it be from home or a coffee shop thousands of miles from home.


If you’re working as a digital nomad or thinking of becoming one, one destination every digital nomad has to visit is New York City. Famously known as the “City That Never Sleeps,” NYC is also fabled for its extraordinary diversity and bustling environment.


As a matter of fact, NYC has just been named the most popular tourist destination in the U.S.!


Whether you’re a coffee nerd or a New Yorker looking for a place to maximize productivity, you know that having an environment conducive to focused work is essential.

Pin this for later:




At A Glance

## 20 Best Coffee Shops In NYC That Are Laptop-Friendly: The Perfect Places To Work



The good news? You’ll have tons of choices when it comes to New York City cafes. Here are some of the best laptop-friendly cafes the city’s different boroughs have to offer:


### Manhattan


Kicking off our list is New York’s most popular borough, Manhattan. This bustling borough is home to some of the city’s most iconic attractions: Times Square, Central Park, the Empire State Building…


Anyone coming in for a visit is in for a treat as the number of tourist spots and cafes stretches to so many different parts of the borough.


#### 1. The Bean

The Bean is a unique cafe that will transport you to another world with its vintage and modern decor.

Their creatively crafted beverage menu boasts signature espresso drinks like the “Frozen Mona Lisa” and “Mother Theresa” latte, as well as their imaginative “Nutella Fitzgerald.” Even the food options show off impressive creativity, such as their colourful “Rainbow Bars” and Nutella stuffed sugar “Bombolini.”

The atmosphere at The Bean fosters inspiration and artistic vibes in its customers. Whether you’re looking for a new spot for your morning coffee or a place to relax with friends over a creative snack, The Bean is the perfect choice.

With subway stops nearby, getting there is easy too. Overall, The Bean offers an excellent combination of creativity, quality coffee, delicious treats, and inspiring surroundings – making it one of the best cafes around!

Menu

Location

#### 2. The Roost

The Roost is a one-of-a-kind café that offers an unparalleled blend of style, sustainability, and comfort. Its chic and contemporary décor make it the go-to spot for freelancers to work or friends catching up over brunch.

The café’s speciality coffee blends are smooth yet strong — perfect for any coffee lover. All delicacies on their menu will satisfy your taste buds – from the savoury sandwiches to their Uber Bavarian Style Pretzel; every bite is delicious.

The service at The Roost is exceptional with friendly staff available to help you navigate through their versatile menu while offering personalized suggestions tailored to meet your preferences perfectly. Additionally, prices are reasonable — a great value-for-money proposition!

What sets them apart from other cafes in town? Their outdoor seating area filled with greenery allows patrons ample opportunities to soak in sunlight while enjoying freshly brewed coffee or meals.

Urban practicality meets artistry at this oasis called ‘The Roost.’ Overall, if you’re looking for a unique experience that strikes a perfect balance between indulgence and eco-consciousness, look no further than ‘The Roost’.

Menu

Location

#### 3. Think Coffee

Think Coffee is a cosy cafe that offers conscious coffee culture in the midst of busy city streets. The warm atmosphere with comfy couches and communal tables makes it an ideal spot to unwind for hours.

They brew premium blends of excellent coffee, robust, smooth and bursting with flavours; their selection also includes teas and other drinks if you’re looking for something different than what typical coffee shops offer. Their menu has vegan and gluten-free choices peppered throughout including breakfast items, sandwiches, salads pastry selections; everybody can enjoy without any worries.

What sets Think Coffee apart is its commitment to sustainability practices that make a positive impact on farming communities. With each sip you take, you’ll feel good knowing your caffeine fix supports organic farming projects too.

In short: Think Coffee provides not just high-quality coffee but strives to be part of the solution for a better world through sustainable initiatives across the board, making it an inspiring cafe destination for conscious consumers!

Menu

Location


### Brooklyn



Known for its rich history and distinctive architectural heritage, the borough of Brooklyn is also home to legendary pizza, popular tourist attractions, and, you guessed it, laptop-friendly cafes with a bustling coffee scene.

#### 4. Freehold

Freehold is a cafe, bar, and lounge in downtown Brooklyn that offers a unique blend of industrial chic decor and top-notch coffee.

Their extensive menu includes traditional drip coffee as well as inventive specialities espresso drinks like the Matchadamia tea — a tasty combination of matcha and macadamia milk.

The food options are equally impressive with their selection of breakfast items, sandwiches, salads, and small plates to choose from. They also offer vegetarian and vegan options for those with dietary restrictions.

What makes Freehold stand out from other cafes is its combination of cafe/bar/lounge atmosphere all within the same space. It’s an ideal spot to get your caffeine fix, for social gatherings or live music nights while providing friendly service throughout your visit.

Despite moderate-to-upscale prices making it slightly more pricey than some other cafes in the area, their knowledgeable staff provides great recommendations ensuring you have an enjoyable experience at Freehold.

Its location is easily accessible by public transit which adds to its popularity among locals in New York City looking for a trendy hangout spot without breaking the bank!

Menu

Location

#### 5. Kos Kaffe

Kos Kaffe is a charming and inviting cafe located in Park Slope, Brooklyn. The cosy atmosphere welcomes visitors with wooden accents, lush greenery, and natural light to create a warm ambience. However, it’s the quality of the coffee that stands out – this gem offers expertly crafted espresso drinks and rich drip coffee that will impress any caffeine enthusiast.

In addition to their amazing beverages, Kos Kaffe also serves delicious food items at reasonable prices. They use organic ingredients as often as possible and even provide eco-friendly products for purchase. This sustainable approach aligns perfectly with the cafe’s commitment to environmentalism.

Kos Kaffe combines everything from its excellent coffee selection to its welcoming environment while ensuring an environmentally friendly ethos throughout the entire experience. If you’re looking for an all-in-one great spot for top-notch coffee and good vibes plus sustainability practices, make sure you visit Kos Kaffe!

Menu

Location

#### 6. Devoción Coffee

Devoción Coffee is a standout coffee spot in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. From its rustic atmosphere to its high-quality blends sourced directly from Colombian farmers and roasted on-site, this cafe provides the ultimate coffee lover experience.

You’ll surely appreciate the unparalleled smoothness of the coffee and the attentive service provided by knowledgeable staff who are skilled at their craft. While slightly pricier than other cafes in the area, Devoción Coffee delivers exceptional value in every penny spent on delectable baked goods or unique breakfast and lunch items.

What truly sets this establishment apart is its sustainable business model that ensures fair prices for farmers while producing top-notch quality brews made fresh by an impressive large coffee roaster situated within the premises.

In sum, Devoción Coffee is a must-visit destination for any enthusiasts looking for new coffee shops to try out – it offers inspiring stories behind each cup served!

Menu

Location

#### 7. Coffee Project New York | Fort Greene

Coffee Project New York | Fort Greene offers a unique coffee experience that stands out from other cafes in the area. With a focus on innovative brewing techniques and carefully sourced beans, this spot offers complex and flavorful cups of coffee that are worth the higher price point.

The open layout creates a relaxed atmosphere, perfect for working remotely or socializing with friends. The friendly staff adds to the welcoming vibe of the cafe.

If you’re feeling hungry, there are plenty of tasty options available including vegetarian and vegan choices. While it may be pricier than some other cafes in the area, Coffee Project New York | Fort Greene’s commitment to quality coffee makes it well worth it.

Overall, Coffee Project New York | Fort Greene is an excellent choice for those looking for an exceptional cup of coffee in a welcoming space with great food options available.

Menu

Location

#### 8. Hungry Ghost Coffee

Hungry Ghost Coffee is a charming café located in the heart of Brooklyn, showcasing a rustic décor that provides an ideal ambience for coffee enthusiasts and foodies alike. The friendly service at this cafe serves as its key highlight alongside high-quality coffee sourced from small farms and roasters.

Apart from delicious coffee, Hungry Ghost offers fresh pastries, locally-sourced sandwiches and breakfast items on their menu that caters to everyone’s taste buds. Not only do they maintain attention to detail when sourcing ingredients but excel at latte art resulting in intricate designs which add a creative touch to your order.

Given its reasonable prices, it remains budget-friendly while being surrounded by shops and attractions on Flatbush Avenue serving exceptional caffeine wrapped up with nature-inspired beauty details intertwined with attentive customer service making it stand out amongst other cafes in New York City.

Menu

Location


### Queens



If entertainment is what you’re after, Queens has more than its fair share of the cultural learning experiences that New York City has to offer. Be it museums, galleries, or other attractions that are unique to the Big Apple, this place has just about everything to tickle your fancy. It’s no wonder people love to work and visit here — the positive energy is positively contagious!


#### 9. Sweetleaf Coffee Roasters

If you are in search of a stylish yet economical coffee shop that serves excellent brews, Sweetleaf Coffee Roasters is the place to go. Located in Long Island City, this café offers unique cold brew options and exceptional coffee quality that will tempt your taste buds.

Not only do they serve delicious breakfast meals including vegan and gluten-free alternatives, but they also have knowledgeable and friendly staff who make customers feel valued.

Moreover, this café’s art-filled walls provide a trendy vibe for visitors while offering them an opportunity to learn about different coffee-making processes through their classes and cupping sessions. Additionally, Sweet Leaf’s affordability makes it budget-friendly for everyone without sacrificing quality.

Overall, whether you’re getting some work done or meeting friends over brunch or drinks; the cosy ambience coupled with delectable lattes with Insta-worthy designs and yummy bites catered towards Instagram aesthetics are just wonderful extras that come along with every visit!

Menu

Location

#### 10. Partners Coffee

Partners Coffee in Long Island City, Queens is a must-visit café for coffee enthusiasts. Its stunning interior design with wooden and metallic elements provides an elegant atmosphere flooded with natural light – making it the perfect spot to relax and unwind or to grab a quick bite.

Partners Coffee is well-known for its exceptional quality of premium beans that are carefully crafted by experts resulting in smooth and robust flavours, offering the ultimate caffeine experience any time of day.

Aside from their signature brews, they offer breakfast and lunch options such as pastries, sandwiches and salads while providing top-notch service with every visit despite higher prices. Being situated in the trendy neighbourhood of Long Island City makes transportation quite accessible together with popular restaurants & shops nearby.

What sets Partners Coffee apart from other cafés is roasting their own beans on-site ensuring freshness at all times while offering informative workshops on everything about coffee-making. In summary; Partners Coffee offers elevated elegance coupled with taste integrity, making it one of New York’s best cafes – definitely worth experiencing!

Menu

Location

#### 11. Paris Baguette

Paris Baguette is a café that offers the perfect combination of Korean-French cuisine. This Queens-based establishment has earned its popularity with freshly baked bread and delicate pastries made daily on-site, all at reasonable prices. Their menu also includes sandwiches, salads, desserts, and exceptional quality coffee roasted to perfection.

The atmosphere is elegant yet comfortable, making it an excellent place to catch up with friends or attend meetings. What sets Paris Baguette apart from other cafes in New York City is their unparalleled service combined with attentive and knowledgeable staff who welcome regulars and first-timers alike.

Located near public transportation in Queens means accessibility isn’t a problem either for those seeking nearby attractions. Overall, Paris Baguette provides an excellent cafe experience that caters to foodies looking for unique tastes while not breaking the bank – making it worth checking out!

Menu

Location


### Staten Island


This borough is located in the southern part of the city and is the greenest neighbourhood among the others. It has a large expanse of the park area and is also historically known for its role in the arrival of immigrant families in the early 1900s.


Currently, Staten Island is home to a diverse population, unique locations, and a myriad of different tourist spots where you can learn about different cultures and ethnic backgrounds too.


#### 12. SIPS + MAKER

SIPS + MAKER is a unique café in New York City that offers more than just exceptional coffee and meals. It has positioned itself as a maker space where patrons can unleash their creativity while enjoying some aromatic brews. Located on New Dorp Lane, Staten Island, this modern café boasts an inviting ambience that attracts all kinds of customers.

The menu features top-notch coffee and yummy food options, including sandwiches, salads, pastries, and breakfast items. The friendly staff adds to the unbeatable service experience offered at SIPS + MAKER. Pricing is mid-range but still affordable for great value for money.

What sets this cafe apart from its competitors is its ability to offer craft-making capabilities ranging from pottery to jewellery-making classes – perfect for artists seeking inspiration or creative hobbyists looking to explore something new.

In summary, SIPS + MAKER Café offers an unforgettable adventure with delicious meals and innovative activities such as mug-making courses– catering not only to caffeine addicts but creatives too!

Menu

Location

#### 13. Every Thing Goes Thrift & Vintage | Book Cafe

Book Cafe in Staten Island is a must-visit for coffee lovers, bookworms, and live music enthusiasts. With its vintage decor, an impressive collection of books for sale, and a diverse menu with excellent coffee blends – this cafe offers something for everyone to enjoy.

What makes it truly special is the combination of its role both as a used book store and community event space offering regular live music performances. The friendly staff provides great customer service at affordable prices while being accessible by car or public transport.

All in all, Book Cafe is cosy, and welcoming with delightful food & drinks plus an added entertainment angle that keeps customers returning time after time! It’s no surprise that it has become a hidden gem loved by locals and visitors alike who find an escape in the peaceful ambience offered here – making this cafe one of New York City’s best-kept secrets!

Menu

Location

#### 14. Beans and Leaves Coffee and Tea Cafe

Beans and Leaves Coffee and Tea Cafe is a top destination for coffee aficionados in New York. Its welcoming atmosphere, highlighted by rustic decor and soft lighting, makes it the perfect place to relax while enjoying an excellent cup of coffee or tea.

The cafe’s extensive selection of high-quality blends caters to different tastes — bold, smooth or mellow — while their gourmet loose-leaf teas add depth. Aside from beverages, the cafe offers breakfast options such as delicious bagels, muffins & croissants ideal for morning commuters. Salads & sandwiches make up lunch orders.

Friendly staff ensures each customer feels valued; their warm approach provides great service & adds more enjoyment to your visit an attractive outdoor seating area complements everything!

Finally, you can enjoy all this without spending too much – prices are affordable but still maintain quality. In summary, whether you’re on the go or taking some time off Beans and Leaves Café has what it takes to please both taste buds & wallets alike making every visit worth remembering.

Menu

Location

#### 15. The Mustard Seed – Cafe & Coffee Co.

The Mustard Seed – Cafe & Coffee Co. is a charming and cosy cafe in Staten Island that serves great coffee, fresh-baked pastries, and delicious breakfast items.

Their impressive selection of flavorful blends will satisfy any coffee lover’s taste buds; complemented by its speciality drinks made with high-quality espresso are simply amazing! You’ll also find their sandwiches and salads very popular among regulars.

The staff is friendly, attentive and knowledgeable about their menu making your visit enjoyable every time. Its reasonable prices make it perfect for those looking for an affordable treat or quick bite in this comfortable setting capable of accommodating groups of all sizes.

Occasionally featuring live music performances they offer a unique vibe at this quaint spot adding to the overall ambience along with the books & gifts contributing even more charm to one’s experience.

Overall, whether you’re stopping by after work or hanging out during weekends, The Mustard Seed-Cafe & Coffee Co offers excellent java goodness accompanied by scrumptious nibbles within its calming ambience without breaking the bank!

Menu

Location


### Bronx


#### 16. Prince Coffee House

Prince Coffee House offers a warm and inviting atmosphere with its rustic-modern decor, making it the go-to spot for high-quality coffee blends. What sets this cafe apart from others is their dedication to sustainability practices through using compostable cups and utensils that help to reduce their environmental impact.

Additionally, they cater to various dietary needs with vegan and gluten-free options while still offering an impressive selection of breakfast and lunch items such as salads, sandwiches, pastries, baked goods, and desserts at affordable prices.

The friendly service combined with the commitment to sustainability practices makes Prince Coffee House an exemplary establishment in the bustling neighbourhood known for Italian-American cuisine and culture. With premium ingredients used in food and beverages served at accessible prices, one can indulge in delightful treats without breaking the bank.

Overall, Prince Coffee House provides quality food & drink options while creating a welcoming environment suitable for all who visit.
