Capital One Cafe is a unique entry in the list of cafes near me with WiFi. It's run by a bank but feels like a modern coffee shop.

- 
Key benefits for workers: - There is a lot of seating, including comfy couches.
- Free seltzer on tap is a nice perk.
- Private 'nooks' are available for taking calls.
 
- 
Other advantages: - The WiFi is free and there's no pressure to leave.
- There are multiple bathrooms, which is rare.
- The security is excellent, so your gear is safe.
 

This is a great spot if you need to take meetings. The environment is professional but relaxed. It's one of the best cafes near me with WiFi for people who need a full-office experience.

## 7. The Bean, East Village, NYC

The Bean in the East Village is a classic choice for cafes near me with WiFi. It has an edgy vibe that many people enjoy.

- 
Work-friendly features: - The cafe is confirmed to be laptop-friendly.
- There are power outlets for charging your devices.
- The menu has a big selection of food and drinks.
 
- 
Things to know: - The tables are close together, so it can feel crowded.
- Staff might ask you to buy more if you stay many hours.
- It's a popular spot, so finding a seat can be a challenge.
 

This cafe is best for people who like a busy, social atmosphere. The energy can be good for creative work. For similar spots in other cities, see Los Angeles coffee shops with WiFi.

## 8. Ludlow Coffee Supply, Lower East Side

Ludlow Coffee Supply is a favorite among cafes near me with WiFi for the downtown crowd. It has a cool, relaxed vibe.

- 
Why people work here: - It's known as a spot for people on laptops.
- The hours are long, from 7am to 7pm.
- The music and people-watching are enjoyable.
 
- 
Important drawbacks: - The WiFi can be inconsistent at times.
- It's a good idea to have a backup hotspot.
- You need to arrive early to get a good seat.
 

This cafe is perfect if you want a trendy environment. The extended hours are great for people with flexible schedules. Just be prepared for possible internet issues.

## 9. Picky Barista, Upper West Side

Picky Barista on the Upper West Side is a reliable option for cafes near me with WiFi. It has a warm and friendly feel.

- 
Advantages for remote work: - There is a dedicated WiFi network for customers.
- The staff is known for being very friendly.
- There are multiple outlets for charging.
 
- 
Key rules to remember: - Laptops are only allowed on weekdays, not weekends.
- The space is comfortable but can fill up.
- The oat milk latte comes highly recommended.
 

This cafe is a good choice for a neighborhood work session. The weekday-only laptop policy helps keep it calm. It's a nice spot if you live or work on the Upper West Side.

## 10. The Granola Bar, Upper West Side

The Granola Bar brings a cozy vibe to the list of cafes near me with WiFi. It's a chain from Connecticut that fits well in NYC.

- 
What makes it work-friendly: - The WiFi is reliable for getting tasks done.
- There are many milk options for coffee drinks.
- The food menu has vegan and vegetarian choices.
 
- 
The overall experience: - The high tables are great for people-watching.
- The vibe is fresh and positive.
- At night, it becomes a wine bar.
 

This spot is ideal if you want healthy food options. The atmosphere is bright and clean. It's a nice change from the typical coffee shop.

## Final Thoughts

Finding the right cafes near me with WiFi can level up your work-from-anywhere routine. The best spots combine good coffee, reliable internet, and a comfortable seat. No matter if you're in New York, San Francisco, or Los Angeles, there are great options. Remember to be a good customer. Buy a few items if you plan to stay a long time. And always have a backup plan if the WiFi is slow. With this guide, you can find a perfect cafe for your next work session. Happy working!

title: 16 Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC (Laptop-Friendly)
author: Theworkingline; The Working Line
text:
Since we were on the topic of the best cafes to work in Manhattan yesterday, I felt like in between some beautiful MAC lipstick dupes and other spring Yankee Candle scents, I’d tell you today about the best cafes to work in Brooklyn NYC.

There are oh-soo-many **cool cafes in Brooklyn to work and study if you’re looking for a good **laptop friendly cafe, and you’ll find them here today.

Needless to say, a lot of the coffee shops to work in Manhattan are stunningly welcoming to freelancers, students, and digital nomads.

Around Chelsea, Soho, and Hell’s Kitchen, you’ll find quite a few coffee shops – and there are a lot of cafes to work in NYC Midtown as well.

But it’s really around Brooklyn Heights, Williamsburg, Park Slope, and Cobble Hill we’ll find some of the best cafes to write in NYC, study on our laptops, and just do some really productive work.

## 16 Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC (Laptop-Friendly)

In this guide, you’ll find some of the best cafes to work in Brooklyn NYC; a lot of which are actually quite famous among New Yorkers.

As much as possible, I’ll mention laptop friendly cafes in Brooklyn with free WiFi, strong coffee, delicious pastries and sandwiches, and power outlets whenever possible.

It’s quite tough to find cool cafes to study in Brooklyn and in New York City in general with power outlets, just because the buildings are quite old and many coffee shops haven’t gotten around to offering customers more power plugs.

In any case, whether you’re looking for cafes in Brooklyn to work or study, I’d always recommend having your laptop charged.

Same if you were working in Rome or Paris, to be honest.

Anyway, since I know you’re here to learn about new coffee shops to work in Brooklyn, let’s get down to it, and help you make it happen!

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Devocion

The first super cool cafe I want to mention is Devocion, which is home during the day to seemingly more students and freelancers you could imagine.

If you’re looking for the best cafes to work in Brooklyn around Williamsburg, Devocion is an institution in the area.

It’s really one of these cool Brooklyn cafes where you won’t feel out of place typing away on your laptop.

During the week, many a freelancer comes to enjoy the free WiFi and coffee imported overnight from Colombia to New York.

Beware, at weekends, Devocion does not offer WiFi, just to allow people to unstick their eyes from the laptop screen and actually catch up with one another.

And if you’re ever looking for other cafes in Brooklyn to work, Devocion also has other locations in Flatiron and Downtown Brooklyn, as well as Manhattan.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Canary Wharf

### Best Cafes in Brooklyn to Work: Vineapple Brooklyn Heights

Now for one of the ultimate best cafes to work in Brooklyn, the super laptop friendly Vineapple Cafe. It’s located on Pineapple Street, really close to Clark Street station in Brooklyn Heights.

If you’re looking for aesthetic cafes in Brooklyn to study your midterms and work away on your laptop, Vineapple is probably one of my favorites.

A few seats outside to observe life going on around you, perfect for freelancers looking for cafes to write in NYC.

But the best part of Vineapple Cafe is probably its backyard, colorful and inspiring, where you can work on your laptop for hours without being interrupted.

Read: The Best Free Views in London

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Sey Coffee

While Sey Coffee in East Williamsburg is not the biggest coffee shop in Brooklyn, you’ll still find lots of freelancers and students working there at every hour of the day.

Sey Coffee offers two things freelancers love in a coffee shop: an open space and delicious coffee from all parts of the world, including Ethiopia, Mexico, and Costa Rica.

Beyond that, two things we digital nomads love even more, power outlets and free WiFi, are also available at Sey Coffee.

That makes it super easy to consider as one of the best cafes to work in Brooklyn when you don’t want to study at home.

Read: The Most Colorful Places in London

### Best Cafes in Brooklyn to Work: Variety Coffee Roasters

Another really cool laptop friendly cafe in Brooklyn is Variety.

I talked about Variety Coffee Roasters in my guide to the best cafes to work in NYC around Manhattan, and here it is again, with their branch in Park Slope.

There are quite a few other cafes to work in Brooklyn which bear the name Variety Coffee Roasters, including Williamsburg, Greenpoint, and Bushwick.

But if you’re ever looking for cafes to work in Park Slope, you’ve got a sure thing with Variety.

Free WiFi, delicious coffee, and a nice spacious coffee shop to enjoy your workday all throughout the day.

Read: The Best Coworking Spaces in Lisbon

### Best Laptop Friendly Cafe in Brooklyn NYC: Brooklyn Roasting Company

Located between Downtown Brooklyn and Brooklyn Heights, the Brooklyn Roasting Company cafe is perfect if you’re looking to make it happen for yourself that day.

It’s spacious and airy, and the Brooklyn Roasting Company has large windows to stare into the void as you’re focusing on your next chapter – or sentence if you’re a writer.

You won’t find as many freelancers and student peers nor as much space for working in the Clinton St coffee shop as you would have in the now-closed Jay Street branch, but it’s still an amazing place to write and work on your laptop.

Read: The Most Colorful Houses in Notting Hill

### Best Cafes in Brooklyn to Work: Freelancers Hub

The Freelancers Hub is located in Industry City, in Sunset Park, and it’s a free coworking space perfect for freelancers who are not feeling like working at a coffee shop – or want to switch up their work environment.

You can either come for a hot desk, or you can sign up as a member for free and enjoy up to 8 days of free coworking a month – even better than a coffee shop in Brooklyn, even with free WiFi, especially if you want to make connections!

In a city where everything from a single espresso to the rent is tough on the wallet, the Freelancers Hub is a great opportunity for freelancers to launch their business and build it up in time.

Read: The Most Colorful Streets in Camden

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Coffee Project Fort Greene

Coffee Project in Fort Greene is another one of the best cafes to work in Brooklyn, especially if you like the exposed brick layout and having other freelancers working nearby.

I don’t know about you, but whether I work in Europe, the UK, or anywhere in the world, I like feeling that other people are working and studying next to me – it makes me feel as if we’re all in this together.

Coffee Project has other cool cafes in New York, notably in the East Village and Chelsea if you’re looking for other cafes to work in Manhattan.

The Coffee Project location in Fort Greene is probably not the biggest study cafe you can find in Brooklyn, but you’ve got free WiFi and a few power outlets in the coffee shop.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC

### Best Laptop Friendly Cafe in Brooklyn NYC: Stumptown Coffee Roasters

Stumptown Coffee Roasters is also one of those really well-known cafes to work in NYC, and they’ve got a really cool location in Cobble Hill.

It’s not the biggest either compared to some other cafes like Devocion, but there is definitely space to enjoy a good cup of coffee and the free WiFi.

For starters, you’ve got a few seats at the entrance of the Stumptown Coffee Roasters coffee shop perfect to enjoy the sunshine on beautiful bright days.

Then, in the back, another room in which you can sit down and start cracking on those projects of yours without being interrupted.

One of the most aesthetic cafes in Brooklyn to work, and laptop friendly at that.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in South London

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Velvette Brew Park Slope

Velvette Brew is another one of these really aesthetic, exposed-brick cafes to work in Brooklyn, but this time, we’re in Park Slope.

It closes pretty early like most coffee shops in NYC – at 6 pm, the work day at Velvette Brew is done.

However, it does open at 7 am, so you’ve actually got a lot of time to make something of your day, something meaningful and successful by your standards.

However, it’s one of the best cafes to work in Brooklyn if you’re looking for good, free WiFi, with a few seats in addition to communal tables. With such a space, who wouldn’t feel inspired to write and study?

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in West London

### Best Cafes in Brooklyn to Work: Manhattanville Coffee

Impossible to talk about the best cafes to work in Brooklyn without mentioning Manhattanville Coffee in Crown Heights.

If you’re looking for a real laptop friendly cafe in Brooklyn, the number of power plugs combined with the free WiFi makes Manhattanville Coffee a perennial favorite of students and freelancers.

The coffee shop is not only super welcoming of freelancers, the coffee is *actually *really good.

Probably one of the most aesthetic cafes in Brooklyn to work, and feel inspired when you lift up your eyes from the screen to see how many other people are trying to make it just like you.

Read: The Best Pink Cafes in London

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Freehold Williamsburg

Next up, you’ve got one of my favorite coffee shops to work in Brooklyn, Freehold in Williamsburg.

No other space in Brooklyn really resembles Freehold, which is a blend of a cafe, coworking space, event space, and even a club.

During the day, you’ve got one of the best laptop friendly cafes in Brooklyn, where every customer can get on the WiFi and enjoy the make-it atmosphere Freehold boasts.

At night, Freehold becomes a club, and if you’d like to enjoy even more activities thanks to Freehold, you’ve got the possibility to join their membership program to get exclusive invites to events.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Lower Manhattan

### Best Laptop Friendly Cafe in Brooklyn NYC: Kos Kaffe

With Kos Kaffe, you’ve got one of the best cafes to work in Brooklyn if you’re close to Park Slope. It’s one of the most popular coffee shops in Brooklyn, at least for students and freelancers.

And while Kos Kaffe really is decently spacious, I can never get over the fact that I have to arrive at a coffee shop to work as early as possible during the day.

If you’ve got the same itch to arrive super early to work from a cafe, Kos Kaffe opens at 8 am – and closes at 5 pm, which gives you plenty of time to be productive with work.

You’ll find lots of freelancers working at Kos Kaffe since you’ve got free WiFi and amazing coffee there, but pay attention to rush hour times.

During these hours, which go from 12 pm to 3 pm during the week and 10 am to 4 pm at weekends, you’ll only be able to use your laptop in certain parts of the coffee shop to allow people to enjoy the delicious sandwiches and pastries that Kos Koffee offers.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work on the Upper West Side

### Best Cafes in Brooklyn to Work: Hungry Ghost

Hungry Ghost in Williamsburg is another one of the coolest cafes to work in Brooklyn, especially given the amount of space they’ve got – and a really good laptop friendly cafe as well!

In addition to amazing coffee, Hungry Ghost also offers free WiFi, and it’s another one of those coffee shops you’ll find students and freelancers working.

During the week, Hungry Ghost opens at 7 am, so if you’re the kind of person who can’t wait to get a cup of coffee to get to work, this one is going to be your new HQ.

And if you’d like to try other coffee shops, Hungry Ghost also has other locations in North Williamsburg, Park Slope and Fort Greene – all amazing cafes to study in Brooklyn.

Read: The Best Coworking Spaces in Rome

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Sweatshop

The Sweatshop is not the biggest coffee shop in this guide, but it’s one of the really cool cafes in Brooklyn, and a bit different since it offers lots of specialty coffee and Aussie specialties.

You’ve got a few seats here and there, along with a communal table, and since The Sweatshop is pretty popular, I’d definitely recommend arriving as early as possible.

Free WiFi, freelancers and students working nearby, and a terrace outside to work on your laptop as soon as the weather gets warmer all combine to make The Sweatshop one of the best cafes in Brooklyn to work.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Lisbon

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Odd Fox Coffee

If you’re around Greenpoint, you’re going to want to pay a visit to Odd Fox Coffee.

The uber-colorful spot is one of the most aesthetic cafes in Brooklyn to work, especially since they’ve got plenty of seating space inside for you to make it happen.

The Greenpoint coffee shop is perfect whether you’re looking to study your books, write on your notebooks, or are looking for a laptop friendly cafe in Brooklyn to work.

Odd Fox currently has two locations; one in Greenpoint, as well as one in Bed-Stuy. Both coffee shops are great for work, enjoying life passing by, make plans for the future… Up to you.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work on the Upper East Side NYC

### Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC: Starbucks Cobble Hill

There are quite a few Starbucks in Brooklyn, and they’re all to some extent some of the best cafes to work in Brooklyn. However, you know Starbucks – they’re kind of the same everywhere.

If you’ve recently moved to Cobble Hill and don’t really know of any coffee shops to study and do work, Starbucks will always be a great idea, although it has much less *personality *than all the Brooklyn cafes I’ve mentioned here today.

On Montague St, you’ve got a pretty good Starbucks with quite a few seats where you’ll find people working all day long.

There’s also another one on Court Street, where you’ll find a really good seating area in the basement – perfect if you’re looking for cafes in Brooklyn to work without being interrupted.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Astoria & Queens

## 16 Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC (Laptop-Friendly)

There you have them, all the best cafes to work in Brooklyn NYC!

From Williamsburg to Cobble Hill, Park Slope, and Crown Heights, you’ve got all you need if you’re looking for really cool and aesthetic places in Brooklyn to study, do some work or even just chill once in a while!

*Until next time!*

title: 14 Best Cafes to Work in East Village NYC (Laptop-Friendly)
author: Theworkingline; The Working Line
text:
If you’re looking for the best cafes to work in East Village NYC, you’re going to be happy you’ve landed on The Working Line today.

Lately, I already told you about some of the best cafes to work in Manhattan, alongside some places to study in Brooklyn.

I’m well on my way to creating guides to all the best laptop friendly places and cafes in New York City – that’s one of my big goals this year after I told you about so many working coffee shops in London, Barcelona, Rome, and Paris.

For now, let’s focus on the best coffee shops to work and study spots in the East Village. It’s one of the areas of Manhattan where you’ll find some of the cutest and quaintest coffee shops.

With its proximity to Brooklyn and the overall artistic vibe of the East Village, it’s easy to understand how there can be so many study cafes in the surroundings – it attracts many students and freelancers on a daily basis.

**And if you’d like to learn more about places to work around the world, check out the following guides:**

- The Best Cafes to Work in NYC Midtown
- The Best Cafes to Work in London
- The Best Cafes to Work in Rome
- The Best Cafes to Work in Paris

## 14 Best Cafes to Work in East Village NYC (Laptop-Friendly)

In this guide, you’ll probably see some laptop friendly cafes in New York City that you’ve actually already seen on The Working Line.

Indeed, some of the best cafes in Manhattan to study, from The Roost to the Book Club, are located in the East Village.

Later on, I will be writing about some of the best coffee shops to work in Chelsea as well as other spots from the Upper East Side to Lower Manhattan and even places like Astoria and Queens – so stay tuned for that.

For now, we are going to be focusing on the best study spots in East Village; some of the best working coffee shops in NYC with free WiFi, great coffee, and power outlets where possible.

### Best Cafes to Work in East Village NYC: The Roost

One of the very best cafes to work in East Village NYC is The Roost, which is not only a coffee shop. Indeed, it offers a pretty wide sitting area and a bar at the end of the shop.

The Roost is located on Avenue B in Alphabet City, and it offers amazing coffee as well as power outlets and free WiFi.

It’s basically a really spacious area where you will find tables, armchairs, and really comfortable sofas on which you can sit for hours to do some very productive work.

It’s not unusual to find freelancers, students, and digital nomads working at The Roost as it’s clearly a spot where you feel at home.

In my opinion, one of the best coffee shops to study in East Village before the place turns into a full-on bar and party place at night.

Read: The Best Places to Study in Rome Italy

### Best Laptop Friendly Cafe in NYC East Village: Perk Kafe

There are several Perk Kafe coffee shops in NYC; one of them is located on the Upper East Side and the other one is in the East Village.

This is not one of the biggest laptop friendly cafes in New York City.

Still, when you’re around the East Village and want to find a good working coffee shop, Perk Kafe is actually a productivity-*triggering *place.

Perk Kafe closes pretty early (like most coffee shops in New York City), but the atmosphere is friendly, heartwarming, and definitely appropriate if you are looking for a laptop friendly cafe in East Village.

If you want to try it out, it is open from 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM most days of the week, and you have quite a few tables and free WiFi. Up to you to decide whether you want to relax, read a good book, or work on your laptop for a few hours.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work near King’s Cross Station

### Best Cafes to Work in East Village NYC: Coffee Project

Coffee Project has quite a few branches scattered throughout Manhattan, but the one we are focused on today is located on 5th Ave, not too far from Bowery.

The coffee shop has quite a few interesting recipes when it comes to their drinks, especially the Deconstructed Latte and some* really* good classic coffee to start the day.

Coffee Project is not the biggest cafe in East Village to study, however, there are a few seats, free WiFi, and a few power outlets scattered throughout the coffee shop.

I would definitely recommend you come as early as possible as Coffee Project reserves some of the tables for people who are just planning to get a drink and a bite and get on with their day – so just keep that in mind before you visit.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work near Tottenham Court Road

### Best Cafes to Study in NYC East Village: The Bean

Now, if you are looking for very spacious cafes to work in East Village NYC, you are going to *love* The Bean.

It is a really huge coffee shop in which you will find a few tables in the front and the back of the shop, and you are bound to find freelancers, students, and digital nomads really grinding on their laptops.

The Bean coffee shop is located on 2nd Avenue, right in the heart of the East Village, and you have free WiFi as well as power outlets which should allow you to work for a good few hours when you visit.

Given just how many people are typing away on their laptops at The Bean every hour of the day, it’s clearly one of these study coffee shops in NYC that you can count on – especially since it’s open from 7 am to 9 pm every single day.

Read: The Best Places to Write in London

### Best Cafes in East Village To Study: Book Club

I told you about the Book Club in my guide to the best cafes to work in Manhattan, and as we’re talking about coffee shops to study in East Village, you will find that the Book Club provides an atmosphere that you cannot find *or feel *anywhere else in New York City.

The Book Club is much more than *just *a coffee shop. Located in Alphabet City on Avenue B, it is also a library and a place where you will be able to share and connect with the community.

The Book Club organizes workshops and activities throughout the month, and it’s open from 8 am to 12 am every single day.

It’s a really cozy place to study, and lots of people come with their laptops and books to study, work a little bit throughout the day, or just read. I mean, it’s an indie bookstore, after all.

That is why I would recommend you come as early as you can as the Book Club is a really popular study coffee shop in the East Village: it fills up quickly, and you wouldn’t want to miss out on that vibe.

Read: The Best Pink Cafes in London

### Best Cafes to Work in East Village NYC: Ninth Street Espresso

Ninth Street Espresso is the coffee shop I would recommend if you’re looking for *utterly amazing* coffee in Alphabet City.

It is not the biggest coffee shop at all, however, you can get some really good work done there.

Ninth Street Espresso on 9th Street is actually bigger than some of the other branches of the cafe (like the one on 10th Street, just a few steps away), so you will be able to use the free WiFi for a good while and really just grind till you drop.

Just make sure you’re not coming with a full workday planned as I do feel there are many other cafes to work in East Village NYC better suited for that.

Read: The Best Coffee Scented Candles

### Best Coffee Shops to Work in NYC East Village: Kona Coffee

Kona Coffee is one of the most famous cafes in the East Village to study, just because it is quite wide, has great opening hours, and offers delicious Hawaiian coffee beans.

Kona Coffee is located near Bowery, super easily accessible from Bleecker Street station, and you have* a lot *of seating space inside.

Given how cozy (understand: tiny) a lot of the New York coffee shops are, it’s easy to understand why students or freelancers come in flocks whenever there is an inspiring (understand: big) space to do work around the corner.

You might have to share your table with someone else, but since Kona Coffee is open from 7:00 AM till 7:00 PM almost every day of the week, you might actually have some space to yourself for a while if you come early.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea London

### Best Cafes to Work in East Village NYC: Everyman Espresso

Next up, you have Everyman Espresso – a decently-sized coffee shop in East Village either which also offers free WiFi and amazing coffee.

Everyman Espresso has a good number of tables which you will probably have to share.

However, since many of the people visiting are also students or freelancers, you will definitely have that motivating atmosphere around you.

Everyman Espresso is bright and airy, and with that quirky decor blended with classic minimalism, you’ve got here one of the best cafes to work in East Village.

And if you are ever looking for a cafe to work in the gorgeous Brooklyn area, Everyman Espresso also has another branch on Park Slope which can come in handy whenever you’re in the area.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Canary Wharf London

### Best Study Spots East Village NYC: Elsewhere Espresso

Elsewhere Espresso is located close to 2nd Avenue, and it’s probably one of the cutest coffee shops to work in East Village.

Granted, you don’t have the biggest cafe here, but Elsewhere Espresso is laptop friendly and has some of the best coffee in New York City.

For starters, you have very friendly staff there and Elsewhere Espresso offers free Wifi inside and outside.

The staff is super friendly, the decor is inspiring – what more could we wish for?

The 6th Street coffee shop is open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. every day of the week, and if you’re looking for the best cafes to work in East Village, you’re definitely going to find yourself very productive there.

However, I would definitely recommend coming there as early as possible as it’s definitely a hidden gem when it comes to finding super cool laptop friendly cafes to study in NYC.

Read: The Best Coworking Spaces in Rome Italy

### Best Cafes to Work in East Village NYC: B Cup Cafe

If you like really colorful and instagrammable cafes, another great option if you’re looking to do some productive work and study, is B Cup Cafe on Avenue B.

Make sure to bring cash, as B Cup Cafe does not accept credit cards.

You’ve not only got amazing pastries and great coffee at B Cup Cafe but also free and super fast Wifi and a spacious study spot.

The coffee shop is *really *vivid in all senses of the word and echoes the artistic atmosphere of the East Village to perfection.

Whether you’re trying to finish your novel, write an article or study while having coffee shop sounds in the background, B Cup Cafe is one of the best options for whoever has an artistic streak in your personality.

Read: The Best Coworking Spaces in Soho London

### Best Cafes in East Village To Study: Pause Cafe

Another one of the best cafes to work in East Village is actually one I already mentioned here on The Working Line.

Pause Cafe is run by a Moroccan owner, something that I always feel close to as I’m half French and half Moroccan.

Obviously, in a Moroccan coffee shop, you would find delicious and super sweet Moroccan pastries, but Pause Cafe also offers great coffee, and lunch bites if you’re planning to stay the day.

There is free Wifi, and just a few power outlets throughout the whole coffee shop, so make sure you come with your laptop and your phone charged.

The coffee shop is open from 7 am to 8 pm most days of the week, so you have plenty of time to be super productive.

If you’re looking for the best working coffee shops in NYC around the East Village, Pause Cafe is one of the most spacious options whether you want to study for a few hours or do some journaling.

title: The 6 Best Coffee Shops To Work in NYC
author: Molly Wilcox
text:
Last Updated on March 27, 2025 by Cassandra Gambill | Published: June 22, 2022

As remote work has become more and more of the norm over the past several years, many are understandably starting to go a bit stir-crazy. And while there’s no place like home, sometimes you just really have to get out. When that’s the case, it’s time to head to one of the **best coffee shops to work in NYC**.

Set up shop at one of these workspaces away from home (which also happen to have great coffee)! Photo credit: Joseph Pearson

## Felix Roasting Co. (SoHo)

Felix Roasting Co. is the epitome of New York City’s Soho neighborhood: picturesque, posh, and polished. Upon walking in, you’re greeted with pink, velour swivel chairs, quaint bistro tables, and painted floors.

The walls are decorated with regency-era inspired paintings and wall sconces. There’s a row of tables on the first floor by the coffee bar, as well as rows of tables on an upstairs mezzanine floor that’s removed from the hustle and bustle below.

Felix Roasting Co. wants you to reimagine your coffee break and workspace. Why rush around the city when you could find refuge in its relaxing atmosphere? At their lounges, rest and relaxation are paired with gilded glamour.

## Nook (Bushwick)

Nook lies in the midst of Bushwick’s most buzzing neighborhood, just a few blocks off of Maria Hernandez Park. The space has huge floor-to-ceiling windows, lots of plants, unfinished ceilings, cozy lights, mismatched chairs and reading nooks throughout.

Not only are they one of the best coffee shops to work in NYC, they also offer acai bowls, baked goods, a large selection of craft beer and many different events. Pop in for a women’s writing group, chess tournament, trivia, knitting and crochet, live jazz, and more.

## Book Club (East Village)

Book Club is an East Village establishment that serves three of the best things in life: books, wine, and coffee. The shop is perfect for someone looking for a snug respite among the chaos that is New York. It’s decorated with dark wood bookcases, old red rugs, leather seats and a long bar with high seats.

Book Club also organizes community events like writers’ workshops, book signings, and drinking and drawing. It offers a great opportunity to engage in your community, or to simply get a few hours of work in over a coffee or glass of wine.

## Devoción (Williamsburg)

Devoción is one of the best coffee shops to work in NYC, although finding a table might be a fête in and of itself.

This coffee shop’s popularity is based on its incredible Colombian coffee that they roast in-store, a large assortment of pastries, and their overall industrial-meets-cozy décor. There are a handful of tables and chairs, a few large, leather couches, and counter spaces along the wall.

The coffee shop has a live plant wall and a huge skylight, as well as some of the best coffee in New York.

## Brooklyn Kolache Co (Bedford–Stuyvesant)

Established in Brooklyn’s bustling Bed-Stuy neighborhood, Brooklyn Kolache Co is not only a perfect place to stay awhile, it also is a show-stopping bakery.

They specialize in small-batch Texas-style kolaches, which are hand-filled sweet and savory pastries. One of the best coffee shops to work in NYC, Brooklyn Kolache Co also offers a full espresso bar and good amount of seating in their artfully decorated, modern shop.

Their most famous kolaches include Houston-style beef sausage, ham and cheddar, chocolate ganache, and blueberry sweet cheese.

**Insider’s Tip:** Looking to while away a rainy morning or afternoon? Check out our article on what to do in NYC when it rains!

## Ludlow Coffee Supply (Lower East Side)

Working at Ludlow Coffee Supply is like working within the comfort of your living room, without working in your living room. In that sense, it’s a perfect home away from home, filled with comfortable couches, decorative rugs, records, beautiful windows, and house plants.

Working there feels like you’ve been invited to work at your friend’s home who always knows where the coolest gallery and restaurant openings are. It’s pristinely decorated to feel like you’re in someone’s living room who is well-traveled and in the know.

Ludlow Coffee Supply is known for cozy, homey vibes as well as delicious food to snack on that expands past pastries and into actual health-conscious meals.

## Talea (Williamsburg and Cobble Hill)

Talea is a Williamsburg-based brewery that sports high ceilings, bright colors, modern décor, lots of greenery, and, most importantly, tons of tables and outlets. On an average workday, people start arriving in the morning, where they can order filter coffee and breakfast tacos, and continue to show up throughout the day.

And the best part about setting up shop in a brewery? When the clock strikes quitting time, your beer is just a few steps away. They brew delicious sours, hazy IPAs, lagers and more and they regularly partner with local kitchens to serve different foods throughout the month.

Talea is a woman-owned brewery in Williamsburg and Cobble Hill, so clean bathrooms and changing tables are in no short supply. However, we recommend working here during the week, as the eatery gets packed on weekend afternoons.

# Best Coffee Shops In NYC To Work Remotely

Remote work in NYC is a delicate balance: you need stellar coffee, dependable WiFi, and an ambiance that says “I’m definitely being productive.” Lucky for you, we’ve rounded up six of the best coffee shops in NYC to work remotely. Whether you’re a local or just visiting, these spots are worth a pit stop for your next “working” session.

### Hungry Ghost Coffee Shop

If you're a remote worker on the prowl for a caffeinated haven, **Hungry Ghost** has your back—and your latte. With 13 spots scattered across NYC, you're practically guaranteed to stumble into one on your way to "work" (read: pretending to work while scrolling TikTok). These bright, bustling cafes come equipped with free WiFi, plenty of seating, and just enough ambient chatter to make you feel productive. Their gourmet coffee, brewed in partnership with the cool kids at Stumptown Roasters, is the kind of fuel your deadlines demand. Not a coffee purist? No problem—they’ve got nitro brews and kombucha on tap to keep your vibes as fresh as your inbox is full.

### Manhattanville Coffee

**Manhattanville Coffee** is Harlem’s answer to your remote workday woes, offering cafe tables, communal tables, and big picture windows perfect for world-watching between emails. It’s the kind of spot where “working hard” feels suspiciously like vibing. The coffee? Top-notch, brewed with beans from Parlor Coffee. Tea drinker? They’ve got you covered with Kilogram tea to keep the zen alive.

### Conwell Coffee Hall

Just steps from historic Stone Street, you’ll stumble upon the “Life and Trust” Bank—a name that screams finance bro, not freelancer hangout. But here’s the twist: on the ground floor lies **Conwell Coffee Hall**, a café so gorgeous you’ll forget you’re answering emails. This is not your average coffee joint—it’s a full-on Art Deco daydream, complete with dramatic floors, sky-high ceilings, and a sleek bar tucked behind an old-school teller cage. And then there’s the mural—a Diego Rivera-esque masterpiece that stretches across the entire wall, blending skyscraper grandeur with apocalyptic vibes. It’s basically the perfect metaphor for your inbox.

### Devoción Café

Head straight to **Devoción Café**, where coffee dreams come true. This Brooklyn gem is tucked inside a revamped warehouse, rocking the kind of reclaimed wood and exposed brick aesthetic that screams “serious coffee drinker” (even if you still add oat milk and sugar). With cozy leather couches, free WiFi, and some of the best brews in town, it’s the ultimate spot to sip, scroll, and pretend you’re crushing that to-do list.

### The Granddaddy

Great coffee? Obviously. Good WiFi? Yep. Bathrooms? You bet. Sassy baristas? Occasionally—keeps things interesting. **The Granddaddy** in Chinatown nails the laptop-friendly café vibe, making it one of NYC’s top spots to park yourself for a work session.

### Cafe-Flor

**Café-Flor** might just be NYC’s most Instagram-worthy workspace. Step inside, and you’re instantly welcomed by the soothing scent of fresh coffee and greenery—it’s like your to-do list just got a little less intimidating. With chic bistro chairs, sleek green leather booths, and an abundance of plants that double as productivity boosters, this spot oozes charm. Bonus: cozy private nooks are scattered throughout, perfect for when you need to dive deep into work—or just escape your inbox. **@cafeflornyc**

title: Tips to Choose the Best Coffee Shop to Get Work Done in NYC
author: Autonomous
text:
# Tips to Choose the Best Coffee Shop to Get Work Done in NYC

## Table of Contents

Startup enthusiasts, freelancers, and seasoned remote workers will find no better atmosphere than a good coffee shop.

The environment, dependable wifi, and flexible workspace of a coffee shop frequently outperform a dedicated small rolling standing desk. For remote workers drawn to the allure of New York City, discovering the ideal coffee shop might be just as important as obtaining suitable housing. So, let’s explore some crucial tips that will help you choose the best coffee shop to get work done in NYC.

## Coffee Shops: The New Remote Workplace

What does remote work mean? It is simply the freedom to choose when and where you work. Nowadays, coffee shops are becoming the new remote workplace as more individuals shift towards work from home computer jobs. There are many pros and cons of working from home, but the flexibility and convenience of remote work are gaining all the hype.

Sometimes referred to as the "coffee shop effect", workers claim that working remotely at cafés increases their focus and productivity. People stay focused because of the background noise and the absence of distractions from other employees.

## How to Choose the Perfect Coffee Shop to Get Work Done in NYC

Workspace necessities include wifi, a nearby toilet, and food because spending several hours in an area with power outlets and free internet necessitates proper nourishment.

Let's look at some pointers for choosing the best coffee shops to get work done in NYC:

### Choose an Appropriate Spot

Not every café is ideal for getting work done, but most cafes can be considered for a peaceful environment. It is recommended that you locate a coffee shop with ample seating. In a perfect world, the seats would be both cozy and located in a rather quiet place. If you choose a store that is too tiny, sitting for longer periods can become a problem. Finding a store that sells food as well as drinks is a good idea to counteract the effects of coffee.

### Consider the Distance

It would be a waste of time to pick a location that is far away, where you have to waste time commuting.

Further advice: Don't pick a spot that's always bustling with people. The good coffee shops to work in NYC will benefit from all the activity, but your productivity will suffer.

### Look for the Perfect Ambiance

The type of music coffee shops play is one of the most important factors to consider. Pick a spot where the noise level is low or nonexistent if you intend to get any serious work done while you're out. In addition, noise-canceling headphones are a lifesaver during conferences and phone conversations.

### Ensure Proper Facilities

When choosing a coffee shop to work in, it’s crucial to ensure that basic facilities are easily available. Look for amenities such as parking (you cannot function without concerns of your car getting towed by the cops), clean toilets, AC, and comfortable chairs.

### Go Through the Menu Beforehand

It's important to carefully assess the budget you wish to spend during the day. So do check the pricing, decide accordingly and organize your day. Also, it’s a good idea to order prior and ask the barista or the management, to deliver you your meals and beverage at specified times of the day.

## Tips to Work Easily in a Coffee Shop without Any Disturbance

### 1. Visit in Off-Peak Hours

If you expect to spend the majority of your day working from a restaurant or coffee shop and have flexibility in your schedule, try going during off-peak hours. It’s better to avoid the rush as much as possible if your local go-to café has a line out the door and no tables to spare.

### 2. Move Your Meeting

Along with slowing down the wifi, hosting a meeting or having a phone conversation in the café might be quite invasive to those around you. If you need to take frequent calls, consider setting up at a table near the entrance where you can stroll outdoors while keeping an eye on your items.

### 3. Bring a Battery Backup

Being ready and independent are key components of a successful remote work environment.

When you arrive at a café and discover every electric outlet is taken, what should you do? To keep your devices charged, be ready with a power bank or high-capacity portable charger. These are a few work from home essentials that don't require outside resources.

### 4. Buy Something and Reorder Often

When you take up space for an extended amount of time while using the café's internet, draining the electricity from their outlets, and using the bathroom, you should be paying for that service. At a minimum, when working from a coffee shop for an hour and a half, it's appropriate to spend at least $5 at the business with tips for staff. If you plan to remain longer, make sure that you always have something to eat or drink at your table. Try to make a purchase every hour to an hour and a half.

## 3 Top Coffee Shops to Work in NYC

If you are not interested in doing your job at home, these are the best coffee shops to work in NYC, and you should consider going without any hesitation.

### Café Flor

Café Flor is more than just a coffee shop; the aroma of fresh coffee balances the aspects of a wine bar and plant boutique.

Café Flor caters to the needs of remote workers by offering a variety of seating alternatives, such as comfortable sofas and tables, suitable for working from home. Even with free wifi, connectivity problems frequently occur, indicating that upgrades are required. This adaptable workplace is ideal for informal discussions, concentrated work sessions, or formal meetings.

### Variety Coffee

There is a distinct quality to the coffee at Variety Roasters' Park Slope location that sets it apart from their other sites; it is the best coffee shop to work in NYC. The cafe is large and bright, with lots of seats and fast wifi. Additionally, Prospect Park is not far away, so you can take a stroll there if you need to unwind in the middle of doing a task. However, Variety's other stores across the city are also rather good.

### Perk Kafe

Perk is basically just a beautiful, straightforward coffee shop on the Upper East Side where you can take a stool and linger for a bit. It isn't very huge or fancy, but they have Stump town coffee, Dough donuts, and - most importantly - wifi and a restroom. So if you’re looking for a coffee shop in this section of town, consider this one.

## Conclusion

Selecting the ideal coffee shop for work involves more considerations than just the coffee itself. It also involves the atmosphere, facilities, and general mood that improve productivity. Taking these works from home tips into account will help you find a coffee shop that complements your working style and increases output. Now that you have these ideas go out and discover the perfect coffee shop to get work done in NYC.

title: 10+ Best Cafés To Work In NYC - Casey La Vie
author: Casey
text:
# 10+ Best Cafés To Work In NYC

If you work from home, sometimes you just need a change of scenery. Getting out of your apartment and into some real clothes can help you boost your productivity and feel more connected to others.

Research actually shows that working outside the house can even help you develop healthier boundaries with your job. And all the ambient buzz and the vibey atmosphere can help improve focus and creativity!

But where should you go? In NYC, my favorite spots are cafés. They’re cozy and welcoming, with plenty of comfortable seating for your laptop. Most offer free Wi-Fi, and you can grab your morning pick-me-up while you settle in for a productive day.

I know there are thousands of cafés in New York City, but not all of them allow remote workers. (They might have no-laptop, no-Wi-Fi policies, especially during busy hours or for extended stays.) To help you find the best cafés and coffee shops to work in, I’ve put together a list of my favorite spots around the city.

## 10+ Best Cafés To Work In NYC

#### Little Ruby’s Cafe

Little Ruby’s Cafe is a warm, inviting space filled with natural light. With plenty of comfortable seating and reliable Wi-Fi, it’s the perfect place to settle in and get work done. It’s an Australian café, so if you’ve ever wanted to try vegemite, this is the place to do so.

The atmosphere is relaxed, so unlike a traditional dining experience, you won’t feel rushed out after finishing your coffee and croissant. You can linger for hours, soaking in the vibe while checking items off your to-do list.

Here’s more on why Ruby’s is one of my favorite cute lunch spots in NYC.

There are multiple locations:

- SoHo: 219 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10012
- Murray Hill: 442 3rd Ave, New York, NY 10016
- East Village: 198 E 11th St, New York, NY 10003
- West Village: 225 West 4th St, New York, NY 10014
- Williamsburg: 98 Berry St, Brooklyn, NY 11249

#### Lafayette Grand Café & Bakery

Housed in a historic building, Lafayette Grand Café & Bakery exudes moody French charm. If you’re looking for a work spot that’s both inviting and refined, this is the place.

They offer free Wi-Fi and plenty of seating, so you’ll never feel cramped. And while you’re there, treat yourself to one of their mouthwatering desserts—they’re worth every penny. (I personally love The Suprême—it’s sweet, creamy, and perfectly chocolatey.)

You can grab anything from a cheap but delicious drip coffee to a premium fresh juice. Either one will give you a boost of energy and motivation to get to work.

Lafayette Grand Café & Bakery is located at 380 Lafayette St, New York, NY 10003.

#### Devoción

Devoción is more of a traditional coffee house, offering light pastries and small bites to enjoy alongside your cold brew or espresso.

Unlike the historic charm of Lafayette, Devoción is bright, modern, and fresh, with plenty of natural light and a minimalist design that’s perfect for focusing on work.

There are plenty of seating options, including communal tables, bar seats, and small tables. Free Wi-Fi and accessible power outlets make it laptop-friendly, but snagging a seat near a plug can be a bit competitive. So bring extra power to keep the work sesh going.

There are several locations:

- Williamsburg: 25 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11249
- Flatiron: 150 E 18th St, New York, NY 10003
- Downtown Brooklyn: 154 Front St, Brooklyn, NY 11201
- East Village: 81 E 7th St, New York, NY 10003

#### Voyager Espresso

If you’re a coffee connoisseur, you’ll love Voyager Espresso. As one of NYC’s multi-coffee roasters, they offer beans from renowned roasters around the world. Their café also serves elevated takes on favorite small bites like avocado toast and oatmeal. These are perfect for a quick snack during your breaks.

Voyager Espresso takes inspiration from the Voyager Spacecraft (hence the name), and their design approach reflects that. This unique spot stands out with its futuristic decor and modern ambiance, featuring sleek marble tables and countertops.

The space is a bit small, and the industrial stools might not be comfortable for long stretches. It’s better for shorter visits when you want a quick change of scenery.

Voyager Espresso is located at 110 William St, LL, New York, NY 10038.

#### Think Coffee

For a spacious coffee shop with both communal workspaces and private booths for distraction-free seating, Think Coffee is a great choice.

While the dining area is large, the cozy and modern vibe keeps the space feeling calm and welcoming. They offer free Wi-Fi and have power outlets available at each location.

Think Coffee serves both coffee and loose-leaf tea. If you’re hungry, you’ll find a selection of sandwiches, baked goods, and other items, including vegan and vegetarian options.

There are nearly a dozen Think Coffee locations from SoHo to Williamsburg.

#### Bluestone Lane Upper East Side Café

Do stunning sandstone archways and vaulted ceilings sound like the perfect dreamy spot for a day of remote work? That’s exactly what you’ll find at Bluestone Lane Upper East Side Café. The second Australian-inspired café on the list!

Located right across the street from the historic Church of Heavenly Rest, much of its design inspiration comes from the church, creating a truly unique and tranquil atmosphere.

They offer plenty of coffee options and a variety of health-conscious food selections to enjoy while you work at communal or individual tables. And if you enjoy seasonal picks, they have plenty of those, too. It’s an ideal, stress-free spot to knock out tasks on your to-do list.

While you’re in the area, check out some of the best bagel spots on the Upper East Side. They’re all perfect if you’re craving this NYC classic. And don’t miss the chance to head across the street to Central Park. You’ll be right at the 90th St Entrance!

Bluestone Lane’s Upper East Side Café is located at 1085 Fifth Ave, New York, NY 10128.

#### Café Grumpy

If Bluestone Lane’s lavish decor feels overwhelming, Café Grumpy offers a quieter, more minimalist alternative with a calm atmosphere.

This no-frills café is quiet and serves high-quality, sustainably sourced coffee, teas, and juices. There’s also no shortage of delectable pastries you can snack on as you enjoy your drink.

It’s the perfect spot to get work done, offering a familiar, distraction-free environment and a straightforward coffee experience.

However, be sure to check the location before you visit. Some Café Grumpy spots don’t offer free Wi-Fi and discourage remote work due to smaller dining areas. It depends on which one you choose!

There are six locations across Brooklyn and Manhattan. The Park Slope location is the only one I’ve experienced that no longer allows remote work. But if anything changes, they update their website frequently to reflect any changes.

#### P&T Knitwear

Despite the name, P&T Knitwear isn’t a textile store! It’s a family-owned indie bookstore and café that’s a favorite remote work spot for literature lovers.

The venue is spacious, offering tables, bar tops, and stadium-style seating. You can pick your perfect spot, enjoy the scent of books, and maybe catch the sounds of a classic movie playing softly in the background.

P&T offers free Wi-Fi, original drinks, and quick treats. And when it’s time to reward yourself after a productive day, why not pick up a good book?

It’s important to note that you don’t *have *to purchase anything when visiting. They’re very welcoming of remote workers looking for a comfortable space to get things done. However, they also note that they’d love to be the place where you work *and *get caffeinated. In my experience, their coffee and selection of snacks is definitely worth it.

P&T Knitwear is located at 180 Orchard St, New York, NY 10002.

#### Black Cat LES

If working from your couch is your favorite perk of remote work, Black Cat LES is the café to visit. Its cozy, living room-style setup with vintage furniture makes it feel like a home away from home.

Beyond the variety of seating options, Black Cat LES offers free Wi-Fi, plenty of power outlets, and even a printer. This café doesn’t just allow remote workers—they truly support them!

While you’re there, enjoy a coffee, smoothie, or tasty light bites like omelets or croissants. And when the workday winds down, relax with one of their free books or board games.

Black Cat LES is located at 172 Rivington St, New York, NY 10002.

#### Kalei NYC

Here’s another café with vintage furniture, but this one offers an elevated vibe thanks to its rotating art exhibits and modern staging.

You can enjoy coffee, tea, and a small selection of carefully chosen snacks. For seating, there are two floors to choose from, plus a rooftop patio. So many options!

If you’re looking for a workspace that’s both invigorating and creatively inspiring, Kalei NYC is one of the best spots in the city.

Kalei NYC is located at 159 Bowery, New York, NY 10002.

#### Lulla’s Bakery

Lulla’s isn’t in Manhattan like most of the recs above, but it’s one of my favorite spots. Get the Dirty Chicha for a unique and indulgent caffeinated pick-me-up.

Tuck into an arepa, a guava croissant, or pan de queso at this Venezuelan spot in Williamsburg.

You can grab a seat at the bar, a booth, or my favorite: the half-booths in front of the windows. They are so cozy.

If you stop in during the day you’ll find the place packed with others getting some work done and if you’re here on a Friday, make sure to stay for happy hour since the owner is a former mixologist from Eleven Madison Park.

Lulla’s Bakery is located at 169 Graham Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11206

### How To Stay Focused At Work While In A Café

##### Choose Your Café Wisely

Not all cafés are going to be the best fit for every type of work and type of worker. Here are some things to consider before picking a café:

- How much space you need to work comfortably
- What tends to distract you most
- Your preferred seating type
- The ideal level of background noise for focus
- Lighting that works best for you—bright and airy or dim and cozy
- The hours you’re most productive (and whether the café is open then)

Thinking about the answers to these questions will help you find the perfect fit.

##### Pick a Low-Distraction Spot

When you go to your café, pick a spot that will let you completely focus. Consider sitting facing a wall or a direction with less visual clutter.

High-traffic areas or window views can be distracting if you’re a people watcher, so be mindful of that when choosing your spot. I’m not usually distracted once I’m locked in, so I love to find a cozy corner to settle into.

##### Headphones On

Even though ambient café noise can be great background noise for work, at peak times, it may be too much. And some cafés, like Kalei NYC for example, tend to have noisier crowds and more eclectic music. Great if you’re meeting up with friends, not so great if you’re trying to sit and focus. I recommend putting on noise-canceling headphones or listening to focus music to stay productive. You could also use Loops ear plugs for some light noise reducing – they’re super cute too.

##### Plan Before You Start

Before jumping right into work, make a list of what you want to accomplish. Make sure you are super specific with your goals, so you can really measure your effectiveness at the end of the day.

You could even consider using the Pomodoro Technique to elevate your productivity. You can hear more about that in my productivity and motivation tips post.

##### One Drink, One Treat

Don’t spend all the money you earn that day at the counter. It’ll be tempting with all the coffee and pastry aromas, but limit yourself to one drink and/or treat a day.

I recommend you start your session with a drink and end it with your treat. This will prevent interruptions in your workflow while still allowing you to fully enjoy your out-of-the-house work experience.

##### Silence Notifications

Digital distractions can be even more disruptive than the ones around you. Silence as many notifications as possible, and consider temporarily blocking social media and other distracting apps or sites.

Just checking one quick text can land you in that trap of “let me just check one more notification.” Put your phone in your bag or laptop case so it’s out of sight, out of mind. Also, don’t forget to put your laptop on DND, too.

I also love to set my Slack status to “focus mode” so my coworkers understand I won’t be replying instantly to any DMs.

##### Bring Backup Power

Most cafés won’t have enough outlets to go around, if they have any at all. Bring a charger, but also bring a power bank to keep your battery full no matter where you are.

##### Develop a Routine

Getting out of the house is healthy when you work remotely. But at the same time, you don’t want to waste half your morning figuring out where to go.

Pick one day a week (or more) to work at a café, and plan ahead. Decide where and when you’ll go at least a few days in advance. Having all the details sorted beforehand will help make your time out of the house both productive and rewarding.

Plus, planning in advance allows you to check online to see peak hours for your café destination.

###### Visit one of these remote-work-friendly cafés and find your flow.

Whether you’re seeking a change of scenery, a boost in productivity, or simply the joy of working with a perfectly brewed latte at your side, NYC’s café scene has something for every remote worker. Grab your laptop, pick your spot, and let the city’s energy fuel your best work.

If you liked these recommendations and decided to check one out, I’d love to hear about your experience! Make sure to keep up with me on IG @caseylavie to see where I’m up to. And don’t forget to sign up for my emails! These let you know each time I post so you can be the first to see all of my latest recommendations—from restaurants and pop-ups to fun bars and exciting events.
