title: My Favorite Coffee Shops Near Fordham LC
author: AVERY GRAFELD; Editor
text:
No longer a sit-down chain, Starbucks has long replaced its spacious, plush seating with stiff metal chairs. There are 17,068 locations in the U.S., but any semblance of community and customer interaction is now restricted to a mobile app or drive-thru line.

I have been guilty of purchasing from this global chain. The convenience, especially given my busy schedule, is unmatched; however, Starbucks has long been accused of violating labor laws by firing pro-union employees. Not to mention, I have noticed a decline in their quality of beverages. Rather than supporting this coffee giant I have stepped towards alternatives, and Fordham Lincoln Center (FLC) students should do the same by considering these local coffee shops instead.

**Birch Coffee: **My favorite coffee shop in proximity to FLC is undeniably Birch. The aroma of blueberry muffins and ground coffee beans is a refreshing change of pace from New York City’s stifling air quality. It may not be a mom-and-pop cafe, but compared to Starbucks, Birch optimizes better ingredients and authentic customer service for a fraction of the cost. My signature order, a large iced dirty chai, costs $6.25 with a student discount. 

Conversely, the same order costs $9.58 on the Starbucks mobile app. With watered-down oat milk and an unpleasant ratio of chai to espresso, convenience is rarely worth the absence of flavor.

**Masseria Caffè & Bakery:** Masseria offers rich and refined Italian coffee paired with flakey frittatas that melt in your mouth. Located across from Birch, it is the perfect spot to do homework on a rainy day. The cafe has a long table with high chairs by the expansive window, and you can people-watch while sipping on my personal favorite — a cold brew — for six dollars. 

**Paris Baguette:** One of the larger chains in this list, Paris Baguette has 4,500 locations worldwide. Although this is not a local New York establishment, a 20 oz. iced dirty chai costs $7.27 — still cheaper than Starbucks — and offers a comforting atmosphere with rustic wooden tables and chairs. I say this is the perfect spot to grind out a homework assignment or catch up with friends.

Cafes have long served as a space for study sessions, first-dates, last-dates and friendly gatherings. Going out for coffee is relatively low-stakes; it’s not overly formal, and centers around a beverage most people are familiar with.

I urge you to break your Starbucks reliance. I promise accessibility is not worth the steep costs and internal labor strife. As consumers, we have substantial power to drive the market, and every purchase should be made wisely, even when going out for something as trivial as coffee.

# 8 Must Try Coffee Shops Near Fordham University

duncan.shea • March 2, 2021

## 8 Must-try Coffee Shops Near Fordham University

 Fordham has much more to offer apart from superb transport and safe neighborhoods. The area has some interesting and life-changing treats for both students, locals, and travelers. In case you're a Fordham University student, these are the best coffee joints for studying or meeting with friends. 


 
 **1. CHOCnyc**

 CHOCnyc is the recommendable top choice for students searching for the best coffee shops near me at Fordham University. CHOCnyc has many cappuccinos and frosted cappuccinos, the caramelized croissant is spectacular, and the paninis will surpass your expectations. 


 
 They have a comfortable environment for studying, working, or meeting with friends. The WI-FI is A-OK. CHOCnyc 
is a walking distance to the subway and the area's best off-campus housing, including Bluesky Living's accommodations.

 
  Kuro Kirin Espresso and Coffee has terrace seating. The people running the place are too sweet. Expect an artistic and calm ambiance, a lot of tables, great WIFI, and outlet access—there is no better place to study for the finals. It's a great environment for homework and meeting with friends. The espresso is great! 


 
  G's is a small respectable coffee bistro that attracts many students from Fordham University. The best espresso here is the frosted mocha, and they also have paper straws for the days. Their Bacon Egg, Cheeses, and OJ/Iced Coffee are to die for. It's a cozy atmosphere great for reading. The servers are kind and go out of their way to guarantee your comfort. 


 
  While Prince is moderately new to Arthur Ave, it has become a great studying spot among Fordham students. With its cutting-edge stylistic layout, comfortable lounges, and sweet treats, you may find yourself spending a whole day in this coffee. Their Wi-Fi is fast. 


 
  Tino's is a full café with big tables, leather seats, and an overall great service designed. The cafe is comparatively quiet compared to on-campus study corners, with prices capped within student living budgets. For breakfast, try the lemon ricotta pancakes, and for dinner, the grilled cheese and tomato soup come highly recommended. 


 
 Found right across the road from the Scarsdale Metro-North train shop, Martine's has a great atmosphere for reading, a coffee date with friends, and quiet 'me times.' They have some of the best caramel frosted espressos in Fordham and Belmont neighborhoods. Martine's featured in one of the episodes of the web series Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee!

 
  When you need world-class caffeine to fuel your studies around Fordham University, Starbucks should be one of the must-try coffee shops on your list. The Fordham University Starbucks is located right off-campus in the Fordham Plaza. They have a great service, great Wi-Fi, and amazing espressos, teas, smoothies, and an assortment of baked goods and breakfast sandwiches. 


 
  Webster Café is a traditional café with great cuisine from Greek treats to Hispanic specialties. Their prices are very reasonable for college students. You can come here with friends or alone to study or to meet new people. They have great coffees, and they make a mean chocolate egg cream. Fordham is famous for its scholastic rigor and Jesuit culture, but we must say that the coffee in the neighborhood is remarkable too.

title: A Culinary Journey Around Fordham Lincoln Center: Exploring Manhattan’s Diverse Flavors
author: Forward Pathway
text:
### Introduction: Fordham’s Culinary Landscape at Lincoln Center

The Lincoln Center campus of Fordham University (2025 USNews Ranking: 91) , nestled in the heart of Manhattan, isn’t just a place of academic pursuits; it’s also a launchpad for culinary exploration. A recent Fordham Now article highlighted some faculty and staff favorites for dining and drinks near the campus, offering a glimpse into the neighborhood’s diverse gastronomic landscape. Recommendations included the Mediterranean flavors of Kashkaval Gardens, the craft beer and comfort food at Alfie’s Kitchen, the Asian delights of Kung Fu Little, the convenient and cultural hub that is The Independent Cafe, the sweet treats at Breads Bakery, and the reliably satisfying Tex-Mex of Burrito Box.

But a university’s dining scene is more than just a list of nearby restaurants. It’s a cultural microcosm, reflecting the tastes, trends, and energy of the students and surrounding community. Food plays a vital role in campus life, providing not just sustenance but also opportunities for social interaction, cultural exchange, and even academic inspiration. Think of late-night study sessions fueled by pizza, celebratory dinners after exams, or casual coffee dates that spark new friendships.

This article aims to expand on the Fordham Now guide, diving deeper into each featured establishment and exploring the broader culinary landscape that surrounds the university. We’ll examine the appeal of Mediterranean tapas and the craft beer scene in Hell’s Kitchen, venture into the world of authentic soup dumplings, and discover the cultural significance of a perfectly baked babka.

Furthermore, we’ll broaden our scope beyond Fordham, drawing comparisons to other university towns and neighborhoods. Consider the vibrant outdoor dining scene near DePaul University in Chicago, or the diverse culinary options surrounding Columbia University in Upper Manhattan. By exploring these diverse food scenes, we can gain a deeper appreciation for the vital role that food plays in shaping the university experience and fostering a sense of community. Get ready for a flavorful journey as we discover the culinary gems hidden in and around these academic hubs.

### Mediterranean Flavors and Craft Beer Delights: Kashkaval Gardens and Alfie’s Kitchen

Let’s begin our exploration with two standout recommendations from the Fordham Now article: Kashkaval Gardens and Alfie’s Kitchen & Craft Beer Bar. Kashkaval Gardens, a Hell’s Kitchen fixture since 1997, offers a taste of the Mediterranean with its tapas-style dining. The appeal of Mediterranean tapas lies in their communal nature and the opportunity to sample a variety of flavors in one sitting. It’s a style of dining that encourages sharing and conversation, making it perfect for a casual meal with friends or a relaxed date night.

The Fordham Now article specifically highlights the 4-dip sampler and the kale salad as popular choices. The 4-dip sampler likely features a selection of classic Mediterranean dips like hummus, baba ghanoush, tzatziki, and muhammara, each offering a unique texture and flavor profile. These dips are typically served with warm pita bread or vegetables for dipping, creating a satisfying and flavorful experience. Even the most ardent anti-kale evangelist might find pleasure in the kale salad. Kale salads, when done well, shed their sometimes tough, bitter reputation. The right dressing – perhaps a lemon vinaigrette with a touch of honey – and the addition of other complementary ingredients like toasted nuts, dried cranberries, and crumbled cheese can transform kale into a surprisingly delightful dish.

The appeal of Kashkaval Gardens might also resonate with those familiar with Chicago’s thriving outdoor dining scene. As patio season approaches, Chicagoans eagerly seek out restaurants with inviting al fresco spaces. Restaurants like The Warbler in Lincoln Square, known for its greenery-laden patio, offer a similar ambiance to what one might expect at Kashkaval Gardens. The Warbler provides a relaxed, inviting atmosphere with diverse seating, colorful cocktails, and a menu that caters to a variety of tastes, mirroring the communal and diverse offerings of Mediterranean tapas. Both venues encapsulate the joy of enjoying good food and company in a pleasant outdoor setting.

Moving on from the Mediterranean, Alfie’s Kitchen & Craft Beer Bar offers a different, yet equally appealing, experience. As the name suggests, Alfie’s specializes in craft beer, cocktails, and elevated comfort food. This combination is a winning formula, particularly in a neighborhood like Hell’s Kitchen, where residents and students alike are looking for a place to unwind and enjoy a good meal without breaking the bank. The mention of a $20 lunch deal, including a burger, fries, and a beer, underscores the restaurant’s commitment to providing value and accessibility.

The craft beer scene in Hell’s Kitchen is vibrant and diverse, with a range of bars and pubs catering to different tastes and preferences. Happy hour, a beloved tradition for students and locals, plays a significant role in the community’s social life. W42ST’s guide to the best happy hours in Hell’s Kitchen highlights several spots worth checking out, including Arriba Arriba, Balcon Salon, and Jasper’s Taphouse. Arriba Arriba, known for its Mexican cuisine and strong margaritas, offers discounted drinks during its happy hour. Balcon Salon, an LGBTQ+ bar, features half-priced drinks every day until 8 pm, creating a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere. Jasper’s Taphouse and Kitchen, with its extensive happy hour spanning from 11 am to 8 pm on weekdays, offers discounts on house lagers, margaritas, and wine.

These happy hour spots, along with Alfie’s Kitchen, contribute to the fabric of the Hell’s Kitchen community. They provide affordable options for socializing, networking, and simply enjoying a well-deserved break after a long day. For university students, in particular, happy hour can be a crucial part of their social lives, offering a chance to connect with friends, de-stress, and explore the local neighborhood without overspending. The combination of craft beer, elevated comfort food, and a lively happy hour scene makes Alfie’s Kitchen a welcome addition to the Fordham Lincoln Center dining landscape.

### A Taste of Asia: Kung Fu Little and the Quest for Authentic Soup Dumplings

Moving eastward from Alfie’s, a brief subway ride from Fordham’s Lincoln Center campus leads to Kung Fu Little, a culinary gem recommended for its steamed buns, soup dumplings, and ramen crafted with fresh, hand-pulled noodles. While seemingly disparate dishes, each represents a cornerstone of Asian cuisine, offering comfort and satisfaction in their own unique way. But it’s the soup dumplings, also known as xiao long bao (XLB), that truly capture the imagination and palates of food enthusiasts in New York City.

The quest for the “authentic” soup dumpling in New York City is a veritable culinary pilgrimage. Eater NY and The Infatuation have both dedicated extensive guides to the city’s best soup dumplings, showcasing the breadth and depth of options available. These guides serve as invaluable resources for those seeking the perfect balance of delicate skin, flavorful broth, and savory filling. Comparing Kung Fu Little’s offerings to other soup dumpling hotspots like La Salle Dumpling Room, Din Tai Fung, and Nan Xiang Xiao Long Bao provides a framework for understanding the nuances of this beloved dish.

La Salle Dumpling Room, near Columbia University, is renowned for its crab-bearing XLB with a flavorful and viscous gravy. Din Tai Fung, a global chain, offers meticulously crafted dumplings with various fillings. Nan Xiang Xiao Long Bao in Flushing, known for its long lines, offers a variety of options, including squash, shrimp and pork, and scallops. Each of these establishments brings its own unique approach to soup dumplings, highlighting the versatility and regional variations of the dish. How does Kung Fu Little stack up against these titans of the soup dumpling world? Is their broth more savory, their skin thinner, their fillings more innovative?

The cultural significance of soup dumplings cannot be overstated. Originating in the Shanghai suburb of Nanxiang, these soup-filled parcels have become a global phenomenon, representing the artistry and ingenuity of Chinese cuisine. The delicate process of crafting each dumpling, ensuring the perfect balance of ingredients and textures, is a testament to the culinary traditions that have been passed down through generations. In New York City, soup dumplings have experienced a surge in popularity, becoming a must-try dish for both locals and tourists alike. This increasing popularity is evident in events like the Soup Dumpling Festival hosted by Nan Xiang, which draws crowds eager to sample a variety of dumpling creations.

But what truly defines an “authentic” soup dumpling? Is it the adherence to traditional recipes and techniques, or is it the willingness to experiment with new flavors and ingredients? Purists might argue that an authentic soup dumpling must be made with a specific type of dough, filled with a particular blend of pork and broth, and served with a traditional black vinegar and ginger dipping sauce. Others might embrace innovation, celebrating the creativity of chefs who push the boundaries of what a soup dumpling can be. Variations abound, with fillings ranging from traditional pork and crab to more adventurous combinations like truffle and seafood. The broth itself can vary in flavor and consistency, from rich and savory to light and refreshing. Ultimately, the definition of “authentic” is subjective, shaped by personal preferences and cultural context. However, the common thread that unites all great soup dumplings is the pursuit of culinary excellence, the commitment to quality ingredients, and the desire to create a truly memorable dining experience.

### Casual Bites and Free Entertainment: The Independent Cafe and Lincoln Center’s Cultural Offerings

Right in the heart of Lincoln Center, within the David Rubenstein Atrium, sits The Independent Cafe, a haven for those seeking reasonably priced sandwiches and coffee. But The Independent Cafe offers more than just a quick bite; it provides a portal into the vibrant cultural landscape of Lincoln Center. The David Rubenstein Atrium itself plays a pivotal role as a cultural hub, offering a diverse range of free events and performances that enhance the university experience and enrich the surrounding community.

Celebrating its 10th anniversary in November 2019, the David Rubenstein Atrium has established itself as a central gathering place within Lincoln Center. Its mission is to make the arts accessible to all, and it accomplishes this through a diverse array of free programming that caters to a wide audience. From dance performances and live music to family shows and talks, the Atrium offers something for everyone. Thrillist highlights the Atrium’s “Dance Floor” series on Friday nights, transforming the space into a lively dance floor with DJs spinning tunes from around the world. Select Saturdays are dedicated to families and young audiences, with events exploring themes of connection, acceptance, and self-love.

amNY further emphasizes Lincoln Center’s commitment to accessibility through its spring programming initiatives. These initiatives, which include free admission or a “choose what you pay” ticketing model, aim to make performances, discussions, and civic activities more readily available to the public. Programs like Lincoln Center Passport, Moments, and Activate offer a variety of opportunities for individuals of all ages and abilities to engage with the arts.

The Atrium’s mission of accessible arts is particularly relevant to the university experience. Affordable cultural activities are essential for students and the community, providing opportunities for personal enrichment, intellectual stimulation, and social interaction. Attending a free performance at the Atrium can be a welcome respite from the pressures of academic life, offering a chance to relax, unwind, and connect with others who share a passion for the arts. Moreover, these cultural experiences can broaden students’ perspectives, foster creativity, and enhance their overall well-being.

Lincoln Center’s programming, with the support of donors like David Rubenstein, extends beyond artistic performances. Recognizing the Atrium’s potential as a civic space, Lincoln Center intends to use it for democracy-related events, citizenship ceremonies, and educational programs focused on civic rights. This commitment to civic engagement underscores the importance of the arts in promoting dialogue, understanding, and active participation in a democratic society. The use of the Rubenstein Atrium to further these goals aligns with the university’s mission to educate informed and engaged citizens who are prepared to contribute to their communities. In essence, The Independent Cafe, nestled within the Atrium, serves as more than just a place to grab a sandwich and coffee; it’s a gateway to a world of cultural and civic engagement, enriching the lives of students and community members alike.

### Sweet Endings: Breads Bakery and the Search for the Best Babka

Breads Bakery, another gem near Fordham’s Lincoln Center, offers a sweet escape with its renowned babka. But this isn’t just any babka; it’s a culinary masterpiece that has earned accolades and captured the hearts (and stomachs) of New Yorkers. To truly appreciate Breads Bakery’s babka, it’s helpful to understand the history and evolution of this twisted sweet bread in New York City.

Grub Street’s article on the best babkas in New York City provides valuable insight into this evolution. Once primarily found in Jewish bakeries, babka has become a mainstream treat, with innovative versions incorporating ingredients like laminated dough, Nutella, and buckwheat. Breads Bakery, under the direction of Danish-Israeli baker Uri Scheft, has played a significant role in this transformation. Scheft’s babka, inspired by the krantz cake of Israel, utilizes laminated dough, a technique borrowed from croissant-making. This results in a lighter, flakier texture than traditional babkas, which are often denser and oil-based. The filling, a generous blend of Nutella and dark chocolate chips, adds a rich, decadent sweetness. Finally, the loaf is drenched in sugar syrup, ensuring lasting moistness and a glossy finish.

Comparing Breads Bakery’s version to other top contenders like Arcade Bakery and Bklyn Larder highlights the diversity of babka styles available in New York City. Arcade Bakery, with its French-trained pastry chef Roger Gural, also laminates its dough, creating a light, golden texture with dark chocolate and walnuts. They even offer a whiskey-pecan variety for those seeking a more unconventional flavor profile. Bklyn Larder takes a different approach with its alternative grain babka, incorporating buckwheat and rye flour. This gives the babka a nutty, earthy flavor, complemented by a honey-tinged chocolate.

The cultural significance of babka extends beyond its deliciousness. As Eater NY’s guide to the best Jewish bakeries in NYC points out, Jewish baked goods are deeply connected to Jewish cultures, religious practices, and palates. Babka, along with other treats like rugelach, challah, and black and white cookies, represents a taste of tradition and the rich history of the Jewish diaspora. These bakeries, both modern and storied, serve as cultural touchstones, preserving and celebrating Jewish culinary heritage.

Even restaurants known for other specialties, like Barney Greengrass, offer their own take on babka. The Infatuation’s review of Barney Greengrass praises their cinnamon babka as a top dessert choice, surpassing other options like rugelach and black and white cookies. This underscores the enduring appeal of babka and its ability to complement a wide range of cuisines.

What, then, are the elements that make a babka exceptional? It’s a combination of factors, including the quality of ingredients, the skill of the baker, and the attention to detail. A truly great babka should have a moist, tender crumb, a rich, flavorful filling, and a visually appealing appearance. The dough should be properly proofed and baked to a golden brown, while the filling should be evenly distributed and not overly sweet. And of course, a touch of artistry in the twisting and shaping of the loaf can elevate the babka from ordinary to extraordinary. Regional variations also play a role, with different cultures and bakeries offering their own unique twists on the classic recipe. Whether it’s the laminated dough of Breads Bakery, the buckwheat flour of Bklyn Larder, or the cinnamon spice of Barney Greengrass, each babka tells a story and offers a glimpse into the diverse culinary landscape of New York City.

title: The Best New York City Coffee Shops for Working Remotely
author: Pia Bello
text:
In New York City, finding a cafe that offers the perfect balance of work-friendly and cozy can be a game-changer for productivity. From Midtown to Soho, the city boasts an eclectic array of cafes and coffee shops tailored to the needs of the modern professional, complete with complimentary wifi and comfortable seating. Whether you’re seeking a quiet corner to write, or a vibrant hub to network and collaborate, this guide unveils the city’s best coffee shops for a productive and enjoyable work experience. From hidden gems to well-known establishments, each cafe offers a unique blend of ambiance, amenities and, of course, exceptional brews for that much-needed caffeine fix. Ahead, see the most work-friendly cafes in Manhattan.

*Subscribe to Observer’s Lifestyle Newsletter*

**Devoción**

*25 East 20th Street, New York, NY 10003
*

*600 Lexington Ave, New York, NY 10022*


*+ Multiple Brooklyn locations*

Devoción brings a taste of Colombia to New York City, with locations in Flatiron and Midtown, plus multiple outposts in Brooklyn. At the heart of their ethos lies a commitment to sourcing farm-fresh coffee from producers in Colombia, ensuring a rich and distinctive brew. The Flatiron location is particularly noteworthy, featuring brick walls and a plant display for a warm, fresh atmosphere. It strikes the perfect balance between comfort and productivity, making it an ideal choice for Manhattan’s working crowd.

**Felix Roasting Co.**** **

*450 Park Ave South, New York, NY 10016
*

*+ Multiple locations*

The interiors at Felix Roasting Co. are inspired by the late-19th-century aesthetic movement in Britain. With locations in NoHo, Hudson Square and a flagship in NoMad, Felix Roasting Co. transports visitors to another era with its carefully curated ambiance. From the blue velvet chairs to the hand-drawn tiled walls and wooden bar, Felix Roasting Co. offers guests a truly immersive experience. If you want to try a special drink, visit the NoMad location and order the store-exclusive Hickory Smoked S’mores Latte for an unforgettable graham cracker-infused experience.

**Ground Central Coffee Company **

*498 7th Ave, New York, NY 10018
*

*+ Multiple locations*

With multiple locations all across the city, Ground Central Coffee Company offers a unique blend of literary charm and cozy ambiance. Each branch boasts an extensive book display, creating a haven for bookworms. The exposed brick walls add a rustic touch, complemented by warm, subdued lighting. The seating options range from plush leather couches to sleek metal chairs, providing a comfortable setting for work or a leisurely coffee experience. Whether you visit the quaint Hell’s Kitchen cafe or the busy Garment District location, Ground Central is a standout destination for both coffee connoisseurs and those seeking a relaxed, bookish escape in the heart of the city.

**Kobrick Coffee**

*24 9th Ave, New York, NY 10014*

Established in 1920, Kobrick takes pride in crafting USDA organic hand-roasted coffee. The cafe’s exposed brick walls, subtle plant decorations and warm lighting create a vintage atmosphere, offering a unique backdrop for your work-from-home (well, work-from-coffee shop) experience. Open from 7 am to 2 am, Kobrick welcomes you to savor their pastries during the day, and as night falls, indulge in their espresso martini—a perfect treat to cap off your productive day.

**Gregorys Coffee**

*649 Broadway, New York, NY, 10012
*

*+ Multiple locations*

A beloved New York City chain, Gregorys Coffee is known for its diverse variety of offerings that cater to every palate, ranging from classic espressos and lattes to novelties like the salted caramel cold brew. Beyond the coffee selection, Gregorys serves a range of all-day breakfast sandwiches and baked goods, making it a one-stop destination for those on the go and those needing a morning-to-night place to work. While Gregorys has numerous locations throughout the city, the NoHo branch stands out for its lush plant display and warm, bright lights, creating a fresh atmosphere.

**Amano Cafe**

*172 West 4th St, New York, NY 10014*

Amano Cafe is a haven for coffee enthusiasts seeking a genuine experience. Its name, derived from the Spanish word for “by hand,” reflects Amano’s commitment to hand-picking beans directly from farmers in Latin America, providing a refreshing alternative to the popularity of mass-produced coffee. Boasting floor-to-ceiling windows, the West Village cafe caters to those who thrive in natural light.

**Think Coffee**

*350 Broadway, New York, NY 10013
*

*+ Multiple locations*

Think Coffee has made a name for itself through its commitment to sustainability and ethically-sourced coffee. The Tribeca location is a personal favorite, thanks to the large windows that flood the space with natural light. With ample seating, it’s an ideal spot for those looking to settle in for an all-day work session or a leisurely catch-up over a cup of coffee. Think Coffee’s blend of sustainability and quality has made it a go-to choice for eco-conscious consumers.

**About Coffee**

*445 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10024
*

*222 Front St, New York, NY 10038*

Nestled in the Upper West Side, About Coffee offers a calm escape from the busy city. The cafe’s warm, bright interior complements the abundant natural light that streams in. With indoor and outdoor seating options, guests can choose their preferred atmosphere for either work or relaxation. Conveniently located just a block from the American Museum of Natural History, About Coffee offers an excellent pre- or post-visit respite. Additionally, the cafe’s proximity to boutique shops in the area provides the perfect opportunity to indulge in some retail therapy and exploration after a work session.

**Afficionado Coffee Roasters **

*750 11th Ave, New York, NY 10019*

Afficionado is a haven for those who appreciate the art of sustainable specialty coffee. Its team goes above and beyond, traversing the world for the highest quality beans. The flagship location in Hell’s Kitchen is filled with vibrant plants, cozy seating and plentiful outlets. For those on the go, Afficionado offers a diverse selection of healthy snacks to power through a busy day. A standout is the Daddy Latte, a best-selling signature drink known among regulars for the infusion of cereal milk.

**Shakespeare & Co. **

*2020 Broadway, New York, NY 10023
*

*939 Lexington Ave, New York, NY 10065*

Shakespeare & Co. is more than a typical bookstore; it’s a cozy retreat that blends coffee, books and creativity. The Lincoln Square location tends to draw in students from John Jay College, Fordham and Juilliard, creating a vibrant community of learners and creatives. Whether you’re perusing shelves, savoring a cup of coffee or lost in your writing endeavors, Shakespeare & Co. is a welcoming space.

title: Off-Campus Study Spots Near Fordham College LC
author: Pia Fischetti
text:
# Off-Campus Study Spots Near Fordham College LC

*Our map provides various locations around Fordham’s Lincoln Center campus that students can study at*

**Background**

When a person plans to study, they most likely consider sitting at a desk in their room or heading to the library. However, according to act.org, there are plenty of places outside of these norms that are very beneficial for studying, such as coffee shops or even outside. Some people “thrive” on background noise or find themselves “inspired” by fresh air on a beautiful day. Similarly, according to learningscientists.org, variable study spaces have many positive effects on a person’s ability to retain information. As explained in the article, “Where Should I Study?” “if you study in lots of different situations with different background sights, smells, noises, etc. then you will be able to use any of those things as a possible access point when you are trying to retrieve the information you learned.” Clearly, there are many reasons to seek out off-campus study spots. Even if a student decides to pursue this type of study environment, though, they may feel lost as to where they should go.

**Why is this map useful?**

While there is information about the various study spots on campus, no such guide exists regarding off-campus locations. Anyone can lookup coffee shops near the Lincoln Center campus on Google or Yelp, but these resources will not inform them how the spot will suit their study needs. With this map, we have solidified a selection of places Lincoln Center students may like to study at. We also wanted to provide students with a wide range of locations to accommodate different study habits: parks for the outdoorsy type, cafes with late hours for the night owls, busy places for the students who work well with background noise, etc. By pointing out these locations, students will be able to study off-campus while still feeling connected to the school community.

**Why doesn’t this map exist?**

There are many possible reasons as to why a map like this does not already exist. One reason that Fordham wouldn’t release this information is that they don’t want it to seem like LC students can’t find a good place to study on campus. However, the point of this map is not to point out flaws in the Lincoln Center campus. It is simply meant to provide students with a chance to further immerse themselves in the surrounding Lincoln Center area, something that Fordham often uses as a selling point for the campus.

Most of the locations on this map are also not designated study spots. The only way someone would know this information is by word of mouth, research, or first-hand experience. Therefore, to create a map like this requires a significant amount of time and effort.

**What can I expect from this map?**

The locations on the map are divided into four categories: parks, libraries, restaurants, and cafés. If you already know what kind of study space you’re looking for, the icons representing each category will instantly help narrow down your search. If not, each pinned location features a brief description that gives you an idea of the atmosphere and whether or not it suits your studying needs. You will also find photos and/or video of each location and other helpful data points, including:

- Walking distance from LC campus
- Access to free wifi
- Access to outlets
- Usual noise level (low/moderate/high)
- Hours of operation

title: A Coffee Snob’s Guide to the Best Cafes in NYC
author: Anonymous
text:
Coffee, cigarettes, and a mild-to-moderate feeling of irritation at life in general: the three power sources that keep New Yorkers going. I enjoy a cup of coffee now and then as a treat or as a way of extending my working hours, but in general I rely more on the other two methods. My partner Michael is the coffee snob of our household. A small marble table in our kitchen has become a shrine to his morning espresso, with jewel-cut glass cups, a sleek grinder, and an espresso machine shaped like a little robot. Together, we decided to rate the cafes we visited together in 2023 and add little sketches and notes when we had time. We rated each spot on a scale of 1-10 for their atmosphere and coffee and then rated non-coffee drinks and pastries when applicable.

The seventeen shops we rated are not all of the spots we visited individually, just the ones we visited together. In all honesty, I probably visit Dunkin Donuts the most often of any coffee shop purely due to its hours and immediate proximity to school. But if you want a good coffee, and I mean actually good coffee, then these are our recommendations.

Best Coffee: Sey

*(Bushwick, Brooklyn)*

Sey is often named one of the best coffee shops in NYC (or even in the USA), and it’s for good reason. Sey’s coffee is consistently lightly roasted and delicious, but its flavors vary wildly. I’ve had juicy and fruity, funky and earthy, floral, and every other flavor note you see printed unconvincingly on the side of coffee bags. When it says “notes of white peach and baking spices”, you actually taste it in the cup. Their technique is consistent and they serve a sweet complex espresso, with a glass of sparkling water, and delightful pourover, albeit a bit pricey.

The only other minor drawback is Sey’s warranted popularity: there’s rarely a place to sit and often a line for the bathroom, but the interior feels modern and spacious with white walls, high ceilings, and hanging plants.

Best Pastries (And Runner-Up for Best Coffee): La Cabra

*(Soho + East Village, Manhattan)*

When it comes to pastries, it’s no contest with La Cabra. In addition to the Instagram-famous cardamom bun (which looks like a beautiful knot tied out of dough) and the oft-considered “best croissant in NYC”, they offer a menu of seasonal treats like apple danishes, hazelnut buns, and passionfruit semlas. Through text, it is hard to convey how different La Cabra’s apple danish is from the mushy, bland ones often on offer at cafes and diners, but they hardly deserve to share the same name. The coffee is first-rate as well, and people know it. On weekends you can expect a line snaking out of the door of both the Soho and East Village locations, and it’s not much better on weekdays. But once you get inside, it’s 100% worth it.

Best Atmosphere: Acre

*(Greenpoint, Brooklyn)*

Acre is one of my favorite spots to sit and draw in the summer, and it’s a perfect place to meet a friend for lunch. The front is filled with carefully selected home goods, handmade ceramics, and jars full of things to stock the perfect Japanese pantry. The middle part of the space is filled with seating, and the back is an outdoor garden where you can relax in the sun when the weather allows. It gets busy on the weekends, but during the week it’s usually a relaxing spot where you can enjoy a hot yuzu tea or a cold coffee jelly (courtesy of Sey). In addition to drinks, pastries, and sundries, there is a lunch menu that offers bento boxes, sandwiches, and other sides. My preferred order is the Japanese fried chicken karaage bento box or the Japanese egg salad sandwich.

Best for Specialty Drinks + Bean Selection: Dayglow

*(Bushwick, Brooklyn)*

Dayglow is a small cafe chain that started in Los Angeles but has expanded to Chicago and New York City. The Los Angeles Times has raved about their LA cafes, calling it a “candy store for Nordic-style roasts”, and the Bushwick location is no different. Inside, you can find a cornucopia of beans from the world over, all packaged in brightly-colored bags and boxes. These beans don’t come cheap, but it’s a great place to try out some new varieties for home brewing. Dayglow also offers a large menu of specialty coffee drinks, many of which are completely vegan. My favorite is one called “The Morning Show”: a drink made with distilled coffee, orange, condensed coconut, and passionfruit.

Most Overrated: Devoción and Coffee Project

Both of these spots are frequently mentioned on other “best of” lists, but they had some of our lowest ratings. Michael likes acidity, but the espresso at Devoción was so tooth-achingly acidic that we went back again a week later to make sure it hadn’t been an accident. Unfortunately, it was the same result. The Williamsburg space is beautiful, with lots of room for people looking to do a little work or read a book, but we were disappointed by the coffee itself. Coffee project also had a similarly sour espresso (not quite as bad), but with no added benefit of a pleasant atmosphere.

What We Noticed Overall:

**Nowhere to sit**

This shouldn’t come as a surprise, and not only because of the ever-increasing rent that makes space a premium in the city. Cafes also want to discourage post-covid work-from-home employees from camping out on their laptops all day, but this has led to a distinct lack of seating and an overall decline in the cozy coffee shop days before the pandemic. Some cafes we visited had creative workarounds for this problem (Acre prevents laptop use on weekends and Sey prohibits it outright). The most spacious locations were Devoción and Loveless, while PPL is so small that it only seats about two people, max.

**Kettl reigns supreme for tea**

Kettl is a local tea company (with cafes in Greenpoint and Bowery) that sources a wide variety of teas directly from Japan. A good portion of the cafes we visited were serving Kettl as their tea option, and there’s a reason: it’s the best!

**If a cafe serves your espresso with a sidecar, that’s a good sign**

Out of all the cafes we sampled, the ones that scored highest on their coffee were the ones that took care to serve their espresso with a small glass of sparkling water on the side. The purpose of the water is to cleanse your palate before and after drinking. This gesture is associated with third-wave coffee culture, so the lack of a sidecar is not necessarily a bad thing, but in our experience, its presence indicated a higher level of care for the craft. If they don’t at least offer a spoon, we would proceed with caution.

title: Here's the Best Coffee on the Upper West Side
author: Antonina
text:
Hi there I’m Antonina! Love NYC as much as I do? **Join my weekly newsletter for fun snippets of daily life in the Big Apple (or follow me on instagram).**

## Best Coffee on the Upper West Side

## Table of Contents. Best Coffee on the Upper West Side

Visiting New York City? If you haven’t decided where to stay (yet) check out my helpful guide on Where to Stay in New York City (The best neighborhoods for first timers +3 to avoid). Don’t have time? Here’s my favorite hotel in NYC, hands down.

### Irving Farm

Serving New Yorkers for more than 20 years, Irving Farm was established in 1996 at Irving Place. The founders of the cafe, Steve and David, purchased a small house-turned-roastary in upstate New York because roasting wasn’t permitted in NYC at that time.

They honed their skills and started producing exceptionally roasted blends they brought over to the city. New York Magazine awarded Irving Farm the title of best coffee in New York City in 2002, so the cat’s been out of the bag for a while now.

Serving some of the best coffee on the Upper West Side, Irving Farm is my go-to spot whenever I’m in the mood

**Website**— Irving Farm New York**Address.** 224 W 79th St, New York, NY

**You might enjoy reading.** 20 Fun Things to Do on the Upper West Side

### Black Press Coffee

I wish I had known about Black Press Coffee sooner, it’s two blocks from my apartment and the constant line of happy locals makes it clear this beloved gem is a neighborhood staple. The Upper West Side cafe bills itself as a specialty coffee shop on a mission to deliver exceptional coffee with a side of great customer service. Thankfully they deliver.

If you’re curious about the cafe’s name, it’s derived from the Black Press, a group of publications that shared valuable information with underrepresented communities who were kept in the dark during important political events.

**Website**— Black Press Coffee**Address.**274 Columbus Ave, New York, NY

### Joe Coffee

First opened in the West Village, Joe’s quickly became a hot spot for locals that love expertly-crafted coffee and good vibes. The café couldn’t be cozier, the intimate setting is perfect for both quick espresso shots and leisurely morning sipping.

Joe’s has a strong commitment to quality, sourcing the finest beans and focusing on precise brewing methods. The staff’s passion for coffee is evident in every cup, which is why it’s one of my favorite cafes on the Upper West Side.

**Website**— Joe Coffee**Locations**. There’s three cafes on the Upper West Side

** Local tip. ** Between you and me, the seasonal menu is always better than the regular one. Ask what’s fresh today.

### Daily Provisions

Daily Provisions is a casual neighborhood bakery and cafe opened by Danny Meyer (the mastermind behind Shake Shack & Gramercy Tavern). Most folks come to this cute neighborhood haunt for the famous crullers and find themselves returning for everything else on the menu. But the great food menu is not where the magic stops! Daily Provisions uses Joe’s beans to make balanced drip coffee and incredible iced Americanos, some of the best in the neighborhood.

**Website**— Daily Provisions**Address.** 375 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY

Daily Provisions appears on our list of.12 Delicious Upper West Side Bakeries

### About Coffee

About Coffee is located right next to the American Museum of Natural History. Cozy and relaxed, the cafe serves up a variety of options that cater to every palate, from classic espresso drinks to milk-based concoctions.

About Coffee stands out for its commitment to sourcing high-quality beans and roasting them in-house. This also one of the best working cafes on the Upper West Side (there’s tons of tables and outlets).

**Website**— About Coffee**Address.** 445 Columbus Ave, New York, NY

** Unpopular opinion. ** Hot take. the best coffee in Upper West Side isn’t at a trendy third-wave spot. it’s at Best Coffee on the Upper West Side.

### Birch Coffee

New Yorkers don’t settle for mediocre coffee and Birch always hits the spot. The Upper West Side cafe is no exception. Swing by for delicious coffee or grab a bag of freshly roasted beans to go. Also, I’d be doing you a disservice if I didn’t mention the delicious toasted almond tea.

**Website**— Birch Coffee**Address.** 750 Columbus Ave, New York, NY Cash only at this spot, so hit an ATM beforehand. learned that one the hard way. The staff is friendly without being overbearing, and the portions are generous enough that you won’t leave hungry. It’s a reliable choice any day of the week.

### Plowshares Coffee Bloomingdale

I originally stumbled upon Plowshares while searching for a quick bite. Intrigued by the small storefront, I was completely impressed by my Americano and soon realized they serve some of the best coffee on the Upper West Side.

Roasting the bean onsite, this cute cafe offers a well-put together menu of well-crafted drinks. Better still, they serve baked goods from Bien Cuit, one of my favorite bakeries in NYC.

**Website**— Plowshares Coffee Bloomingdale**Address.** 2730 Broadway, New York, NY

**Local’s Recommendation.** Make sure to swing by the Cathedral of St. John the Divine while you’re in the area, it’s the fifth largest church in the world and the architecture is breathtaking.

### Blue Bottle Coffee

Blue Bottle Coffee hails from San Francisco, a city respected for its mastery of coffee. You’ll find Blue Bottle all over. Specializing in pour-overs, Blue Bottle Coffee has mastered every caffeinated drink you can think of.

From foamy lattes, airy cappuccinos to vibrant iced Americanos, everything is exceptional. If you find yourself in need of a strong cup, make a beeline towards Blue Bottle Coffee for the best coffee on the Upper West Side.

**Website**— Blue Bottle Coffee**Address.**279 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY

### Bluestone Lane

Bluestone Lane is best known for offering exciting (and healthy) Australian brunch fare, but the coffee is worth a trip alone. Having to wait in line is. Their coffee is half the draw, which is why I consider this one of the best cafes in the Upper West Side.

**Website**— Bluestone Lane**Address.**417 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY The atmosphere is buzzy and energetic, exactly the kind of place where you’ll want to linger over your meal. I first discovered this place on a whim and it immediately became part of my regular rotation. The consistency is what keeps me coming back. you always know what you’re getting.

title: Top 8 Best Study Spots in Chicago - BookScouter Blog

text:
Many people know 📍Chicago as the Windy City with its impressive skyline and finger-licking deep-dish pizza. However, it is equally famous for its thriving academic culture. Boasting numerous universities and colleges, Chicago attracts students from around the globe. If you’re a student aspiring to excel academically, finding a conducive environment to study is crucial. Sometimes, we all need a change of scenery, being tired of the same old places like your college library or dorm room. That’s why we’ve compiled a list of the top **8 best study spots in Chicago** to help you find the perfect place to hit the books. So let’s explore them together!

Looking for more great places to study? Take a look at the best study spots in New York City.

## Common Cup

**📍*** 1501 W Morse Ave, Chicago, IL 60626*

🕙*Monday – Friday 7:00 am – 4:00 pm | Saturday – Sunday 8:00 am – 4:00 pm*

This is one of the most popular study spots among students and young professionals. You can find Common Cup in the very heart of the city’s vibrant Lakeview neighborhood. What makes this place so good for studying? The answer is as simple as that – because it has all you need for a productive study session, i.e., cozy ambiance, comfortable seating, and free Wi-Fi, of course. So why not grab a coffee here and dive in some studying?

**📍*** 2212 N Clybourn Ave, Chicago, IL 60614*

🕙*Monday – Tuesday closed | Wednesday – Thursday 4:00 pm – 11:00 pm | Friday 4:00 pm – 12:00 am | Saturday 1:00 pm – 12:00 am | Sunday 1:00 pm – 7:00 pm*

Sometimes, a quiet environment is not enough for students to enjoy studying; they need something unique. Well, in this case, you should check Kibbitznest. This bookstore and café is known for its vintage decor and relaxed ambiance. With a wide selection of books to browse through, you can take breaks and indulge in some light reading. Plus, their delicious food and beverages will keep you fueled throughout your study session.

## Harold Washington Library

**📍*** 400 S State St, Chicago, IL 60605*

🕙*Monday – Thursday 9:00 am – 8:00 pm | Friday – Saturday 9:00 am – 5:00 pm | Sunday 1:00 pm – 5:00 pm*

If you need a peaceful environment to concentrate on your studies, consider visiting Harold Washington Library, the central library of the Chicago Public Library system. This location is not just a regular library, but also a significant historical site. You can appreciate its impressive architecture and access numerous helpful study materials.

## Metropolis

**📍*** 1039 W Granville Ave, Chicago, IL 60660*

🕙*Monday – Sunday 6:30 am – 5:30 pm *

Located in the Edgewater neighborhood, Metropolis on Granville is a favored destination for students and coffee enthusiasts. Renowned for its delectable coffee, welcoming ambiance, and ample seating, it is an ideal place to concentrate and accomplish some dedicated studying.

## Drawing Room at the Chicago Athletic Association

**📍***12 S Michigan Ave, Chicago, IL 60603*

🕙*Monday – Tuesday 2:30 pm – 10:00 pm | Wednesday – Friday 3:00 pm – 11:00 pm | Saturday – Sunday 2:00 pm – 10:30 pm*

For those seeking a high-end location to study, look no further than the Drawing Room at the Chicago Athletic Association. Housed in a meticulously restored 19th-century structure, this refined lounge provides a serene and stylish setting for academic pursuits. The luxurious seating and intricate furnishings transport you to a bygone era as you delve into your studies.

## Map Room

**📍***1949 N Hoyne Ave, Chicago, IL 60647*

🕙*Monday  – Saturday 7:30 am – 2:00 am | Sunday 11:00 am – 2:00 am*

With its dimly lit ambiance, rustic decor, and comfortable seating, it provides a laid-back atmosphere for productive studying, so you are sure to feel right at home while delving into your books or laptop.

## Golden Apple

**📍***2971 N Lincoln Ave, Chicago, IL 60657*

If you’re a night owl or simply prefer to study during late hours, Golden Apple is the perfect spot for you. Open 24/7, this cozy cafe in Lincoln Square offers a peaceful atmosphere and a variety of tasty treats to keep you fueled throughout the night.

**📍***1201 W Roscoe St, Chicago, IL 60657*

Two Hearted Queen in Lakeview is a hidden gem that offers a beautiful outdoor patio where you can soak up some sun and enjoy a quiet study session. This charming café features a cozy and rustic ambiance, complete with exposed brick walls and vintage furniture. Whether you prefer a quiet corner or a communal table, you’ll find the perfect spot to concentrate and get work done.

These were the **best places to study in Chicago**: from cozy cafes to serene libraries and even unconventional bookstores, Chicago offers a wide variety of options to suit every taste. Break the monotony of your regular study routine and explore these incredible study destinations. title: 14 Study Cafes in Brooklyn with Outlets (Actual Power Access & Laptop-Friendly Hours)
author: SethAmazon
text:
Finding a Brooklyn cafe where you can actually work means navigating a borough where “laptop-friendly” translates to “we have two outlets for forty people and you’ll compete with someone’s MacBook charger sprawled across three tables,” most spots close inexplicably at 5pm despite Brooklyn’s creative workforce, and that perfect cafe you discovered gets replaced by a juice bar charging $14 for cashew milk smoothies. Whether you’re a Pratt student escaping campus, a freelancer bouncing between gigs in Brooklyn’s tech scene, or studying for certifications while living in a shoebox with roommates who don’t understand noise boundaries, you need cafes with wifi that handles bandwidth-heavy work, outlets that physically exist rather than representing theoretical concepts, and hours that acknowledge human schedules.

This guide covers where Brooklyn workers and students genuinely find productive workspace, from Williamsburg warehouses with extension cords to Park Slope neighborhoods that survived gentrification while maintaining cafe culture. You’ll find honest intel about outlet reality, weekend brunch invasion schedules, co-working masquerading as cafes, and which spots maintain functional existence beyond Instagram aesthetics. For more options across the region, explore study spots across New York or browse StudyNearby’s complete directory.

## 1. Devoción – Williamsburg

**Address:** 69 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11249

**Best for:** Dramatic warehouse space, abundant outlets at communal tables, Williamsburg location

Devoción’s Williamsburg location delivers what Brooklyn cafes promise but rarely provide: genuine abundant power access, soaring ceilings creating space to breathe, and layout that doesn’t make you feel guilty for existing with a laptop. The dramatic skylights flood the warehouse with natural light, plants create indoor jungle atmosphere, and the long communal tables feature outlet strips ensuring power availability regardless of where you sit.

Wifi handles demanding work including video calls and large file transfers with the warehouse proportions accommodating 60+ people comfortably. The Colombian coffee roasted on-site provides quality justifying specialty pricing, and remote work guides consistently rank this among Brooklyn’s most laptop-friendly spaces. The aesthetic inspires Instagram posts but the infrastructure actually supports productive work.

Located on Grand Street in Williamsburg with subway access via L train (Bedford Avenue) and G train (Metropolitan Avenue). The Williamsburg location serves Brooklyn’s creative class and tech workers. Street parking operates with typical North Brooklyn impossibility; the L train provides better access. The warehouse sits in Williamsburg’s developed area with restaurants and shops within walking distance.

**Practical details:**

- Hours: Mon-Fri 7am-7pm, Sat-Sun 8am-7pm
- Transit/Parking: Subway L (Bedford Ave), G (Metropolitan Ave), buses B62, B67; limited street parking (nearly impossible); bike racks abundant
- Amenities: Strong wifi, outlets at communal tables (genuinely abundant), restrooms, Colombian coffee roasted on-site, light food menu, dramatic skylit warehouse
- Nearby features: Williamsburg, Brooklyn Brewery nearby, East River waterfront, McCarren Park

**Downside:** Closes 7pm eliminating evening work; Williamsburg location requires travel from other Brooklyn neighborhoods; specialty pricing ($6-8 drinks); popularity creates weekend crowds.

## 2. Cafe Grumpy – Multiple Locations

**Address:** Multiple locations: Greenpoint (193 Meserole Ave), Chelsea (224 W 20th St, Manhattan), Grand Central (Manhattan)

**Best for:** Local roaster, multiple neighborhoods, established laptop culture

Cafe Grumpy operates several locations across Brooklyn and Manhattan providing house-roasted coffee with genuine laptop-friendly atmosphere established over years of serving creative workers. The Greenpoint flagship offers most spacious layout with the best outlet coverage, while maintaining the quality and culture across all locations. The brand built reputation on supporting laptop workers before “third space” became marketing jargon.

Wifi performs reliably across locations with outlet availability varying by specific spot (Greenpoint provides best coverage, other locations more limited). Capacity differs by location but generally accommodates 30-40 people with the established brand creating loyal customer base treating locations as neighborhood offices. The house-roasted coffee program emphasizes quality beans and skilled preparation.

Multiple locations provide geographic flexibility serving Greenpoint, Chelsea (Manhattan), and Midtown Manhattan. The Greenpoint location benefits from neighborhood character and somewhat easier logistics than Manhattan density. Each maintains consistent coffee quality while adapting to space constraints and neighborhood populations.

**Practical details:**

- Hours: Daily 7am-7pm (varies slightly by location)
- Transit/Parking: Varies by location; Greenpoint G train, limited parking; other locations have respective access
- Amenities: Reliable wifi, outlets (varies significantly by location), restrooms, house-roasted coffee, light food menu
- Nearby features: Varies by location; Greenpoint waterfront, McCarren Park nearby

**Downside:** Closes 7pm across locations; outlet coverage highly variable (Greenpoint good, others limited); some locations very small with minimal capacity.

## 3. Brooklyn Public Library – Central Branch

**Address:** 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn, NY 11238

**Best for:** Free comprehensive access, multiple floors, abundant outlets

Brooklyn’s central library at Grand Army Plaza provides free alternative to cafe costs with four floors of study space, genuine enforced quiet zones, outlets at nearly every study position, and the architectural grandeur making grinding through dense material feel important. The 1941 Art Deco building underwent renovation adding modern amenities while preserving historic character.

Free wifi throughout with strong speeds handling demanding academic and professional work. Study rooms can be reserved online through Brooklyn Public Library system. The building provides varied environments from silent reading rooms to collaborative spaces, with different floors maintaining different noise policies. Computer labs offer access for those without laptops.

Located at Grand Army Plaza at the entrance to Prospect Park, the library sits at major transit hub with 2/3 trains at Grand Army Plaza and multiple bus routes. The location serves Park Slope, Prospect Heights, and surrounding neighborhoods. The plaza provides open space and Prospect Park access for study breaks.

**Downside:** Limited Sunday hours (1pm-5pm); extremely popular meaning competition for silent study rooms during peak hours; weekend closes 6pm Saturday.

## 4. Hungry Ghost – Multiple Brooklyn Locations

**Address:** Multiple locations: Prospect Heights (781 Fulton St), Fort Greene (253 Flatbush Ave), Williamsburg (218 Bedford Ave)

**Best for:** Neighborhood options, Stumptown coffee, local multi-location

Hungry Ghost operates nine Brooklyn locations (plus Manhattan spots) providing consistent Stumptown coffee with laptop-friendly culture adapted to each neighborhood. The Prospect Heights location near Barclays Center offers spacious layout, Fort Greene serves that arts community, and Williamsburg provides L train corridor access. Each maintains quality while reflecting local character and space constraints.

Wifi performs adequately for typical work with outlet availability varying dramatically by specific location (Fort Greene and Prospect Heights better, Williamsburg more limited). Capacity differs by footprint from cozy 20-person spots to more generous 40-person locations. The Stumptown coffee program provides Seattle-roasted beans with skilled preparation, and the brand’s longevity in Brooklyn creates established neighborhood presence.

Multiple Brooklyn locations serve different neighborhoods providing geographic flexibility critical in sprawling Brooklyn. Prospect Heights serves central Brooklyn and Barclays commuters. Fort Greene attracts arts community. Williamsburg serves L train corridor. Each location adapts to neighborhood population and available space.

- Amenities: Good wifi, outlets (varies significantly by location), restrooms, Stumptown coffee, light food menu
- Nearby features: Varies by location; Prospect Heights, Fort Greene, Williamsburg neighborhoods

**Downside:** Closes 7pm across locations; outlet coverage extremely inconsistent (some locations very limited); capacity varies from tiny to moderate; some spots uncomfortably crowded.

## 5. Partners Coffee – Multiple Locations

**Address:** Multiple locations: Williamsburg (44 Charles St), Park Slope (132 7th Ave), Bed-Stuy (261 Malcolm X Blvd)

**Best for:** Brooklyn roaster, neighborhood presence, outlet access varies

Partners Coffee operates Brooklyn-roasted coffee with multiple neighborhood locations providing alternatives to chains. The Park Slope location offers most study-optimized environment with better outlet access, while Williamsburg and Bed-Stuy locations serve those specific communities. The Brooklyn-based roaster emphasizes quality beans and neighborhood cafe culture.

Wifi supports typical work demands with outlet availability varying significantly by location (Park Slope best coverage, others more limited). Capacity differs from 25-40 people depending on footprint. The house-roasted coffee program maintains quality standards, and the multiple locations create backup options when one fills or disappoints on outlet access.

Multiple Brooklyn locations serve Park Slope, Williamsburg, and Bed-Stuy providing geographic variety. Park Slope location benefits from neighborhood character and families creating daytime traffic patterns different from pure Williamsburg hustle. Each adapts to local population while maintaining consistent coffee quality.

- Transit/Parking: Varies by location; most near subway access; Park Slope easier parking than Williamsburg; bike-friendly
- Amenities: Reliable wifi, outlets (varies significantly by location), restrooms, Brooklyn-roasted coffee, light food
- Nearby features: Varies by location; Park Slope, Williamsburg, Bed-Stuy neighborhoods

**Downside:** Closes 7pm; outlet access highly variable requiring advance scouting; some locations very small; quality varies by specific spot more than brand consistency.

## 6. Cafe Ghia – Bed-Stuy

**Address:** 24 Irving Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11237

**Best for:** Bed-Stuy location, wine bar hybrid, late hours

Cafe Ghia operates as coffee bar during day transitioning to wine bar evenings, providing workspace from morning through early evening before wine service dominates. The Bed-Stuy location serves that developing neighborhood with hours extending later than typical Brooklyn cafes (open until 11pm). The dual identity means coffee-focused morning atmosphere while acknowledging evening transformation.

Wifi available with outlets at some seating positions (limited compared to warehouse-scale cafes but functional). Capacity accommodates 30-35 people across bar and table seating with the coffee bar hours maintaining study-friendly atmosphere before evening wine bar scene begins. Coffee quality maintains solid standards, and food menu extends beyond pastries.

Located on Irving Avenue in Bed-Stuy between Putnam and Madison, the cafe sits in developing Brooklyn neighborhood with G train access at Bedford-Nostrand. The Bed-Stuy location provides alternatives to saturated Williamsburg and Park Slope while serving that neighborhood’s creative workers and residents.

## 8. Bibble & Sip – Gowanus

Bibble & Sip brings their cream puff cafe concept to Gowanus/Park Slope border providing dessert-focused cafe with laptop-friendly seating. **Prioritize warehouse-scale spaces over converted brownstones.** Devoción’s Williamsburg warehouse provides genuinely abundant outlets at communal tables. **Scout specific locations before committing to multi-location brands.** Hungry Ghost has nine Brooklyn locations with outlet access varying from “functional” to “nearly nonexistent.” Partners Coffee’s Park Slope outpost provides better coverage than Williamsburg. Cafe Grumpy’s Greenpoint beats their other spots. Multi-location brands adapt to building constraints, making location-specific research essential.

**Use Brooklyn Public Library as free outlet-abundant baseline.** Central Library at Grand Army Plaza provides outlets at nearly every study position across four floors, eliminating both cost pressure and outlet anxiety. When cafe outlet gambling becomes frustrating, the library’s guaranteed electrical access provides reliable alternative. The free access saves money for actual coffee rather than buying outlet access.

**Understand that “laptop-friendly” doesn’t guarantee outlets.** Brooklyn cafes market laptop-welcome culture while offering minimal electrical infrastructure. Actual outlet abundance requires specific confirmation through visits, Google reviews mentioning outlets, or asking staff directly before settling in. Marketing and reality diverge dramatically in Brooklyn’s cafe scene.

**Plan around early closing times endemic to Brooklyn.** Most Brooklyn cafes close 6-7pm, earlier than Manhattan or 24-hour Austin/Portland cultures. Cafe Ghia’s 11pm closing and some later options exist, but evening work generally requires planning around limited hours. **Build neighborhood rotation rather than borough-wide searching.** Brooklyn’s sprawl makes cross-neighborhood cafe hopping impractical. Build 3-4 viable options within your immediate area (Williamsburg residents rotating Devoción, Cafe Grumpy, Hungry Ghost; Park Slope residents using Partners, Black Brick, Konditori). Geographic clustering saves travel time when outlets disappoint. Visit StudyNearby’s complete directory for more locations.

**Accept that Brooklyn aesthetics often prioritize design over function.** Scandinavian-minimalist cafes (Konditori, Sey) and French-inspired spots (L’Imprimerie) create Instagram-worthy interiors while limiting electrical infrastructure. Beautiful design and abundant outlets rarely coexist in Brooklyn. Choose function or aesthetics; rarely get both.

**Leverage subway lines for neighborhood access patterns.** L train serves Williamsburg and Bushwick (Devoción, Variety, Sey). G train reaches Greenpoint and Bed-Stuy (Cafe Grumpy, Cafe Ghia). 2/3 trains serve Park Slope and Central Library. R train hits Park Slope’s 7th Avenue corridor. Match cafe choices to your regular subway routes rather than fighting cross-borough transfers.

**Scout outlets during initial visit before committing hours.** Walk through space identifying outlet locations and counting total outlets versus seating capacity. Check if outlets actually work (some Brooklyn cafes have dead outlets). Observe if existing laptop users monopolize limited power access. This 5-minute reconnaissance prevents wasted setup when discovering no outlets exist after claiming table.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Which Brooklyn cafes actually have abundant outlets?**

Devoción Williamsburg provides genuinely abundant outlets at communal tables—this is Brooklyn’s gold standard for power access. Cafe Grumpy’s Greenpoint location offers best coverage in that brand. Brooklyn Central Library guarantees outlets at nearly every study position across four floors. Most other Brooklyn cafes have limited outlets (6-10 total) requiring strategic positioning or early arrival.

**Are there free study spots with outlets in Brooklyn?**

Brooklyn Public Library system provides completely free access with outlets at most study positions. Central Library at Grand Army Plaza offers four floors with extensive power access. Neighborhood branches throughout Brooklyn provide smaller-scale alternatives. These eliminate both cost pressure and outlet anxiety while providing superior electrical infrastructure to most cafes.

**Which neighborhoods have the best cafe outlet access?**

Williamsburg offers Devoción with exceptional outlets plus Cafe Grumpy and Hungry Ghost options. Greenpoint provides Cafe Grumpy’s flagship with good coverage. Park Slope has multiple options though outlet access varies. Bed-Stuy and Bushwick cafes typically have more limited power infrastructure. Williamsburg warehouse-era buildings generally provide better electrical access than brownstone conversions.

**Do Brooklyn cafes welcome laptop users?**

Most Brooklyn cafes market laptop-friendly culture during off-peak hours, though attitudes vary. Devoción, Cafe Grumpy, and Hungry Ghost explicitly welcome extended laptop sessions. Specialty roasteries (Sey, Variety) tolerate laptops with purchase expectations. Dessert-focused spots (Bibble & Sip, Konditori) appreciate turnover during peak hours. Purchase periodically and respect peak times.

**What are the latest-closing cafes with outlets in Brooklyn?**

Cafe Ghia stays open until 11pm though it transitions to wine bar evenings. Most Brooklyn cafes close 6-7pm significantly earlier than Manhattan options. The early-closing culture requires planning daytime work or using Brooklyn Public Library for evening sessions. Brooklyn lacks the 24-hour cafe culture found in some other cities.

**Can I find cafes with outlets near subway lines?**

L train corridor (Williamsburg, Bushwick) has Devoción, Variety, Sey, and others. G train serves Greenpoint (Cafe Grumpy flagship), Bed-Stuy (Cafe Ghia, Stonefruit). 2/3 trains reach Central Library and Park Slope options. R train hits Park Slope’s 7th Avenue corridor. Most Brooklyn cafes sit within blocks of subway access; outlet availability varies regardless of transit proximity.

**Which spots work best for all-day sessions?**

Brooklyn Central Library provides best infrastructure for extended sessions with free access, abundant outlets, varied environments, and 9pm weekday closing. Devoción’s warehouse space accommodates long sessions with outlet abundance and capacity. Cafes with full food menus (Stonefruit, Bibble & Sip) support meal transitions. Most Brooklyn cafes close 6-7pm limiting “all-day” to roughly 8am-6pm maximum.

**How do I avoid weekend brunch crowds at Brooklyn cafes?**

Visit before 9am or after 2pm to avoid peak brunch invasion (9am-2pm weekends). Specialty coffee roasteries (Sey, Variety) attract fewer brunch crowds than pastry-focused spots. Brooklyn Central Library stays reliably quiet weekends. Williamsburg and Park Slope see worst brunch density; Bed-Stuy and Bushwick somewhat better. Weekday visits eliminate brunch chaos entirely.

**Are outlets actually available or always occupied?**

Even cafes with decent outlet coverage see power access occupied during peak hours (10am-4pm weekdays). Early arrival (before 9am) improves outlet odds significantly. Brooklyn Central Library’s abundant outlets reduce competition compared to cafes. At limited-outlet cafes, expect to wait for power access or work on battery during busy periods. Scout outlet locations during reconnaissance visits.

**What should I bring for Brooklyn cafe study sessions?**

Bring laptop fully charged as outlets aren’t guaranteed despite cafe claims. Power bank backup (20,000mAh minimum) provides 4-6 hours emergency power. Headphones for ambient noise management in busy cafes. Water bottle as cafe purchases add up. Light layers as Brooklyn cafes run variable temperatures. Subway card for easy movement between backup locations when outlets disappoint.
