title: The Top 10 Coffee Shops on the Upper West Side
author: Kaylan Kha
text:
*Updated February 15, 2026*

# Coffee Shops on the Upper West Side

Read on to find the best Coffee Shops on the Upper West Side…

While Gossip Girl was wreaking havoc on the Upper East Side, Ted and his friends from *How I Met Your Mother*** **were living it up on the Upper West Side. The Upper West Side has been the backdrop for many other shows like 

*You*and

*Only Murders in the Building*. Makes sense, since it’s a neighborhood with a lot of charm, character, and cultural history. The iconic Lincoln Center and the American Museum of Natural History are just a few institutions that attract both locals and tourists to this area.

Like the Upper East Side, the majority of coffee shops here are locally owned—and not dominated by large chains. There is no shortage of cozy neighborhood coffee shops here, but these are the **Top 10** **Coffee Shops on the Upper West Side.**

### 1. Black Press Coffee

Black Press Coffee is a specialty coffee shop serving Upper Manhattan; with one location on the Upper West and the other on the Upper East, they’ve got both sides of Central Park covered! They partner with Parlor Coffee, a roaster in Brooklyn, to provide high-quality coffee beans and roasts to patrons.

Their menu was simple and had the typical espresso-based drinks you’d see. I ordered their **Latte **($5), but I almost got the **Turmeric Latte **($5.75) because it sounded interesting. The coffee was full-bodied and smooth, making for a great cup of coffee. It had the right ratio of milk to espresso. They also sell pastries for those who want to grab a quick bite! 

It’s in close proximity to the Natural History Museum (about a five minute walk), so I would recommend getting a drink here before your visit!

📍274 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10023

### 2. Patis Bakery

Located within the Arthouse Hotel, Patis Bakery is one of the best places to get a cup of joe to start the day! It’s an artisan cafe with several locations throughout New York City and New Jersey that’s offering American and European favorites.

From sandwiches to pizza, there are so many options of great food here. Their drinks menu is also pretty expansive, as there’s a whole section for speciality lattes! I ordered the **Shiitake Sesame Focaccia **($6.95) alongside a **Truffle Twist **($5.50). The focaccia was topped with a parsley pesto, smoked onion, and shiitake mushrooms. It was jam-packed with umami flavor and was the perfect salty counterpart to go with my sweet latte. 

The Truffle Twist latte tasted like if a Ferror Rocher chocolate was dropped into some espresso; it had espresso, milk, hazelnut, and chocolate ganache. It was a very decadent drink, but I still enjoyed it! There is no lack of options at Patis, so be prepared to spend some time reading the menu and deciding what you want.

📍2178 Broadway, New York, NY 10024, United States

### 3. Picky Barista

Picky Barista is a family-owned cafe and espresso bar that’s been serving the Upper West Side community for more than 15 years. They serve Stumptown coffee and homemade pastries; If you enjoy the coffee, you can purchase Stumptown retail beans at the shop. They’ll even grind the beans on the spot for you!

I got a **Drip Coffee **($3) made with the Hair Bender blend. As their most popular coffee, I was expecting some delicious coffee—and I was not disappointed. I could taste notes of citrus and dark chocolate, which are two flavors I think are great together. The citrusy notes highlighted a light acidity that was balanced by the warmth of the chocolate. 

I’m a sucker for baked goods, so I had to try one of Picky Barista’s homemade pastries. The **Balkan Croissant with Jam **($3.75) was everything you would want a croissant to be: buttery and flaky. It had a tasty filling; I’m not sure what kind of jam it was, but it was both tart and sweet!

There is such a great ambiance here, as its vibes are what you would find in some of the best cafes. Good coffee and vibes…what more could you ask for?

📍667 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10025

### 4. Charlotte Cafe

With respect to its royal namesake, Charlotte Cafe aims to “evoke a sense of sophistication and classic charm.” I thought the cafe was very quaint and welcoming; the soft lighting and ample seating made for a lovely environment. I liked how spacious it was, as I could definitely see myself working remotely here with the free wifi.

I had to try the **Cappuccino **($3.95) because this place is like an Italian cafe (and Italians really know how to make a cappuccino!). The drink was creamy and rich with a good amount of steamed milk on top—perfect for my taste buds because I enjoy frothy cappuccinos. There were also a variety of different baked goods on display here.

What made Charlotte Cafe a stand-out place in my eyes was the friendly staff. The baristas were so nice when taking my order and made me feel very welcome! Even though it was only my first time here, Charlotte Cafe is already my new favorite corner spot.

📍2541 Broadway, New York, NY 10025

### 5. Daily Provisions

If you could only get one thing at Daily Provisions, it has to be their crullers. They’re some award-winning pastries in my book! After trying them, those crullers were the only breakfast pastries I could think about for the longest time.

The **Cinnamon Cruller **($4.95) is a popular item; it reminds me of a churro in donut form. The outside is crispy and perfectly fried (much like a churro), but the inside is fluffy and airy. I had it paired with their **Cold Brew** ($4.75) that had notes of chocolate fudge, molasses, and cinnamon. I would say the two went really well together because the coffee helped cut through the sweetness of the cruller.

Daily Provisions is a great place for all-day fare: breakfast, lunch, dinner—you name it, they have it! There can be a lot of people on weekday mornings and you might have to wait a long time, but I do believe the wait is well worth it.

📍375 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY 10024

### 6. Irving Farm New York

Irving Farm New York is a coffee chain that opened its first store on Irving Place in Gramercy back in 1996. Since then, they’ve opened multiple storefronts across Manhattan in neighborhoods like Greenwich Village and East Village.

I’ve come to realize that a lot of cafes in New York are quite small, but this location is anything but small. With a lot of tables and seating, it seems to be a popular spot for people to either study or work remotely (no free wifi though). There’s also a skylight in the back seating area and a few tables in the front for outdoor seating!

I got a **Matcha Latte **($6.25) and a **Cinnamon Cardamom Bun** ($4.75). The matcha was earthy with a subtle sweetness. For a place that doesn’t specialize in matcha, the drink was pretty good! The bun was the perfect morning pastry, as it was both delicious and filling. The hints of citrus and floral tones made this a delightful bite. 

With so many locations, there’s no excuse for you to not visit Irving Farm!

📍224 W 79th St New York, NY 10024

### 7. Solid State Coffee

One of the best local coffee shops has to be Solid State Coffee. The shop itself is below sidewalk level, which gives it an intimate and cozy feel. They’re serving up some great food and exceptional coffee here.

Along with the traditional breakfast favorites like **Avocado Toast **($15) and a** Breakfast Plate **($20), they also have some special items: **Syrniki **($14), which are cheese mini-pancakes served with jam, and **Cacio e Pepe Grits **($16). For a small shop, they’ve got some big menu items! 

I wanted to try the **Cortado **($4.75). A cortado has equal parts espresso and steamed milk and no foam, unlike a cappuccino. The drink was well-balanced, as the addition of the milk helped make the drink smoother overall. It was definitely a strong coffee—I felt so energized after drinking it! 

Solid State Coffee is a cute, hole-in-the-wall coffee shop that’s easy to miss if you’re not paying attention. Come here for high quality cups of coffee!

📍104 W 71st St, New York, NY 10023

### 8. About Coffee

On the corner of W 81st Street and Columbus Avenue, you can find About Coffee. Here, they’re serving up coffee roasted by Gimme! Coffee. There is a section on their menu for special drinks—some of which I’ve never seen before at other places. The two that stood out to me were the **Caffe Cardamo **($4.50) and the **Oatmeg **($6). The former is essentially a cortado with cardamom and the latter (I’m assuming) is an oat milk latte with nutmeg.

It’s so close to both Central Park and the Natural History Museum, making it the perfect place to stop by before continuing with the activities you have planned for the day. There’s also a good amount of space in the cafe for you to relax and cool off (especially if the summer heat gets unbearable).

About Coffee has been consistently churning out solid drinks for the community and as they say, it has always been about coffee!

📍445 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10024

### 9. Plowshares Coffee Roasters

Plowshares Coffee Roasted opened their flagship location in 2014 on the Upper West Side, with a second location in West Harlem opening a few years later. That cafe has a 1940s vintage Probat coffee roaster in store where you can watch it roast beans! You even have the option to purchase their house roasted beans.

While there are great lattes here, the standout would have to be their **Nitro Cold Brew **($6). The coffee itself is pretty strong, while also still being very smooth and fresh. Some cold brews I’ve tried before have a slight bitterness to them, but this one doesn’t have that problem. 

This is a great neighborhood spot to grab some excellent coffee; because they started off as wholesale coffee roasters, you know they know how to craft coffee!

📍2730 Broadway, New York, NY 10025

### 10. The Muffins Cafe

A few blocks down from the Joe Coffee Company UWS storefront sits The Muffins Cafe! It seems like the kind of place only the local New Yorkers would know about—with its homey and friendly vibe, it wouldn’t surprise me to learn that it’s a community favorite.

Its classic cafe fare (pastries, sandwiches, and salads) is extensive, as there are so many options to choose from. I ordered a **Decaf + Hazelnut Iced Coffee **($5). Some people think that decaf coffee tastes different from regular caffeinated coffee, but the two taste the same to me. I can’t tell the difference (other than the caffeinated one keeping me up at night!). I loved the flavor of the hazelnut syrup; it didn’t have that cloying sweet taste that many artificial syrups do. 

I came in the morning for a quick drink, so I didn’t get a chance to try anything else. I’ll have to return to try something in their case of pastries and a sandwich! Don’t overlook The Muffins Cafe because it’s a solid local spot on the UWS!

📍222 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10023

### 11. Alice’s Tea Cup

Forgive me — this is a tea spot, but it’s worthy of mentioning. This whimsical hole-in-the-wall is the perfect small business vibe.

The pumpkin scone was decadent, flavorful and moist, and comes with delicious clotted cream and raspberry jam.

The crowd skews older, it seemed like it was mostly neighborhood residents catching up when I went Saturday afternoon. People sipped their tea with 3-tiered trays.

📍102 W 73rd St, New York, NY 10023

## Coffee Shops on the Upper West Side

The Upper West Side is full of charm and historic buildings that make me feel as if I’m in an old New York movie. It possesses a different atmosphere than the Upper East Side—although both are still great and much preferred than lower Manhattan. A perfect morning for me consists of a nice stroll around the blocks with a drink, so here are my recommendations for **Coffee Shops on the Upper West Side…**

title: 17 Best Coffee Shops on the Upper East Side + Amazing Tips
author: Girlwiththepassport; Girl
text:
If you’re channeling your inner Blair Waldorf (shameless Gossip Girl reference) and are looking for the poshest and **best coffee shops on the Upper East Side** then this ultra-snazzy post is for you. 

I mean, I have lived in the city for 30+ years and drink coffee every day. So, to say that I know a thing or two about the **best coffee in NYC **is an understatement. 

In particular, I love grabbing. a cup of Joe at some of the **best cafes on the Upper East Side**. 

The coffee is great, the ambiance is amazing, and I just feel super plush with my flat white made with oat milk.

Plus, some of these coffee places on the Upper East Side are just a great place to relax after exploring epic Upper East Side landmarks like the MET, Guggenheim, and Central Park.

That being said, not every coffee shop on the Upper East Side is amazing. Some are downright gross and super overpriced.

So, I’m gonna give you the inside scoop on coffee shops to avoid and coffee shops to relax the day away in this epic local guide.

*This post may contain affiliate links. Please see my disclosure for more information. As an Amazon Associate, I earn a small commission from qualifying purchases.*

**Contents**show

## Best Coffee Shops on the Upper East Side

## 1. Maman

Maman is a French-inspired bakery that originated in SoHo. However, this epic spot quickly established itself as a local gem in the heart of the city.

Its reputation remained on the DL until Oprah declared their chocolate chip cookies as one of her ultimate “favorite things.”

This acclaim sparked a surge in the bakery’s popularity. As a result, you can now find Maman all across the city, including the Upper East Side.

So, stop by to admire Maman’s charming decor and exquisite delft china. Their robust coffee only adds to its allure, as does the quiche, chocolate croissant, macadamia nut cookie, and lattes.

**Local Tip: **Order the nutty chocolate chip cookies. They are to die for and make this one of the best dessert spots in New York City. 

**Address:** 1424 3rd Ave, New York, NY 10028

**Hours:** Open daily from 7:30 am to 6:00 pm, except on weekends when they open at 8:00 am.

**Price:** Coffee starts at $3.50.

## 2. Eat Pretty

Previously known as Yorkafe, Eat Pretty is one of the best-hidden gems in New York City‘s Upper East Side.

See, this Upper East Side cafe underwent an enchanting rebrand, transforming into a pink paradise that comes complete with outdoor seating shaded by miniature umbrellas.

Although the interior is more than a little cozy, there’s plenty of space for you to enjoy al fresco dining on pink benches.

You’ll also love all of the pastel-hued flowers and giant teddy bears that surround the cafe. Don’t worry about crowds though since this place is pretty under the radar.

If you’re unsure of what to order, try a latte, hot cocoa, avocado toast, steak taco, or the Bagel BLT.

Each of these items has received rave reviews from either me or my friends (or both).

And of course, remember to indulge in a cupcake for dessert since all of the sweets here are baked fresh on the premises, except the croissants.

## 3. Hutch & Waldo

This enchanting little cafe has a distinctive Australian vibe and has become an integral part of the Upper East Side’s food scene since its inception in 2016.

The delightful interior combined with an impressive New York City brunch menu has earned it a loyal following.

That being said, I thought their Brekkie Sando was very average the last time I was here. Yes, the bread was good but the rest of the sandwich fell flat for me.

However, many visitors love their grilled chicken salad with sweet potatoes and a kale and quinoa salad. So, maybe opt for that instead.

Their coffee was also really good. I ordered the flat white and can highly recommend it. Yeah, I never miss a chance to order a flat white in an Aussie-style cafe.

**Address:** 247 E 81st St, New York, NY 10028

**Hours:** Open daily from 8:00 am to 3:00 pm.

**Price: **Entrees start at $11.00/$12.00 each.

## 4. Ella’s Cafe Espresso and Wine Bar

Opened in 2021, this espresso and wine bar is one of the best cafes on the Upper East Side where you can enjoy a wide variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.

See, it’s a charming little Mediterranean-inspired wine bar/coffee shop that will make you instantly feel like you’re at home, with family.

It’s also a tranquil oasis in which you can enjoy an expertly brewed cup of coffee and pair it with delectable Mediterranean/Israeli cuisine.

In particular, the Toastini is exceptional and packed with amazing flavor. Order it with a delish chai latte and you’ll keep coming back for more.

However, feel free to stop by in the evenings and unwind with a flatbread, and a calming glass of Israeli wine/beer.

**Local Tip:** The coffee here is strong but really good. There are also a ton of vegan options at the vegan-friendly restaurant in NYC. 

**Address: **1465 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10075

**Hours:** Open daily from 7:00 am to 8:00 pm, except on the weekends when they open at 8:00 am. 

**Price: **Croissants start at $4.00 each. 

## 5. 787 Coffee

At 787 Coffee, it’s not just about the coffee – it’s about the experience.

From the moment you step into this cafe on the Upper East Side, you’re greeted by the welcoming aroma of beans freshly roasted in Puerto Rico.

You’re drawn to the cozy wooden furniture and the white-washed brick walls that add a bit of vintage charm to one of the best coffee shops on the Upper East Side.

Your eyes wander to the bookshelves filled with adorable trinkets, amplifying the cafe’s quaint ambiance.

However, what really sets this coffee shop apart is its innovative menu, with coquito and horchata lattes that celebrate the company’s Puerto Rican heritage.

And let’s not forget the food – a delicious selection of chocolate chunk cookies, scones, and empanadas.

But the real standout? The marzipan latte. It’s not just a coffee, it’s a masterpiece.

**Address:** 228 E 80th St, New York, NY 10075

**Hours: **Open daily from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm. 

**Price:** Varies

## 6. Variety Coffee Roasters

If you’re a coffee aficionado who loves the nuanced flavor of expertly roasted beans then Variety Coffee Roasters is one of the best coffee shops on the Upper East Side for you.

When you step into any of their six locations across Brooklyn and Manhattan, you’re instantly welcomed by the aromatic smell of freshly brewed coffee.

The Upper East Side location stands out with its lush greenery, stunning bubble lights, and expansive floor-to-ceiling windows that let in lots of ambient light.

Sure, this location is usually packed with people. But, the coffee is delicious and the cafe is stunning.

Plus, if you’re feeling a bit hungry, you can indulge in one of their pastries, which are freshly baked in-house.

Local Tip: Stop by Goodwill after so that you can shop at one of the best thrift shops in Manhattan.

**Address: **1269 Lexington Ave, New York, NY 10028

**Hours:** Open daily from 7:00 am to 9:00 pm. 

**Price:** Coffee starts at $2.50 each. 

## 7. Madame Bonte

Unlike many of the other coffee shops on the Upper East Side, Madame Bonte has three locations – one at 84th Street (between 1st and 2nd Avenue), one at 2nd Avenue (between 94th and 95th), and one at East 66th Street (between 2nd and 3rd Avenue).

I prefer the 84th Street location since there is an expansive downstairs sitting area. It has a sleek, sophistication about it that is accented by modern pictures and sleek, clean lines.

There’s also a lovely backyard patio where you can sit down and relax with your specialty coffee, gourmet sandwich, or artisanal pastry.

I always get the iced chai latte and almond croissant when I stop in here. It’s also nice that this spot turns into a charming little wine bar in the evening where you can grab a drink with a few friends.

**Address:** 318 E 84th St, New York, NY 10028

**Hours:** Open daily from 7:30 am to 10:00 pm, except Sunday/Monday when they are open from 7:30 am to 5:00 pm. 

**Price:** Coffee starts at $2.75 each. 

## 8. Cafe Bleriot XI

Cafe Bleriot XI features an astounding French ambiance that makes it one of the best Instagram spots in New York City.

It’s an Upper East Side coffee shop that offers you not just a cup of coffee, but a delightful experience steeped in history and charm.

The rustic wooden seating, marble tabletops, vintage decor, and historic paintings adorning the walls transport you to an era of elegance and grandeur.

Named after the pioneering French aviator, Louis Blériot, the café embodies his spirit of adventure and innovation.

Carrying forward Blériot’s belief in the power of a good breakfast, the café prides itself on its delectable menu.

Their robust coffee and savory spinach and goat cheese quiche are personal favorites that I enjoy every time I’m here.

Despite limited seating, the café exudes a relaxed vibe, further enhanced by the friendly and welcoming staff.

So, a visit to Bleriot café offers a refreshing escape from bustling city life, making it an essential stop on your NYC café exploration.

**Address: **226 E 83rd St, New York, NY 10028

**Hours:** Open daily from 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, except on Sundays when they open at 8:00 am.

**Price:** Drinks start at around $4.50 each.

## 9. Miss Madeleine

This is probably the most authentic French bakery you will find in the city since the owners came over here from France.

Yup, they took over “Canele by Celine” and transformed it into a place where you can get authentic, handmade, French pastries like croissants, Madeleines, jams, breads, cakes, and more.

I love the chocolate croissant, the French-style cheesecake, and the ham and cheese quiche.

Just be forewarned that there really isn’t any seating and that this is more of a grab-and-go type place.

However, you can snap a photo with the bubble gum pink exterior and look at pics of people’s super cute pets that are hung up on the wall.

**Address: **400 E 82nd St, New York, NY 10028

**Hours: **Open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm, Saturday from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm, and Sunday from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

**Price:** Most desserts are around $6.50 each. 

## 10. Ralph’s Coffee

With a distinct charm and a unique green vibe, Ralph’s Coffee has carved a niche for itself among the multitude of cafes on the Upper East Side. I

Its ambiance is reminiscent of a bygone era and seamlessly blends with contemporary aesthetics to attract caffeine enthusiasts and Instagram aficionados alike.

The robust espresso paves the way for a memorable coffee experience, thanks to the superior quality of the La Colombe beans they use.

There’s also plenty of outdoor seating so that you can indulge in the age-old pastime of people-watching.

The only caveat? The popularity of this café often leads to a wait. So. arrive early if you want to nab a table.

I also wouldn’t order food. I had the blueberry corn muffins and they were kind of gross.

**Address:** 888 Madison Ave, New York, NY 10021

**Hours:** Open Monday to Thursday from 10:00 am to 6:00 pm, Friday/Saturday from 10:00 am to 7:00 pm, and Sunday from 12:00 pm to 6:00 pm.

**Price: **$5.50 for a latte.

## 11. Bluestone Lane

Looking to refuel in the middle of the day? If so then stop by Bluestone Lane.

It sits inside an old church near the MET and is one of the best cafes om the Upper East Side that is known for its Aussie-style breakfast and coffee.

So, be sure to order a delicious flat white as you take in the stunning vaulted ceilings and intricate stonework around you.

Despite its popularity leading to occasional queues, the efficient service and friendly staff ensure your wait isn’t a hassle.

From their iconic Avocado Smash to the nutritious Ancient Grains Bowl, the cafe’s menu is a delightful mix of Aussie faves.

Just be sure to pair your meal with a comforting chai tea or a golden milk latte, and you’ll enjoy the perfect brunch before checking out some of the free activities on the Upper East Side.

**Address:** 1085 5th Ave, New York, NY 10128, United States

**Hours:** Open Monday through Thursday from 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, Friday from 7:00 am to 6:00 pm. Saturday from 7:30 am to 6:00 pm, and Sunday from 7:30 am to 5:00 pm.

**Price:** Entrees start at around $11.00 each.

## 12. Oslo Coffee Roasters

Oslo Coffee Roasters are producers of fine artisanal coffee that first started their business back in 2011 in Brooklyn.

Over the years, the company has blossomed, opening various locations throughout the city, including one on the Upper East Side.

This humble shop is renowned for brewing some of the best coffee on the Upper East Side and sees a steady stream of patrons, eager to get their daily caffeine fix.

Tucked away on a tranquil, tree-lined street, Oslo Coffee Roasters is committed to supporting local businesses by sourcing only local ingredients.

So, a visit to this shop promises delectable espresso-based beverages and cold brews, all made from their very own coffee roast.

I love their macchiato and always sip on one while reading one of the many newspapers in the cafe.

**Address:** 422 E 75th St, New York, NY 10021

**Hours:** Open daily from 7:00 am to 4:00 pm, except on weekends when they open at 8:00 am.

**Price: **$3.25 and up.

## 13. Black Star Bakery

Black Star Bakery is one of the best coffee shops on the Upper East Side that offers a contemporary atmosphere perfect for both work and relaxation.

With its spacious seating and modern layout, it stands out as one of the premier coffee shops in the area.

Whether you’re seeking a place to chill with your laptop or indulge in delectable baked goods, this spot has got you covered.

Delight in their signature iced white mocha paired with a sumptuous chocolate chip cookie. Or, try a Belgian waffle for a touch of European flair.

**Local Tip:** Head out back and grab a seat since they have great outdoor seating.

**Address:** 1597 York Ave, New York, NY 10028

**Hours: **Open Monday through Friday from 7:00 am to 4:00 pm and on weekends from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

**Price:** Entrees start at like $8.50 each.

## 14. Café Sabarsky

Café Sabarsky offers a delectable fusion of culture, history, and gastronomy – and all right on Fifth Avenue.

Nestled within the Neue Museum, one of the most unique museums in NYC, the café exudes an air of European elegance, reminiscent of early 20th-century Vienna.

The interior features vintage Wagner fabric, furnishings by Adolf Loos, and an opulent Bösendorfer grand piano.

The menu has a tantalizing array of German-Austrian flavors, with highlights including the crisp wiener schnitzel, hearty bratwurst, and divine desserts such as the Sachertorte and the apfelstrudel.

Given its popularity, reservations are highly recommended. Though the prices are steep, the unique ambiance, coupled with the rich culinary offerings, make Café Sabarsky worth the splurge.

Remember to savor their coffee as well, it’s a must-try!

**Address:** 1048 5th Ave, New York, NY 10028

**Hours:** Open Thursday/Friday from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm, Saturday/Sunday from 9:00 am to 8:00 pm, and Monday from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm.

**Price:** Coffee starts at $8.00 each.

## 15. Mellow Yellow

The magic of this cafe on the Upper East Side lies not only in its quirky, relaxed ambiance but in its deliciously unique menu.

Reminiscent of a laid-back Mediterranean diner, the decor strikes a balance between rustic and funky.

This isn’t a place for formalities. But, it is a place where you can soak up positive vibes while savoring some of the best coffee on the Upper East Side.

The eclectic charm is almost as enticing as the standout dishes on offer like moussaka, shakshuka, and a green omelet sandwich.

To complete the experience, indulge in the rich, aromatic chai latte and you’ll deffo be coming back for more.

**Address:** 1729 1st Ave., New York, NY 10128

**Hours:** Open daily from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

**Price:** A Turkish Coffee is like $5.50.

## Unique Cafes on the Upper East Side

## 16. Hex and Co.

Truth be told, Hex and Co. isn’t on this list because they serve amazing coffee. Sure, the coffee is okay.

But, this cafe on the Upper East Side is listed because they have an AMAZING selection of board games to choose from. Like, over a thousand to be exact.

So, if you’re looking for things to do on the Upper East Side today and have a group of friends then swing by Hex and Co.

Prices start at just $10.00 per player. Plus, they have a great selection of coffee, killer cocktails, and some rad pub grub too.

Just don’t add this Upper East Side cafe to your list of things to do solo in NYC since you need a group to dive into epic games like Dungeons and Dragons.

**Address: **1462 1st Ave., New York, NY 10075

**Hours: **Open daily from 11:00 am to 11:00 pm. 

**Price:** Starts at $10.00 per person. 

## 17. Stella and Fly

Full disclosure? This is one of the best cafes on the Upper East Side which is mostly a wine bar.

However, they do serve a wide variety of coffees and even have chess boards that you can use if you want to embrace your inner Bobby Fischer.

So, if you’re looking for more of a chill, Upper East Side coffee shop vibe then stop by during the day. This place is super cozy and lined with brick and lots of wood furniture.

I love to come here and get the grilled cheese sandwich. You can also stop by for happy hour around 3:00 pm and get a well-priced charcuterie board.

**Local Tip: **If you’re looking for fun things to do at night in NYC then stop by for trivia night on Monday at 8:00 pm. You could win shots or a bottle of wine to take home. Also try the Dirty Coffee. 

**Address: **1705 1st Ave., New York, NY 10128

**Hours:** Open Sunday through Wednesday from 7:00 am to 1:00 am, Thursday from 7:00 am to 2:00 am, and Friday/Saturday from 7:00 am to 3:00 am. 

**Price: **Cocktails start at $13.00 each. 

## Map of the Best Coffee Shops on the Upper East Side

## Best Coffee Shops on the Upper East Side FAQs

## Which Coffee Shop is the Most Popular?

Starbucks is the most popular coffee shop in the world. It was started in Seattle in 1971 and gets its name from the famous novel, “Moby Dick”.

## Which US city has the Best Coffee Shops?

The US city with the best coffee shops is San Francisco, closely followed by Portland, Oregon, and Seattle, Washington.

## Who has the Most Coffee Shops in the US?

Starbucks has the most coffee shops in the US. In total, there are over 16,000 Starbucks coffee shops in the US.

## What is the Most Beautiful Coffee Shop in the World?

The most beautiful coffee shop in the world can be found in Budapest, Hungary. It is New York Café and has an opulent interior filled with gilt and velvet.

There is also a sumptuous menu filled with top-notch dishes.

title: 20+ Late Night Study Spots NYC Open Past Midnight • Over Here New York
author: Julie Anne Loquinario
text:
# 20+ Late Night Study Spots NYC Open Past Midnight

Look, I get it. The apartment is too loud, your roommate decided to host an improv practice in the living room, or maybe your brain just doesn’t turn on until the sun goes down. If you’ve lived here long enough, you know the struggle: New York City, the “City That Never Sleeps,” actually started taking naps around 10:00 PM somewhere in 2020.

Finding a spot with reliable WiFi, caffeine, and an outlet after dark feels like hunting for a unicorn in a haystack. But don’t worry, I’ve done the legwork (and drank a questionable amount of espresso) to find the places that are actually open.

If you’ve been scrolling through **late night study spots in NYC Reddit** threads looking for answers, look no further. Here is the verified, local-approved list of where to get work done when the rest of the city is signing off.

**NOTE: **Hours in NYC change faster than subway delays. Always check Google Maps or call ahead before trekking across the city at midnight.

## The Only Verified List: 20+ Late Night Study Spots NYC (Open Past Midnight)

**The “Actually Good Coffee” Late Night Spots**

These are the holy grail: actual cafes that stay open past the standard 7:00 PM curfew.

**Kobrick Coffee Co. (Meatpacking District)**

This is arguably one of the **best late night study spots in NYC**. By day, it’s a bustling cafe; by night, the lights dim slightly, but the caffeine keeps flowing. They are open until **2:00 AM** most nights. The vibe is old-school cool with brick walls and velvet chairs.

- **Location:**24 Ninth Ave, New York
- **Website:**https://www.kobricks.com | +1 800-562-7491 | info@kobrickcoffee.com
- **Good for:**Deep work, espresso martinis (if you’re done studying).
- **WiFi:**Yes.

**Book Club Bar (East Village)**

A bookstore that serves wine? Yes, please. But it’s also a fantastic study spot. They are open until **12:00 AM** Sunday through Wednesday and **1:00 AM** on weekends. It’s cozy, quiet-ish (it gets louder as the night goes on), and perfect for reading or typing up a paper.

- **Location:**197 East 3rd Street, New York
- **Website:**https://www.bookclubbar.com | +1 646-678-4160 | info@bookclubbar.com
- **Good for:**Humanities majors and creative writers.
- **Note:**It’s a bar, so bring ID.

**Qahwah House (Williamsburg & West Village)**

If you want arguably the best Yemeni chai in the city, come here. The Williamsburg location is usually bustling until **11:00 PM or 12:00 AM** (check specific location hours as they vary slightly). The energy here is infectious—lots of groups, laptops open, and the smell of cardamom is incredible.

- **Location:**Multiple Locations (e.g., 162 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn,m)
- **Website:**https://www.qahwahhouse.com |+1 313-908-4521
- **Good for:**Group study sessions.

**Molasses Books (Bushwick)**

Bushwick locals know this gem. It’s a used bookstore that doubles as a cafe and bar. Open until **12:00 AM** nightly, it has that distinct “I’m working on my screenplay” energy. It’s one of those **free places to study in NYC** where you can browse books when your brain needs a break (just buy a tea to support them).

- **Location:**770 Hart St, Brooklyn
- **Contact**: https://www.instagram.com/molassesbooks
- **Good for:**A chill, unpretentious atmosphere.

**The Roost (East Village)**

Business in the front, party in the back. The front section is a gorgeous espresso bar with wood paneling that stays open late (usually **12:00 AM** or later). The back turns into a bar, but the front remains a solid sanctuary for laptop users.

- **Location:**222 Avenue B, New York
- **Website:**https://www.instagram.com/theroostnyc
- **Good for:**Aesthetics and strong coffee.

**K-Town & Bubble Tea Havens**

When you need sugar to keep your eyes open, head to Koreatown or a bubble tea shop. These are reliable **late night study spots near me** if you are in Midtown or downtown.

**Grace Street Coffee & Desserts (Koreatown)**

This place is massive and almost always packed with students. Open until **11:00 PM** on weekdays and **12:00 AM** on weekends. The WiFi is fast, and the shaved snow is a verified reward for finishing that chapter.

- **Location:**17 W 32nd St, New York
- **Website:**https://www.bygracestreet.com
- **Good for:**High energy, late-night sugar rushes.

**Prince Tea House (Multiple Locations)**

Whether you are in the East Village, Chinatown, or Flushing, Prince Tea House is a reliable savior. Most locations stay open until **11:00 PM or 12:00 AM**. The decor is very “Alice in Wonderland,” and the pots of tea are endless.

- **Location:**Multiple Locations (e.g., 36-39 Prince St, Flushing)
- **Website:**https://www.princeteahouse.com | info@princeteahouse.com
- **Good for:**Unlimited refills of hot tea.

**Oasis Cafe (Flushing & East Village)**

A legendary spot for Queens locals. The Flushing location is open until **12:00 AM** or **1:00 AM**. It’s known for its pastries and being a hub for students cramming for finals.

- **Location:**196-30 Northern Blvd, Flushing
- **Website:**https://www.theoasiscafe.com | +1 718-357-4843 | info@oasiscafenyc.com
- **Good for:**Late-night cheesecake.

**The Old Faithfuls: 24-Hour Diners & Classics**

Sometimes you need a booth, endless coffee refills, and a plate of fries at 3:00 AM.

**Remedy Diner (Lower East Side)**

Yes, it is open **24 hours**. If you are wondering **where to study in NYC on a Sunday** at 4:00 AM, this is the answer. It’s clean, the staff is used to laptop users (as long as you keep ordering), and the WiFi is usually functional.

- **Location:**245 E Houston St, New York
- **Website:**https://www.remedydinerny.com | +1 212-677-5110 | remedydiner@yahoo.com
- **Good for:**The all-nighter crowd.

**Coppelia (Chelsea)**

A Cuban diner that never sleeps. Open **24 hours**, Coppelia is vibrant and busy. It’s louder than a library, but the white noise is perfect for some people. The food is also significantly better than your average diner.

- **Location:**207 W 14th St, New York
- **Website:**https://www.ilovecoppelia.com
- **Good for:**Lomo Saltado at 2:00 AM.

**Court Square Diner (Long Island City)**

A beacon of light in Queens. This classic metallic diner is open **24/7**. It’s right off the 7 train, has big booths, and the staff won’t rush you if it’s not a peak Friday night rush.

- **Location:**45-30 23rd St, Long Island City
- **Website:**https://www.courtsquarediner.com
- **Good for:**Spreading out your textbooks.

**Waverly Diner (West Village)**

Another **24-hour** icon. It feels like stepping back in time. The neon sign is a welcome sight for weary students. Just make sure to tip your server well if you plan on camping out in a booth.

- **Location:**385 6th Ave, New York
- **Website:**https://www.waverlydiner.com | 212-675-3181 | waverlydiner@gmail.com
- **Good for:**Classic NYC nostalgia.

**Midnight Express (Upper East Side)**

For the uptown crowd, this **24-hour** diner is a reliable staple. It’s standard diner fare, but it’s quiet enough in the off-hours to get serious reading done.

- **Location:**1715 2nd Ave, New York
- **Website:**https://www.midnightexpressdiner.com | 212-860-2320
- **Good for:**UES locals.

**Empanada Mama (Hell’s Kitchen)**

Open **24/7**. While it can get rowdy with the post-bar crowd on weekends, weeknights are manageable. The empanadas are portable, one-handed food perfect for typing with the other hand.

- **Location:**765 9th Ave, New York
- **Website:**https://www.empanadamama.com | +1 212-698-9008
- **Good for:**Tasty snacks while working.

**Veselka (East Village)**

The Ukrainian soul of the East Village. While their hours have fluctuated post-2020, they are currently open late (often until **12:00 AM** or later, check their site as they ramp back up to 24 hours). Pierogies are brain food.

- **Location:**144 2nd Ave, New York
- **Website:**https://www.veselka.com
- **Good for:**Comfort food.

**Cafe Reggio (Greenwich Village)**

Open until **2:00 AM or 3:00 AM**. This place is historic—home of the original cappuccino in the USA. It’s dark, moody, and filled with art. The tables are small, so it’s better for reading than a dual-monitor setup.

- **Location:**119 MacDougal St, New York
- **Website:**https://www.caffereggio.com | (212) 475-9557
- **Good for:**Feeling like a philosopher in the 1920s.

**The “Lobby Surfing” Technique (Free-ish & Fancy)**

Finding **free late night study spots in NYC** is tough, but hotel lobbies are the ultimate hack. You should buy a drink to be polite, but generally, these are large, comfortable spaces.

**Ace Hotel Lobby (NoMad)**

The OG of hotel lobbies. It’s dark, has long communal tables, and is open late. The lobby bar serves drinks and coffee. It fills up fast, but if you snag a spot, you can stay for hours.

- **Location:**20 W 29th St, New York
- **Website:**https://acehotel.com/new-york
- **Good for:**Networking while procrastinating.

**Ace Hotel Brooklyn (Boerum Hill)**

The Brooklyn cousin is just as cool but slightly more spacious. The lobby has a massive fireplace and plenty of seating. It’s a great spot to work until the late hours.

- **Location:**252 Schermerhorn St, Brooklyn
- **Website:**https://acehotel.com/brooklyn
- **Good for:**A cozy fireplace vibe.

**Public Hotel (Lower East Side)**

Take the neon escalators up to the lobby. There are plenty of sofas and tables. It’s a very “scene” spot, but plenty of people work there late into the evening.

- **Location:**215 Chrystie St, New York
- **Website:**https://www.publichotels.com | 212 735 6000
- **Good for:**Feeling fancy while studying.

**The Roxy Hotel (Tribeca)**

The Roxy has a beautiful, jazz-club style lobby that is open to the public. It’s comfortable and generally has a relaxed atmosphere on weeknights.

- **Location:**2 6th Ave, New York
- **Website:**https://www.roxyhotelnyc.com
- **Good for:**Jazz vibes.

**Outer Borough Gems**

**Martha’s Country Bakery (Williamsburg & Queens)**

The Williamsburg (Bedford Ave) and Austin St (Forest Hills) locations are open late, often until **12:00 AM** or **1:00 AM**. It is a bakery first, so expect the smell of warm chocolate cake to distract you.

- **Location:**Multiple Locations (e.g., 263 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn)
- **Website:**https://www.marthascountrybakery.com
- **Good for:**Dessert lovers.

**Opera Cafe Lounge (Sheepshead Bay)**

If you are deep in Brooklyn, this Turkish spot is open until **1:00 AM**. It’s huge, has a great outdoor section (heated), and the tea service is fantastic.

- **Location:**2255 Emmons Ave, Brooklyn
- **Website:**https://www.operacafelounge.com
- **Good for:**Late night hook outlines and tea.

Finding a place to focus in this city shouldn’t be a second job. Whether you need the silence of a bookstore or the chaos of a diner, one of these spots will have your back.

If you’ve finished your studying and are looking for a way to relax with a special someone (or just treat yourself), check out our guide on **15+ Cozy Indoor Date Ideas In NYC For Winter**.

title: Top Study Spots in NYC for Back-to-School Season - The Webster Apartments
author: Webster Blogger
text:
As the new school year approaches, finding the perfect study spot can make all the difference for students in NYC. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to focus in the busy city, a cozy café for group projects, or a library with endless resources, New York City has plenty of options to suit your needs. Here’s a guide to some of the best study spots in the city.

**The New York Public Library – Stephen A. Schwarzman Building**

Located at 476 5th Ave, the main branch of the New York Public Library is an iconic and historic study spot. The Rose Main Reading Room is renowned for its beautiful architecture and quiet atmosphere, making it an ideal place to focus on your studies.

**Highlights:**

- Free Wi-Fi and plenty of outlets.
- Quiet and spacious with ample seating.
- Access to vast resources and materials with library card

**Tips:**

- Arrive early to secure a good spot, especially during peak study times.
- Take breaks to explore the exhibitions and the beautiful library building.

**Brooklyn Roasting Company**

With 4 different locations offered around Brooklyn, this café offers a relaxed atmosphere with excellent coffee. The industrial-chic design and large windows create a bright and inviting space perfect for studying.

**Highlights:**

- Free Wi-Fi and comfortable seating.
- Great selection of coffee and snacks.
- Friendly atmosphere conducive to studying.

**Tips:**

- Grab a seat by the window for natural light and a great view.
- Try their famous cold brew to keep you energized.

**Bluestone Lane Collective Café**

Located at 55 Greenwich Ave, this Australian-inspired café offers a welcoming environment with great food and coffee. The light and airy interior make it a pleasant place to spend a few hours studying. It is currently undergoing renovations but should be back up and running in time for your first study session.

**Highlights:**

- Free Wi-Fi and a relaxed atmosphere.
- Delicious menu with healthy options.
- Friendly staff and a community vibe.

**Tips:**

- Try their avocado smash for a healthy and tasty study snack.
- Take advantage of the outdoor seating on nice days.

**WeWork**

With multiple locations throughout the city, WeWork offers flexible coworking spaces perfect for students and interns needing a dedicated study area. Membership provides access to comfortable seating, fast Wi-Fi, and a professional environment.

**Highlights:**

- Flexible membership options.
- Professional and quiet workspace.
- Networking opportunities with other professionals.

**Tips:**

- Explore different WeWork locations to find your favorite spot.
- Utilize the meeting rooms for group study sessions or projects.

**Housing Works Bookstore Café**

Located at 126 Crosby St, this bookstore café is a cozy and quiet spot ideal for studying. The charming interior and the smell of books create a perfect study ambiance. Plus, almost all of the profits go towards the many Housing Works services and programs dedicated to taking care of low-income New Yorkers.

**Highlights:**

- Free Wi-Fi and comfortable seating.
- Unique bookstore environment.
- Café offering coffee, tea, and snacks.

**Tips:**

- Find a seat in the back for a quieter study session.
- Browse the bookstore for a study break and discover new reads.

**The Bean**

Located at multiple locations across the city, The Bean is a popular choice among students for its cozy environment and excellent coffee. Each location offers a relaxed atmosphere, perfect for hitting the books.

**Highlights:**

- Free Wi-Fi and ample seating.
- Great coffee and tasty snacks.
- Friendly and laid-back vibe.

**Tips:**

- Visit the East Village location for a unique artsy atmosphere.
- Enjoy a vegan pastry while you study.

**Argo Tea Café**

With several locations across the city, Argo Tea Café is a popular choice for students looking for a quiet place to study. Known for its wide selection of teas and comfortable seating, Argo Tea provides a serene environment perfect for focused study sessions.

**Highlights:**

- Free Wi-Fi and plenty of seating.
- Variety of teas and healthy snacks.
- Calm and peaceful atmosphere.

**Tips:**

- Choose a seat by the window for natural light.
- Explore their seasonal tea offerings for a refreshing study companion.


Finding the right study spot can enhance your productivity and make your back-to-school transition smoother. Whether you prefer a quiet library, a cozy café, or a professional working space, NYC has a study spot that fits your needs. Explore these locations and find your perfect place to hit the books and achieve your academic goals. For students in their first year in the city, check out our guide on what to expect when you move to NYC.

title: 25 Best Things to Do on the Upper West Side: A Local's Guide
author: Aldrin; Ally Gibson
text:
#### 31 Best Things to Do in Central Park: My Favorite Spots as a Local

Are you looking for unique things to do in Central Park? I've listed all my favorite spots, so follow my lead and you’ll have a perfect visit to the park.

*This post may contain affiliate links. If you click on a link and make a purchase I may earn a commission at no additional cost to you.* * Learn more.*

The Upper West Side was the first neighborhood I lived in when I moved to New York at 18.

I was attending an acting conservatory in the neighborhood, so ended up living in student housing at The Stratford Arms on 70th and Broadway.

The building was famously the hotel that Holden Caulfield had stayed in during his city adventure in *Catcher in the Rye*. Naturally, I assumed it’d be a pretty nice place to live.

Turns out living in that building was going to be my first adventure.

About a day after my parents dropped me off, I learned that the school had bought this historic building from a group that had been using it as a halfway house.

Part of the terms of the purchase was that the halfway house residents got to basically live out their lives there. Needless to say, I have a ton of bizarre stories from my years living there.

I also have many memories of running around the neighborhood with the schoolmates, who would quickly become some of my best friends.

I grew so much in my two years living on the Upper West Side. It will always have a very special place in my heart.

Recently I booked a trip home to New York for this summer, and I can guarantee the UWS is a neighborhood where I’ll be spending a lot of time.

If you want to explore some of my favorite things about the area, follow my guide to the best things to do on the Upper West Side.

Have you ever seen the film *You’ve Got Mail*?

If you have, then (spoiler alert!) you’ll instantly recognize this as the park where Meg Ryan and Tom Hanks reunite at the end.

You’ll find Riverside Park is a quiet neighborhood park. It runs along the Hudson River from 72nd Street to 158th street.

**Local’s Tip:** If you visit in the summer, keep an eye out for the goats they keep around to maintain the grass. 

Seeing the New York City Ballet perform is a serious treat. Watching them dance is like stepping into a dream.

If you’ve never been to the ballet before, Lincoln Center is the place to give it a go.

You’ll be watching some of the best ballerinas in the country perform.

You must catch *The Nutcracker* if you’re in town during the holidays. It’s one of their most beloved shows and a true Christmas classic. 

Another one of my favorite Lincoln Center activities is catching a performance of the NY Philharmonic Orchestra.

Ever since catching my first show here a few years ago, I try to see a show here at least once a year.

This is another once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to see the best musicians play together under one roof.

Catching a show at the Beacon Theater has been on my bucket list for a while now.

This small theater has an intimate feel and outstanding acoustics giving it the ability to draw some pretty big names here like Bob Dylan and Jerry Seinfeld.

Keep an out on their schedule and book your tickets early!

A large majority of my favorite NYC memories take place in Central Park.

Scoring tickets to Shakespeare in the Park and having a sunset picnic in front of Belvedere Castle is at the top of my list for when I’m home later this summer.

If you haven’t been to the park before, also check out Bethesda Terrace, Strawberry Fields, and Tavern on the Green while you’re on the west side of the park.

Midsummer Night Swing is one of the hottest summer dance parties on the UWS. There’s always a theme to the evening, plus live music and dance lessons from the performers.

They held the evenings in Damrosch Park, which is right behind the ballet building.

This is a seriously unique city event that I’m ashamed to say is still on my bucket list. Friends who have gone have raved about what a marvelous time this event is.

But like everything in the city, you’ll want to book your tickets well ahead of time.

Every Sunday on 77th and Amsterdam you’ll find fantastic shopping at the Grand Bazaar.

When I was living in the neighborhood, I used to love grabbing an iced latte and strolling around this place.

You’ll see everything from antiques, furniture, to unique designers and artisanal food booths.

The market operates year-round, making it an easy choice any afternoon.

One of my all-time favorite things about the city is how many performing arts venues there are.

The UWS has one theater in particular that I really love catching shows at, The Vivian Beaumont.

It’s run by Lincoln Center and has a habit of reviving gorgeous classics like S*outh Pacific*, *My Fair Lady*, and *The King and I*. 

Plus it brings new hits to the city, like *War Horse*, *Oslo*, and *Ann*.

The shows here are popular with locals, so book early!

The UWS may not have as many jazz spots as the village, but it has some solid choices.

These are some of my favorite spots to listen to jazz on the Upper West Side:

Another thing that I’m looking forward to on my return home is spending some quality time chilling on rooftops.

The UWS has a ton of great options if you’re looking for a way to cool off during the summer. These are the rooftops that I can’t wait to hang out at again:

You’ll find the New York Historical Society along a gorgeous stretch of Central Park West.

It’s both a library and a museum and a unique little neighborhood spot.

Their special exhibits are always epic. I saw one they did on *Harry Potter* and another on *Madeline* that were both marvelous. 

The museum is fairly small, so I’d say only pay admission if there’s an exhibit that you’re dying to see.

Want to check out some epic dinosaur bones and rocks from space?

Then you’ll want to head down the street from the NYHS, to the American Museum of Natural History.

This is one museum you’ll want to plan on spending the entire morning or afternoon exploring.

Don’t forget to check out the giant blue whale and the Hayden Planetarium while you’re there. Those are some of my favorite parts of the museum.

*Plan ahead by booking one of these awesome tours of the museum!*

After living in the neighborhood for two years, I think I’ve been to every bakery and cafe around sampling their desserts.

Typically, when I find myself in the neighborhood, I always swing by one of two of these spots for a sweet treat:

Visiting the NYC Metropolitan Opera offers an unparalleled cultural experience, combining world-class performances with stunning architecture.

I used to go at least once a year while I was living in the city, and it was always a highlight.

It’s truly one of the most beautiful theaters I’ve been in.

The Met Opera, founded in 1883, has a long tradition of presenting innovative works and featuring famous performers.

The opera house itself is home to two magnificent murals by Marc Chagall, “The Triumph of Music” and “The Sources of Music,” which add a unique artistic flair to the venue.

They were installed in 1966 to celebrate the transformative power of music and enhance the grandeur of the Met Opera experience, and are a total must-see!

The UWS has some of my favorite restaurants in the city.

When I was in school I would treat myself to dinner out once or twice a week.

I’ve spent countless hours at some of these spots learning lines and catching up with friends.

I still love planning nights out over here so that I can hit up some of my favorite dining spots.

If you’re looking for a knock-out meal, make reservations at one of these UWS gems:

Swinging by the Shops at Columbus Circle is always a welcome treat.

They’ve got plenty of basic shops like J. Crew and Lululemon to classics like Stuart Weitzman and Ted Baker.

It’s also a substantial area to grab a quick 

Tartinery has a great cafe if you’re in search of a proper sit-down lunch.

**Local’s Tip:** Stop by the Whole Foods on the bottom level to pick up all of your picnic needs!

Another one of my favorite city activities is going out for an afternoon tea with friends at Alice’s Tea Cup on the UWS.

Alice’s has been my neighborhood go-to anytime I’m craving tea and scones. They also make delicious crepes!

This spot is *Alice in Wonderland* themed and absolutely adorable. They even have little fairy wings for kids to wear as they brunch.

It gets quite hectic on the weekends, so I typically get a tea and a scone or two to go with some extra clotted cream.

Then take my goodies to the park to enjoy on a bench while I read.

If you’re wondering what is on display at a folk art museum, let me fill you in.

At the American Folk Art Museum, you’ll see things like quilts, drawings, and sculptures.

I love checking out their gift shop. They always have unique gifts for my friends who love crafts.

The museum is fairly small and free to enter, so it’s an easy decision to visit.

Did you know the Upper West Side has one of the biggest mausoleums in North America?

General Grant’s Tomb is a seriously impressive historical stop while you’re uptown.

If you really want to explore and learn a bit of the history, set up a free tour of the mausoleum.

The Upper West Side has a very strong history with bagels and smear.

If you’re looking for an authentic NY bagel, this is the neighborhood to hit up.

Both Zabar’s and Barney Greengrass serve up some of the best bagels around.

Grabbing a bite at either place will be a brilliant decision!

This neighborhood has some of the best architecture in the city.

If you love wandering around staring at old buildings, these are the spots you’ll want to check out:

Nicholas Roerich is a Russian-born artist whose paintings focus on the great outdoors, specifically the Himalayas.

His art has a bit of a spiritual vibe to it and is overall relaxing to wander around looking at. Plus, you’ll also spot artifacts from all of his travels.

The entire experience feels really intimate and the staff are all super helpful.

You’ll find this small museum inside a brownstone at 319 West 107th Street.

It’s free to visit the Nicholas Roerich Museum, though they encourage donations.

Since I went to school in this neighborhood, I think it’s safe to say I’ve hit up a lot of the bars in this neighborhood.

These are some of my go-to Upper West Side bars:

Even when I was living on the Upper East Side, I would always plan on catching films on the UWS because they have some of the best movie theaters in uptown Manhattan.

I would take great joy in grabbing a coffee and strolling across Central Park to catch the latest indie film or big budget hit at one of these theaters:

After writing this, one thing is certain—my return to NYC cannot come soon enough!

I’m already having dreams of NYC bagels, park picnics, and of course *Shakespeare in the Park*. 

Let me know in the comments below what you’re most looking forward to checking out the next time you’re on the Upper West Side.

title: Perk Up! The Buzz on Upper West Side Coffee Spots
author: Tracy Zwick
text:
**By Tracy Zwick**

We’re deep into PSL (pumpkin spice latte) season, so it’s a perfect time to talk about coffee and where Upper West Siders get it. This cultural phenomenon was started by Starbucks over 20 years ago, and though the Upper West Side recently lost several Starbucks locations, the result of a corporate restructuring plan, plenty of coffee purveyors remain.

We’ve got chains as well as neighborhood havens where you can fuel up and hunker down with a laptop or a book, or join a friend for a quiet chat. Here’s an overview of where you can get your joe on the UWS, and maybe get a little work done, too.

We start at the southern end of the neighborhood and work our way north on this list. It’s not comprehensive (the neighborhood has an abundance of coffee spots!), and Starbucks is so well known and so ubiquitous that we haven’t included its dozen or so UWS outlets; they’re everywhere. But please add your favorite spots and feedback in the comments.

*Capital One Cafe:** 1843 Broadway (at West 60th Street) *

If you take your coffee with banking services, Capital One Cafe’s a great option and it’s just steps from the Columbus Circle subway station. Discounts on food and beverages apply for the bank customers, and the space was designed with co-working in mind, so bring your laptop. They’ve got free WiFi and plenty of outlets for plugging in your electronics.

*Cafe Aroma***:** 1873 Broadway (between West 61st and 62nd streets) 

A family-owned business with three other locations in the city, Cafe Aroma serves hot and cold coffee and other drinks, pastries, bowls, and sandwiches. Located near the Fordham University campus in the West 60s, they offer 15% off for students with ID.

*Le Pain Quotidien***:** Sheep’s Meadow in Central Park near West 69th Street

For coffee in a bucolic setting – or at least as countrified as you’ll find in Manhattan – there’s Le Pain Quotidien, the fast-casual cafe chain serving breakfast, sandwiches, soups, baked goods, and drinks, situated near the middle of Central Park. There are plenty of tables, many of which are outdoor, or you can place a to-go order and find a seat on a park bench, or bring a blanket.

*Frame***:** 305 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 74th and 75th streets) and 2459 Broadway (at West 91st Street)

With a location next to Hummus Place on Amsterdam Avenue and another one steps from Symphony Space, Frame offers coffee and Thai food with a focus on specialty lattes and croffles (a waffle-croissant mashup). Also on the menu are sandwiches and savory items, including a smoked salmon avocado sandwich croffle.

*Sote Coffee Roasters***:** 329 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 75th and 76th streets)

Opened in 2024, this cozy spot has been adopted by Upper West Side Run Club as their hub for post-run coffee, chats, and hangouts. Owned by husband-and-wife Besa Bislimi and Arber Beqiri, both natives of Albania, Sote is focused on fresh, locally-roasted coffee, and community.

*Da Capo***:** 322 Columbus Avenue (between West 75th and 76th streets) 

Da Capo fashions itself “an artisanal espresso bar by day, and cocktail bar and restaurant by night” with a “downtown vibe, uptown.” Open for coffee and pastries starting at 9 a.m., De Capo starts offering a full lunch menu around noon, and brunch on weekends.

*Züri Coffee***:** 2218 Broadway (at West 79th Street)

Right at the West 79th Street subway entrance, Züri is an intimate spot with just a few tables but plenty of local fans, and, of course, hot and cold drinks. Yelp reviewers note the “cute, very friendly small space” and the “smooth and refreshing” cold brew.

*Maman***:** 429 Amsterdam Avenue (at West 81st Street)

There are dozens of Mamans, from New York to DC to Florida. They’re recognizable by their signature vintage decor, floral accents, baked goods, and coffee. Salads, soups, sweets, and seasonal drinks (pumpkin pie matcha latte, vanilla honeybutter latte, and spiced caramel apple cider, to name a few) fill out the menu. There are plenty of tables if you’re bringing your laptop, but last time I checked, no WiFi.

*Casasalvo***:** 473 Amsterdam Avenue (at West 83rd Street)

This new-ish espresso bar with two other NYC locations offers the classics – espresso and cappuccino – with optional flavors like pistachio, hazelnut, and truffle. Dokito coffee, from Rome, makes Casasalvo’s private-label blend. Italian dolci, like cornetti (Italian croissants) and cannoli, have become local favorites.

*Fellini***:** 523 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 85th and 86th streets)

With five NYC locations, Fellini promises “la dolce vita” in an Italia-cized setting with ample cafe tables and seating. A “refined” coffee and wine bar, the menu includes coffee, tea, and juices along with sandwiches, pizzas, and dolci.

*La Farine***:** 2394 Broadway (between West 87th and 88th streets) 

Calling itself a “boutique bakery and wine bar,” La Farine offers more seating than many coffee joints, with outdoor and indoor tables along with an upstairs lounge. Its menu features breads, cakes, cookies, sandwiches, quiche, and soups, along, of course, with hot and cold coffee drinks and teas.

*Green Lane Coffee***:** 204 West 96th Street (between Broadway and Amsterdam avenues)

Founded in 2020 in Brooklyn, Green Lane came to the UWS in 2024. Located right next to the eastbound M96 bus stop, it sells coffee classics (espresso, drip coffee, latte) as well as special drinks like Cold Brew & Yuzu, Strawberry Foam Matcha, and a drink called “Cinnamon Bun on Ice.”

*Silver Moon Bakery***:** 2664 Broadway (between West 101st and 102nd streets)

A beloved neighborhood institution for 25 years, Silver Moon’s longtime owner and baker Judith Norell recently partnered with Buttercup Bake Shop and moved just a few blocks south of the bakery’s original location at West 105th Street and Broadway. Coffees, tea, pastries, sandwiches, soups and breads galore comprise this local jewel’s menu. Outdoor tables only.

**Picky Barista****:** 2680 Broadway (at West 102nd Street); 667 Columbus Avenue (at West 92nd Street); and 245 West 72nd Street (between West End Avenue and Broadway )

Picky Barista, a family-owned cafe and espresso bar, has three UWS locations and one on the UES. The aesthetic is 1920’s-era, and the coffee is by Stumptown. Seating is available and the menu is Balkan-influenced, reflecting the owner, Dragan Bulic’s background. Breakfast dishes are served until 4 p.m.

*City Coffee & Bar***:** 914 Columbus Avenue (at West 105th Street)

“We are the vibe!” is how City Coffee & Bar describes itself on Instagram. This coffee shop by day and nightlife spot after dark offers fresh coffee, a breakfast menu and cafe atmosphere with tables where you can settle in.

*Typhoon Cafe***:** 947 Columbus Ave. (between West 106th and 107th streets)

Typhoon opened about five months ago, just two blocks from Central Park, selling prepared hot and cold Thai coffee drinks along with bags of beans to-go. They’ve also got Thai and Western sweets to pair with your Black Orange (espresso with orange juice), Okinawa (matcha with coconut water), or Typhoon Special (red lime soda with cotton candy).

*Hungarian Pastry Shop***:** 1030 Amsterdam Avenue (at West 111th Street)

This iconic Morningside Heights cafe across the street from the Cathedral of St. John the Divine has been serving coffee and sweets since 1961. Famous for its carrot cake, strudel and Hungarian delicacies, the space has an intellectual, Viennese konditorei vibe. There’s no WiFi, but if you bring a book (or your own hotspot) you won’t be bothered for hours. Plenty of tables are available, and your cup of coffee is bottomless.

*Qahwah House***:**  2869 Broadway (between West 111th and 112th streets)

With two large floors full of tables for quiet working, reading, or conversation, this is a relatively new UWS coffee-scene standout. The upper level features floor-to-ceiling windows making it both spacious and sunlit. Coffees, teas, and Yemeni sweets & snacks make up the menu that draws Columbia students as well as remote workers and neighbors.

*Oren’s Coffee***:** 2882 Broadway (between West 112th and113th streets) 

This longtime independent Columbia-area coffee purveyor is instantly recognizable by its red-and-white striped awning. It doesn’t have much seating, but that doesn’t seem to bother the many Oren’s regulars. A limited assortment of baked goods, including croissants, cookies and cinnamon rolls, are also available.

*Blue Bottle Coffee***:** 2901 Broadway (at West 113th Street) and 279 Amsterdam Avenue (at West 73rd Street)

With an uptown location as a retail tenant of Columbia University, Blue Bottle prides itself on its beans and roasting. With tables for working or chatting, and WiFi, it’s suitable for a work-and-sip experience, if you can find a spot to sit. Pastries and viennoiserie from Bouchon Bakery complement the drinks menu.

*Hex & Co.***:** 2911 Broadway (at West 114th Street)

Best known as a boardgame haven, Hex & Co. is also a coffee shop! During the day, when most if not all the tables are free from gamers, you can have an uninterrupted cuppa and conversation. Breakfast, “quick bites,” and of course, drinks are available – including La Colombe coffee, cider, hot chocolate, smoothies, and sodas.

*Sipsteria***:** 1264 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 122nd and 123rd streets), and 774 Amsterdam Avenue (at West 98th Street) 

A coffee shop by day and wine bar by night, Sipsteria is locally owned, and has engaged with the community, inviting run clubs, for example, to meet there. Jazz nights have included student musicians from Manhattan School of Music, and the menu of morning pastries has included cinnamon buns, pistachio croissants, and a gluten-free blueberry financier.
