title: 15 Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC (Laptop-Friendly)
author: Theworkingline; The Working Line
text:
If you’re ever looking for the best cafes to work in Chelsea NYC, you will find here some really amazing laptop-friendly coffee shops handpicked for you.

So far, I have written here plenty of guides about the best cafes to work in Manhattan, the East Village, and anywhere from Lower Manhattan to the Upper East Side.

And since Chelsea is such a cute part of New York City, one where digital nomads and students meet to work day in, day out, I thought it would be good to tell you about some good study coffee shops.

That way, you’ll know exactly where you can be the most productive!

## 15 Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC (Laptop-Friendly)

Chelsea offers plenty of amazing things to do from walking the High Line, one of the most interesting and beautiful parks in New York City, to its beautiful market and the Whitney Museum.

But we are not here to learn about the best things to do in New York City today, are we?

So here, here are, without further ado, the best cafes to work in Chelsea NYC.

And if you were wondering how I chose these specific laptop friendly cafes, I make it a point to select places in which you will find free Wi-Fi and power outlets as often as possible.

But as always, I would recommend you come early in the morning, as New York City is one of the most bustling cities in the world, and you might have to fight to snatch the best seats.

### Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC: Bean & Bean

I have talked about Bean & Bean in the past, since it is indeed one of the best cafes to work in Manhattan.

This beautiful rustic-feeling place is open from 7 am to 7 pm almost every day, and only closes an hour earlier on Saturdays and Sundays.

Located on 8th Avenue, Bean & Bean offers plenty of seating space, and you also have a lot of power outlets available to charge your devices.

Just a really rustic/industrial laptop friendly cafe, and one of the top spots in Chelsea if you’re looking for some inspiration and/or the best places to write in New York City.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Brooklyn NYC

### Best Laptop Friendly Cafe in Chelsea: Intelligentsia

Then you have Intelligentsia, located in the High Line hotel and right in the heart of Chelsea.

This one closes much earlier than Bean & Bean, since it opens from 7 am to 3 pm every day of the week.

If you want to have the best seats to work on your laptop, you will have to come *as early as possible*.

Indeed, Intelligentsia tends to fill up quickly with people who come to study, and are looking for the best cafes to work in Chelsea – just like us.

You have a few power outlets in there, free WiFi, as well as comfortable sitting space… and the fact that Intelligentsia is actually a coffee bar makes it an even more inspiring place to work.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Astoria & Queens

### Best Coffee Shops to Work in Chelsea NYC: Coffee Project

Coffee Project has a few locations around New York City and the one on 7th Avenue, super close to the Ruben Museum of Art, is yet another one of the best cafes to work in Chelsea.

This is one of the biggest laptop friendly cafes in the area, and you will for sure see other freelancers and students working on their laptops there – lovers of minimalist decor, Coffee Project is for you!

There are a few power outlets in the coffee shop, free WiFi as well as delicious, delicious drinks, and a really inspiring atmosphere.

You won’t feel cramped up in the slightest there, for starters.

And since Coffee Project is open from 7 am to 7 pm most days of the week, the opening times in themselves make it an amazing place to work in Chelsea to be productive away from home.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Lower Manhattan

### Best Cafes to Study in Chelsea NYC: Variety Coffee Roasters

One of the best cafes to work on the Upper East side is Variety Coffee Roasters, which also has locations in other places in New York City – including one in Chelsea.

You have anything you might wish for when you’re working at Variety Coffee Roasters, from power plugs to free Wi-Fi, and *a lot *of seating space.

Plus, the opening times are *amazing*.

It is not very common to come across cafes open late to study in New York.

Well, Variety Coffee Roasters is open from 7 am to 9 pm every day of the week, which makes it one of the very best cafes to work in Chelsea, study, or just chill for a few hours.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in the East Village NYC

### Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC: Telegraphe Cafe

Telegraphe Cafe is probably one of the smallest working coffee shops in Chelsea NYC, but oh boy. The quality of the French fare served at Telegraphe is reason enough to wake up early in the morn and get on to work.

During the week, Telegraphe opens from 7.30 am to 6.30 pm, which gives you plenty of times to get in the zone and be productive.

And since the cafe is located right in the heart of Chelsea, a few minutes away from the Rubin Museum of art, why not plan a full day in the area?

You could start with some studying at Telegraphe Cafe and reward yourself with some tasteful art-watching!

Great atmosphere, really good coffee, and an outdoor space perfect to sip on your coffee while reading a good book? Definitely one of the best cafes to work in Chelsea.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Midtown NYC

### Best Coffee Shops to Work in Chelsea NYC: Kona Coffee Roasters

Kona Coffee Roasters on 7th Ave has a few branches which are some of the best cafes to work in NYC, but the one in Chelsea is probably one of my favorite study cafes in this whole guide.

Why?

Because Kona Coffee is known for their excellent coffee, along with simple breakfast and brunch bites made to perfection.

It’s open from 7 am to 7 pm most days of the week, and you’ll find a couple of power plugs here and there.

Needless to say, come as early as you can to get a seat near the power outlets – and be prepared to work in solidarity with other freelancers and students already grinding on their laptops!

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Oxford Street London

### Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC: Cafe Flor

Now this one could definitely have been included in my guide to the most instagrammable cafes in NYC, couldn’t it? Cafe Flor is that quirky, green and floral little coffee shop perfect for studying as the seats are utterly comfortable.

The 8th Ave Cafe Flor offers free WiFi along with plenty of Parisian cafe styled chairs and tables, which would almost make you think that you’re in Paris working on those pages.

Not many power outlets, so come with your devices charged, but honestly, when you see the beauty of this laptop friendly cafe, you won’t even mind.

Plus, Cafe Flor open from 8 am to 9 pm almost every day of the week – for those who work without looking at the clock, those opening times are a blast!

It’s just that inspiring, and offers really creamy drinks to top up your perfect work day.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Milan

### Best Study Coffee Shops in Chelsea NYC: Bluestone Lane

Bluestone Lane on Manhattan West is one of the cutest laptop friendly cafes in Chelsea, and probably one of the lesser-known.

That’s definitely a perfect cafe to read, but if you want to settle at Bluestone Lane with your laptop too, that’s definitely possible.

Beware, it closes pretty early – opening times: 7 am to 4 pm most days.

A huge cafe, not many power outlets but free WiFi, and amazing atmosphere – plus, the huge windows allow you to look out on life passing by outside.

Personally, I love coffee shops of any kind when I’m writing on The Working Line; it doesn’t really matter whether the light is dim or the windows are bright.

But somehow, when the space is airy, I always seem to lose myself in observing life outside – which can be really good for inspiration!

In any case, Bluestone Lane is indeed one of the best cafes to work in Chelsea, but if you’re also looking for some of the best breakfast in NYC, that’s probably a spot you’re going to want to have on your list.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Lisbon

### Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC: 787 Coffee Chelsea

787 Coffee on 15th St is one of the smallest working coffee shops in the city, but boy, isn’t that the cutest!

All you need to know about 787 Coffee is that power outlets and WiFi are available, but beyond that, the decor makes for a big part of its personality.

Neons, wood and painted bricks – the study cafe has everything I like, all in one place.

787 Coffee is open from 7 am to 6 pm, so you’ve got plenty of time to come in and order amazing coffee before sitting down and starting to type away furiously on your keyboard.

Probably one of the smallest, but one of the best places to work in Chelsea if you like trendy vibes.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Rome

### Best Coffee Shops to Work in Chelsea NYC: Paper Coffee

Paper Coffee is located inside the Made Hotel, and from the delicious coffee to the inviting communal tables, you’ve got plenty to be inspired by.

Another one of the best coffee shops to work in Chelsea, Paper Coffee plays on good opening times too; from 8 am to 6 pm every day of the week.

Up to you to choose a large table to share with some other freelancers, or decide if you really just want to be in your zone, all alone on one of the single tables.

Power outlets and free WiFi, great setting – is that one of the best cafes to work in NYC or what?

Read: The Most Instagrammable Cafes in Paris

### Best Coffee Shops to Work in Chelsea NYC: Old Country Coffee

Ah, that’s one is going to be perfect for those looking for the best cafes to read in NYC – with such a background, Old Country Coffee makes for an inspiring spot!

But since it also offers power outlets and free WiFi, laptop people rejoice; you’ve just found another one of the best coffee shops to work in Chelsea!

The opening times are really interesting too – Old Country Coffee on 34th opens at 6 am on weekdays, and closes at 7 pm from Monday to Wednesday, and at 9 pm every other day.

That gives you plenty of time to get in the zone, get some coffee for study motivation, take out your laptop, and start grinding.

Read: The Most Instagrammable Cafes in Rome

### Best Laptop Friendly Cafe NYC Chelsea: Seven Grams Caffe

I chose to include Seven Grams Caffe in case you never find any free space in the other working coffee shops in Chelsea, just because it offers a really nice atmosphere.

Seven Grams Caffe is pretty small, actually, but the quality of the coffee and their delicious pastries and cakes will make you come back.

And while you don’t have many power plugs in this Chelsea coffee shop at all, you do have free WiFi perfect to stay and work for a couple of hours.

I’d actually recommend visiting Seven Grams Caffe for those looking for the best cafes to read in NYC, as the atmosphere clearly is that inviting for readers and old school writers – pen and paper.

Good opening hours too, since Seven Grams Caffe welcomes us from 7 am to 6 pm almost every day of the week!

Read: The Most Instagrammable Cafes in Edinburgh

### Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC: King’s Street Coffee

King’s Street Coffee not only offers really good seating space, but also a view on the bright outside – which, I said it before, is always very inspiring for me when I’m writing.

At King’s Street Coffee, you’ll find one of the best cafes to study in Chelsea, since the number of seats is incredible for NYC, and you’ve also got amazingly fast WiFi.

On top of that, snacks and coffee will help you replenish that stomach of yours during the day – although I don’t know about you, but my only filling during the day is coffee after coffee when I’m writing.

King’s Street Coffee is open from 7 am to 5 pm on weekdays, with shorter opening times at weekends, and is closed on Sundays.

Come during the week, as early as you can, and you’ll have a chance of working in one of the best laptop friendly cafes in Chelsea!

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in London

### Best Cafes in Chelsea NYC to Study: Citizens of Chelsea

If you want to come work at Citizens of Chelsea, come after the rush of breakfast – you’ll thank me later.

This Aussie-style coffee shop is perfect to study, and it’s not missing a single thing from WiFi to power outlets.

The single tables are perfect for those who just want to work away on their laptops without being disturbed.

If you get a breakfast sandwich or a pastry during your productive time, best believe you’ll understand why Citizens of Chelsea is such a famous study coffee shop in Chelsea.

And in addition to that perfect indoor space, Citizens of Chelsea also has an outdoor space in which you can either relax or keep working while using the free WiFi.

Careful though, the coffee shop is open from 8 am to 4 pm during weekdays – come early to get a guaranteed seat!

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Barcelona

### Best Cafes to Work in Manhattan Chelsea: Gregorys Coffee

Very close to the refreshing Madison Square Garden, Gregory’s Cafe is the last one in this guide that makes for a perfect laptop friendly study space in Chelsea.

Gregory’s Coffee actually has a few branches around town, and I’ve already mentioned it several times on The Working Line because it’s just that good.

This one opens at 7 am and closes at 5 pm – you’re going to want to come early if you want to get those work hours in!

Is it the rustic background mixed with a modern feel?

Is it the free WiFi?

Is it the great atmosphere, so digital nomad-friendly you can *virtually* touch it? (pun intended)

In addition to free WiFi, Gregory’s Coffee also has a few power outlets scattered around the space – which finishes to make it one of the best cafes to work in Chelsea NYC pretty much at any time of the day.

Read: The Most Colorful Cities in the World

## 15 Best Cafes to Work in Chelsea NYC (Laptop-Friendly)

And there you have them, all the best cafes to work in Chelsea NYC, from your cute and quaint study spots to really big coffee shops!

There are oh-so-many-more amazing laptop friendly cafes in New York City, so make sure you check out my other guides to the Upper West Side, Brooklyn, Astoria and more – and find your perfect pick!

*Until next time!*

title: 16 Charming Coffee Shops in Chelsea (Local's Can't Help But Love!)
author: Antonina
text:
I’m convinced the most important part of exploring a new neighborhood is starting with that choice cup of coffee and with a neighborhood as lively and vibrant as Chelsea, competition is *steep*. When it comes to coffee in Chelsea, I’m incredibly picky. so trust me when I say these spots deliver. Everyone claims to be the best, but let’s be real – without taking out a personal loan, there’s no way any person can afford to try it all.

Lucky for you, I’ve lived in New York City for years and constantly find myself meandering my way back to Chelsea to “just try one more spot.” So, over the years, I’ve created a list of the best coffee shops in Chelsea to help anyone searching for a great cup of coffee.

<**Quick Summary.** Looking for coffee shops in Chelsea? Here are my top picks. Kobrick Coffee Co., La Colombe Coffee Roasters , Seven Grams Coffee, and more.

Hi there I’m Antonina! Love NYC as much as I do? **Join my weekly newsletter for fun snippets of daily life in the Big Apple (or follow me on instagram).**

## Best Coffee Shops in Chelsea

## Table of Contents. Chelsea Coffee Shops

### Table of Contents. Cafes in Chelsea NYC

Visiting New York City? If you haven’t decided where to stay (yet) check out my helpful guide on Where to Stay in New York City (The best neighborhoods for first timers +3 to avoid). Don’t have time? Here’s my favorite hotel in NYC, hands down.

### Kobrick Coffee Co.

- **Website.**Kobrick Coffee Co.
- **Address.**24 9th Ave, New York, NY 10014

Kobrick Coffee Company has stood the test of time and provided locals with some of the **best coffee in** **Chelsea for more than 100 years**. The 4 generations of Kobrick’s who have run the company have fine-tuned the roasting process, getting it down to a science. 

In order to keep optimal freshness, Kobrick Coffee Co. hand roasts their coffee in small batches. They serve fair trade, organic, and Rainforest Alliance-certified drinks so New Yorkers can rest assured knowing they’re sipping on a sustainable cup of Joe.

A full array of drink concoctions can be found on Kobrick Coffee shop’s menu. Expect to find classic drinks like cappuccinos and cold brews. However, if guests are feeling adventurous, there’s also the ability to order a coffee cocktail, judgment-free, of course.

### La Colombe Coffee Roasters

- **Website.**La Colombe Coffee Roasters
- **Location.**601 W 27th St, New York, NY 10001

With an array of coffees, teas, and treats, the Chelsea cafe takes it one step further and offers certain specialty drinks on-tap. The company has grown so much so, that you can find cans of cold brew and draft coffees at grocery stores throughout the country.

### Seven Grams Coffee

- **Website.**Seven Grams Coffee
- **Address.**275 7th Ave, New York, NY 10001

If the name of this Chelsea cafe looks familiar to you, it’s probably because you’ve seen it come up on *every* list of the best cookies in New York City. Popular for their chocolate chip cookie (which practically melt in your mouth), Seven Grams also happens to be one of the best coffee shops in Chelsea.

This Chelsea coffee shop is named Seven Grams because they believe it takes exactly 7 grams of premium coffee grounds to make. The perfect shot of espresso. The coffee is unfussy and does not need to be over complicated with different milks or flavorings. The premium espresso speaks for itself. It’s some of the smoothest coffee in Chelsea and the flavor really packs a punch.

### Blue Bottle Coffee

- **Website.**Blue Bottle Coffee
- **Address.**20 Hudson Yards #228, New York, NY 10018

Blue Bottle Coffee hails from San Francisco, one of those left coast cities well respected for its mastery of java. While the proud east coaster in me wants to ding t for that, I just can’t. They’ve definitely perfected one of the best coffee shops in Chelsea. Their Chelsea cafe is located in Hudson Yards, a massive mall full of high-end shops and restaurants.

Specializing in pour-overs, Blue Bottle Coffee has mastered all the drinks we’ve come to love. From foamy lattes and airy cappuccinos, to vibrant iced Americanos – everything is exceptional. The atmosphere is airy, minimalist, and clean. While thisn’t a great spot for studying, it’s still a great coffee shop in Chelsea to catch up with a friend.

### Variety Coffee Roasters

- **Website.**Variety Coffee Roasters
- **Address.**261 7th Ave, New York, NY 10001

If you’re looking for one of the best coffee shops in Chelsea that you can work from, Variety Coffee Roasters is the place to be. The cafe gets *flooded* with natural daylight and is a great spot to study or work remotely. The coffee shop has copious tables and chairs which typically makes finding a spot pretty easy.

You’ll find multiple outlets sprinkled throughout the cafe to charge your laptop and stay for hours. What really makes Variety Coffee Roasters one of the best coffee shops in Chelsea? *They have a bathroom! *The number of times I’ve found myself attempting to work at a cafe only to cut my time short because there’s no bathroom available is ridiculous. 

Also, any cold brew fans in the house? I’ve found that Variety Coffee Roasters serves some of the smoothest cold brew in NYC, without that unpleasant, bitter taste – highly recommend!

** Unpopular opinion. ** Unpopular opinion. most “specialty coffee” shops in NYC are more about aesthetics than actual good coffee.

### Fabrique Bakery

- **Website.**Fabrique Bakery
- **Address—**348 W 14th St, New York, NY 10014

At Fabrique Bakery, everything is made in-house and always served fresh. This Swedish bakery originally started in Stockholm and now has two other locations in London and New York City. Famous for their cardamom buns, when I tell you, run don’t walk. I mean it! Perfectly dense, flavorful, and unlike anything I’ve ever had.

For those who don’t know what a cardamom bun is, it’s honestly a bit complicated to explain. but I’ll try. Essentially, cardamom buns are best described as a cross-breed between a cinnamon roll and pull-apart bread.

Typically a soft, flakey interior with a crunchy exterior and stuffed with a sugary cardamom dusting. Regardless, New York City is lucky to have a location. I recommend sampling any (all) of Fabrique Bakery’s treats while savoring some of the best coffee in Chelsea.

### Café-Flor

- **Website.**Café-Flor
- **Location.**218 8th Ave, New York, NY 10011

Café-Flor is a spacious cafe perfect for getting work done during the day and gathering with friends to unwind with a glass of wine by night. This Chelsea cafe is part coffee shop and part retail shop selling flowers and home decor.

Walking into Café-Flor you’re immediately greeted with an intense aroma of coffee and flowers, so if you’re sensitive to smell this may not be the place for you. You’ll find bistro chairs and green leather booths that add to the charm making this one of the. Cutest coffee shops in Chelsea (as well as one of the cutest cafes in all NYC for that matter).

Cafe Flor is laptop-friendly and outlets are easy to access so expect to find New Yorkers busy at work with a great cup of coffee nearby.

### Daily Provisions

**Website.** Daily Provisions**Address.** 440 W 33rd St Suite 90, New York, NY 10001

Daily Provisions was opened by Danny Meyer, the mastermind behind Shake Shack, Gramercy Tavern, and so many other iconic NYC restaurants. Most folks trek to this cute Chelsea coffee shop for crullers and find themselves returning for everything else on the menu.

Ordering the crullers is non-negotiable, no doubt, but the true star of the show are the breakfast sandwhiches, some of the best in NYC. Don’t sleep on the BEC (bacon, egg, and cheese). The coffee is top-notch too, serving Joe’s coffee, the iced americanos are an easy favorite.

### 787 Coffee

**Website.** 787 Coffee**Address.** 256 W 15th St, New York, NY 10011

Now this Chelsea coffee shop isn’t unique to the neighborhood, but that doesn’t mean it doesn’t deserve a shout out. 787 Coffee is some of the best coffee in New York City, *period*. The coffee is consistently great and the baristas are always top-notch. I especially love the purpose-driven mission of this charming cafe, which is to provide a farm-to-cup coffee experience while supporting the local community.

The coffee is grown and processed on a farm in Puerto Rico by the owners of the cafe. The goal is to grow coffee. It’s a beautiful thing and the result is exceptional – some of the best coffee in Chelsea!

### Terremoto Coffee Room

**Website.** Terremoto Coffee Room**Address.** 328 W 15th St, New York, NY 10011

Anyone searching for a local, authentic, quality coffee shop in Chelsea needs to try Terremoto Coffee Room. Everything about this Chelsea coffee shop feels intentional and well-thought-out. It’s one of those places where you can tell right off the bat that customers come first.

The walls are lined with fun artwork and dark wallpaper giving all the cozy vibes. The cafe is tiny though, so. Occasionally, Terremoto Coffee Room has a live jazz band playing outside the shop while folks sip on their cappuccinos.

### Telegraphe Cafe

**Website.** Telegraphe Cafe**Address.** 107 W 18th St, New York, NY 10011

One of the best coffee shops in Chelsea to grab a bite to eat is Telegraphe Cafe. You can expect to find a. This Chelsea coffee shop is family-owned & operated and has been around since 2003.

This spacious spot is welcoming, inviting, and great when you’re hungry. I recommend the roasted pepper & onion breakfast sandwich on a croissant. Pair that with a strong cup of coffee and you’ll be unstoppable the rest of the day.

### Yanni’s Coffee

**Instagram.**Yanni’s Coffee**Address.** 96 7th Ave, New York, NY 10011

Not only is Yanni’s one of the most adorable coffee shops in Chelsea, but it’s also more affordable than most. Granted New York City prices are outrageous, but an Americano for less than $5 feels like a win.

Yanni’s is a small, clean cafe filled with natural light and has seating against the windows, making this a great spot for people-watching. Don’t forget to add a treat to your coffee order **because the pastries come from Balthazar’s.**

But wait, there’s more; not only do they sell some of the most delicious baked goods, Yanni’s goes the extra mile and makes cookies from scratch! Offering vegan options as well, it’s easy for anyone needing an energy boost to find something at this Chelsea coffee shop.

### St. Kilda Coffee

**Website.**St. Kilda Coffee**Address.** 213 8th Ave, New York, NY 10011

St. Kilda Coffee is an unassuming little nugget of a Chelsea coffee shop. At first glance, you may not even notice this even a cafe because the font they use has a trippy wavy design. If it wasn’t for the intense aroma, I probably would’ve walked right by it and been none the wiser.

This Australian coffee shop is modern and minimalistic with fun pops of green from the plants sprinkled throughout the cafe. Serving Sey Coffee (which is hands down some of the best in NYC), it’s easy to spend hours lounging at this Chelsea coffee shop. The coffee is bold, doing exactly what you want caffeine to do, and the staff is friendly.

# Top 10 Coffee Shops In Chelsea

A guide to the best coffee shops in Chelsea, NYC

There are 27 districts in New York, all with something different to offer locals and tourists alike. The Big Apple is constantly busy, which can make it feel overwhelming at times. Fortunately, there are plenty of cute coffee shops to sit back, escape the chaos and enjoy a fresh cup of coffee. Whether you’re looking for a quick coffee to go to or a comfy coffee shop in NYC to spend an afternoon, there is something for everyone. If you have time to spend exploring the artsy side of New York, in Chelsea, you will find a neighborhood strewn with art galleries and class, and to go with that you will find some of the best cafes in New York. Below, we will tell you what we think the 10 best coffee shops in NYC are.

## Seven Grams Caffe

Getting great coffee right alongside fabulous food is a difficult task, but Seven Grams Caffe has managed to nail them both. All of the sweet snacks on offer here, which includes mouth-watering brownies, are baked on-site. As well as this, they have the roast only finest coffee beans on-site, which means you’re in for a true NYC experience. You can grab a treat bag and a coffee to go, or you can spend an afternoon being productive in one of the best coffee shops to work in NYC.

When it comes to the coffee and snacks, Seven Grams is faultless. However, if you’re visiting New York on a budget, you will be best off visiting another Chelsea cafe on this list. That being said, we believe the price is justified.

## Bean & Bean

All you need to do is look at the name Bean & Bean and it’s enough to put a smile on your face. Fortunately, their quality coffee Chelsea will give you a smile as well. If a powerful shot of espresso is more your beat, Bean & Bean are the places to be. To go with your morning coffee, you should grab one of their delicious baked goods. When it comes to cafes in Chelsea NYC, this cafe has plenty of seating making it a fantastic choice for getting a spot of work done.

## Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar

You can find an Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar in many different locations, but that doesn't mean it doesn’t deserve a spot on this best of Chelsea list. Intelligentsia sources only the best roast from around the world and can give any specialty roaster a run for their money. Although you can find Intelligentsia Coffee in many different places, the Highline Coffeebar is worlds apart because of its incredible outdoor area full of stunning greenery for you to get lost in. If cozy coffee shops NYC are your style, this is the perfect destination to escape the concrete jungle.

## Cafe Grumpy Manhattan West

This entry is for all you people looking for a true home-from-home experience. Although this chain cafe closed the doors on Chelsea, the journey to Cafe Grumpy, arguably one of the best cute cafes in Manhattan, is well worth it. Located just 3 miles away from the art district, Cafe Grumpy Chelsea are still serving up some of the best coffee you’ve ever tasted. You will never get bored visiting this cafe because they are constantly shaking up the menu, and they have an assortment of tasty treats to compliment your brew.

Cafe Grumpy originally started in Brooklyn, but soon expanded throughout New York. Seeing as they’ve done it once, we hope that this Chelsea best chain will be reopening its doors in the art district in the near future.

## Variety Coffee Roasters

If you’re looking for a Chelsea coffee with plenty of breathing room to relax in, you can rely on Variety Coffee Roasters. Their seating area is enormous, which is a difficult feat to accomplish in this neighborhood. Beyond that, their shop is welcoming, and you can easily vanish for a couple of hours after fighting through the busy streets. These specialty coffee masters provide flawless drinks while keeping the prices reasonable, which is one of the reasons we keep going back. The accompanying snacks may not be award-winning, but there really is nothing to complain about with this quality Chelsea coffee house.

## Joe Coffee Company

Opened in 2007, the Joe Coffee Company Chelsea is one of the newest on this list. The location is unique because it’s tucked away inside a historic London Terrace. They take their coffee seriously, but their baristas will always find the time to have a chat with you, which is refreshing in a city so busy. No matter what time of day you head down, they will be able to seat you because there is generous seating on offer. If you enjoy specialty coffee, you will be glad to know that Joe Coffee Company pour up some of the best coffee Chelsea.

If you love a delicious cup of joe from Joe Coffee Company as much as we do, then you can support the business by heading to their online store. You can buy branded mugs so you can feel like you’re right there, even when you’re at home. If you need to kit out your kitchen with coffee-making equipment, you can find everything you need through their online store.

## Terremoto Coffee

If you’re looking for something traditional and cozy, Terremoto Coffee is one of the best cafes in Manhattan, and definitely among the best cafes in NYC. The baristas at Terremoto are all highly skilled in their craft, with their specialty being pour-over coffee. If you enjoy a dark-roasted coffee you may be disappointed by your visit because they lean towards a lighter roast. However, this doesn't make a difference to us because their coffee gets us going for a busy day in New York. Apart from a lack of dark-roast coffee, and the fact you may struggle to get a seat, there isn’t anything to fault Terremoto Coffee over.

## Day Drinks Chelsea Market

If you’re looking for something niche and quirky, then Day Drinks is easily one the coolest cafes in NYC. Their menu is relatively small, with their focus being on iced coffee and chilled nitro espresso. Alongside delicious cold coffee, they do flavorsome dry-hopped tea, which feels like an IPA. All of their coffee is kegged onsite, which reduces their carbon footprint and increases control. If Chelsea market coffee is what you’re looking for, you can’t go wrong with Day Drinks. If you don’t like what’s on the menu, the bartender will work with you to create the drink of your choice - everyone's a winner here.

## St Kilda Coffee

One of the best coffee shops near Chelsea market, St Kilda Coffee prides itself on delivering only the finest quality coffee worldwide. Coming over from Australia, this small roaster knows perfectly how to do morning coffee. If you haven’t had time for food in the morning, they even serve the best breakfast Chelsea NYC that caters to vegans as well. Just like the majority of other cute cafes in NYC, you will struggle to find a seat here because the building is so small, so make sure you leave plenty of time. If you’re a coffee nerd, you will be happy to know that St Kilda Coffee takes care to ensure that their total dissolved solids (TDS) rate is over 1.35% for every single cup.

## Blue Bottle Coffee

Blue Bottle Coffee is similar to its Intelligentsia competition because it isn’t a New York-only coffee shop; you can find their coffee in Tokyo, Boston, and Los Angeles. With coffee in all of these places, it proves that they’re doing something right, which is why they’ve made it onto this list of best coffee shops in Chelsea. You will find plenty of seating at Blue Bottle, and the coffee isn’t overpowering because they roast on the light side. This coffee shop is welcoming, has tasty java, and ample seating, which is why it’s one of the really good places to write in NYC.

If you take time to read their story, you will find that they are truly passionate about coffee, being created by a Californian musician edging on the side of lunacy. Although Blue Bottle has only been around since 2000, they’ve done well to cement itself as one of the greatest Chelsea coffee shops.

New York is a busy city where there is always something going on, even in the art neighborhood of Chelsea. Thankfully, the area is home to the best coffee spot in NYC. Whether you’re looking to get some work done, grab a coffee on the way to work, or have an entirely different coffee experience, there is something in Chelsea for everyone. You will find different types of people at all of these coffee shops, so it’s worth putting the time aside to explore them all. If you find a coffee shop you like, head to their website to see if they have a branch in other states of America, it’s important to support your local coffee shops.

# 10 Enchanting Coffee Shops in Chelsea NYC

Chelsea is one of the artistic neighborhoods in New York City. It is known for galleries, historic architecture, and a vibrant culinary scene. Among all these offers, coffee shops stand out as quaint abodes both for locals and visitors. If it is a cozy spot to sip your morning brew or trendy to catch up with friends over a cup, Chelsea has it. Here's a list of 10 magic coffee shops you can't skip.

## 1. Blue Bottle Coffee

The first one located at Hudson Yards, known for its minimal design and good pour-over coffee, is something not to miss in the world. The cozy, peaceful café lets you slowly relish each expertly made cup, but most patrons rave about New Orleans iced coffee-the ultimate rich but refreshing flavor mix.

## 2. Café Grumpy

Café Grumpy, a Brooklyn native, has taken its mark in Chelsea with its welcoming atmosphere and fine brews. The single-origin coffees they serve change seasonally, and the place is perfect for coffee lovers who would like to savor the taste of different beans. The outdoor seating area makes it a nice place to hang out.

## 3. 787 Coffee

This unique café sources its beans directly from Puerto Rico, making every sip at 787 Coffee a farm-to-cup experience that benefits local farmers. The commitment to sustainability and community makes 787 Coffee not merely somewhere to grab a drink but a very intentional decision for conscious consumers.

## 4. Seven Grams Caffe

A staple of the Chelsea coffee scene, Seven Grams Caffe is dedicated to making sure your espresso is at its finest within a comfortable space. Here, the passion really shines, because the baristas take so much pride in crafting each perfect cup. Pastries complement their perfectly brewed coffee very well and, therefore, a great stop for breakfast or a later afternoon pick-me-up.

## 5. Variety Coffee Roasters

Known for its exceptional quality and friendly atmosphere, Variety Coffee Roasters is a must-visit for any coffee lover. They focus on sourcing high-quality beans and roasting them to highlight their unique flavors. The café's inviting vibe makes it an excellent place to unwind or work on your laptop.

Yanni’s is a small but mighty coffee shop that prides itself on simplicity and quality. With a limited menu that includes expertly made espressos and delicious pastries, it's the perfect spot for those looking for a quick yet satisfying coffee experience.

## 7. Citizens of Chelsea

This café unites great coffee with a warm atmosphere and yummy food options. Citizens of Chelsea is famous for its friendly staff and comfortable seating, making it an excellent place to catch up with friends or enjoy some quiet time with a book.

## 8. Terremoto Coffee

A relatively new player in the Chelsea coffee scene, Terremoto Coffee prides itself on providing quality brews in a visually appealing setting. The attention to detail in preparation of the coffee and the design of the shop distinguish it from the rest of the cafés in the area.

## 9. Fabrique Bakery

While mainly famous for their Swedish pastry, Fabrique Bakery also houses some fantastic coffee to complement everything that they prepare. The decor inside is incredibly inviting and almost encourages you to spend more time here enjoying its culinary delights.

## 10. Stumptown Coffee Roasters

A pioneer in the specialty coffee movement, Stumptown has gained a favorite position among coffee enthusiasts. Their Chelsea location boasts a wide selection of coffees that are brewed to perfection and attention to detail.

title: Best Coffee Shops in Chelsea, NYC – Local Spots Not to Miss - A Brit and A Southerner
author: Chris Boothman
text:
New York City is home to a plethora of amazing attractions, iconic structures, delicious restaurants and awesome local coffee shops. In fact, the Big Apple pretty much has a coffee shop on every street corner, such is the demand for the best Cup of Joe across the city by locals and visitors alike. While it’s near impossible to put together a list of all coffee shops across Manhattan, each time we visit we want to take time to focus on one of the many neighborhoods across the city. One of our favorite neighborhoods is the Chelsea area, so what better place to start than by visiting the best coffee shops in Chelsea!

We have been fortunate to experience a small number of these coffee shops during our visits to New York City, and while we initially put together a collection of the **best coffee in New York City** (in an attempt to cover all of Manhattan), we quickly realized we needed to focus our attention on more specific locations given the abundance of coffee shops across the city.

## Best Coffee Shops in Chelsea

Whether you are inspired by the trendy, vibrant coffee shop atmosphere so you can relax with your favorite book, or perhaps you are looking to catch up on some work while indulging in your favorite espresso, there are plenty of options throughout the Chelsea neighborhood. Here are some of our favorites that we recommend checking out.

- **Coffee Project New York**
- **Yanni’s Coffee**
- **787 Coffee**
- **Kona Coffee and Company**
- **Think Coffee**
- **St. Kilda Coffee**
- **Telegraphe Cafe**
- **Terremoto Coffee Room**

Let’s take a look at some of these favorite spots in the Chelsea neighborhood and perhaps you will be inspired to visit some of these during your next visit to the Big Apple.

## Coffee Project New York

Coffee Project New York was founded in 2015 by Chi Sum Ngai and her partner Kaleena Teoh to share their passion for coffee with the city’s East Village neighborhood.

However, their entry into New York’s coffee shop industry didn’t stop with this location and they have since expanded into the Chelsea neighborhood (among others) and offer a welcoming atmosphere in their shop located on 7th Avenue.

A Passion Project of Coffee, Milk and Heart.

Coffee Project New York

It is certainly inspiring to hear that Ngai and Teoh’s mission as a coffee roaster is to improve the quality of life for every person in the supply chain, from producers to consumers. After visiting the location in the Chelsea neighborhood, we can 100% attest that the customer service, ambience throughout the coffee shop, and of course, the beverages available are all reflective of the high standards expected by the co-founders.

We visited during the fall season and sampled the “Not Pumpkin Spice Latte” and it was delicious, and definitely a great way to warm up during the colder temperatures. However, the selection available ranging from House Drip to stereotypical espresso options make this the perfect place to stop if you want to enjoy some of the best coffee in the neighborhood.

CHELSEA | MANHATTAN Coffee Project NY 155 7th Ave New York NY 10011Phone: (917) 388-3399

## Yanni’s Coffee

One of the best locally owned coffee shops in the heart of Chelsea is Yanni’s Coffee. Located along 7th Avenue, Yanni’s Coffee is proud to serve only the finest single origin coffee & tea to locals and visitors alike. When you step inside the small yet quaint coffee shop, you are greeted by the friendly baristas who are focused solely on delivering an excellent experience to everyone that walks through their doors.

The interior of the coffee shop has a very airy feel to it (I couldn’t decide whether it felt like a Japanese or European design, but when I found out that Yanni’s Coffee originated from a Greek inspired founder, Ioannis Blentzas, it definitely made perfect sense), with modern decor and ample plant life to provide the perfect atmosphere for guests awaiting their perfectly manicured espresso.

Whether you are tempted by one of Yanni’s signature drinks, or perhaps prefer to stick to a Flat White or Latte, you can be sure that you will be leaving with a well-crafted drink.

Don’t forget to sample one of the home-cooked cookies – the oatmeal white chocolate is an excellent choice, while the traditional chocolate chip cookie looked equally appetizing. The relaxed vibe of Yanni’s Coffee, combined with the homemade sweet treats and carefully concocted beverages create the perfect coffee shop experience and definitely is one of our favorites not only in Chelsea, but across anywhere in New York City!

YANNI'S COFFEE 96 7th Ave New York NY 10011Phone: (646) 833-7333

## 787 Coffee

If you are looking for a little international flavor in your espresso, look no further than the vibrant 787 Coffee Shop that has roots (or coffee beans) all the way from the mountains of Puerto Rico. Visitors to this trendy coffee shop can learn all about the history of the roasting process at 787 Coffee, starting with the planting in Puerto Rico to the meticulous handcrafted serving by the local baristas in the Chelsea neighborhood.

From the mountains of our coffee farm in Puerto Rico to YOUR door.

787 Coffee

I spent a few minutes talking to the local barista about his opinion on preparing the “perfect” handcrafted beverage, and he emphasized that while there are important steps a barista takes, the real cup of coffee is created through the whole process starting with those coffee beans planted in Puerto Rico. It’s only when you hear about such a detailed process that you realize there is so much more to know than what you can see in the local coffee shop.

787 Coffee epitomizes the “From Farm to Cup Coffee” experience and so, if you are looking to sample the freshest coffee in New York City, you certainly won’t find many more fresher than what is available at this coffee shop. When you think about local coffee shops, 787 Coffee definitely meets the definition of this as they completely bypass the middle-man (the distributor) and grow their own beans on their farm on the mountainous slopes of Maricao, Puerto Rico.

787 COFFEE 256 W 15th St New York NY 10011Phone: (773) 797-2118

## Kona Coffee and Company

Ready to sample stereotypical Hawaiian coffee in the Chelsea neighborhood? Head over to Kona Coffee and Company which is the only coffee shop that brings Hawaii’s premium Kona coffee to New York City.

Established in 2017 and located on the corner of West 21st Street and 7th Avenue, Kona Coffee and Company was founded by Hawaiian native, Tae Kim. Kim arrived in the Big Apple and missed not only the island of Oahu, but also the coffee that he had been brought up with all his life prior to moving to New York. Kona Coffee and Company was founded with the philosophy that a great cafe is not just a place to enjoy your favorite beverage, but also “a space where New Yorkers from all walks of life can connect and unwind from their busy lives with a cup of coffee.”

Similar to 787 Coffee where the local coffee shop experience is the focal point, Kona Coffee eliminates the middle man distributor and is proud to offer visitors the opportunity to sample fresh espresso beverages from the coffee beans cultivated on the slopes of Mauna Loa and Hualalai.

In terms of the interior of Kona Coffee and Company, visitors will enjoy a space that epitomizes a peaceful environment where everyone can relax and enjoy their drink in comfortable surroundings. The open space feel along with the relaxing vibes create the perfect ambience for guests to get away from the stereotypical hustle and bustle of 24/7 New York City life!

KONA COFFEE AND COMPANY 201 W 21st St New York NY 10011Phone: (917) 522-6120

## Think Coffee

It is refreshing to know that there are a plethora of local businesses out there that are not only interested in creating a beneficial service for their customers, but also that they are giving back to local communities and global projects in need. Think Coffee in the heart of the Chelsea neighborhood epitomizes this and their philosophy is “every time you enjoy a cup of think coffee, you know you’re making a difference.”

From menstrual activism in Ethiopia to clean water access in Nicaragua, among others, Think Coffee is proud to be part of these incredibly important projects to help others in need gain access to things we in the first world frequently take for granted.

With a number of local establishments scattered throughout New York City’s neighborhoods, Think Coffee has a real footprint in the Big Apple to help promote these critical global projects to locals and visitors alike. The coffee shop in Chelsea has a spacious area for customers to enjoy their favorite beverage and the perfect vibe to setup and catch up on work.

THINK COFFEE568 6th Avenue New York NY 10011

## St. Kilda Coffee

The eclectic nature of Chelsea’s coffee shop scene continues with the Australian inspired St. Kilda Coffee located on 8th Avenue. Focused on delivering exceptionally curated coffee from around the globe, St. Kilda Coffee brews everything with precision, ensuring that guests leave knowing that they have sampled a perfectly manicured beverage regardless of their choice.

We nerd out on coffee. And hope you enjoy it! …drink it black and drink it bright.

St. Kilda Coffee

With a typical coffee menu to choose from (along with tea and hot cocoa for the non-coffee drinkers), visitors will have ample options along with a decadent collection of fresh pastries that are the perfect accompaniment to your preferred drink. Each day, visitors can learn about the specific coffee that is available that day, including the roaster, region, farm and what notes of flavor they can expect from that particular bean.

While St. Kilda Coffee is one of the smaller coffee shops, and perhaps not your chosen spot if you want to relax for a while, this is definitely a great spot to visit to grab a coffee and pastry to go to kickstart your day exploring the rest of New York City!

ST. KILDA COFFEE213 8th Avenue New York NY 10011Phone: (646) 756-4660

## Telegraphe Cafe

A post highlighting a variety of coffee shops in a neighborhood wouldn’t be the same without including a French inspired location. Telegraphe Cafe has a very Parisienne feel to it and this family owned coffee shop in the heart of Chelsea is definitely a spot worth visiting if you are looking to enjoy a location that “values you as a friend”.

With French style croissants and other pastries, a variety of sandwiches and other light snacks, and of course, a wide coffee selection, there are plenty of options for every customer to enjoy something that satisfies their appetite. Whether you are inspired to sample a hot drink or perhaps prefer an iced alternative, there are ample options for everyone to choose from.

The vibe throughout Telegraphe Cafe definitely has a very French cafe appearance and style. Imagine sitting in a local establishment in a French arrondissement, and what you envision is likely similar to what you can experience inside this coffee shop in the Chelsea area.

TELGRAPHE CAFE107 West 18th Street New York NY 10011Phone: (212) 488-5810

## Terremoto Coffee Room

Are you ready to sample a Prince inspired “Purple Rain Latte” or perhaps David Bowie’s “Space Oddity Latte”? Where better spot in the Chelsea neighborhood to sample one of these than the wonderfully named Terremoto Coffee Room. Focused on delivering the best quality to visitors from across the city and around the globe, Terremoto Coffee Room has the unique selling point of being able to pull five different coffees however you want it prepared.

You may be wondering where the name Terremoto derives from? It is actually the Spanish word for “earthquake” and given that coffee stereotypically is known to “shake you and wake you up”, it’s a fitting name for this local coffee shop.

Terremoto frequently offers some of the most exotic coffees available on a seasonal basis, ranging from the second most expensive coffee derived from the grand Elida Estates in Panama to Gesha Village in Ethiopia.

While Terremoto offers these distinctive coffee blends, it’s also noticeable when you walk into this local shop that there is plenty of New York City throughout the interior. Owner, Richard Agudelo, emphasizes the importance of having local NYC available throughout the shop and the tables and bench are made from recycled wood from the dance floor at Roseland Ballroom.

The infamous celebrities that set foot through the doors at Terremoto may have inspired some of the most popular beverages, but the one that is the most enticing for those with a sweet tooth is surely Agudelo’s favorite, the Colombian Caramel Latte (also known as the Terremoto Latte).

TERREMOTO COFFEE ROOM107 West 18th Street New York NY 10011Phone: (212) 488-5810

## Summary

New York City is home to a diverse variety of coffee shops, and each neighborhood can likely lay claim to having a selection that offers unique opportunities for visitors who love sampling local establishments. However, we would certainly argue after visiting a number of the available options that the Chelsea area is unequivocally one of the best areas, especially if you are looking to sample a diverse array of coffees from across the globe.

Each of the coffee shops featured above are unique and offer something a little bit different to the others. However, one thing is consistent across all of these and definitely contributes to our opinion that the Chelsea neighborhood is one of the best, and that is the focus on providing a customer centric, friendly experience. Every coffee shop we visited, we immediately felt welcomed and part of the “family” which is something that local establishments frequently have that chain coffee shops do not.

We cannot wait to explore more of Chelsea’s coffee scene and are always welcoming of suggestions in the comments section below. The coffee shop is constantly changing throughout New York City and regardless of your preferred option, you can be sure that any of the above recommendations will give you an experience you can cherish!

The shop itself is pretty tiny, but it can get packed—and that’s how you know it’s a great spot! There are a few benches outside and limited seating inside, so I would recommend taking your drink to-go.

I’m not a coffee aficionado by any means, but their cappuccino ($4.75) was **well-balanced and had the right amount of foam**. 

Aside from coffee and tea, they also sell cookies. Their cookies are **GIANT**, reminding me of the ones at Levain Bakery. I didn’t get a chance to try them this time, but I’ll have to come back to grab a chocolate chip walnut cookie!

📍96 7th Ave, New York, New York 10011

### 2. Variety Coffee Roasters

Variety Coffee Roasters in Chelsea is one of 8 locations, with the original location in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The interior of the shop was very welcoming and gave off a vintage feel, with its checkered tiles and gold detailing.

I went on a Saturday morning and while there were a few people at the tables, it wasn’t too busy. This was one of the few times I wished I was a student again—just so I could study in this coffee shop.

I got a hot latte, which came out to $4.50. The latte was **delicious and rich**, which made sense since Variety has **locally-roasted coffee**. One thing to note is that it costs $0.50 to add ice, so be sure to have some extra $$$ in the summertime! 

📍261 7th Ave. New York, NY 10001

### 3. Coffee Project New York

I didn’t plan on visiting Coffee Project New York, but I just so happened to stumble upon this great place while searching for St Kilda Coffee (which I never ended up finding).

The seating area was spacious and had large windows facing the street that let in **a lot of natural light**. 

Their glass case of pastries was calling to me, so I opted for an orange cranberry muffin ($4.75) to go with their house drip ($3.75). The sweetness of the muffin **perfectly complemented the bitterness of the coffee**. 

They also sell food here for those who want something more than the light bites that are usually offered at cafes. Coffee Project New York would be a great spot for a lunch or coffee date!

📍155 7th Ave, New York, NY 10011

### 4. Telegraphe Café

Telegraphe Café has such a homey atmosphere, which makes sense because it’s family-owned and operated.

Their menu was quite extensive, ranging from breakfast to salads and sandwiches to coffee. I took a long time deciding what to get, but the person taking my order was patient and didn’t rush me. Shoutout to their **friendly staff**!

I ended up ordering the Moccachino ($4.57). It’s a double shot of espresso covered with hot chocolate milk. It was actually my first time having a mocha and I wasn’t disappointed.

It was** chocolatey and velvety**—everything I imagined it would be. I would compare it to **a hot chocolate with a coffee kick**, so if that sounds good to you, then the Moccachino at Telegraphe Café is the way to go! 

📍107 W 18th St New York, NY 10011

### 5. Fabrique Bakery

As I was walking into Fabrique Bakery, I ran into a lady and she told me 2 things: 1) that this was her favorite spot and 2) that I should try the cardamom bun.

They had a large selection of fresh baked goods, which all smelled **HEAVENLY**. I tried their iced latte ($5.75). The coffee was** bold with a slight floral note** and the milk added that smoothness to the drink. Definitely one of the better lattes I have tried! 

I didn’t take the lady’s suggestion to get the cardamom bun (which I’m already regretting), but now I’ll have an excuse to visit again! I already know it’s going to become one of my favorite coffee shops in the city.

📍348 W 14th St New York, NY 10014

### 6. Joe Coffee Company

Joe Coffee Company is a popular NYC coffee shop and this location sits in the heart of Chelsea. Despite this being a chain, there is excellent coffee being served here.

The shop could do with a larger seating area, but there is still a decent amount of space. It might be hard to grab a seat on a busier day, so be prepared. Even so, it’s a great place to stop by to grab a quick coffee or bite.

I tried the Nitro Cold Brew with hazelnut syrup ($4.82 + $0.92). The nitrogen made the cold brew **creamier and less acidic**, while the hazelnut syrup added a touch of **nuttiness and sweetness**. It was the perfect balance of flavors—exactly what I needed for a midday pick-me-up! 

📍405 W 23rd St New York, NY 10011

### 7. Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar

The Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar is a double decker bus that’s been converted to a coffee shop, making it such a cool place to visit*. *There’s both outdoor seating and indoor seating within the High Line Hotel.

I’ve tried Intelligentsia coffee back in Los Angeles, so I know that it will be a solid cup of coffee. The Avena Latte ($6.25), which is their “Black Cat latte made with oat milk, spiced with orange peel, ginger, vanilla, and cinnamon,” spoke to me—so I *had *to order that one. 

I’m a sucker for **warm, fall flavors** and this drink was absolutely **DELICIOUS**. It tasted like a more mature version of the PSL; not exactly the same flavor profile, but you get the idea. I would highly recommend trying the Avena Latte if you’re looking for a little spice. 

📍180 10th Ave at 20th St New York, NY 10011

### 8. Seven Grams Caffé

Seven Grams Caffé is just on the next street over from Variety Coffee Roasters; so if you’re looking to do a Chelsea coffee shop crawl, start on Seventh Avenue.

This is a specialty roaster whose name comes from the Italian standard that “the perfect espresso shot is made out of exactly seven grams of ground premium coffee”. In an ode to their namesake, I had to try their espresso ($3) by itself! The espresso shot was **strong and concentrated**, with (what I believed to be) **hints of caramel**.

This cafe might also look familiar if you’ve done a lot of research on New York City eats—that’s because Seven Grams Caffé is featured on many of the “Best Cookies in NYC” lists. Knowing that, I couldn’t leave without a chocolate chip cookie ($6) in hand. It was **gooey, crunchy-on-the-outside, but chewy-on-the-inside**—which is how I like my cookies to be. 

I might have come to try the coffee, but the cookie was the star of the show! ⭐

📍275 7th Ave, New York, NY 10001

### 9. Kona Coffee Roasters

I looooved this coffee shop. From the clean interior to the actual drinks, I loved everything about Kona Coffee Roasters.

The fast-paced lifestyle in the Big Apple can be overwhelming at times, but having the coffee here transported me back to my time in Hawaii amongst palm trees and sandy beaches.

I got an iced Hawaiian Latte ($5.70), which was infused with coconut and macadamia flavors. The latte was** creamy, nutty, and tropical**. It wasn’t overly sweet; that helped enhance the natural flavor of the **Kona coffee beans**. I miss it already… 

I already know what I’m going to try when I return to Kona Coffee Roasters (the Coconut Matcha).

📍348 W 14th St New York, NY 10014

### 10. Urbana Cafe and Gallery

Urbana Cafe and Gallery was** aesthetically pleasing** and had such a **great atmosphere**. There was plenty of seating with many people working on their laptops, which made me wish I had my favorite book with me so that I could sit for hours and read. 

The walls were lined with artwork that the cafe says was “thoughtfully curated”. I thought it was a great homage to the gallery culture present in Chelsea.

I tried their Pistachio Vanilla Latte ($7) that was made with pistachio milk and French vanilla syrup. This was the first time I had pistachio milk in a latte and I really enjoyed it! It tasted **creamier than other milk alternatives**, and the** touch of sweetness** from the syrup really rounded the drink out. 

📍348 W 14th St New York, NY 10014

## Best Coffee in Chelsea NYC

If you’re ever in the area, remember to visit these shops for the **best coffee in Chelsea NYC! **

- Yanni’s Coffee
- Variety Coffee Roasters
- Coffee Project New York
- Telegraphe Café
- Fabrique Bakery
- Joe Coffee Company
- Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar
- Seven Grams Caffé
- Kona Coffee Roasters
- Urbana Cafe and Gallery

Here’s to the **Best Coffee in Chelsea NYC**—cheers!

If you’re in Chelsea, why not head over and check out the Best Shopping in the West Village?

title: 10 Best Coffee Shops in Chelsea 2026: Great CafÃ©s to Try â Corner Coffee Store
author: Sean Brennan
text:
There are a lot of people in New York City, to put it mildly. A city of nearly 10 million people with countless more commuting daily needs an equally staggering number of restaurants, snack spots, and yes, coffee shops. There are so many great coffee hideouts in New York that we think the reason itâs the city that never sleeps is simply due to how much coffee New Yorkers drink. With numerous great shops to choose from in the Big Apple, we think it makes more sense to break down our favorites by neighborhood. In this article, we will share our 10 favorite places to grab a cup in Chelsea. If youâre a resident of the West Side neighborhood looking to branch out or just have a hankering for some java while visiting the art galleries and Chelsea Market, this guide is here to help you find the best coffee Chelsea has to offer.

## The 10 Best Coffee Shops in Chelsea:

## 1. CafÃ© Grumpy

Kicking things off, we have CafÃ© Grumpy. Originally a Brooklyn-based company, CafÃ© Grumpy has expanded with several locations around New York, including this one in Chelsea. The atmosphere is comfortable and homey in the best possible way, and there is plenty of seating. We especially liked the outdoor patio area. Itâs a great place to relax and get away from the hustle and bustle of the city. The coffee is the primary draw at CafÃ© Grumpy. They serve a rotating menu of single-origins and blends, and weâve yet to have one that wasnât excellent. The light bites and pastries are nothing to write home about, but they get the job done. If you want some of the best coffee anywhere in New York, head over to Chelsea and stop by CafÃ© Grumpy at 224 West 20th Street.

## 2. Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar

Intelligentsia is hardly exclusive to Chelsea, but it makes the list because of the coffeeâs quality combined with the incredible location. Letâs start with the coffee. If youâre familiar with Intelligentsia coffee, you know what to expect, but if youâre not, weâll break it down for you. Intelligentsia sources and roasts world-class specialty coffee that can go toe to toe with any specialty roaster. Their coffee is seriously good, and the only drawback is the price. There are many places you can buy Intelligentsia coffee, but few are as impressive as the Highline Coffeebar. The outdoor seating area is breathtakingly beautiful, with copious greenery creating a coffee oasis in the middle of the concrete jungle. From the local artwork to the string lights at night, Highline Coffeebar is the total cozy package. You can experience the coffee and sights for yourself at High Line Hotel 180 10th Ave at W 20th street.

## 3. Seven Grams Caffe

Many coffee shops have excellent coffee, some have delicious food, but only a select few have both. Seven Grams Caffe is a rare breed of coffee shop that makes top-notch coffee alongside mouthwatering treats. If you have a sweet toothâand no willpowerâwe donât recommend coming here because you wonât be able to resist the downright decadent chocolate chip cookies and other baked goods. Seven Grams Caffe roasts their own coffee and bakes their own cookies and brownies for a truly 100% New York experience. Itâs impressive how good they are at both, we could gush for hours over their espresso drinks and cookies, but we think you probably get the point. The only downside is the price. Seven Grams is an expensive coffee shop, even by New York standards, and the prices are the only thing keeping this out of our number one spot. Still, we recommend checking them out at 275 7th Ave. We promise it will be an unforgettable experience.

## 4. Terremoto Coffee

Terremoto Coffee is a small, traditionally decorated coffee shop on the West Side of Manhattan. Their coffee is excellent, high-quality specialty coffee that comes with an equally high price. However, if you like pour-over coffee, itâs worth the elevated cost because the baristas at Terremoto are skilled and make excellent pour-overs. They serve a variety of single-origins that change occasionally, so youâll just have to keep coming back to try the latest. The coffee is on the lighter side, which isnât a bad thing, but if you prefer bold, in-your-face dark roasts, you might find the coffee at Terremoto lacking. However, if you enjoy light, complex, nuanced espresso and coffee, Terremoto is the place for you. You can pay them a visit at 328 W 15th St.

## 5. Variety Coffee Roasters

Variety Coffee Roasters has something that is difficult to find elsewhere in Chelsea: space. The seating area is spacious with high ceilings that give the shop a welcoming vibe that feels like a breath of fresh air after riding crowded subways all day. You wonât have to worry about snagging a seat here, making it a great place to park for a few hours with some work and delicious coffee. Specialty roasters like Variety often charge exorbitant prices for their handcrafted masterpieces, but the prices here are surprisingly low and competitive. The best part is, despite the lower price, the coffee is out of this world. They have a modest selection of blends and single origins to choose from as well as a small selection of baked goods. Check them out at 261 7th Ave.

## 6. Bean & Bean Chelsea

Thereâs something about the name Bean & Bean that makes us smile. Luckily, the coffee at Bean & Bean also makes us smile. They make some of the best espresso weâve had anywhere in the city, and their baked goods and pastries are nothing to sneeze at either. The interior of Bean & Bean is bright and cheery, with plenty of seating and easily accessible outlets for charging your laptop or phone. Weâve never had a problem finding a seat here, and itâs a go-to place for getting work done, thanks to the wide availability of seats and charging stations. You can find them at 318 8th Ave.

## 7. Yanni's Coffee

Yanniâs Coffee is a small, no-nonsense coffee shop that serves up delicious coffee and espresso. The menu at Yanniâs is limited but donât let that fool you. Everything they serve is expertly crafted and delicious, from the Americano and cappuccino to the matcha tea and cookies. Although the premises and menu are both small, Yanniâs knows what theyâre about and sticks to doing those things well. It is quite small, so itâs probably best to expect to pick up your coffee to go, especially during busier times. If you want to check out a cozy Chelsea coffee spot, head over to 96 7th Ave to Yanniâs.

## 8. Blue Bottle Coffee

Like Intelligentsia at number two, Bluebottle isnât exactly a local New York cafÃ©. Nowadays, Bluebottle coffee is available not only in New York but also in Boston, Los Angeles, Tokyo, and about a dozen other locations worldwide. Just because they arenât a small, hometown cafÃ© doesnât mean they donât serve up some great coffee. If youâve been to any Bluebottle before you get the same experience at their Chelsea location: great coffee, decent seating area, and an all-around enjoyable experience. If you like light roasts, Bluebottle will be right up your alley because they tend to roast on the lighter side, making excellent coffee for espresso and pour-over. You can visit them in Chelsea at 450 W 15th St.

## 9. St Kilda Coffee

The penultimate shop on our list is St Kilda Coffee, a small Australian roaster featuring single-origin coffee. They specialize in filter coffee and espresso and have a seasonally rotating menu of beans to choose from. We really like St Kilda coffee but itâs also a great place to grab a quick breakfast before work. Their menu isnât extensive but doesnât have the typical pastries and some breakfast staples, including gluten-free and vegan choices. St Kilda Coffee is not a large shop so you might struggle to find seating even away from the usual busy hours. If you can snag a seat, youâll be able to enjoy your delicious Americano or pour-over in a cozy, unassuming atmosphere. Theyâre definitely worth your time, so swing by 213 8th Ave when you get the chance.

## 10. Joe Coffee Company

Last but not least, we have a great place to grab a cup of joe: Joe Coffee Company. Sorry, we couldnât resist. In all seriousness, Joe Coffee Company is a friendly, welcoming coffee shop that serves excellent specialty coffee. The staff and baristas are a pleasure to talk to and happy to chat when theyâre not busy. There is plenty of seating, so you should be able to hang out for a while whenever the fancy strikes. The aesthetics and decor stood out to us as being unique but understated, giving it the feeling of sipping a hot cup of joe in a close friendâs house. If you want to try their coffee and maybe grab a muffin to go with it, you can find them at 405 23rd St. **Looking for more coffee shops?**
