title: Study Spots Not Far from Your Pillow
author: Kally Compton
text:
**In-building study spaces:**

FOUND Study offers not only great rooms, a fitness center, and a communal kitchen but it has some great study spots for residents. You can get cozy on the couches in the study lounge or study up in one of the in-building classrooms. Ask your resident advisor where you can find these awesome study spaces.

**Cafés:**

Local cafés are a great place to crank out some work as you get energized with your favorite tea or coffee. Whether you’re craving a nice oat milk latte or a matcha drink, there are great cafés with indoor seating right around the corner from FOUND Study - Midtown East:

**Blank Slate Coffee + Kitchen Midtown**

**941 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10022**

Blank Slate is a personal favorite of mine. I would hang out there all the time in between classes at Maxwell Hall. This cozy study spot is only a five minute walk from FOUND Study. I recommend ordering a rose latte and setting up your study space at the communal table or one of the comfy booths. If you get hungry after work’s done, they have some great food too like avocado toast and salads!

**Blue Bottle Coffee**

**10 E 53rd St, New York, NY 10022**

Blue Bottle is another favorite with great coffee and seating. They have locations all over the city, and the one on East 52nd is only a seven minute walk from the new res hall. They’re only open until 6pm, but if you like to do your homework during the day you can grab an iced coffee and get your work done at their bar style table or one of the bistro tables!

**Libraries:**

Of course, the most spot that’s most conducive to studying … is a library, especially if you need some peace and quiet to write that essay! Luckily there are some great NY Public Library locations near the building, including the most famous location by Bryant Park.

**New York Public Library - Stephen A. Schwarzman Building,**

**476 5th Ave, New York, NY 10018**

This library has a variety of study spaces, including quiet rooms with lovely architecture and outdoor tables. It is about a 16 minute walk from FOUND Study, but it’s right around the corner from LIM’s 5th Ave building. This is one of my favorite places to study, so I highly recommend!

**58th Street Library**

**127 E 58th St, New York, NY 10022**

If you want a library that’s a little closer, no worries!—there’s one right up Lexington Ave about 8 minutes away. This location is a bit smaller than the Stephen A. Schwarzman library, but there are still plenty of tables and couches to hit the books!

**Adrian G. Marcuse Library (Maxwell Hall)**

**216 East 45th Street, New York, NY 10017**

Naturally, one of the greatest conveniences of FOUND Study – Midtown East is how close it is to LIM’s campus. The Adrian G. Marcuse Library in Maxwell Hall is its own study-sanctuary right in your “second home” in NYC. It has private rooms, computer labs, and quite corners to choose from, surrounded by an unmatched selection of arc.

title: The Best Cafes in Greenwich Village — The Glazer Team
author: Jay Glazer
text:
# The Best Cafes in Greenwich Village

Yes, we love New York City. We love every inch of this micro-universe hiding in plain sight. We love its eccentricity, boasting persona, and that evergreen vibe—Earth's capital of wanderers and wonders. And just like any other organism, it has a beating heart - you guessed it, it's Greenwich Village. The Bohemian Capital remains, until this day, one of the most significant landmarks in the U.S. The womb of American democracy, counterculture movement, artists' haven, urban microcosmos, and a place where a distant traveler consumed with diversity may finally rest and call it home. Not much has changed since the last century. Its gates are still wide open, and evolution, creativity, and human rights are still the name of the game. Let's grab a cup of New York's finest and chat. Enjoy our best cafes in Greenwich Village.

**Where to go**

The Village takes pride in accommodating the diverse needs of its residents and visitors. Every living soul (and that's about 8 billion of them) would and will find that one spot that ticks all the boxes. Disappointment is off the table (cafe pun).

**Caffe Reggio**

Located at 119 Macdougal Street, Caffe Reggio is known as the herald of America's incoming coffee ingenuity craze. Opened in 1927 by an Italian immigrant, Domenico Parisi, it was the first cafe ever to serve the glorious cappuccino - and the rest is history. Jack Kerouac and other prominent writers considered this Rennaisance Italy shrine their creativity portal; today's aspiring novelists and poets enjoy the same ritual - and that's precisely why Greenwich Village is on any NYC home buyer's checklist. It's a time machine (but don't tell anyone).

**Banter**

This beautiful Aussie spot is something to add to your Village rotation. With tons of natural light and delicious food, Banter has been marauding people's hearts since 2016: affordable, cozy, calm atmosphere and excellent music selection. With plenty of healthy options, breakfast and/or brunch will not leave you feeling disappointed. If you're visiting, don't miss out on Nutella french toast, Banter Bowl, and the Golden Folded Eggs (Avocado toast - goes without saying). And if you've decided to experience New York City in Autumn, fear not - there's outdoor seating with heaters. 169 Sullivan St; check it out.

**Outro NYC**

There are plenty of reasons to love and visit Outro cafe, the first being direct-trade beans (one of the few places in the city that brews Counter Culture beans). If you ask the locals about this cozy little gem, they'll probably tell you it's one of their favorite spots for getting some work done while indulging in earthly delights. Large tables are great for meetings and studying; the patio is just incredible. Outro nyc is famous for its variety of waffles and low-key atmosphere. The legend has it - taro coffee is the bomb. If you like what you're reading, head to 816 Broadway and witness greatness in person.

**O Cafe**

Speaking of the best cafes in Greenwich Village, have you heard of this hidden gem? Locals, refrain from raising your hands. This New York City nook is known for its Brazilian cheese bread, but that's just the icing on the cake. We all know New Yorkers aren't that keen on providing the best customer service, but when at O's, seamless customer experience is mandatory. If you're interested in some top-tier food and staff, you've opened the right door. Whatever your order - frittata, coconut rice veggie curry, or polenta cake - prepare to get amazed. 482 6th Ave, New York, NY

**NewsBar Cafe**

Whether you've popped by for a quick freelancer session or are just in the mood for a homemade breakfast accompanied by a relaxing chanson, NewsBar is your embracing host. They take pride in its cozy atmosphere and eagle-eye attention to detail when crafting a perfect meal. The cafe means business. Gluten-free and dairy-free options are also available for all of us, gentle snowflakes. Although it can get pretty busy, finding a seat will (almost) never be a problem. Goat cheese/beets sandwich and jalapeno cheddar biscuit sandwich are simply a must! 107 University Pl; stop by any time.

**Bus Stop Cafe**

Slipping this place is a sin for any Village visitor. This charming corner place (597 Hudson St) has been around forever. You will find its immaculate menu saliva-inducing and your wallet - exhaling with relief. We love their brunch special - free coffee and a cocktail with your entree. The staff keeps the place buzzing while old Fitzgerald and Sinatra tunes keep the atmosphere light and incredibly welcoming. Be sure to give Cesar's salad with anchovies a chance! Russian Panini and grilled chicken and goat cheese wrap are a supreme delight.

Places like this are exactly why people decide to move to a new city. If you're only visiting, be warned - you will have no other option but to make NYC your home after a trip like this (at least for a little bit).

**Stumptown Coffee Roasters**

30 W 8th St - look no further for that perfect cup you're quietly yearning for. Just a short walk from Washington Square Park, this old-timey cafe offers a superior coffee experience. Stumptown Coffee Roasters takes pride in inclusivity, and the rainbow galore is there to prove it. Despite being dangerously close to NYU, it's far from what you'd call a (student) beehive. Drop by and watch some of the finest NYC baristas serve top-notch beans extravaganza (Hairbender being an all-time favorite). Hot brew - cold brew; one cannot go wrong. Nitro cold brew is the stuff.

**Mille-Feuille Bakery**

Love goes through the stomach, right? We can't think of a better Greenwich Village introduction. Located at 552 LaGuardia Pl, right next to Washington Square Park, this utterly charming and delightful shop should most definitely be your must-stop on your way to the park. French-style picnic? Don't mind if I do. Whether you go for quiche Lorraine or almond croissants, you can't go wrong with Mille-Feuille's petite pastries. Or - you can sign up for their macaroon baking class and thank yourself later.

**The best cafes in Greenwich Village served**

The best advice we can give to a person touring the best cafes in Greenwich Village: don't have breakfast before leaving your hotel room/house.

title: 14 Gorgeous West Village Coffee Shops Locals Love
author: Antonina
text:
I have a coffee problem. Not the drinking-too-much kind (okay, maybe that too) but the I-need-to-try-every-new-shop kind. The West Village is my favorite neighborhood in New York City and it happens to be stacked with gorgeous coffee shops on practically every cobblestone block. Here are the West Village cafes I keep going back to, the ones where the coffee is as good as the atmosphere.

**You might enjoy reading.** 20 Great Things to Do in the West Village (our most popular guide).

## The Best Coffee in the West Village

## Table of Contents. Best Greenwich Village Coffee Shops

### West Village Cafe Guide (Table of Contents)

**Visiting New York City? **If you haven’t decided where to stay (*yet*) check out our helpful guide on Where to Stay in New York City (The best neighborhoods for first timers +3 to avoid). Don’t have time? Here’s my favorite hotel in NYC, hands down.

##### My Personal Food Guide for NYC

**Back by popular demand for 2024—** My personal list of the 15 BEST restaurants in New York City (where you’re guaranteed to have a memorable meal) is back for 2024. See more information here. 

### Bar Pisellino

Arguably the most authentic espresso bar you’ll find this side of the Atlantic, Bar Pisellino is a place you need to try for those in search of the cutest cafes in the West Village. A personal favorite, my husband I are frequent fliers at this cozy joint.

I love the espressos and take them at the counter before heading out to explore the neighborhood. Sometimes we swing by for apéro. Longtime readers know Bar Pisellino is a staple in my West Village arsenal, can’t recommend it enough!

### Travelers Poets & Friends

Run by an endearing Italian sporting a melodic accent, Travelers Poets & Friends was recommended to me by a fellow reader. Jack of all trades, Travelers Poets & Friends is a cafe, bakery, restaurant and Italian marketplace doling out fresh baked goods. Handmade pasta (you can watch it being made in the window), incredible focaccia and some of the best coffee in the West Village.

My husband I paid them a visit on Sunday and knew we were in good hands when we heard the maestro behind the espresso machine call out orders with a delicious Italian accent. We opted for our tried-and-true Americanos and tossed in a maritozzi (light Italian buns filled with fresh whipped cream) because it was too tempting to pass up.

The maritozzi reminded me of the ones we had in Rome last summer, I was so impressed. As for the americano? Exceeded expectations, it was excellent. After the visit, Travelers Poets & Friends was promptly added to our West Village arsenal, it’s a true neighborhood gem you don’t want to miss.

### Fellini Coffee

**Website.**Fellini Coffee**Address.** 174 7th Ave S, New York, NY 10014

The smallest coffee shop in the West Village, Fellini is a popular neighborhood haunt. Order your coffee at the walk. The coffee is excellent, but there’s one unusual drink worth calling out, the protein-ccino (cappuccino with 20 grams of protein). It flies under the radar and I kind of love that about it.

### Joe’s Coffee

Situated on a scenic corner between Waverly Place and Gay Street, Joe’s is the quintessential neighborhood coffee shop. You’ll find Joe’s all over the city (there’s 25 outposts now), but the West Village cafe is the original location.

The endearing vibes alone warrant a visit, but thankfully the coffee is top-notch. Joe’s serves some of the strongest drip coffee in the West Village, making it an easy morning habit for locals. There’s ample indoor and outdoor seating and the cafe stays open until 8pm, it’s the perfect place to retreat for some respite before dinner.

### Stumptown Coffee

Stumptown Coffee has locations all over the country, but not without reason. Hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Stumptown. They have a few cafes in NYC, but the Greenwich Village outpost is my favorite. Pro tip. come on a weekday to avoid the crowds. weekends here can get hectic. The menu isn’t enormous, but everything on it is done well. which I always prefer over a place that tries to do too much and nails nothing.

** Unpopular opinion. ** Hot take. you don’t need to spend $7 on a latte to get great coffee in West Village.

### Café Kitsuné

**Website.**Café Kitsuné**Address.** 550 Hudson St, New York, NY 10014

Café Kitsuné might be the most well-known cafe in the West Village, which is a bit strange when considering Kitsuné is a French clothing brand first and foremost. But hey, if you can make a mean matcha, who am I to ask for your resumé?

There’s plenty of seating at the cafe, but laptops are prohibited inside (allowed outside). If you’re looking to shake things up try the Black and White Latte, an exclusive NYC drink inspired by the iconic New York cookie. Speaking of cookies, don’t sleep on the incredible fox cookie.

### Caffe Reggio

**Website.**Caffe Reggio**Address.** 119 MacDougal St, New York, NY 10012

Cafe Reggio is the most iconic cafe in Greenwich Village. Opened in 1927, this bohemian establishment is credited with introducing the cappuccino to America.

Charming to the max, the interior is full of interesting paintings dating back to the Italian renaissance and a bench that belonged to the Medici family (a prominent Italian political family that produced four Popes).

Caffe Reggio is also a full-fledged restaurant with breakfast, lunch and dinner service. But at its core it’s famous for one thing.*cappuccino*, a must-order at this iconic West Village cafe. 

### The Elk

**Website.**The Elk**Address.** 128 Charles St, New York, NY 10014

The Elk is a cafe moonlighting as a general store. Or maybe it’s the other way around? It’s hard to tell, but one thing is certain. the coffee is worth a detour. Founded by a Vancouver BC Canada native, Claire Chan, the decor is inspired by her Pacific Northwest roots, inviting the outdoors in.

The cafe relies on Parlor Coffee (Brooklyn-based roasters) for expert espresso extractions and creative drinks. There’s also a few healthy bites on offer if you’re feeling peckish during your visit. As for the shop? You’ll find an interesting mishmash of home, wellness and lifestyle items to peruse.

### Rosecrans

**Website.**Rosecrans**Address.** 7 Greenwich Ave, New York, NY 10014

Part-cafe, part-plant shop, the abundance of plants earns Rosecrans a spot on our list of the most beautiful cafes in Greenwich Village. Most of the tables are taken during the morning hours, but that’s okay since you can drink your coffee. While admiring the plants and flowers available for purchase (my favorite pastime is gawking at the prices). There’s a charming old-school New York feel to this place that I absolutely love. it feels like stepping back in time.

### Do Not Feed the Alligators

**Website.** Do Not Feed the Alligators**Address.** 337 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10014

Sometimes I don’t feel cool enough for Do Not Feed the Alligators, but I test my luck anyways. Brewing single origin beans from small local roasters, this chic West Village coffee shop makes expert pour-overs and espresso-forward drinks.

Warm and inviting, the put together corner bookstore adds a touch of intrigue. Come evening, the lights dim, the. Laptops aren’t allowed, which makes it a great spot to catch up with a friend.

### Jack’s Coffee

**Website.** Jack’s Stir Brew Coffee**Address.** 138 W 10th St, New York

Jack’s Stir Brew Coffee dates back to 2003 when Jack Mazzola opened a small cafe in the hopes of serving his community. Relying on organic coffee, Jack’s Coffee grew to a handful of locations throughout the city (serving 50,000 people a week on average).

Jack’s was the first NYC coffee house to serve ethically sourced, shade-grown organic coffee exclusively. Jack had been working directly with farmers and purveyors way before it became the industry standard.

text:
Greenwich Village, with its tree-lined streets and historic charm, is one of New York City’s most iconic neighborhoods. It’s also one of the best places in the city to grab a cup of coffee. Whether you’re a local on the hunt for your new go-to spot, a student needing a study nook, or a tourist seeking a break between sights, this guide will help you find your perfect cup.

From cozy cafés with vintage vibes to modern spots serving meticulously sourced single-origin beans, the best coffee shops in Greenwich Village each offer something special.

**1. Joe Coffee Company – Waverly Place**

**Address:** 141 Waverly Pl, New York, NY 10014

Joe Coffee is a NYC staple, and the Waverly Place location feels like it was made for Greenwich Village. With a warm, rustic interior and a reputation for consistent quality, this shop is ideal for a quick espresso or a quiet morning of people-watching.

**Why locals love it:**

- **Rich espresso drinks**with perfectly textured milk
- Seating that suits laptop warriors and casual meetups
- Consistent quality from a locally trusted brand

**2. Third Rail Coffee – Sullivan Street**

**Address:** 240 Sullivan St, New York, NY 10012

Just a stone’s throw from NYU, Third Rail is a small but mighty café known for its smooth espresso and curated coffee menu. It’s not built for long work sessions—seating is limited—but it’s ideal for a quality grab-and-go experience or a quick chat with friends.

**Highlights:**

- Rotating coffee offerings from top-tier roasters
- Strong, flavorful espresso-based drinks
- An intimate, no-frills vibe

**3. Porto Rico Importing Co. – Bleecker Street**

**Address:** 201 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10012

Founded in 1907, Porto Rico is a Village institution. While it feels more like an old-school general store for coffee lovers than a sit-down café, it’s a must-visit for anyone serious about beans. Come here to stock up on freshly roasted blends, or grab a cup to go and take a walk through the neighborhood.

**What makes it unique:**

- A huge variety of coffee beans available by the pound
- A historic feel with shelves stacked floor-to-ceiling
- Some of the **most affordable and flavorful brews**around

**4. Stumptown Coffee Roasters – West 8th Street**

**Address:** 30 W 8th St, New York, NY 10011

The Portland-born Stumptown has a stronghold in the Village with its sleek, modern café near NYU. It’s a great place for those who appreciate third-wave coffee done right. Expect detailed pour-overs, expertly pulled espresso, and a space that feels both functional and cool.

**Perfect for:**

- Coffee nerds who love single-origin brews
- Remote workers needing strong Wi-Fi and outlets
- Fans of clean, minimalist interiors

**5. Caffé Reggio – MacDougal Street**

**Address:** 119 MacDougal St, New York, NY 10012

If you want history with your cappuccino, Caffé Reggio is the place. This legendary café claims to have brought the *first espresso machine* to America. With velvet seats, antique art, and an old-world European ambiance, it’s as much about the atmosphere as it is about the coffee.

**Why it stands out:**

- Rich Italian espresso and full pastry menu
- Ideal for reading or long conversations
- One of the most iconic coffee shops in NYC

**6. Birch Coffee – 7th Avenue South**

**Address:** 56 7th Ave, New York, NY 10011

Birch Coffee has carved out a name for itself in Manhattan for its balance of *craft and community*. The Greenwich Village location feels like the perfect mix of cozy and contemporary. It’s a smart pick if you want **a well-rounded menu and good vibes**.

**Top features:**

- Friendly baristas and welcoming atmosphere
- Brew options for every preference, from cold brew to pour-overs
- Space to sit down and work without feeling rushed

**7. Partners Coffee – Charles Street**

**Address:** 44 Charles St, New York, NY 10014

Formerly known as Toby’s Estate, Partners Coffee is a roaster-driven shop with a polished aesthetic. Their beans are roasted in Brooklyn and brewed with precision. The Charles Street location is stylish, relaxed, and perfect for those who appreciate attention to detail in every cup.

**Notable for:**

- House-roasted beans with clear tasting notes
- Gorgeous space with natural light and modern design
- Thoughtfully crafted seasonal drink menu

**Tips for Navigating Coffee Culture in the Village**

Greenwich Village isn’t just about *finding* a good cup of coffee—it’s about discovering what you enjoy most in a café experience. Whether you’re looking for an espresso bar that knows your name or a quiet place to finish a paper, here are a few things to keep in mind:

- **Seating is precious**: Many coffee shops in the Village are small, so try to avoid peak hours if you’re planning to stay a while.
- **Explore different neighborhoods within the Village**: West Village and NoHo each have their own flavor and unique cafés.
- **Don’t be afraid to ask baristas for recommendations**: The staff at these shops are passionate about their craft and often love chatting about their favorite beverages and brewing methods.

**Final Sips**

There’s no shortage of great coffee in Greenwich Village, but the best experience really comes down to your personal vibe. Want cozy and historic? Head to Caffé Reggio. Prefer something sleek and modern? Try Partners or Stumptown. Need a study spot? Joe Coffee and Birch have your back.Wherever you go, **the best coffee shops in Greenwich Village** aren’t just about the coffee—they’re about the community, the energy, and the small joys that come from finding your go-to cup.

title: The 21 best coffee shops in Greenwich Village New York City
author: Emma Lou
text:
# The 21 best coffee shops in Greenwich Village New York City

Emma Lou

• Updated: 2024-10-30Greenwich Village, a charming neighborhood in New York City, is home to a variety of coffee shops that cater to diverse tastes and preferences. These coffee shops in Greenwich Village offer a cozy atmosphere, unique blends, and delectable pastries, making them popular spots for locals and tourists alike. Whether you're looking for a quiet place to work or a lively space to socialize, you're sure to find a coffee shop in Greenwich Village that suits your needs.

Table of Contents

- 1. Third Rail Coffee
- 2. McNulty's Tea & Coffee Co
- 3. THE ELK
- 4. Amano Cafe
- 5. The Coppola Cafe
- 6. Cafe Panino Mucho Giusto
- 7. Caffe Reggio
- 8. Kobrick Coffee Co.
- 9. St Jardim
- 10. Rosecrans Florist & Cafe
- 11. The Uncommons
- 12. Café Kitsuné West Village
- 13. ad hoc : cafe
- 14. Blackstone Coffee Roaster
- 15. Merriweather Coffee + Kitchen
- 16. Porto Rico Importing Co.
- 17. Bar Pisellino
- 18. Buvette Gastrotheque
- 19. Café at Pop Up Grocer
- 20. Madman Espresso & Bakery
- 21. Judy's Cafe

## 1.Third Rail Coffee

Rotating selection of single-origin coffees, roasted in-house

During my visit, I ordered a latte and was impressed with the baristas' expertise. The coffee served was of high quality, and the latte art was a nice touch, demonstrating the baristas' skills and attention to detail.

## 2.McNulty's Tea & Coffee Co

Hand-roasted coffee in-house, Extensive tea selection

As a resident of California, I always make a point to stop by this store during my trips to NYC. I highly recommend their peachy green tea, which is truly extraordinary. The store's staff is also noteworthy, known for their friendliness and exceptional service.

## 3.THE ELK

Stylish interior design, offers free Wi-Fi, accommodates large groups

One reviewer had a positive experience with the service, mentioning that the barista was attentive and friendly, while another reviewer noted that the barista seemed overwhelmed and not very friendly. The establishment offers drinks including coffee, matcha, and cappuccino. Despite the range of options, some customers were not impressed with the quality of the drinks and thought they were overpriced.

## 4.Amano Cafe

Hand-pour coffee methods, Japanese-style tea service

However, other reviews report mixed experiences with the service, citing inconsistent interactions with employees who may appear indifferent or unhelpful. While some customers rave about the delicious coffee, others find it underwhelming and unremarkable. Overall, the quality of service and coffee can vary greatly depending on the individual experience.

more: The 32 best restaurants in Greenwich Village New York City

## 5.The Coppola Cafe

Independent coffee shop, supports local roasters

In summary, the Coppola Cafe is a must-visit destination for coffee lovers in New York. Its charming ambiance, combined with its delicious and artfully prepared coffee, make it an ideal spot to relax and refuel. Whether you're a local or a tourist, this café is sure to provide a memorable coffee experience.

See Also:

## 6.Cafe Panino Mucho Giusto

Handmade Italian sandwiches, artisanal coffee, and a welcoming atmosphere.

The panini served at this place is almost perfect, it's a must-try. However, it's worth noting that they only accept cash as a form of payment. Despite this minor inconvenience, the panini is still a standout menu item.

more: 15 of the best bars in Greenwich Village New York City

## 7.Caffe Reggio

Oldest Italian coffee house in Greenwich Village, hand-built espresso machine

The coffee shop offers a range of delicious pastries to complement their great coffee and espresso. This is not a modern, corporate coffee chain, but a unique and independently run establishment. Its charm and character make it a popular spot among locals and visitors alike, who come to enjoy the tasty drinks and treats in a welcoming atmosphere.

## 8.Kobrick Coffee Co.

Offers coffee subscriptions, partners with local roasters

This coffee shop is not just a place to get your daily caffeine fix, but also a spot to try unique and flavorful coffee drinks. The coffee cocktails offered are a standout feature and a true representation of the diverse and innovative food and drink scene in New York City. Whether you're a coffee connoisseur or just looking to try something new, this coffee shop has something for everyone.

## 9.St Jardim

Adorable outdoor seating, Rotating art exhibitions

The venue itself is a charming new addition to the local scene, offering a cozy and inviting atmosphere. It functions as both a cafe and wine bar, making it a versatile spot for different occasions. The drinks are consistently described as smooth and not too bitter, suggesting a careful and thoughtful selection process. The overall vibes of the place are upbeat and enjoyable, making it a popular spot for social gatherings and casual outings.

See Also:

## 10.Rosecrans Florist & Cafe

In addition to coffee and food, the establishment also offers a selection of flowers and plants for sale.

## 11.The Uncommons

Board game theme with thousands of games to play

The atmosphere at The Uncommons is warm and welcoming, making it an ideal place for spending quality time with friends or meeting new people who share a passion for board games. The coffee shop’s ambiance is comfortable and inviting, providing a perfect setting for game nights and events. Whether customers are looking to relax, socialize, or explore new games, The Uncommons offers an exceptional experience for board game enthusiasts of all levels.

## 12.Café Kitsuné West Village

Japanese-French cafe concept, Pastry from Maison Kitsuné

On the other hand, the ambiance of the place is quite pleasant, creating a cool and relaxed atmosphere. Customers appreciate the indoor vibe and the option of outdoor seating. Despite the issues with the staff, the positive aspects of the environment still make it a decent spot to spend some time.

## 13.ad hoc : cafe

Offers nitro cold brew and vegan options

Visitors can look forward to a comfortable and cozy seating area, perfect for catching up with friends or spending some quality alone time. The food and drink offerings are delicious and appealing, making it an ideal spot for a quick bite or a leisurely coffee break. Whether you're looking for a place to socialize or a quiet space to focus, this establishment is an excellent choice.

## 14.Blackstone Coffee Roaster

In-house roasted coffee beans, community-focused

Recently opened in the same area, Blackstone has become a popular spot for residents looking for a quick and delicious stop. The cafe stands out with its kindhearted staff, excellent food, and health-conscious options. Coffee lovers are also in for a treat, as Blackstone serves great coffee, making it a must-visit for both coffee connoisseurs and foodies alike.

## 15.Merriweather Coffee + Kitchen

Friendly staff, natural light, and community atmosphere.

In my opinion, the best food I've ever had in a New York café was the BLAT, which was bursting with flavor. The iced tea was also fantastic, perfectly refreshing and tasty. The staff were friendly, helpful, and contributed to the excellent atmosphere of the café. I highly recommend visiting this café.

## 16.Porto Rico Importing Co.

Historic 1907 Cuban café with live music

The cappuccinos served here are widely regarded as some of the best in town, and at a reasonable price. The location is perfect for those who prefer to grab their coffee and go, or sit on the outdoor benches. In addition to their popular cappuccinos, this establishment also boasts a wide selection of whole bean coffee. A friend specifically recommended this place for its variety of whole coffee beans, and anyone looking for high-quality beans would be wise to give this spot a try.

## 17.Bar Pisellino

Known for its intimate and romantic ambiance with fresh flowers and fairy lights

The hot chocolate at Bar Pisellino is a must-try, featuring a scoop of vanilla ice cream that adds to its heavenly flavor. The Americano is also a great choice, providing a robust coffee experience. The waitstaff is friendly and adds to the overall enjoyable ambiance of the cafe. Despite fighting a cold, the reviewer still opted for a non-alcoholic beverage and was not disappointed.

## 18.Buvette Gastrotheque

Local roastery, specialty coffee drinks, vegan-friendly options

The food and coffee are both delicious at this establishment. We went on a Saturday morning and only had to wait a few minutes to be seated. Although the tables are close together, it did not detract from our enjoyable experience. In fact, we plan to return again.

## 19.Café at Pop Up Grocer

Collaboration with various roasters

This cafe is not only a place to grab coffee, but also a cute spot that features a constant rotation of independent products. The selection of products changes regularly, providing frequent visitors with new items to try. This aspect of the cafe adds an element of excitement and discovery to the shopping experience.

## 20.Madman Espresso & Bakery

Warm up with a cup of their specialty coffee from caffevita.com, pioneer of the Farm Direct movement popular in Seattle since 1995. And what better way to complement your coffee than with a delicious focaccia from their select collection?

See Also:

## 21.Judy's Cafe

If you're in the mood for a light snack, Judy's Cafe also offers a selection of freshly baked pastries and sandwiches to complement your drink. The café's warm and welcoming atmosphere, combined with quality coffee and delicious treats, will make it your go-to spot in the Village when you're looking for a caffeine fix.

## 5 Diverse Coffee Spots in Greenwich Village

Central Village offers a slightly different Village feel—more old-school, more local, and rich with food history. During winter, this stretch is ideal for warming up with great coffee while exploring one of Manhattan’s most storied neighborhoods.

Here are **5 standout coffee spots, **perfect additions to a winter walk through the Village.

#### 1. **Porto Rico Importing Company**

A legendary New York City coffee institution, Porto Rico Importing Company has been part of Village life since 1907 and remains one of the most authentic coffee shops in the neighborhood (not a sit down cafe, a great store to buy coffee beans and a great cup of coffee.

**Website**

https://www.portorico.com

**Google Maps**

https://maps.google.com/?q=Porto+Rico+Importing+Company+201+Bleecker+St+New+York+NY

**Why it stands out**

- 
One of NYC’s oldest coffee roasters

Hundreds of beans sourced from around the world 
- 
Iconic winter stop on historic Bleecker Street 
- 
Deep roots in Village culinary history 

Porto Rico Importing Company perfectly reflects the kind of food storytelling highlighted on a **Foods of NY Tours**.

#### 2. Senza Gluten by Jemiko 100% Gluten‑Free Cafe & Bakery

title: 17 Best New York City Cafes (Serving Great Coffee in NYC)
author: Antonina
text:
Incapable of playing second fiddle, New York City offers the best of everything and coffee is no exception. Chock-full of charming corner cafes and shoe-box sized coffee shops, you’ll find everything from the latest artisanal brews to time-honored institutions that have been serving New Yorkers for 100+ years. On that note, here’s a quick roundup of the best coffee in New York City.

## The Best Coffee in New York City

## (Click Here for the Table of Contents)

### Best New York City Cafes (Table of Contents)

**Visiting New York City?** If you haven’t decided where to stay (yet) check out our helpful guide on Where to Stay in New York City (The 10 Best Neighborhoods & 3 to Avoid). Don’t have time? Here’s my favorite hotel in NYC, hands down.

### Devoción

**Website.** Devoción **Address.** 69 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11249 (Flagship)

 Fresh Colombian coffee brewed within 10 days of being picked

Devoción is unapologetically committed to serving the freshest cup of coffee in New York City. How so? For starters, beans are sourced directly from Colombian coffee producers, dry-milled in Bogotá, and then rapidly shipped to New York for roasting. **This ensures the coffee is served roughly 10 days after being picked.**

In terms of ambiance, all three locations exude an air of rustic charm. Housed in restored historic buildings with exposed brick and wooden floors, it’s the perfect place to nestle in with a fresh cup of coffee and good book in hand.

### Porto Rico Importing Company

**Website.** Porto Rico Importing Co.**Locations.** Greenwich Village, East Village, Lower East Side

 Bulk coffee order, old school vibes

Serving New Yorkers since 1907, Porto Rico Importing Company is one of the oldest coffee shops in New York City. Founded in the East Village, you. Run by the third generation of the Longo family, Porto Rico offers 130 varieties of coffee from around the world.

Open sacks of coffee beans are stored under vintage signs, oozing an old-world charm few can resist. From Indonesia to Brazil, expect to find top-notch coffee sold in bulk. Don’t need five pounds? That’s fine too, you can order coffee by the cup at checkout.

### Abraço

**Website.** Abraço**Neighborhood.** East Village**Address.** 81 E 7th St, New York, NY 10003**Best for.** Felling like a local and cozy coffee dates 

Opened in 2007, Abraço is a cozy European-inspired cafe that moonlights as a cocktail bar in the evenings. Using beans roasted in-house, the espresso. Always balanced, the rich shot is the closest you’ll get to Italy without checking bags.

Considering Abraço is an espresso bar first and foremost, you can be sure that any espresso-based drinks will impress, but locals know that’s only half the story. The party doesn’t start without a gander at the pastry case, the olive oil cake is a must-order in my book and pairs perfectly with a cappuccino.

The petite outdoor patio is a hit during the summer months, so invite a friend, pick up a slice of olive oil cake and spend time catching up over proper coffee and really good treats.

**Good to know —** Abraço is one of the few New York City coffee shops that doesn’t offer alternative milk options, only whole milk on offer. A bit unusual, so it’s worth calling out.

### Joe’s Coffee

Situated on a scenic corner between Waverly Place and Gay Street, Joe’s flagship location in the West Village is the quintessential New York City neighborhood coffee shop. You’ll find Joe’s all over the city (there’s 25 outposts now), but the West Village location is worth the trek.

The endearing vibes alone warrant a visit, but thankfully Joe’s serves some of the strongest drip coffee in NYC, making it an easy morning habit for locals. There’s ample indoor and outdoor seating and the cafe stays open until 8pm, it’s the perfect place to retreat for some respite before dinner.

### Arabica

**Website.** Arabica**Locations.** Dumbo & Lower East Side

 Epic view of the Brooklyn Bridge

Hailing from Kyoto, at Arabica you get coffee with a view. Enormous half-dome windows perfectly frame the Brooklyn Bridge making this one of the most Instagrammable coffee shops in NYC. But don’t make the mistake of thinking such a cute cafe produces sub-par coffee. On the contrary, the in-house roasting machines ensure every cup is perfectly smooth.

**Something to Note —** The matcha at this NYC cafe has left me disappointed more than once, stick to coffee.

** Unpopular opinion. ** Hot take. the best coffee in New York City isn’t at a trendy third-wave spot. it’s at Best New York City Cafes (Table of Contents).

### Coffee Project New York

**Website— **Coffee Project New York**Best for.** Coffee connoisseurs

Helmed by certified coffee grader and roasting championship competitor, Chi Sum Ngai, you can bet Coffee Project New York serves some of the best coffee in NYC. Sourcing the finest coffee from around the world, the company’s ethos focuses on improving the quality of life for every person involved in the coffee supply chain.

As such, there’s an emphasis on small-scale producers and family farms that prioritize improved working conditions for farmers. Hard not to love that. In terms of coffee, Ngai’s perfectionism shines through, each cup is expertly made to let the beans sing. Excellence is the only word that comes to mind.

** Local tip. ** Insider move. ask for the off-menu special. Regulars know about it, and now you do too.

### Sey Coffee

**Website.** Sey Coffee**Address.** 18 Grattan St, Brooklyn, NY

 Bright cafe, great coffee

Airy and bright, this New York City cafe strives to produce beautiful coffee in a peaceful, plant-filled space. Seasonally sourced, the been are delicately. The hard work pays off, Food & Wine recently crowned them the best coffee shop in New York State.

**Local’s Tip.** Sey Coffee has a popular subscription program where you can sign up to receive a monthly supply of coffee beans. It’s a great gift for a coffee connoisseur!

### Kobrick Coffee Company

**Website.** Kobrick Coffee Company**Neighborhood.** Chelsea**Address.** 24 9th Ave, New York, NY

 Sustainable small-batch coffee

Kobrick Coffee has withstood the test of time, providing locals with some of the best coffee in New York City for more than a century* (opened in 1920!)*. The four generations of Kobricks to run the shop have fine tuned small-batch roasting over the past hundred years. 

There’s an emphasis on organic, fair trade and Rainforest alliance certified beans, so New Yorkers can rest assured knowing they’re sipping on a sustainable cup of coffee that doesn’t compromise on flavor.

### Qahwah House

**Website.** Qahwah House**Locations.** Williamsburg & Greenwich Village**Best For.** Yemini coffee and great pastries 

Qahwah House is a popular Yemeni coffee shop in Williamsburg that serves organic coffee imported from Yemen. You can order a strong drip and find yourself content, but if you want to dive into a more exciting afternoon, opt for the Adeni chai.

Deeply aromatic and rich, the chai is made with evaporated milk and served in a glass carafe to be enjoyed at your leisure. Pair it with the sabaya pastry (flaky layered pastry made with Yemeni butter and honey) and you’ll be in for quite the experience.

The staff behind the counter are extremely friendly so don’t be afraid to ask questions. They’re eager to give recommendations on traditional drinks and pastries.

### Partners Coffee

**Website.** Partners Coffee

 One of the best laptop-friendly cafes in NYC

Within a decade of opening, Partners Coffee has gone from a single cafe in Williamsburg to five across the Big Apple. The beans are roasted in-house which results in consistently smooth and strong coffee, making this a reliable working cafe in NYC for uncompromising coffee aficionados.

Scoring a table shouldn’t prove too difficult at the spacious cafe. The best part? Once seated, you won’t need to do any notorious juggling acts. The tables are large enough to comfortably fit a laptop, notebook, coffee and meal from the tantalizing lunch menu.

### Ten Thousand Coffee

**Website.** Ten Thousand Coffee**Locations.** Midtown and Financial District**Best for.** Creative foamy coffee drinks

Ten Thousand Coffee is the new kid on the block, but they hold their own among the best coffee shops in New York City. The cafe gets its name from the 10,000 hour rule, which argues that 10,000 hours of practice leads to expertise. Fans of sweet drinks will love this spot because the cafe specializes in creamy and foamy concoctions, think caffeinated desserts.

### PlantShed

**Website.** PlantShed**Address.** 555 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10024 (Flagship)

 Part cafe, part plant shop

All my fellow plant moms will be in a state of euphoria at PlantShed. The original Upper West Side outpost has been one of the most treasured coffee shops in New York City for more than 40 years. Plants and flowers are available for sale so it’s not uncommon to see folks walking out the door with a latte in one hand hanging pothos in the other.

### Hungry Ghost

**Website.** Hungry Ghost**Neighborhood.** Brooklyn and Manhattan

 Great on the run coffee option

Serving exceptional Stumptown coffee, Hungry Ghost has 12 cafes in New York City. Each location is sun-drenched and exudse an airy feel, but I’m partial to the Park Slope locale. The founder of Hungry Ghost approaches coffee like a sommelier, with a focus on proper sourcing, roasting and brewing techniques, he’s keen to produce the best coffee in New York City. The atmosphere is buzzy and energetic, exactly the kind of place where you’ll want to linger over your meal. This one of my go-to spots whenever I find myself in the neighborhood. I never get tired of it. It’s the kind of spot that makes exploring this part of the city feel rewarding. Whether you’re a regular or just passing through, you’ll feel right at home here.

### Ralph’s Coffee

**Website.** Ralph’s Coffee**Neighborhood.** Upper East Side**Address.** 888 Madison Ave, New York, NY 10021

 Posh vibes and intragram-worthy photo ops 

Ralph’s Coffee is a posh Upper East Side cafe with very charming retro vibes. It’s one of the most popular coffee shops in the New York City and has the long lines to prove it. Between the elegant decor and knock-out coffee (using La Colombe beans), you’ll feel like a million bucks. There’s a handful of outdoor tables to lounge at, but don’t expect to find any open seats easily because they fill up.

You Might Enjoy Reading.15+ Best Things to Do on the Upper East Side (Local’s Guide)

### Do Not Feed the Alligators

**Website.** Do Not Feed the Alligators**Neighborhood.** Greenwich Village**Address.** 337 Bleecker St, New York, NY

 Cafe that turns into a cocktail bar in the evening 

Do Not Feed the Alligators (DNFA) sources beans from small roasters to make expertly brewed pour-overs and espresso-forward drinks. The warm, mismatched furniture invites conversations, while the put together bookstore adds a touch of intellectual intrigue to the popular NYC coffee shop.

Come evening, the lights dim, the wine flows, and the café transforms into a cozy little bar, showcasing DNFA’s chameleon-like charm. Laptops aren’t allowed, which makes it a great NYC cafe to meet someone new (the exceptional coffee is an easy ice breaker).

## Best NYC Coffee Shops. Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the oldest coffee shop in Manhattan?**

Caffe Reggio in the Greenwich Village is the oldest coffee shop in Manhattan, serving New York City since 1927. It’s said the first cappuccino in America was made at Caffe Reggio.

**Do you tip at coffee shops NYC?**

Most locals tip anywhere between 15-25% at coffee shops in NYC.

**What are the best coffee shops in Brooklyn?**

Sey Coffee, Devoción, and Partners Coffee serve some of the best coffee in Brooklyn.

**Is it okay to work in a New York City coffee shop?**

After the pandemic many coffee shops across New York City opened their doors to remote workers, and many cafes still provide WiFi, outlets, and coffee to help you have a productive day.
