The open wifi and abundant outlets make this a laptop warrior's dream, and the fact that it's open very early until very late means you can work on your own schedule. Pricing is surprisingly affordable for the quality and space you're getting, making it easy to justify that third latte of the day.

my go-to spot to get work done, meet with friends or enjoy time sam james coffee cheap price great food lots of space phone call booths open wifi — @tishamouse

drinks are super average but is a super nice spot to get work done! quiet, not busy and lots of outlets — @yeggi

very nice ambiance and great to work at. can get loud sometimes. open very early and closes very late — @keanem

title: The Best Coffee Shops in New York City
author: Melissa McCart
text:
There’s no shortage of cozy neighborhood coffee shops in New York City, welcoming in customers with frothy cappuccinos and friendly conversation. And while every New Yorker has their favorite corner spot, some cafes rise above the rest with expertly brewed cups of coffee and award-winning pastries.

# The Best Coffee Shops in New York City, According to Eater Editors

Where to find expertly brewed cups of coffee in NYC

Here, we’ve rounded up our favorite places for a cup of coffee right now. And for related guides, check out Eater NY’s picks for the best Queens coffee and tea spots.

**For this update:** We’ve added **Kinship Coffee Roasters**. And, for now, we’ve removed Brooklyn Ball Factory.

# The Best Coffee Shops in New York City, According to Eater Editors

Where to find expertly brewed cups of coffee in NYC

There’s no shortage of cozy neighborhood coffee shops in New York City, welcoming in customers with frothy cappuccinos and friendly conversation. And while every New Yorker has their favorite corner spot, some cafes rise above the rest with expertly brewed cups of coffee and award-winning pastries.

Here, we’ve rounded up our favorite places for a cup of coffee right now. And for related guides, check out Eater NY’s picks for the best Queens coffee and tea spots.

**For this update:** We’ve added **Kinship Coffee Roasters**. And, for now, we’ve removed Brooklyn Ball Factory.

## Clubhouse Cafe

This coffee shop in the South Bronx near Yankee Stadium is operated by Bronx youth in conjunction with nonprofit South Bronx United. It serves as a workforce development program that helps young people develop skills. Coffee comes from Devoción, and cookies, croissants, and muffins are baked at Mottley Kitchen, and desserts like cakes from Sully & Vanilla, both also in the South Bronx.

## Variety Coffee Roasters

Variety first started roasting coffee in 2014: It now has multiple locations around the city, including this popular shop on the Upper East Side that’s a good spot for working. The coffee brand is known for its nutty, chocolatey roasts, and you can now find its coffee at other cafes throughout the city, as well as at Three Decker Diner in Greenpoint, run by Variety owner Gavin Compton.

## Mokafé Coffee House

Coffee culture in Astoria is strong, so anything will be a contentious pick, but Mokafé stands out for its flavors: bright and fruity with a roast that’s light enough that a pour-over produces a dark reddish hue. The growing chain is a partnership between a Yemeni American family and a Guatemalan American coffee guru, who’s worked at roasteries and cafes in his native country for over a decade. Together, they source directly from small farms in Guatemala and Yemen, where the fruits of the coffee plants are hand-picked and air-dried with the beans, and then removed, producing those fruit-forward notes. The Yemeni beans, imported green, get roasted in Long Island and shuttled into the Astoria storefront to brew into a number of drinks like maple oat lattes. The space is modern with sage green, light wood, and golden accents that extend into the quiet room behind the shop. *— Caroline Shin *

## Kinship Coffee Roasters

The Astoria-forever coffee roaster is all about specifically sourced beans used for espresso drinks, cold brews, and seasonal options alongside baked goods. There are two other locations in the same Queens neighborhood on Broadway and 21st Street, plus its first expansion into Manhattan to come later.

## St Kilda Coffee

St Kilda roasts its beans in Brooklyn and is known for fruity notes like pear, peach, boysenberry, and plum. There are two Hell’s Kitchen locations, with the other on West 44th Street.

## Hi-Collar

Visit this East Village spot that’s a kissaten during the day and an izakaya at night. The cafe serves pour-overs and siphon coffee from single-source beans and blends. Lunch options include Japanese-style spaghetti, variations on hayashi rice, and omurice.

## La Cabra

The lines at the original East Village coffee shop snake out the door during rush hour, and, truth is, it’s worth it. This Danish import has excellent coffee, exquisite pastries, table service, and an appealing Scandinavian style. If only every day could start with a perfect cappuccino in an earthenware cup and a cardamom bun. There’s a second location in Soho and the roastery in Bushwick.

## Lê Phin

The East Village cafe is named after the instrument used to brew coffee in Vietnam. Find Vietnamese iced coffee, Vietnamese-style brewed hot coffee, as well as lattes that use culturally relevant ingredients like pandan and black sesame. The small, sunny storefront has a few seats inside.

## Abraço

There’s nothing in coffee quite like Abraço, an East Village shop with so much personality that it’s hard to take it in all at once. There’s the coffee, with wild-haired co-owner Jamie McCormick often working the bar. There are the pastries, such as co-owner Liz Quijada’s justifiably famous orange-scented olive oil cake. And there’s the scene, the chatty locals who, in the words of Frank Zappa, make this “the top freako watering hole and social HQ.” Also, if you’re lucky, they’ll be playing your favorite vinyl from start to finish.

## Coffee Project

Started in the East Village in 2015, Coffee Project has since grown into a destination for coffee nerds with multiple locations in Manhattan (including this one in the East Village), Brooklyn, and Queens. The shop sells standard cafe drinks, plus seasonal pour-overs, deconstructed lattes, nitro cold-brew flights, and other drinks.

## Suited

Suited in the Financial District works with some of the biggest names in New York roasting right now, including Sey and Little Wolf, along with a handful of international roasters whose beans are available from the shop. There is a full menu of standard cafe drinks, but stick to a cup of espresso or drip to appreciate the thoughtful sourcing that’s happening here. There are also daytime foods like egg and cheese sandwiches, ricotta pancakes, and grilled chicken wraps.

## Sey Coffee

Sey is regarded as one of the better microroasters in NYC. Founders Tobin Polk and Lance Schnorenberg favor a light, clean Nordic-style flavor profile preferred by the coffee cognoscenti. The bright and airy sky-lit warehouse, decorated with potted plants, Sey Coffee feels more West Coast than Bushwick.

## Dayglow

This Los Angeles import, Dayglow, is a coffee shop and bar that carries coffee from 10 to 20 different coffee roasters at a time. It also roasts its own beans, which have dark chocolate, lychee, butterscotch, and mandarin notes. The Bushwick cafe is also home to the company’s beer and cocktail bar, Niteglow (get it?).

### See more

## % Arabica

For the freshest of fresh-roasted coffee beans, it’s hard to beat the international chain % Arabica. The Kyoto-based import opened its first U.S. location in Dumbo in 2021 with a souped-up espresso machine, baked goods from Balthazar, and a “green bean corner” where customers can buy beans to be roasted on the spot in minutes. There are three other NYC locations in Manhattan.

## Cholita

From brother-sister team Bryan and Suzette Siranaula, originally from Ecuador, this Ridgewood coffee shop gallery space features an array of coffee drinks from Ecuadorian and other South American roasteries.

## Yafa Cafe

Cousins Ali Suliman and Hakim Sulaimani opened Yafa Cafe in 2019 to spotlight Yemeni coffee culture in Sunset Park. It’s still going strong as a neighborhood cornerstone where the Yemeni-rooted food is just as good as the assortment of coffees. The cousins also started to roast an in-house line of coffee during the pandemic, offering blends and Yemeni single-origin roasts for sale from the shop. There’s a second location in downtown Brooklyn.

title: Best Financial District Cafes - One Wall Street
text:
For upwards of a billion people across the planet, coffee is a staple—and sometimes the best part—of the day. For many daily java drinkers, coffee is truly a magical elixir. It readies us to wake up for the day and stay alert and is the perfect beverage to enjoy with dessert or to sip while catching up with a friend. During summer months, nothing beats a cold brew, while a steaming-hot cup of coffee is the perfect antidote for a frosty winter day. Whatever the season, coffee-loving residents of One Wall Street can savor a cup at one of the nearby cafes in their historic Downtown neighborhood, prepared with flair by a talented crew of local baristas and perfectly paired with a delectable baked good.

Located in Brookfield Place, Cafe District is one of the neighborhood’s stalwarts for expertly crafted espresso drinks, including the gloriously decadent Nutella Latte. In addition to these coffee offerings, the larger marketplace includes a patisserie serving up classic French delights—from pastries and chocolates to macarons. For a heartier option, patrons can pick up a sandwich on a perfectly chewy baguette or a sweet or savory crepe.

At nearby 787 Coffee, guests are guaranteed to taste some of the freshest coffee around. This cafe specializes in Puerto Rican beans from their farm in the mountains of Maricao, Puerto Rico, where their coffee trees are sustainably planted and grown without environmentally harmful pesticides. Their beans, which are shipped twice weekly, can also be purchased to enjoy from the comforts of home.

A quintessentially New York institution, Cafe Grumpy is probably best known as the place to go for a perfectly brewed cup of coffee in hip surroundings. The location on Stone Street offers a full espresso, coffee, and tea menu, as well as a collection of pastries, with seating available as well to sip a warm drink while taking refuge from the cold. The decor is also a sophisticated mix of natural materials and warm lighting, which preserves the grand scale and details of the original building.

Finally, 10,000 Coffee, so-called from the oft-repeated rule that it takes 10,000 hours to achieve expertise—namely, crafting the perfect cup of specialty coffee. The must-try specialty coffees include the Einspanner, a traditional Viennese coffee, the Caramel Café Latte, as well as the Jeju Green Tangerine Matcha. Not to be outdone, their specialty pastries, like their blueberry crème cheese and coconut crème croissants, are worth the trip alone to this chicly designed cafe.

Whether it’s for a midafternoon break or an indulgent weekend treat during a walk in the neighborhood, each of these cafes offers One Wall Street residents plenty of skillfully crafted drinks, pastries, and experiences for keeping warm and fully caffeinated all winter long. For those looking for something closer to home, the One Club bar or Whole Foods downstairs also offers a variety of caffeinated drinks that will satisfy your cravings.

Price : $

Address : 20 Old Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11201

Pretty Moment : a beautiful French bakery with a little cafe on the second floor – this started as a bakery in an apartment in Cobble Hill (4f) during the pandemic!

Good for : authentic French croissants and baguettes with your coffee – some of the best in the city!

Price : $

2. Sogno Toscano, West Village

Address : 17 Perry St, New York, NY 10014

Pretty Moment : a lovely Italian cafe serving sandwiches, pastries, wine and of course coffee! The indoor and outdoor seating is both beautiful.

Good for : coffee, wine, sandwiches, live music on some evenings

Price : $$

Address : 169 Thompson St Suite B, New York, NY 10012

Pretty Moment : cute little storefront on a cobblestone street in Greenwich Village

Good for : bagels! their coffee is good too, but mostly go for the bagels. There is only outdoor seating, but I recommend

Price : $

4. Tea & Sympathy, West Village

Address : 108 Greenwich Ave, New York, NY 10011

Pretty Moment : a charming English tea shop with proper tea cups, saucers and teapots

Good for : proper English scones and tea! More of a sit down cafe (no laptops)

Price : $$

5. Patisserie Vanessa, Upper East Side

Address : 1340 Lexington Ave, New York, NY 10128

Pretty Moment : a French patisserie in a historical district on the Upper East Side, lovely outdoor and indoor tables

Good for : delicious French pastries and Provencal tea

Price : $

Address : 40A 10th Ave, New York, NY 10014

Pretty Moment : a stunning space in Chelsea with expansive views over the Hudson River and Little Island.

Good for : Has cozy spaces both to work and chat, laptops allowed. I recommend signing up for the Korean tea ceremony on the weekends!

Price : $$

## Pretty Cafes with a Modern Vibe (and EXCELLENT coffee)

I’d like to preface this section by saying that every cafe I have recommended on here has good coffee as that is the baseline. However, the following coffee shops truly serve some of the best coffee in the city, espressos, drip coffee, and my favorite – delicate pour overs.

1. WatchHouse, Fifth Ave, Midtown

Address : 660 5th Ave, New York, NY 10103

Pretty Moment : a hip new cafe near Rockefeller Center with a fresh, beautiful ambience

Good for : really delicious and high quality coffee! I recommend for working with laptops or coffee with friends. They serve a good decaf espresso too. The blood orange danish is absolutely delicious.

Price : $

Address : 284 Lafayette St, New York, NY 10012

Pretty Moment : modern Nordic ambience, clean and beautiful

Good for : the most delicious cup of coffee, work, catching up with a friend or a book

Price : $

I hope this roundup of Pretty Cafes in NYC helps. I’ll keep adding to the list as I post about new (or new to me) pretty cafes in the city.

Happy cafe hopping, wishing you a well caffeinated NYC day / trip!

title: Cutest Plants and Flower Cafes and Coffee Shops in NYC
author: Serena
text:
# Cutest Plants and Flower Cafes and Coffee Shops in NYC

**Looking for those viral plants and floral cafes in NYC? This post tells you the best plants themed and flower coffee shops in New York City.**

New York City has no shortage of cute cafes and it is the perfect city for any coffee lovers.

I say New Yorkers are quite spoiled when it comes to coffee. Why? You will literally find 3 different coffee shops within one block in New York City!

New Yorkers are so spoiled that it is no longer just about great coffee, the theme and aesthetics of the coffee shop also matter a lot….I mean A LOT.

The good news is that there are a ton of super pretty coffee shops in New York City and with the rise of flower shops turned coffee shop, you really can get the best of both worlds! Delicious coffee + plants and flowers make mornings a lot better.

I went around New York City in search of the prettiest plants and flower cafes so you don’t have to! Read along this article to see what are some of the best lush and floral cafes around the city (and yes this includes Queens and Brooklyn as well).

*This blog contains occasional affiliate links, where I receive a small commission on sales of the products/hotels that are linked at no additional cost to you. In addition, as an Amazon Associate, I earn from qualifying purchases*.

## Plants & Flower Cafes in Manhattan

You are probably not surprised to hear this but Manhattan has the most number of plants themed and floral cafes in New York City! Here is the list of the flower coffee shops (and will continue be updated as I find more)!

#### Remi43 Flower & Coffee

**Address**:  810 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10017 <— the bigger one

                 906 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10017  <– smaller one**Hours**: 7am – 6pm daily

Remi Flower & Coffee has 2 different locations in midtown east. Located only a few blocks away, both cafes are Instagrammers’ favorites with their beautiful interior and cute coffee (yes even their drinks are cute).

Remi Flower & Coffee features an actual flower shop as well as a coffee bar with seating. Their menus consists of different drinks and baked goods.

Remi43 on 43rd street is the bigger of the two cafes, with a much larger interior and a second floor. If you are looking for a beautiful setting to study or work then you would appreciate Remi43 for its wifi, outlet (by the high tables) and bathroom.

Whether you are looking to buy flowers or just enjoy the vibe, you will certainly enjoy Remi Flower & Coffee.

**Pro tip**: their prettiest drinks are the lavender latte and rose latte.

#### Ariston Coffee Bar

**Address**: 78 5th Ave, New York, NY 10011**Hours**: 7:30am – 7pm Monday to Friday; 8am – 7pm on Saturday; 9am – 6pm on Sunday

If you want the WOW factor then Ariston Coffee Bar is the one. Located near Union Square, Ariston Coffee Bar is a family owned flower shop with 40 years of history.

With multiple locations of its flower shops, the location near Union Square includes a large two story coffee shop with Devocion coffee, pastries and is perfect for dates or just meeting up with friends. It is also a great place to study or work with its wifi, outlets (upstairs) and bathrooms.

Depending on the season you visit, Ariston Coffee Bar changes its interior decoration regularly.

#### Maman

**Address**: Multiple Locations. The photos below are taken at 375 Hudson St, New York, NY 10014**Hours**: 7:30am – 6pm everyday

When it comes to aesthetics Maman’s gotta be one of the most well known french coffee shops in New York City. With more than 20 locations in New York City, you will have no difficulty finding a Maman no matter where you live.

All of the Mamans have a similar rustic theme; even their coffee cups are pleasing to the eye. Having been to several different Mamans in the city, the most beautiful one would have to be the one near Soho.

The interior of this particular cafe is rustic and chic, with lush green plants and a quaint atmosphere. As a full service cafe, you can find a variety of drinks, baked goods and brunch food that will delight all of your senses.

This particular Maman is also a great place to work/study from because there are outlets along the wall, and the building has free wifi and a bathroom.

#### Cafe Lyria

**Address**: 166 Crosby St, New York, NY 10012**Hours**: 8am to 5pm daily

New York has its fair share of French cafes but how about a Greek inspired coffee shop?

Tucked away in the lobby of 166 Crosby Street, Cafe Lyria is a true oasis in the middle of a bustling Noho. Here you will find lush greeneries and a number of Greek art pieces and statue.

Greek inspired decorations are not the only things you will find at Cafe Lyria, they also have Greek inspired coffee and the most famous drinks are the Lyria as well as Freddo Cappuccino.

Apparently this place was famous on Tiktok (which I didn’t realize since I don’t use Tiktok), but if it’s viral on Tiktok you know this place is pretty.

#### PlantShed Cafe

**Address**: 193 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10003

                 1 Prince St, New York, NY 10012

                 555 Columbus Ave, New York, NY 10024

                  723 Amsterdam Ave, New York, NY 10025**Hours**: 7am – 7pm Monday to Friday; 8am – 7pm on weekends (2nd Ave & Amsterdam Ave. locations)

             8am – 7pm daily (Prince St. location)

             9am – 7pm daily (Columbus Ave location)

PlantShed Cafe is a floral cafe chain in Manhattan that blends its lush greenery with delicious coffee and baked goods with a focus on wellness.

Opened in 2018 in Nolita and the Upper West Side, PlantShed Cafe has expanded to 2 more locations in Manhattan and one in New Jersey, offering a traditional flower shop retail experience with an unique cafe experience.

At each PlantShed Cafe you will find a variety of different flowers, tropical plants and succulents; making you feel you have stepped into an oasis in the middle of the busy and bustling city.

#### Ost Cafe

**Address**: 511 Grand St, New York, NY 10002**Hours**: 7:30am – 3pm Monday to Friday; 8am – 3pm Saturday and Sundays

Tucked away in LES, this cozy neighborhood cafe boasts a old world industrial vibe with its exposed bricks.

It’s not a floral cafe by any means but I do love the plants combined with the rustic interior. One thing I love about Ost Cafe is that most customers are locals that live around there and the price of drinks are actually very reasonable compare to other cafes in Manhattan.

#### Cafe Atelier

**Address**: 112 Hudson St, New York, NY 10013**Hours**: 7am – 6pm Monday to Friday; 8am – 6pm Saturdays; 8am – 5pm Sundays

Another flower shop + cafe combo to put on your list is Cafe Atelier, located in Tribeca.

Owned by Alice Kil, this cute flower cafe not only offers instagram worthy rose latte and lavender latte that are decorated with real flowers, they also offer pastries and a nice afternoon tea sea that are not found at other cafes.

In addition, Cafe Atelier offers **flower arrangement and candle making class**, which you can sign up on their website. 

#### Urban Backyard

**Address**: 180 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10012**Hours**: 7:30am – 6pm Monday to Friday; 8:30am – 7pm Sat & Sun

Urban Backyard is a small yet cozy cafe in Soho (yup in case you haven’t noticed, Soho has a lot of cute coffee shops).

The interior or Urban Backyard has a very zen feeling with its lush green plants and wooden furniture. This earthy feeling is accomplished by their cactus themed cupcakes (which are only available after 12pm).

Besides the usual coffee drinks, you will also find seasonal drinks like autumn spiced latte, ube latte, peppermint Candy Mocha as well as a variety of homemade pastries like the earl grey banana bread.

If you go early during the day you may be lucky enough to get a table but there are also some seatings outside. I was able to score a table with outlet there but there is no wifi available unfortunately.

#### Rosecrans Florist & Cafe

**Address**: 7 Greenwich Ave, New York, NY 10014**Hours**: 8am – 8pm daily

If there is one floral cafe that I have to pick it would probably be Rosecrans. Located in the West Village, Rosecrans is a super cute flower shop with a cafe inside.

The interior is absolutely beautiful with so many flowers and plants. It’s the perfect place to go on a date or just relax and read a book while absorbing the floral scent in the air. They have a variety of great coffee and teas as well as pastries including the Instagrammable Teddy Bear Madelaine.

Note that you cannot use laptop or iPad inside (they have signs on each table). You can only use laptop outside.

**Read Next**: Review of Plaza Hotel Afternoon Tea in NYC

#### Cafe-Flor

**Address**: 218 8th Ave, New York, NY 10011**Hours**: 7am – 8pm Monday to Thursday; 7am – 12am Friday; 8am – 12am Sat; 8am – 8pm Sunday

Cafe-Flor is more than just a coffee shop, it is a coffee shop combined with flowers and plants and it turns into a bar at night.

The space is large and roomy and the interior is tastefully decorated, making one feel like they are in a old French movie. There are plants and flowers everywhere and you will find lots of paintings and art works in one of the two rooms at the cafe.

Cafe-Flor is perfect to meeting friends or reading a book; although you can certainly work or study here, there is no wifi at the cafe (or it doesn’t work very well) and the music can be loud.

#### Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar

**Address**: High Line Hotel 180 10th Ave at, W 20th St, New York, 10011**Hours**: 7am – 4pm daily

Located in the High Line Hotel in Chelsea, Intelligentsia Coffee is hidden gem that you must not miss. This is the only Intelligentsia Coffee location in New York City and attracts numerous coffee lovers.

The cafe has both an inside and outside section, with the inside elegantly decorated and the outside simply aesthetically pleasing. There is a red double decker bus in the courtyard decorated with flowers, making it the perfect Instagram spot. You can go to the top of the bus to enjoy your coffee in the summer also!

#### Urbana Cafe and Gallery

**Address**: 144 10th Ave, New York, NY 10011**Hours**: 7am – 7pm Monday to Friday; 8am – 8pm Sat & Sun

A couple of blocks south from Intelligentsia Coffee Highline Coffeebar is another lush green cafe called Urbana Cafe and Gallery.

Decorated with art works and lush green plants, Urbana Cafe and Gallery is the perfect simple and peaceful cafe to work and study from. Their coffee is exceptionally good and there are a ton of other flavored latte drinks and baked goods to choose from.

**Read Next**: Tea Around Town Afternoon Tea Bus Tour in NYC

## Plants & Flower Coffee Shops in Brooklyn

Floral cafes are not just a Manhattan thing, in fact some of the cutest cafes can be found in Brooklyn.

#### PPL

**Address**: 189 Roebling St, Brooklyn, NY 11211**Hours**: 8am – 5pm Monday to Friday; 9am – 5pm Sat & Sun

Quietly tucked away in Williamsburg, PPL is a hidden gem that is gaining popular thanks to Social Media.

This small and cozy cafe offers the highest quality tea imported from Japan and coffee drinks and is run by a local Japanese couple. The inside is tastefully decorated with plants and gives off a vintage vibe. There is only one bench inside so not much seating space but it is a coffee shop not to be missed.

They have pop-up events in the shop sometimes. If you want to take photos of this tiny coffee shop it’s best to check their Instagram and avoid days when they have pop-up events going on.

#### Homecoming

**Address**: 92 Berry St, Brooklyn, NY 11249**Hours**: 8am – 6pm Monday to Thursday; 8am – 7pm Friday to Sunday

When it comes to flower coffee shops in Brooklyn, Homecoming is probably on everyone’s list.

Located in the center of lively Williamsburg, Homecoming is a popular coffee shop with a florist inside. This space also has a nice private backyard where you can enjoy your coffee as well as outdoor seating. Besides flowers and drinks, Homecoming also has a small selection of pottery that you can purchase.

There is no bathroom at Homecoming for guests, so plan accordingly if you plan to stay and work/study for more than a couple of hours.

#### Carlota

**Address**: 65 Richardson St, Brooklyn, NY 11211**Hours**: 10:30am – 6pm Tuesday to Friday; 10am – 5pm Saturday; closed Sunday and Monday

Carlota is a true hidden gem in Williamsburg; it is more known for its flower shop than the cafe part. As you sip on your coffee, you can admire at all the beautiful flower arrangements and the vases the cafe has to offer. Do keep in mind that sometimes the shop is closed when the owner is out delivering flowers.

#### Debutea Brooklyn

**Address**: 71 Smith St, Brooklyn, NY 11201**Hours:** 9:30am – 9pm daily

Debutea is a beautiful tea shop in downtown Brooklyn, known for their high quality and innovative tea drinks. This tea house is no ordinary bubble tea shop as they don’t use fructose, powder, creamer or artificial flavoring in their drinks.

The interior is pretty with flowers and plants at a couple of corners. There is a quiet area in the back that is perfect for working and studying. If you do get hungry they have yummy poke bowl, salad and other healthy food options.

## Plants & Floral Coffee Shops in Queens

#### Kunst Coffee Haus

**Address**: 212-08 41st Ave, Queens, NY 11361**Hours:** 8am – 6pm Monday to Friday; 9am – 6pm Saturday & Sunday

Kunst Coffee Haus is one of the only plants and flower coffee house that I found in Queens (so far) but it is a good one for sure.

Located in Bay Side, Kunst Coffee Haus offers a variety of coffee drinks, desserts and brunch options. If you want the instagram worthy latte then be sure to get the Rose Latte or the Rose Matcha Latte. There are also many cute seasonal drinks like the sweet potato latte and peppermint mocha latte (although menu may change each year).

The interior is cozily decorated with tons of plants and some flowers, making you feel like you are in a botanic garden or a conservatory. There are two levels inside and additional seating outdoors.

## Bonus: Flower Cafes in New Jersey and Connecticut

I know you came here to look for flower coffee shops in New York City but I would hate to not include some of the other floral cafes in the tristate area.

If you are looking for flower cafes in **New Jersey**, then be sure to stop by **Casa De Flora Bar** in Bloomfield New Jersey.

There are a couple of cute flower coffee shops in **Connecticut**:

- Hayfields Cafe & Florist in North Salem
- Verde Galerie Flower Shop & Cafe in Stamford

So what do you think is the best plants or flower cafes in New York City? Yeah I know it’s a hard decision to make given they are all very pretty and unique in their own ways.

There are definitely a number of these cafes that I would keep going back to in order to try different drinks and food.

**Are the flower cafes good for working/ studying?** To be honest most of the “flower” cafes are actually not great for working or studying since they have very small tables and don’t have outlets or wifi. But the plants coffee shops are definitely great for working. If you are looking to study from a flower cafe, then my recommendation would be **Maman** (the specific one in this post) and the upstairs of **Ariston Coffee Bar** where there are outlets.

title: Nolita Neighbourhood Guide • New York City • The Wanderbug
author: Genevieve Lauren
text:
*Welcome to The Wanderbug, a travel blog written for humans, by a human. I'm Genevieve, and every guide is personally written by me and based on my firsthand travel experiences.*

Nolita is one of New York City‘s most charming downtown neighbourhoods. It’s a tiny neighbourhood, only spanning a few blocks, but bursting with history, character and things to do, making it a must-visit neighborhood in New York City.

**I lived in Nolita for nearly two years,** so this neighbourhood has such a special place in my heart! I wrote this Nolita neighborhood guide to share all of the best things to do in Nolita, the best restaurants, bars and cafes in Nolita and some of my favourite spots in the neighbourhood.

Some of the best things to do in Nolita include shopping at NYC’s best bookstore, **McNally Jackson**, eating some of the best pizza in the city at **Prince Street Pizza** (take out) and **Pasquale Jones **(restaurant), visiting the beautiful **Elizabeth Street Garden**, browsing the small **Nolita Market** for jewellery and accessories, or visiting some of the city’s best bars, restaurants and cafes like **Estela**, **Mother’s Ruin** and **Ruby’s Cafe.**

**Planning a trip to New York City?**Check out my complete guide Where to Stay in New York City for First Time Visitors .

Nolita is great for boutique shopping from independent and mid-size brands, with many jewelry, skincare, homewares and accessories boutiques in particular.

It gets very busy on weekends, as it’s home to so many great restaurants, bars and cafes (especially Australian ones!), as well as a deliciously high density of bakeries & ice cream shops!

## Free Printable: 5 Day New York City Itinerary

Get a copy of my 5-Day New York City Itinerary for First Time Visitors into a free, downloadable PDF – each day’s itinerary is on a single page, making it printer-friendly and easy to reference on-the-go! Click here to get your copy!## Where is Nolita?

Nolita is wedged between SoHo, Greenwich Village, NoHo, the Lower East Side and Little Italy (Nolita = North of Little Italy). It’s a short walk to Nolita from West Village, Chinatown and East Village too.

To get the subway to Nolita, catch the #4 or #6 Subway to Spring St.

## What does Nolita stand for?

Nolita means North of Little Italy. The neighbourhood was once part of Little Italy, in the 18th and 19th centuries, but today, as Little Italy has shrunk, Nolita has become a unique neighbourhood in its own right. It has a very different atmosphere to Little Italy. Little Italy can feel very touristy, Nolita is a neighbourhood has a greater variety of restaurants, bars, cafes and shopping.

## Best Things to do in Nolita

### Elizabeth Street Garden

Elizabeth Street Garden is a gorgeous, one-acre community sculpture garden tucked away in the backstreets of Nolita. It’s open at around midday every day, and has free entry. It’s such a beautiful spot, and is the perfect place to bring a book or lunch.

### Nolita Outdoor Market

Nolita Market is an artisan market that pops up every weekend along Prince Street, between Mulberry & Mott Sts. There is some really beautiful jewelry here, and even though it’s small it’s worth a browse.

## Best Restaurants in Nolita

Nolita has plenty of great Italian food, thanks to it’s proximity to, and history as being part of, Little Italy. There are iconic pizza joints and Italian restaurants, as well as a number of great Asian restaurants and Michelin-starred restaurants like The Musket Room and Estela.

### Estela

Estela is one of the most respected restaurants in the USA, without any of the pretension. Credited with starting the share plates trend in the US, Estela is a forward-thinking restaurant that delivers spectacular Modern American food and warm service, without any fuss. This was our last dinner in Nolita, before we moved out of the neighbourhood and it was so special. Don’t miss their signature, and widely imitated, endive salad. Make a reservation!

### The Musket Room

The Musket Room is one of my favourite restaurants in New York City. The Michelin-starred restaurant balances indulgence, inventiveness and warmth to create the ultimate neighbourhood spot. If you can’t make it for dinner, at least enjoy cocktails and snacks in their adorable garden out the back – it’s one of the best kept patio secrets in New York!

### Rubirosa

Rubirosa is regarded as an instant classic. This cosy restaurant is one of the best Italian restaurants in New York City, is super popular and *always* has a wait time, so pop your name down early and then grab a drink at Mother’s Ruin or YN Bar around the corner while you wait. They’re famous for their vodka pizza, but I couldn’t go past their ricotta ravioli.

**Favourite dish: **ricotta ravioli

### Pasquale Jones

Pasquale Jones is one of the best Italian restaurants in New York City. It’s from the same owners as Charlie Bird in SoHo, which is another of my favourites. They’re famous for their little neck clam pizza, which is best shared between two, along with a few appetizers.

Like Charlie Bird, the atmosphere is warm, intimate and buzzy, with moody lighting, sleek interiors and a hip hop soundtrack. You’ll need to book a few weeks in advance, or drop by before 4pm to put your name down for the waitlist in the evening. The bar seats are a good option, and if you’ve got some time to kill before your table is ready, head to nearby La Compagnie for a pre-dinner drink.

**Favourite dish: **white clam pie, and the burrata (however it’s currently being served!)

### Lovely Day

Lovely Day is a tiny and trendy Thai restaurant, which makes it possible to go out for dinner and not blow the budget. You’ll definitely need to wait for a table on Friday or Saturday nights, and it’s a bit noisy and crowded, but the food is delicious and it won’t break the bank.

## Brunch & Coffee in Nolita

Brunch is big business in Nolita, especially at the several Australian cafes and coffee shops which have taken the neighbourhood by storm (there are four!).

### Ruby’s Cafe

A Nolita favourite for more than ten years, Ruby’s is an Australian cafe which is permanently packed. A table is worth the wait, whether you’re stopping in for coffee, brunch or dinner – the meals are delicious and well priced and the coffee is consistently perfect.

**Favourite dish:** Egg sandwich

### Cafe Integral

Tucked away on a quiet part of Elizabeth Street near Little Italy, Cafe Integral serves fine Nicaraguan coffee that the owners can proudly stand behind – they visit the farms they buy from in Nicaragua and roast in small batches in New York City. Cafe Integral is my favourite independent coffee shop in New York City. There’s not much room for seating, take your coffee to Elizabeth Street Garden instead!

### Epistrophy

Epistrophy is one of my favourite cafes in Nolita. It was founded by a group of friends from Sardinia, Italy, and the menu reflects Sardinian culture and cuisine. I love love love the food here, it never disappoints! It’s perfect for brunch or dinner, and gets quite busy on weekends.

### Urban Backyard

Urban Backyard is a hole in the wall on Mulberry Street, just south of Kenmare St. It’s the most adorable coffee shop in New York City, with excellent coffee, rose & lavender lattes, lovely tiny cupcakes and a range of beautiful tea.

### Bluestone Lane

Bluestone Lane is quickly taking over New York – and the rest of the US! The popular cafe chain was founded by Australians who live in New York, and they now have multiple coffee shops & cafes all over New York City. This location, on Kenmare Street, is my favourite of their cafes. It’s beautifully designed and is just as good for a healthy breakfast as it is for a boozy brunch.

### The Grey Dog

The Grey Dog is a charming and cosy farmhouse-style cafe, which offers home-style comfort food of the American midwest. It has a few locations around New York, but their Nolita location is constantly packed. Love the simple yet delicious food here, and the affordable prices. The pancakes here are the best!

### Fiat Cafe

Fiat Cafe is a super cute cafe on Mott St, with a very-Instagrammable hot pink wall (not pictured) and a French-leaning brunch & lunch menu. Note that it’s cash only!

### Black Seed Bagel

Black Seed Bagel makes some of the best bagels in New York City – and my personal favourites! They’ve recently renovated and re-opened their Nolita store, which frequently sees long lines on the weekends. There are only a few tables, so take your bagel to go and eat it in Elizabeth St Garden instead.

## Best Casual Restaurant & Takeaway in Nolita

### Prince St Pizza

It’s not a restaurant, but Prince Street Pizza is one of the most popular slice shops in New York City. There will be a queue snaking out the door from when they open, until the early hours of the morning. Every time you walk past, you’ll hear tourists ask incredulously “Can it be that good? It’s *just *pizza.” It really is that good and it is 100% worth the wait. Try the SoHo Square or the pepperoni.

### Zooba

I am *obsesssed *with this new takeaway spot, direct from Cairo. Healthy, affordable and DELICIOUS, I can’t get enough of Zooba’s Egyptian street food. My favourites are the tamayya, and David loves the hawawshi – beef patties that are 45% pressed vegetables, served in baladi bread with delicious toppings.

### Tacombi

A fun, casual Mexican spot on Elizabeth Street, Tacombi is housed in a warehouse-style space and is a great spot for dinner & drinks.

## Ice Cream & Dessert in Nolita

Nolita is full of classic New York City desserts, from traditional ice cream shops, to Italian cannoli to Brooklyn Black Out cake and my personal favourite, banana pudding. Brace your sweet tooth!

### Cafe Belle

This is probably a contentious opinion, but I think the best cannoli in New York are not in Little Italy, but just a bit further up the street at Cafe Belle in Nolita! The Scala family, by way of Sicily in Italy and then Brooklyn, have been serving hand-baked, authentic Italian pastries for more than 70 years. I am obsessed with the chocolate covered cannoli, which are piped with ricotta filling to order.

### Van Leeuwen Ice Cream

Van Leeuwen is one of the most popular ice cream chains in New York City, with the aim to revive the art of traditional ice cream making using ingredients perfected by nature, rather than science. They use many local artisanal producers, and all the ice cream is still made fresh in Greenpoint, Brooklyn. There are plenty of dairy-free and vegan options too. Take your scoop to the small park opposite, or around the corner to Elizabeth St Garden. My favourite flavour is the Brooklyn Brown Sugar!

### Milk Bar

Christina Tosi’s famous Milk Bar empire made a name for itself with Cereal Milk soft serve, Crack Pie (now renamed Milk Bar Pie) and Compost Cookies, and you can try the lot at their tiny shopfront on Mott Street. Get in the mood for Milk Bar’s creations by checking out the episode featuring Milk Bar on Netflix’s *Chef’s Table.*

### Little Cup Cake Bake Shop

Little Cup Cake Bake Shop is famous for having the best chocolate cake in the USA (according to *Food & Wine) *but I can’t go past their heavenly banana pudding. Banana pudding is big business in New York, so if you haven’t tried one, don’t miss out. It sounds so-so, but is actually America’s greatest contribution to dessert.

**Favourite treat: **banana pudding or coconut cake

## Best Bars in Nolita

### Compagnie des Vins Surnaturels

Somewhere between the edges of SoHo and Nolita, Compagnie is a fantastic wine bar with a bible-like bottles list, a diverse list of wines by the glass and great happy hour specials ($5 off wines by the glass, and cheese & salumi options for $5 a piece). Love this spot!

### Mother’s Ruin

Mother’s Ruin is the best of both worlds: a laidback local hangout, with a commitment to premium cocktails. You’ll get cocktails just as good as you’d find in a scene-y and expensive bar with a strict door policy, yet you can come as you are feel right at home.

### Sweet & Vicious

Sweet & Vicious has been a popular Nolita hangout since the 90s (and arguably, since before Nolita was Nolita). I love the courtyard here, the fact that I’ve never had to wait at the door or the bar and their $10 frozen margaritas.

### Spring Lounge

Spring Lounge is a classic New York City dive bar, and is PACKED every day after work. It’s popular with New Yorkers looking to blow off some steam without breaking the budget and has a really fun atmosphere. It’s known as the Shark Bar to locals, for the fake Shark pinned to the walls inside.

## Best Shopping in Nolita

### McNally Jackson Books

The holy grail of all book stores. McNally Jackson has three locations in New York, but the Nolita location is the best in my opinion. They have such a wonderfully curated selection of books and magazines, and offer the top indie bestsellers (nationally) for 20% off, which makes it so easy to scoop up the book of the moment. There’s a cafe attached, so you can dive straight into your book with a coffee & cake.

### Mejuri

Mejuri makes elegant and affordable everyday luxury possible with their range of stylish and well-priced jewelry. They have a popular online store, but I much prefer to shop for jewelry in person at this store.

### Sezane

A beautiful mid-range clothing store by a popular Parisian label. The Nolita boutique is Sezane‘s only physical store in the US.

### Goods for The Study

From the crew behind McNally Jackson, Goods for The Study is a beautiful stationery store. It has two halves – one dedicated entirely to pens and pencils, and the other for paper stationery.

### Everlane

One of the few physical stores of the ultra popular clothing brand, the Everlane store is always busy and often has a queue out front!

### Abnormal Beauty Co (The Ordinary)

A runaway success, The Ordinary and the rest of Deciem’s beauty brands have made a name for themselves by offering customers affordable but high quality skincare. I love this store and being able to shop their full range of products in one place.

title: The Nolita Guide: A Local’s Map to the Best Restaurants, Bars and Shops
author: Paul Jebara
text:
# The Nolita Guide: A Local’s Map to the Best Restaurants, Bars and Shops

The downtown neighborhood that fashion built, the Italians never left and the rest of us keep trying to crack—here’s where to eat, drink and shop in Nolita.

Read MoreSix blocks wide, four blocks tall, written in a typography all its own: Nolita is a neighborhood anomaly that ignores Manhattan's grid system and is better for it. Named streets—Mulberry, Mott, Elizabeth—replace numbers between Houston and Kenmare, Bowery and Lafayette. Federal-era row houses lean into narrow tenements with their original cornices still bolted on, while stunted London planes throw shade onto sidewalks barely wide enough to pass a stroller.

Despite its storied roots, the name itself is a 1990s real estate fabrication. Brokers stitched "NOrth of Little ITAly" together in the mid-’90s to describe the wedge that had drifted from the old immigrant neighborhood after Italian families moved to Bensonhurst and Long Island, and Chinatown pushed north. The *Times* documented the moniker in November 1996, calling it Nabokovian, and by 1998, the rebrand was already moving prices.

What the rebrand didn't cover up was four centuries of accumulated weight. Joseph-François Mangin—the same architect who drew City Hall—designed the Basilica of St. Patrick's Old Cathedral in 1809, 50 years before the Fifth Avenue version got commissioned. Martin Scorsese grew up in a third-floor walk-up on Elizabeth Street and once described the cathedral roof as "God's point of view." Sicilian and Neapolitan immigrants packed Mulberry tenements in the 1880s. The Puck Building rose in 1885 with two gilded statues of Shakespeare's sprite still scolding pedestrians from the corners. The 1909 Beaux-Arts Police Headquarters at 240 Centre Street processed every NYPD officer in the city until 1973, then became the address where Calvin Klein and Cindy Crawford kept apartments.

Today, the neighborhood is at a détente. Fourth-generation butchers work blocks from Korean noodle bars opening this May. Michelin-starred kitchens hide behind Mulberry storefronts you'd walk past. The Feast of San Gennaro turns 100 this September. Elizabeth Street Garden survived a decade-long eviction fight last fall and entered a new political phase under the incoming mayor in January. McNally Jackson's flagship moved to SoHo in 2023 (it was really just a six-block move west on Prince Street, but still). Café Gitane and its infamous avocado toast—a paragon of early aughts food Instagrams—shuttered in December after 30 years, with no warning. None of this has dulled the place. It's still one of the few corners of Manhattan where you can stumble onto a Prohibition tunnel, a fourth-generation cheesemonger handing you a number or a hidden courtyard you didn't know you were looking for, even when you're following a guide.

## An Insider's Guide to Nolita

- Estela
- The Musket Room
- Rubirosa
- Café Habana
- Boni & Mott
- Jeju Noodle Bar
- The Mulberry
- La Compagnie des Vins Surnaturels
- Spring Lounge

- Aimé Leon Dore
- Madhappy

- Di Palo's Fine Foods

- Stop by Storefront for Art and Architecture

**Where to Eat**

					
					## 
				
					**Estela**
									
			

							- 
							*47 East Houston Street, New York, NY 10012*

Ignacio Mattos has held the star and the room for a decade-plus, which in downtown years is a small geological era. The endive salad with walnuts and Ubriaco rosso is the kind of dish you order without consulting the menu. Same for the ricotta dumplings under raw mushroom and the burrata toast that launched a thousand imitations. Late-night at the bar is when the room turns over to industry—the people on the stools beside you are usually working dinner shifts elsewhere.

## 
				
					**The Musket Room**
									
			

							- 
							*265 Elizabeth Street, New York, NY 10012*

Owner Jennifer Vitagliano runs a Michelin-starred Elizabeth Street townhouse with a creative team composed entirely of women: chef Mary Attea and pastry chef Camari Mick, both named *Food & Wine* Best New Chefs in 2024. The omnivore tasting is the destination; the vegan tasting is the one critics have admitted they prefer. The bar takes walk-ins, which is where Pete Wells once observed the actual energy radiates from. Best back garden in Nolita, and that's not damning by faint praise.

## 
				
					**Rubirosa**
									
			

							- 
							*235 Mulberry Street, New York, NY 10012*

The Pappalardos have run this corner since 2009. AJ opened it as a tribute to his father Joe's Staten Island pizzeria, Joe & Pat's. After AJ died unexpectedly in 2015, his sister Maria stepped in beside their father and chef Albert Di Meglio, and the place has somehow gotten better—a sentence that should be impossible to write about a room that turns this many tables. Order the Tie-Dye pizza: vodka, marinara and pesto on a thin crust from a 57-year-old family recipe. Then the vodka rigatoni. Then a Negroni and the chocolate budino, in that order, even though no one asked.

## 
				
					**Café Habana**
									
			

							- 
							*17 Prince Street, New York, NY 10012*

Sean Meenan opened this Cuban-Mexican corner in 1998 in a former Dominican diner. Twenty-eight years later, the grilled corn—slicked with cotija, mayo, lime and chili—has not budged from the top of the order list, and neither has the Cubano, which arrives pressed flat enough to slip under a door.

## 
				
					**Boni & Mott**
									
			

							- 
							*238 Mott Street, New York, NY 10012*

Algeria-born Mehdi Mokrani opened this Mediterranean spot with his brother, Foued and cousin, Salim Ben, in 2024. Menu standouts include citrus-glazed lamb chops with amba marinade, half chicken under ras el hanout and mussels with green apple and chorizo, which sounds like a dare and lands like a thesis. The wallpaper, by neighborhood artist Pili Weeber, is a hand-drawn catalog of local landmarks: Katz's, Elizabeth Street Garden, Thai Diner.

## 
				
					**Jeju Noodle Bar**
									
			

							- 
							*204 Elizabeth Street, New York, NY 10012*

Douglas Kim's West Village original was the first noodle restaurant in America to win a Michelin star—a sentence that aged better than most 2019 sentences. The Nolita version opens in May 2026 with a Korean comfort menu built around ramyun and a handful of dishes you won't find at the original. Walking past the construction this spring, the buildout looks more ambitious than the West Village space ever was.

## Where to Drink

## 
				
					**The Mulberry**
									
			

							- 
							*240 Mulberry Street, Lower Level, New York, NY 10012*

The basement under Rubirosa, opened in 2023 by Phil Meynell, Leo Jacob and Justin Sievers, has filled the see-and-be-seen vacancy that Pravda left when it shuttered. Come for caviar service, dirty martinis with the brine pulled forward and murals by Emelie Törling. The DJ booth that runs past midnight will keep you there.

## 
				
					**La Compagnie des Vins Surnaturels**
									
			

							- 
							*249 Centre Street, New York, NY 10013*

The New York outpost of the Paris original opened in 2015 and is perhaps downtown's most serious wine room, offering a thousand-plus bottles and about 30 by the glass, and a toad-in-the-hole locals order without looking up. Experimental Cocktail Club reopened directly below it in 2025, which means you can ladder from a serious wine room to a serious cocktail room without crossing a sidewalk.

## 
				
					**Spring Lounge**
									
			

							- 
							*48 Spring Street, New York, NY 10012*

Known to its lifers as the Shark Bar—fiberglass sharks bolted to the walls, 1920s growler-shop bones, 12 craft taps. Free hot dogs on Wednesdays at 5 p.m; free bagels on Sunday afternoons. The doors swing at 8 a.m. and don't shut until 4 a.m. The morning shift feels uniquely New York City: contractors before site, off-shift bartenders before bed, the occasional novelist before deadline.

## 
				
					**Mother's Ruin**
									
			

							- 
							*18 Spring Street, New York, NY 10012*

Mother’s Ruin is open 11 a.m. to 4 a.m., every day. A frozen-cocktail slushie machine churns whatever the bar program is feeling. Menu items include a French onion soup grilled cheese and a Bronx No Resolutions that has outlasted three vodka trends. The kitchen runs until 11:30 p.m., which is why this is where the industry actually ends up after the industry's official afterparty.

## 
				
					**Onieal's Grand Street**
									
			

							- 
							*174 Grand Street, New York, NY 10013*

Chris Onieal opened this 19th-century building as a cocktail bar in 1995. The Tammany Hall-era Prohibition tunnel that once connected the basement to the old Police Headquarters across Centre Street is now the wine cellar—not a metaphor, an actual brick passage with a key. Aiden and Steve's "Scout Bar" in *Sex and the City*, for the small percentage of you who needed that note.

**Where to Shop**

					
					## 
				
					**Aimé Leon Dore**
									
			

							- 
							*224 Mulberry Street, New York, NY 10012*

Teddy Santis founded ALD in 2014, opened the original Mott store in 2016 and turned this Mulberry flagship into the gravitational center of modern Nolita after the 2023 renovation. The vintage Porsche 356 inside has its own Instagram following, which is a sentence that says something about either the car or the audience or both. Café Leon Dore next door pours an espresso the staff calls the "two one four."

## 
				
					**Madhappy**
									
			

							- 
							*207 Mulberry Street, New York, NY 10012*

The L.A. mental-health-forward label opened its first New York flagship late last year, debuting 1,800 square feet across two floors of blue-dyed concrete and Douglas fir, designed by PlayLab Inc. The ground-floor café, the Pantry, partners with Hotel Drugs for Japanese coffee, Sofreh for Persian baked goods and Tom's Juice. NYC-exclusive merch leans Yankees, Mets and Lucali—a trifecta that implies a brand strategist who rides the train.

## 
				
					**Brain Dead**
									
			

							- 
							*202 Elizabeth Street, New York, NY 10012*

Kyle Ng and Ed Davis opened the L.A. collective's first New York store in May 2025. The hippo sculpture inside is a sibling to the one at their Dover Street Market L.A. outpost—make of that what you will. Streetwear with graphics sharper than ALD's prep aesthetic and a customer base that overlaps less than the block radius would suggest.

## 
				
					**Albanese Meats & Poultry**
									
			

							- 
							*238 Elizabeth Street, New York, NY 10012*

Vincenzo and Mary Albanese opened this butcher shop in 1923. Coppola installed the now-faded red sign as set dressing for *The Godfather Part III,* and the family kept it, because of course they did. Longtime owner Moe Albanese died in 2020, but his granddaughter, Jennifer Prezioso, runs it solo now, Monday through Saturday, noon to 6 p.m. Original 1940s tile floor, original butcher block, original methods. Prezioso got married inside Elizabeth Street Garden in 2024—locals call her the unofficial mayor of the block.

## 
				
					**Goods for the Study**
									
			

							- 
							*234 and 236 Mulberry Street, New York, NY 10012*

Sarah Mcnally's stationery spinoff sprawls across two adjacent storefronts: one for paper and desk goods, one for pens and inks, both open noon to 8 p.m. daily. The McNally Jackson flagship that defined Nolita literary life moved to SoHo in 2023 after a 136 percent rent hike—a number worth pausing on—which makes Goods for the Study the under-the-radar standard-bearer for the neighborhood's bookish identity. Pick up a Blackwing 602 and a Midori notebook and pretend you've been writing all along.

## 
				
					**Di Palo's Fine Foods**
									
			

							- 
							*200 Grand Street, New York, NY 10013*

The Di Palos have been selling cheese on this corner since 1925, with origins in a 1910 latteria a few doors down. Lou, Marie and Sal Di Palo run the front, while the fifth generation runs the Enoteca next door. Lou flies to Italy multiple times a year to source, and will tell you why the pecorino he just got off a plane is the one you want, in a soliloquy that's worth the wait, whether you're buying or not.

## What to Do

## 
				
					**Visit Elizabeth Street Garden**
									
			

							- 
							*209 Elizabeth Street, New York, NY 10012*

The one-acre L-shaped sculpture garden between Prince and Spring is open and saved—for now. The late Allan Reiver built it; his son Joseph runs the nonprofit. After a decade of legal trench warfare over a proposed senior-housing project, the Adams administration designated the lot as official city parkland in November 2025. The developers sued. Mayor Mamdani took office in January, conceded that housing on the site is "nearly impossible," and his Open New York allies have pledged to undo the parkland designation this year. Open daily, free, with 150-plus public events annually. Patti Smith performed "People Have the Power" at the Olmsted Brothers gazebo last April.

## 
				
					**Tour the Catacombs at the Basilica of St. Patrick's Old Cathedral**
									
			

							- 
							*263 Mulberry Street, New York, NY 10012*

Mangin's 1815 Gothic Revival cathedral—designed by the same architect who drew City Hall—served as the seat of the Archdiocese of New York until the Fifth Avenue successor opened in 1879. The 1866 fire gutted the interior; the rebuild added the cast-iron columns still in place. Pope Benedict Xvi designated it a minor basilica in 2010. The catacombs underneath—35 family crypts and five clerical vaults holding Delmonicos, a Civil War general and the Tammany boss "Honest John" Kelly—opened to public tours run by Tommy's New York.

## 
				
					**See the New Museum's New Wing**
									
			

							- 
							*235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002*

The contemporary-art institution on Nolita's eastern edge reopened in March after a two-year closure, and the OMA-designed seven-story expansion is the biggest cultural news the neighborhood has had in a decade. Shohei Shigematsu and Rem Koolhaas designed the 60,000-square-foot annex with executive architect Cooper Robertson; the laminated-glass façade with metal-mesh interlayer roughly doubles gallery space. Tschabalala Self's four-story relief *Art Lovers* anchors the "kiss point" between buildings, while the inaugural show, *New Humans: Memories of the Future*, runs through summer with 150-plus artists.

## 
				
					**Stop by Storefront for Art and Architecture**
									
			

							- 
							*97 Kenmare Street, New York, NY 10012*

The 1993 Steven Holl and Vito Acconci pivoting-panel façade is a contemporary architectural landmark in its own right—nearly 100 feet of tapering triangular space whose hinged walls swing open onto Kenmare like a Calder mobile that someone learned to weld. Founded in 1982 by Kyong Park, Storefront has been a launching pad for downtown architectural thinking for over four decades. Pair with a New Museum visit; it's a five-minute walk and a useful palate cleanser between the two scales of building.

title: The SoHo Coffee Guide: 12 best cafes for work, rest and play — SoHo Weekly News
author: Raj Mehta
text:
SoHo’s coffee scene is compact enough to walk, competitive enough to be excellent, and varied enough to fit almost any mood, a two-hour laptop sprint, a first date, a quick cortado between errands, or a long catch-up with out-of-town friends.

What’s changed in the last few years is how purpose-built cafés have become. Some lean into hospitality for remote work, with strong Wi-Fi and seats that do not punish your back. Others are basically coffee labs, dialed in for espresso and filter with minimal fuss. And a handful play double duty as bookstores, fashion-adjacent hangouts, or all-day spaces that turn into wine bars after the workday.

This guide is organized by intent. Pick your purpose, then pick your café. Prices are typical SoHo ranges as of spring 2026, expect about $4 to $6 for drip, $5 to $7 for an iced latte, and $7 to $10 for matcha or specialty drinks. Hours and laptop policies change, especially around weekends. If you are traveling in a rush, check the café’s website or Google listing before you go.

## Best cafes in SoHo to work on a laptop with Wi-Fi

If your goal is to actually get something done, the basics matter: reliable Wi-Fi, enough seating, outlets where possible, and a room that tolerates quiet focus. These are the SoHo-area spots I recommend most often to neighbors and coworkers who ask where they can post up without feeling like they are taking someone else’s table.

- **Urban Backyard**, 180 Mulberry St (just east of SoHo in Nolita), urbanbackyardnyc.com. Typical hours: daily until around 5 pm. Why it works: varied seating, a calm interior, and a menu that goes beyond espresso, including matcha and ube. What to order: pour-over or an iced latte, plus a pastry. Typical spend: $8 to $15.
- **Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar (SoHo)**, 112 Water St is the original brand’s downtown orbit, but the SoHo outpost commonly cited by students is near the core shopping grid, butler-nyc.com. Why it works: free Wi-Fi and a welcoming attitude toward laptops. What to order: cappuccino and a pastry. Typical spend: $9 to $18.
- **Bibliotheque**, 796 Broadway, bibliothequenyc.com. Why it works: a rare hybrid, bookstore-café-wine bar. Practical detail: laptop-friendly earlier in the day, then transitions later, plan to wrap work by late afternoon. What to order: a latte or their spiced seasonal drink, then a glass of wine after. Typical spend: $10 to $25.
- **Harney & Sons SoHo**, 433 Broome St, harney.com. Why it works: if coffee spikes your anxiety, this is a tea-first alternative with plenty of seating. What to order: a pot of tea or iced tea. Typical spend: $6 to $18.
- **The Lost Draft**, 111 Elizabeth St (Little Italy/Nolita edge), thelostdraft.com. Why it works: a second-floor setup and a work-friendly vibe. What to order: cold brew and a breakfast sandwich. Typical spend: $10 to $20.

Reporting note: if you routinely need a guaranteed desk-and-outlet setup in the neighborhood, do not overlook hotel lobbies that welcome non-guests. We recently rounded up options citywide in New York hotel lobbies offer public oases for work and leisure, a useful backup plan when SoHo cafés are slammed.

## Best coffee in SoHo for espresso, pour-over, and serious beans

SoHo has no shortage of pretty cafés, but if your purpose is high-quality coffee, consistency and barista skill matter more than the wallpaper. These are the places where the coffee is the point.

- **La Cabra SoHo**, 284 Lafayette St, us.lacabra.com. Hours: Mon to Fri 7 am to 8 pm, Sat to Sun 8 am to 8 pm. Why it’s here: transparent, bar-forward service and a seasonal lineup that shines as both espresso and filter. What to order: a cardamom bun and a filter coffee, or a cortado. Typical spend: $9 to $16.
- **Gasoline Alley Coffee**, 310 Lafayette St, gasolinealleycoffee.com (or Google listing). Why it’s here: local favorite energy, strong baristas, and quick service for to-go. What to order: cappuccino. Typical spend: $6 to $12.
- **Happy Bones**, 394 Broome St, happybonesnyc.com. Why it’s here: reliably good espresso drinks in a small footprint. Best for: quick meet-ups or a caffeine stop between shops. Typical spend: $7 to $15.
- **Now or Never Coffee**, 180A Lafayette St, nowornevercoffee.com (or Google listing). Why it’s here: modern, polished coffee program, good for both espresso drinks and a sit. Typical spend: $7 to $16.
- **Felix Roasting Co. (SoHo)**, 104 Greene St, felixroastingco.com. Why it’s here: visually theatrical, but with a coffee program that can back it up. Practical detail: seating varies, but Wi-Fi is generally available. Typical spend: $10 to $25.

If you are comparing beans and brew methods, the Specialty Coffee Association’s brewing and freshness guidance is a helpful north star, especially for understanding why some cafés taste brighter or more bitter than others. See the SCA’s resources at sca.coffee.

## Best cafes in SoHo for socializing and people-watching

Sometimes the purpose is not productivity. It is a low-stakes hang, a coffee walk that turns into an hour, or a place where visiting friends can feel the neighborhood’s energy. For that, you want seating, buzz, and a menu that can stretch from coffee to food.

- **Balthazar**, 80 Spring St, balthazarny.com. Why it works: classic SoHo scene, strong bakery counter, and a room that feels like a Parisian set. Best for: an unhurried morning coffee with a pastry, or a full brunch. Typical spend: $8 for coffee and a croissant, $25 to $45 for a meal. For the deeper background, read Balthazar maintains its status as SoHo’s Parisian cornerstone.
- **Jack’s Wife Freda (SoHo)**, 224 Lafayette St, jackswifefreda.com. Why it works: upbeat brunch energy and a menu that encourages lingering. Best for: groups and visitors. Typical spend: $18 to $35 per person with coffee.
- **maman**, 239 Centre St (near the SoHo edge), mamannyc.com. Why it works: French-country aesthetic that’s friendly for catch-ups. Typical spend: $10 to $25.
- **Café Leon Dore**, 214 Mulberry St, aimeleondore.com. Why it works: street window ordering and a prime people-watching setup outside. Practical detail: it is part of a clothing store, and the vibe is as much fashion as coffee. Typical spend: $6 to $14.

Social tip: SoHo can get crowded fast on weekends. If you want conversation without shouting, aim for Friday mornings, or weekday afternoons after the lunch wave.

## Best cafes in SoHo for a quick coffee between shopping stops

SoHo is a shopping neighborhood first, which means the ideal caffeine stop is fast, close to your route, and good to go. These are the spots I send friends to when they are bouncing between Greene, Prince, Spring, and Broadway.

- **Darby Coffee Club**, 52 Prince St, darbycoffeenyc.com (or Google listing). Why it works: tiny, efficient, and excellent for a flat white to-go. Typical spend: $6 to $12.
- **Blank Street Coffee (SoHo)**, multiple small-format locations around the neighborhood, blankstreet.com. Why it works: speed and consistency when lines are long elsewhere. Typical spend: $5 to $10.
- **La Cabra SoHo**, 284 Lafayette St. Why it works: quick service even when busy, plus pastries worth detouring for.

Pair your coffee run with a retail stop. If you are on a shopping mission, our neighborhood retail coverage can help you plan a loop, including WeWearAustralian opens first global flagship store in SoHo and Babylist opens 20,000-square-foot flagship store in SoHo. For a luxury escape with grand views, consider the Queensberry tiny house.

## Best cafes in SoHo for a quiet reset and solo time

For a decompression coffee, you want softer lighting, fewer stroller traffic jams, and a room that feels like a pause button. These picks are more about mood than maximum throughput.

- **Bibliotheque**, 796 Broadway. Why it works: browse art books, sip something warm, and take a break from the street. Practical detail: arrive earlier if you want to read or work before the evening shift.
- **Harney & Sons SoHo**, 433 Broome St. Why it works: tea calm, and a slower pace than the peak espresso bars.
- **Housing Works Bookstore Cafe**, 126 Crosby St, housingworks.org/locations/bookstore-cafe. Why it works: a true neighborhood institution where purchases support Housing Works’ mission. Typical spend: $6 to $20.

If your solo time includes culture, keep an eye on local art pop-ups. Our recent coverage of SoHo loft soirée showcases emerging local artists is a reminder that the neighborhood’s creative scene still surfaces in intimate rooms.

## Best cafes in SoHo for groups, meetings, and low-key first dates

SoHo is not the easiest place to find a four-top that will not make you feel guilty. For meetings and dates, the winning formula is: seating, a menu that can escalate into food, and acoustics that let you hear each other.

- **Jack’s Wife Freda**, 224 Lafayette St. Best for: casual meetings over brunch. Tip: go earlier on weekends.
- **Balthazar**, 80 Spring St. Best for: classic date energy, especially if you upgrade to a full meal.
- **Urban Backyard**, 180 Mulberry St. Best for: a relaxed work meeting with coffee, matcha, and pastries.
- **Felix Roasting Co.**, 104 Greene St. Best for: impressing an out-of-towner with maximalist interiors, while still getting a legitimately good drink.

On the business side, SoHo’s café churn is tied to broader pressures like commercial rents. For context on the policy conversation, see New York landlords oppose commercial rent control bill.

## Map it: a one-hour SoHo coffee crawl you can do on foot

If your purpose is exploration, not settling in, here’s a simple walking crawl that hits very different styles of SoHo coffee within about an hour. Start at La Cabra (284 Lafayette St) for a filter, walk west toward Greene Street for Felix Roasting Co. (104 Greene St) if you want an espresso drink in a dramatic room, then cut down to Prince Street for Darby Coffee Club (52 Prince St) for a quick flat white to-go, and finish at Housing Works Bookstore Cafe (126 Crosby St) to browse books with a second cup.

If you are planning a full day in the neighborhood, bookmark The ultimate guide to things to do in SoHo (2026 edition) and build your coffee stops around galleries, shopping, and a late lunch.

For a cross-city reminder of how downtown neighborhoods are wrestling with housing and community needs, I’ve also been reading about projects outside New York, including Boston Mayor proposes $4.9B budget amid fiscal crunch, which underscores how budgets ripple into street-level quality-of-life everywhere.

Finally, a practical safety note: SoHo’s busy retail corridors can attract opportunistic theft. Keep your laptop bag zipped and your phone off the café table edge. Our coverage of SoHo boutique robbed of up to $2 million in luxury apparel is a timely reminder to stay alert, even on a coffee run.

title: 17 Satisfying SoHo Coffee Shops (Local's Guide)
author: Antonina
text:
SoHo in New York City is known for its charming cast-iron buildings and cobblestone streets. It’s also home to some really cute coffee shops that are worth checking out. After spending a lot of time in the neighborhood, I’ve put together a list of what I believe are the best coffee in SoHo.

Whenever my friends visit the city and stay in SoHo, this the exact list I share with them. So whether you’re looking to focus on some work or catch up with a friend, there’s a SoHo cafe for you.

**Note to the reader.** If you feel like one of the best cafes in SoHo is missing from this list, please drop me a comment below and I’ll check them out ASAP!

## Charming Cafes in SoHo

## Table of Contents. Best Coffee Shops in SoHo

### Table of Contents. Best Coffee Shops in SoHo

…

**Visiting New York City?** If you haven’t decided where to stay (yet) check out our helpful guide on ** Where to Stay in New York City (10 Best Neighborhoods +3 to Avoid)**. Don’t have time? Here’s my favorite hotel in NYC, hands down.

### Urban Backyard

**Website.** Urban Backyard **Address.** 180 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10012

If you’re a fan of succulent plants and cupcakes this the spot for you. Urban Backyard is a small oasis in the heart of Little Italy and one of the cutest cafes in SoHo. Popular for their realistic mini cupcakes with frosting piped into the shape of succulents, they’re almost too cute to eat (*almost*). 

Despite its small size, the SoHo cafe offers a unique selection of coffees and teas, making it a go-to spot for a mid-day pick-me-up. Committed to sustainability, Urban Backyard sells natural and reusable products and prepares sauces and syrups in-house with fresh ingredients.

The cozy, rustic ambiance, adorned with greenery, transforms this small space into a charming escape from the city, making it one of the it where friendly staff are ready to offer recommendations.

**Something to Note —** Urban Backyard no longer sells the mini succulent cupcakes in store. You have to pre-order them online and pick up in store.

### Cafe Leon Dore

**Website.** Cafe Leon Dore**Address.** 214 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10012

Cafe Leon Dore is a charming coffee shop in SoHo that makes you feel like you’ve stepped into a Parisian cafe. With a menu inspired by Greek coffee and treats, the distinct flavors offered by this coffee shop are unparalleled.

Their iconic Freddo cappuccino is what put them on the map and keeps New Yorkers coming back for more. One sip of their cloud-like foam and you’ll understand the hype. After many lattes, cappuccinos, and Americanos, Cafe Leon Dore is one of the best cafes in SoHo.

### Ground Support Cafe

**Website.** Ground Support Cafe**Address.** 399 W Broadway, New York, NY 10012

Ground Support Cafe offers an inviting environment filled with natural light and friendly workers. It’s not uncommon to see the SoHo coffee shop filled with happy locals catching up with friends or eagerly clicking away on their laptops, knee-deep in work.

In a world full of coffee shops touting the freshest coffees, it’s commonplace to see a lot of coffee beans go to waste. Behind the scenes, farmers are forced to cut their losses and toss any leftover beans, but Ground Support Cafe has made an effort to curb this problem.

Ground Support Cafe buys the previous season’s coffee beans, mixes them with fresh beans, and roasts them with precision to churn out incredible cups of coffee. It’s a win-win situation where they reduce waste, help local farmers recoup their losses, and the customer enjoys one of the best SoHo coffee shops!

### Gasoline Alley Coffee

**Website.** Gasoline Alley Coffee**Address.** 325 Lafayette St, New York, NY

Gasoline Alley Coffee is technically in NoHo, but it’s so good and *so close *to SoHo that it deserves a spot on our list of the it. This bright and fast-paced cafe churns out some of the best coffee in the neighborhood. Gasoline Alley is on the smaller side, but both ends of the shop open up and offer ample seating outside, so finding a spot to rest your feet won’t be a problem. The menu is simple and straight to the point; I highly recommend the iced Americano and pair it with a flakey croissant. 

**Local’s Tip.** Right next door to Gasoline Alley Coffee is Funny Face Bakery, mentioned on our list of 15 Seductive Cookies in New York City Are (Easily) Worth the Calories. Swing by and try the s’mores cookie!

### Now or Never Coffee

**Website.** Now or Never Coffee**Address.** 30 Grand St, New York, NY

Not only is Now or Never Coffee one of the it, but it’s also one of the cutest cafes in the neighborhood. In 2014, founder Sehwan quit his corporate job in search of his true passions. After brainstorming at a local coffee shop with a *life-changing* macchiato in hand, Sehwan knew that the field of coffee was his calling. 

From then, it became his personal mission to learn everything there is to know about coffee and to create something memorable, and we’re all better for it. Fast forward to 2019, Sehwan opened Now or Never Coffee, which has become one of the it.

** Unpopular opinion. ** Hot take. the best coffee in SoHo isn’t at a trendy third-wave spot. it’s at Table of Contents. it.

### Balthazar’s Bakery

**Website.** Balthazar’s Bakery **Address.** 80 Spring St, New York, NY 10012

If you’ve been dying to get brunch at the uber-famous Balthazar restaurant for quite some time but can’t seem to score a reservation, I learned a trick – visit the bakery next door! Seriously, the BEST chocolate donuts I’ve ever had – perfectly dense and chocolatey.

Oh, and the chai latte from this place can’t be missed. Although this technically a bakery, their drinks and baked goods are worth writing home about, so I feel confident in adding them to a list of the best coffee shops in SoHo.

** Local tip. ** Between you and me, the seasonal menu is always better than the regular one. Ask what’s fresh today.

### La Cabra

**Website.** La Cabra**Address.** 284 Lafayette St, New York, NY 10012

Established in 2013, La Cabra, meaning “the goat” in Spanish, has earned its reputation as the GOAT (greatest of all time) in the eyes of the hip and young, thanks to its in-house coffee roasting. Originating from Denmark, the SoHo coffee shop offers locally sourced food and exceptional coffee in a friendly atmosphere.

The cozy and inviting space mirrors traditional Danish cafe aesthetics, offering some of the best coffee in SoHo alongside incredible baked goods – a testament to La Cabra’s exceptional quality despite its small size.

### Blank Street

**Website.** Blank Street**Address.** 181 Prince St, New York, NY 10012

Blank Street Coffee in SoHo earns its reputation as one of the best coffee shops for a simple reason. exceptional quality and a welcoming vibe. They source top-notch, ethically sourced beans, and their skilled baristas craft each cup with precision. The chic yet cozy ambiance adds to the experience, making it a go-to spot for those who appreciate excellent coffee in a comfortable setting. It’s intimate and warmly lit. great for date night or a quiet meal when you need a break from the city’s pace. I’ve been coming here for years and the quality has never once dropped.

### La Colombe Coffee Roasters

**Website.** La Colombe Coffee Roasters**Address.** 154 Prince St, New York, NY 10012

### Butler

**Website.** Butler**Address.** 177 Lafayette St, New York, NY 10013

Opened in 2016 by Ryan Butler and co-founders, Butler in NYC serves up a put together menu that pairs perfectly with their top-notch Intelligentsia coffee. Known for its smoothness, this coffee comes from the reputable Chicago-based roasters Intelligentsia.

Whether it’s morning or afternoon, Butler has your perfect cup of hot or iced coffee. The sleek SoHo location, with its inviting interiors, is a popular spot for friends to chat or individuals to work on laptops. It’s a top-notch coffee shop in SoHo, offering a spacious and well-lit environment in which to enjoy your coffee with a good book.

### PlantShed

**Website.** PlantShed**Address.** 1 Prince St, New York, NY 10012 

All my fellow plant lovers will be in a state of euphoria at PlantShed. Their original Upper West Side location has been an oasis in the concrete jungle for more than 40 years. The plant craze has been in full swing over the last few years, and PlantShed has capitalized on. This by creating one of the best coffee shops in SoHo, all while basking in abundant green foliage.

The plants & flowers are also for sale, so it’s not uncommon to see folks walking out with a latte in one hand a hanging basket in another. Like the other best coffee shops in New York City, most of their locations have spaces for guests to hang out. Whether it’s to get work done or read a book, PlantShed provides a Garden of Eden-like reprieve from the bustling city.

### Citizens Cafe

For a vibrant, delicious cup of coffee, check out Citizen’s, an Australian-based cafe that opened in 2016. Co-founders Justin Giuffrida and Andrew Geisel aimed to create a community-focused space, emphasizing relationships and familiarity.

The kind staff, beautiful setting, and top-notch drinks make Citizens one of the best coffee shops in SoHo. I recommend ordering the Smashing Avocado—a really good combination of multigrain toast, pickled onion, feta, and beetroot hummus for a delicious and memorable meal.
