title: Best Coffee Shops for Meetings in NYC: How to Choose
author: Staff Writer
text:
# Best Coffee Shops for Meetings in NYC: How to Choose

**The best coffee shops for meetings** make a conversation feel smoother, sharper, and more productive. In New York City, where office space is limited and schedules move fast, cafés regularly stand in for conference rooms, catch-up spots, and low-pressure interview settings.

But not every café works for a client intro, recruiter chat, or team brainstorm. The right choice comes down to a few practical factors: **noise level, seating comfort, Wi-Fi reliability, outlet access, service speed, and location**.

This guide explains how to choose the **best coffee shops for meetings** in NYC, which neighborhoods tend to work best, and how to match the setting to the type of conversation. If you want a café that supports the meeting instead of distracting from it, start here.

## What Makes a Coffee Shop Good for Meetings?

The **best coffee shops for meetings** balance comfort, function, and tone. You need enough ambient energy to avoid awkward silence, but not so much noise that you have to repeat every sentence.

Look for tables that fit more than two drinks, chairs you can sit in for an hour, and enough breathing room between guests. If the room feels cramped or the line spills into the seating area, the meeting will feel rushed.

Service matters too. A café with quick ordering, clean tables, and a steady flow removes friction at the start of the conversation — and that small detail can set the tone for everything that follows.

### Wi-Fi, Outlets, and Table Size Matter

For working sessions, the basics matter more than aesthetics. **Reliable Wi-Fi, accessible power outlets, and tables large enough for two laptops** are what turn a nice café into a genuinely useful meeting-friendly coffee shop.

If you expect to review notes, open a deck, or share files, confirm those details before you suggest the place. Many **meeting-friendly cafés** also offer a mix of seating — from two-tops to communal tables and quieter corners.

### The Menu Should Support a Longer Stay

A strong meeting café serves more than one good drink. Coffee, tea, pastries, and light food make it easier to stay past the first 20 minutes without needing to relocate.

That matters in NYC, where a quick coffee can easily turn into a longer work conversation. The **best coffee shops for productive meetings** make that transition feel natural rather than forced.

## How to Choose the Best Coffee Shop for Your Type of Meeting

Not every meeting needs the same setup. The **best coffee shops for meetings** depend on who you are meeting, how long you plan to stay, and whether you need privacy, polish, or open space.

### Client Meetings: Polished but Relaxed

For client meetings, choose a café that feels polished, organized, and easy to find. A clean design, dependable service, and a location near transit all help create a strong first impression.

In Manhattan, business-heavy areas often work well because they offer more seating turnover and clearer logistics. Aim for a place that feels stylish without being overly crowded or scene-driven.

### Networking Chats: Lively and Approachable

For networking, some background energy is useful. A bright café with moderate foot traffic keeps the mood casual and removes the pressure that comes with a formal setting.

The **best coffee shops for networking meetings** are usually central and easy to reach. When both people are squeezing the conversation between work blocks, convenience matters as much as atmosphere, especially if you also keep tabs on networking events in Williamsburg for NYC professionals.

### Team Brainstorms: Roomy and Flexible

Creative sessions need space. If two or three people will be sharing screens, notebooks, or ideas, skip the tiny neighborhood spot with six seats and a long line.

Look instead for larger cafés, roasteries, or all-day spaces with **communal tables, natural light, and enough ambient sound** to keep the energy up. Brooklyn often works well for this style of meeting.

### Interviews or Sensitive Conversations: Quieter Corners

Some meetings call for more privacy. For interviews, feedback sessions, or delicate conversations, larger cafés, hotel coffee bars, and quieter weekday spots tend to work better than busy neighborhood staples.

Avoid peak hours when possible. Even the **best coffee shops for meetings** can fall short if the room is packed, the blender runs nonstop, or tables sit too close together.

## Best NYC Neighborhoods to Find Meeting-Friendly Coffee Shops

New York has no shortage of cafés, but some areas are better than others for a real conversation. If you are trying to find the **best coffee shops for meetings in NYC**, location matters almost as much as the café itself.

### Flatiron and Midtown for Convenience

Flatiron and Midtown are strong picks for business meetings because they sit near major subway lines and dense office clusters. You will often find more spacious cafés, hotel-adjacent coffee bars, and polished spots built for quick turnover.

These neighborhoods are useful for recruiter chats, client intros, and short professional catch-ups. The tradeoff is crowding during rush windows, so **timing your arrival matters**.

### SoHo and NoMad for a Polished, Client-Facing Feel

If presentation matters, SoHo and NoMad offer some of the **best coffee shops for client meetings** — strong design, quality menus, and an elevated atmosphere that signals professionalism without formality.

These areas suit brand meetings, creative discussions, and casual pitches. Just choose carefully. Some cafés here look great but offer limited seating, few outlets, or strict laptop policies.

### Brooklyn for Longer Creative Sessions

Williamsburg, Greenpoint, and Downtown Brooklyn often deliver on space, atmosphere, and a slower pace. These neighborhoods are good fits for freelance meetings, brainstorms, and collaborations that need more than a quick table turn.

Many Brooklyn cafés also feel less rushed than central Manhattan options. That can make a **longer work meeting easier to sustain** without pressure to move on, particularly if you already use quiet cafes for remote work in NYC as part of your routine.

### Upper West Side and Upper East Side for Quieter One-on-Ones

For calmer conversations, uptown neighborhoods can be a smart choice. They often have local cafés with more breathing room and less intense foot traffic than downtown hotspots.

Sometimes the **best coffee shops for meetings** are not the trendiest ones. They are the places where you can hear each other, stay for an hour, and leave feeling the conversation moved forward.

## Meeting Etiquette That Helps You Get Invited Back

Even the **best coffee shops for meetings** have limits. If you are using a café as a workspace, good etiquette helps both your guest and the business hosting you.

### Buy Enough and Do Not Linger Thoughtlessly

If you plan to stay a while, order like it. At minimum, each person should buy a drink. For longer meetings, add food or a second round.

This matters even more in smaller independent cafés where **table turnover keeps the room running**. If the place fills up and people are waiting, wrap up or move on.

### Arrive Early and Scout the Room

Showing up 10 minutes early can save the meeting. You can claim a better table, check outlet access, and confirm the noise level is workable before your guest arrives.

The **best coffee shops for work meetings** can feel very different at 8:30 a.m. versus 11 a.m. Build your timing around that reality.

### Keep Your Setup Minimal

A coffee shop is not a boardroom. Avoid spreading across a large table with chargers, folders, and extra devices unless the space clearly supports it.

Keep the setup light, stay aware of the room, and adjust if it gets busier. It makes the meeting feel **cleaner, more focused, and more professional**.

## How to Spot the Best Coffee Shops for Meetings Before You Commit

You may not always have time for a trial run, but a quick check helps. Before you send the invite, look at recent photos, reviews, and social tags for clues about seating, outlet access, crowd levels, and laptop policies.

The **best coffee shops for meetings** usually get described in practical terms: spacious, calm, laptop-friendly, easy to find a seat, or good for work. If reviews focus only on aesthetics, style may outweigh function.

### Questions to Ask Before You Choose

**How long will the meeting last?** A 20-minute intro can happen almost anywhere. A 90-minute strategy session needs more comfort and space.

**Do you need Wi-Fi or power?** If yes, verify both before suggesting the spot to your guest.

**How much privacy do you need?** For sensitive topics, avoid tiny, crowded cafés with tables packed together.

**Will your guest know the area?** Choose somewhere easy to locate and within walking distance of transit.

**Does the café actually welcome longer stays?** Some beautiful places are built for fast turnover, not extended work meetings.

Answer those questions first, and finding the **best coffee shops for meetings in NYC** gets much easier. For broader standards around public Wi-Fi and safe browsing, it helps to review guidance from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

## FAQ: Best Coffee Shops for Meetings

### What are the best coffee shops for meetings in NYC?

The best options are cafés with **reliable Wi-Fi, comfortable seating, moderate noise levels, and easy transit access**. In NYC, Flatiron, Midtown, NoMad, SoHo, and parts of Brooklyn consistently offer strong meeting-friendly choices across different budgets and styles.

### Are coffee shops good for business meetings?

Yes. They work well for client intros, networking chats, interviews, and quick team check-ins. **Coffee shops work best when the meeting does not require full privacy** and the café has enough space to stay comfortable for the duration.

### What should I look for in a coffee shop for a work meeting?

Focus on **table size, seating comfort, noise level, Wi-Fi quality, outlet availability, cleanliness, and transit access**. A good meeting café should feel easy and functional, not distracting.

### How long should you stay at a coffee shop for a meeting?

Most coffee shop meetings work best at **30 to 90 minutes**. If you expect to stay longer, order more than one item and avoid peak rush periods to respect the space and other customers.

### What time is best for a coffee shop meeting in NYC?

**Late morning (10–11:30 a.m.) and mid-afternoon (2–4 p.m.)** are often the safest windows. Avoid the early commuter rush and the lunch peak if you want better seating options and a manageable noise level.

### Can you use a coffee shop for a job interview?

Yes, for informal or first-round interviews. Choose a **quieter café during off-peak hours**, arrive early to secure a corner table, and pick a location that is easy for both parties to reach. Avoid loud or trendy spots where privacy is limited.

## Choose the Space as Carefully as the Agenda

In a city built on movement, the **best coffee shops for meetings** offer something genuinely useful: a place to slow down enough to connect, plan, and make progress.

Start with the basics — easy location, enough space, manageable noise, and a menu that supports the time you need. Then match the setting to the moment, whether that means polished and central, creative and roomy, or quiet and local.

**Choose the café with intention, and the meeting usually goes better.** If coffee meetings are part of your NYC routine in 2026, keep this guide handy before you send the next calendar invite.

title: The Best Coffee Shops in New York City | Wit & Whimsy
author: Meghan
text:
There is no shortage of cute coffee shops across New York but I definitely play favorites when it comes to getting my caffeine fixes. When it comes to the best coffee shops in New York City, I personally don’t ever go to Starbucks unless I’m at an airport as I’d personally rather support smaller, more boutique shops when I’m spending my money on coffee.

That being said I now typically make my own coffee given I work from home but when scheduling coffee catch up dates or meetings, the following locales are those I can’t get enough of. I’ve lived in New York City for over fourteen years so these spots have been curated over the years of (a lot) of coffee intake.


## The Best Coffee Shops in New York City

If you’re looking for a great list of the best coffee shops in New York City, look no further. I’ve rounded up nearly thirty spots across New York City that I rely on when I am looking for the next good cup of coffee.

### Arabica

They serve my favorite espresso drinks in the city, hands down. They’ve expanded a lot over the years – and are originally from Japan but their iced lattes and iced americanos are divine. You’ll often find me at their Dumbo location which boasts great views.

### La Cabra

This Danish café is a hit among tech workers and coffee aficionados for its high-end pour-overs and minimalist aesthetic. Known for cult-favorite pastries like cardamom buns (they’re so good!), it’s earned a dedicated following and now has locations in Soho and East Williamsburg.

### Coffee Project

This East Village spot is a great little hole in the wall friendly establishment. They have killer cold brew and one of my favorite almond croissants in the city.

### Bluestone Lane

This Aussie cafe popped up all over Brooklyn and Manhattan and is super popular for good reason. They make an awesome flat white and their avocado toast is some of my favorite in the city.

People also love the matcha latte served here. This is a favorite spot of mine for breakfast meetings.

### Ferrane Bakery

This work-friendly bakery also serves up solid cups of coffee that pair perfectly with their delightful cinnamon buns and cardamom buns.

### Prodigy Coffee

This spot used to be my go-to when heading into the office at my last job but it’s good I no longer frequent it as much because I couldn’t resist their banana bread. It is to die for! Nestled on a charming street in the West Village their coffee is delicious and I adore their decor.

### Ludlow Coffee Supply

Whenever I find myself on the Lower East Side, I am sure to pop in to this rustic, laid back spot that delivers great coffee.

### Partners Coffee

This establishment was – until a few years ago was – called Toby’s and they serve delicious coffee in beautiful spaces. Their West Village location is such a good spot to get a cup and a pastry and sit down to enjoy reading or catching up on email.

You’ll also find locations in Williamsburg, Long Island City and other neighborhoods throughout the city.

### Bar Pisellino

On a charming corner in the West Village, I love to enjoy the Italian coffees at this spot at one of their outdoor tables. This is a true personal favorite spot of mine to enjoy regularly. It’s like a little visit to Italy without ever leaving NYC.

### Felix Roasting

When visiting Soho and in need of a good coffee spot to catch up with friends, this bright and airy spot has loads of seating to enjoy. They also have a smaller location near Madison Square Park.

### Intelligentsia Coffee

If you’re in Chelsea and looking for a charming, tucked away spot, head to the Highline Hotel and inside you’ll find a little Intelligentsia Coffee coffee bar.

### Ralph’s Coffee

This cute spot used to be nestled in the Ralph Lauren store on Fifth Avenue, but then the store closed, the coffee endeavor shuttered, too. Thankfully the coffee was so popular that Ralph Lauren has now opened shops on Madison Avenue in their Women’s Store, in the Flatiron on Lower Fifth and a semi-permanent coffee cart at Rockefeller Center.

Each location is an Instagram dream and remains a favorite spot of mine to meet up with friends for a coffee catch up date. And while they’ve since opened up around the world in various locations like London and Paris, the originals in New York feel very “only in New York.”

Do I think its amazing coffee? No. But the branding wins me over every time.

### Blue Bottle Coffee

A few outposts of this San Francisco coffee chain exist across New York and serve up delightful, strong cups of specialty coffee in bright, airy spots. For true coffee aficionados, their elegant design and quality pours, like macchiatos and filter coffee, tend to impress every time.

### Mud

An East Village favorite of mine. It’s the only place in New York I take my iced coffee with milk *and *sugar because it is just so darn good.

### The Elk

If you’re looking for a cozy and quaint coffee shop off the beaten path, head to The Elk. It is tucked away on a tree lined street close to the Hudson River in the West Village and I personally love to enjoy their cold brew while parked on one of their cute benches outside.

### Maman

Their cups are just the best! The French inspired cafes have since popped up all over NYC and are cozy and casual and the pastries are not to be missed.

### Butler

I love this spot’s strong cold brew. There are a few locations around the city including a popular outpost in Dumbo, Brooklyn.

### Fellini Coffee

An adorable corner coffee shop in the West Village. It has the smallest footprint in real estate but makes up for it in charm. They are serving up great coffee and their little corner tables make for the perfect spot to people watch.

You’ll find another location in Soho now, too.

### Stumptown Coffee Roasters

This spot’s nitro cold brew may as well be rocket fuel so if I have a big day, I head here. Their Greenwich Village and Cobble Hill locations are favorites of mine. I always love the bustling vibe on weekends at their Greenwich Village location.

If you visit the Cobble Hill outpost and are looking for other good spots to enjoy in the neighborhood, don’t miss my What To Do in Cobble Hill, Brooklyn guide.

### Cafe Kitsune

One of my Paris favorites (via Japan) opened a bright and airy spot in the West Village. They also now have a location in Boreum Hill, Brooklyn.

### Oslo Coffee

This small craft company serves up artisan brews at a few locations in New York City.

### Joe Coffee

Delicious signature coffees and warm, welcome staff, this spot’s Brooklyn Heights location is a favorite for a cup of joe. Their baked goods are pretty reliable as well. Not the best but good when you need something.

### La Colombe

Great coffee and reliable baked goods, La Colombe has outposts throughout the city including neighborhoods like the Financial District. They are well known for their Draft Lattes.

. . .

For those of you in New York – what do you think are the best coffee shops in New York City? I’d love to hear your favorites!

title: Best Breakfast Meeting Spots NYC: Top Morning Picks
author: Staff Writer
text:
# Best Breakfast Meeting Spots NYC: Top Morning Picks

**The best breakfast meeting spots NYC professionals rely on share one quality: they make the meeting easier, not harder.** In New York, morning meetings often outperform long lunches or late drinks. They are easier to schedule, easier to keep on time, and sharper in focus.

The right venue should feel polished but not stiff, efficient but not rushed, and impressive without being overdone. Whether you are meeting a client, interviewing a candidate, or catching up with a colleague, the setting shapes the outcome.

This guide covers what to look for in a **business breakfast spot in NYC**, which neighborhoods make the most sense, and how to match the venue to the meeting goal.

## What Makes the Best Breakfast Meeting Spots NYC Professionals Actually Use?

Not every great breakfast place works for business. A packed brunch café may serve excellent food, but loud music and tight tables can derail any conversation before it starts.

The **best breakfast meeting spots NYC** professionals return to consistently share a few traits: easy transit access, prompt service, reliable coffee, and enough space to talk without straining to hear.

### Look for a Balanced Atmosphere

A strong venue feels lively, not chaotic. Hotel dining rooms, polished all-day cafés, and classic breakfast rooms often get this balance right.

**Energy helps. Noise hurts.** If you have to repeat yourself across the table, it is not the right place for a working breakfast.

### Prioritize Timing and Service

Morning meetings run on tight schedules. Slow lines, long ticket times, and brunch-style waits can throw off the entire plan.

The best places for breakfast meetings in NYC typically open by 7 or 8 a.m., seat guests quickly, and bring coffee fast. That keeps the meeting moving and the agenda on track.

### Choose Menus With Range

Some breakfast meetings are quick coffee conversations. Others are full sit-down discussions. Good venues make both easy.

**A business-friendly breakfast menu should offer flexibility** — pastries, eggs, oatmeal, fruit, and lighter options. Variety lets guests order what feels comfortable without overthinking it. For more café-specific criteria, see how to choose coffee shops for meetings in NYC.

## Best Neighborhoods for Breakfast Meetings in NYC

Location matters almost as much as the restaurant itself. Few people want a long cross-town trip before 9 a.m., so a smart **NYC breakfast meeting venue** should feel practical for everyone involved.

### Midtown for Convenience and Client Meetings

Midtown remains one of the strongest choices for business breakfasts. It suits finance, legal, media, and corporate schedules, and it offers a wide range of polished hotel restaurants and weekday-friendly cafés.

For guests arriving by train or heading straight to an office tower, Midtown is often the safest pick. Many of the **best breakfast meeting spots NYC** workers rely on are clustered near Grand Central, Bryant Park, and the Plaza District.

### Flatiron and NoMad for Creative Professionals

Flatiron and NoMad feel business-ready without feeling rigid. They work well for founders, consultants, editors, marketers, and brand teams who want style with structure.

You will find design-forward cafés, hotel dining rooms, and all-day spots that make a strong first impression while still supporting real, focused conversation.

### SoHo and Tribeca for Low-Key Polish

For meetings with creative clients, agency partners, or out-of-town guests, SoHo and Tribeca offer a more curated mood. Settings here often feel elevated, calm, and visually polished.

**These neighborhoods work best when image matters** but you still want a relaxed, comfortable tone throughout the meeting.

### Downtown Brooklyn for Practical Hybrid Meetups

In 2026, Downtown Brooklyn remains a useful **breakfast meeting zone** for professionals moving between boroughs. It offers strong café culture, easier pacing, and far less Midtown intensity.

For freelancers, recruiters, startup teams, and hybrid workers, it can be a smart and efficient alternative to Manhattan.

## Types of Breakfast Meeting Spots That Work Best in NYC

The phrase **best breakfast meeting spots NYC** does not point to one type of venue. The right choice depends entirely on the purpose of the meeting.

### Hotel Restaurants for Polished First Impressions

Hotel breakfast rooms are often the most reliable option for client-facing meetings. They typically open early, offer full table service, and accept reservations — three things that matter when the stakes are high.

They also send the right signal. If you are pitching, interviewing, or hosting a senior contact, a hotel setting makes the meeting feel deliberate and well-considered.

### All-Day Cafés for Casual Networking

For mentoring chats, informal coffee meetings, or low-key team check-ins, all-day cafés often hit the right note. Look for spots with enough seating, a calm soundtrack, and service that does not feel rushed or indifferent.

**The best breakfast meeting cafés in NYC** make it easy to talk, order, and leave on schedule without any friction. The NYC restaurant grading system can also be a useful final check when narrowing down options.

### Classic New York Breakfast Rooms for Reliability

There is still real value in an old-school breakfast room. Familiar dishes, attentive service, and a composed dining room can put people at ease quickly.

These venues work especially well in industries where tradition still carries weight. They feel dependable — which is often exactly the point of choosing them.

### Bakery-Cafés for Short, Efficient Catch-Ups

Not every meeting needs a full meal. Sometimes a bakery-café is the smarter choice, especially for internal check-ins or quick networking introductions where time is limited.

This format works best when the goal is speed, convenience, and a low-pressure setting that keeps things moving.

## How to Choose the Right Spot for Different Meeting Goals

Choosing among the **best breakfast meeting spots NYC** offers gets easier when you start with the outcome. Ask what the meeting needs to accomplish before you pick the venue.

### For Client Meetings, Choose Polish and Predictability

If the goal is to build trust or make a strong impression, choose a venue with reservations, full table service, and a broad but simple menu. Avoid places known for long waits or high volume during weekday mornings.

**Professionalism often comes down to removing friction.** Your guest should be focused on the conversation, not the logistics of getting seated or flagging down a server.

### For Interviews or Recruiting Chats, Keep It Calm

A breakfast interview should feel welcoming, not tense. Choose a venue with enough privacy for a serious discussion but without so much formality that it feels heavy or intimidating.

Look for comfortable seating, steady service, and a menu that is easy to navigate — especially for someone who may already be nervous.

### For Internal Team Meetings, Keep It Efficient

When meeting coworkers before office hours, convenience matters most. Pick a spot near transit or near the office, with fast service and a straightforward menu that does not slow anyone down.

The best **business breakfast spots in NYC** succeed because they respect the clock. People should be able to meet, eat, and move on with the day without feeling like they lost an hour. If your team sometimes prefers a less formal setup, these quiet cafes for remote work in NYC can offer a helpful alternative.

### For Networking, Choose Energy Without Noise

Networking breakfasts benefit from a room with a little life to it. Some background buzz can ease awkwardness and make the meeting feel natural rather than forced.

Still, volume should stay low enough for clear conversation. Stylish cafés and flexible hotel lounges tend to strike this balance best for **professional morning meetings in NYC**.

## Practical Tips for Booking Breakfast Meetings in NYC

Even the **best breakfast meeting spots NYC** can disappoint if the details are off. A few simple choices can make the entire meeting feel sharper from the moment you walk in.

### Book Ahead When Possible

If the restaurant takes reservations, use them. Weekday breakfast slots in business-heavy areas fill quickly, especially Tuesday through Thursday when demand peaks.

A confirmed table removes uncertainty and helps everyone arrive settled and ready to focus.

### Arrive 10 Minutes Early

Getting there first gives you time to assess the room, request a better table if needed, and order coffee before your guest arrives. It also gives you a backup window if the space feels louder than expected.

**Arriving early reads as prepared — and in a business context, that matters.**

### Choose Seats With Intention

A booth, banquette, or corner table usually works better than a small two-top in the center of a busy room. If you expect to review a document or open a laptop, ask for more surface space when you arrive.

### Keep the Order Simple

Unless the breakfast is clearly social, simple dishes work best. Coffee, tea, eggs, toast, yogurt, oatmeal, and pastries keep attention on the conversation rather than the food.

**Heavy or messy orders can slow the pace and create unnecessary distraction** during what should be a focused, productive meeting.

## FAQ: Best Breakfast Meeting Spots NYC

### What are the best breakfast meeting spots NYC professionals prefer?

The **best breakfast meeting spots NYC** professionals prefer offer early hours, prompt service, comfortable seating, strong coffee, and a moderate noise level. Hotel restaurants, polished cafés, and classic breakfast rooms are consistently the safest choices for business use.

### Where should I have a business breakfast in NYC?

Midtown is ideal for convenience and corporate meetings. Flatiron, NoMad, SoHo, and Tribeca work well for creative or client-facing breakfasts. Downtown Brooklyn suits many hybrid teams and borough-crossing professionals in 2026.

### Are hotel restaurants good for breakfast meetings in NYC?

Yes. Hotel restaurants are strong choices because they open early, provide polished table service, and typically offer more space and quiet than neighborhood cafés. They are especially useful for client meetings, pitches, and interviews.

### How early should I schedule a breakfast meeting in NYC?

Most **NYC breakfast meetings** work best between 8:00 and 9:30 a.m. That window allows enough time for a real conversation while still fitting comfortably into a normal workday schedule.

### Should I make a reservation for a breakfast meeting in NYC?

Yes, whenever the venue allows it. A reservation reduces wait time, creates a smoother arrival experience, and helps the meeting start on schedule — all of which reflect well on the person who organized it.

### What should I look for in a breakfast meeting venue in NYC?

Look for early opening hours, reliable coffee, table service or fast counter service, manageable noise levels, and seating that gives you enough space and privacy to hold a real conversation. **Transit access and proximity to your guest's office or commute route** should also factor into the decision.

## Start Planning Smarter Morning Meetings in NYC

Finding the **best breakfast meeting spots NYC** offers is less about hype and more about fit. The right venue helps you think clearly, speak comfortably, and move through the morning with confidence.

Start with the neighborhood, match the setting to the purpose of the meeting, and choose a place that respects the pace of the workday. **Save this guide before your next client breakfast, interview, or team catch-up** so your next morning meeting starts on the right note.

Felix Roasting Company is a haven for Instagram enthusiasts! It stands out as one of the cutest cafés in NYC, offering many opportunities for captivating photos. In a city where a coffee shop graces nearly every corner, Felix elevates the standard in hospitality, comfort, and flavor, turning the ordinary into the extraordinary. Adorned with velvet-lined booths and colorful ceiling tiles, it’s not only one of the cutest cafés in NYC but also one of the most refined.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: Multiple locations

## 3. Butler Bakeshop

Their sleek and beautifully designed interior makes this one of the cutest cafés in NYC. Their SoHo location is often filled with friends catching up or individuals engrossed in their work. With ample seating and abundant natural light, it’s an ideal spot for a coffee break in the city.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: Multiple locations

## 4. Plowshares Coffee

Plowshares Coffee boasts a spacious interior with plenty of seating, adorned with an abundance of plants. The large windows flood the café with natural light, making it a perfect spot for people-watching. Roasting their own coffee beans and offering a thoughtfully curated menu of expertly crafted drinks, this quaint café is worth a visit.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 2730 Broadway, New York, NY 10025

## 5. Remi Flower & Coffee

Remi Flower & Coffee is a place where coziness meets comfort. This coffee spot also doubles as a floral shop, making it one of the cutest cafés in NYC. Specializing in the most beautiful hand-tied flower arrangements, their coffee follows suit. The latte art alone is worth writing home about. New York City doesn’t skimp when it comes to coffee, and Remi Flower & Coffee proves this to be true. There’s something undeniably posh about sipping your coffee, gazing at the city views, and being surrounded by gorgeous flowers. It’s easy to lose track of time daydreaming in this charming New York City café…


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 906 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10017

## 6. PlantShed SoHo

For fellow plant enthusiasts, PlantShed is a sanctuary. Their original Upper West Side location has been an oasis in the concrete jungle for over 40 years. The SoHo branch, however, is home to one of the most charming cafés in NYC. Riding the wave of the plant craze, PlantShed created a space where you can enjoy some of the finest coffee in New York City amidst lush greenery. Plants and flowers are also available for purchase, so it’s not unusual to see patrons leaving with a latte in one hand and a hanging basket in the other. Most of their locations offer ample space for guests to bring their laptops and settle in, whether to work or read a book. PlantShed provides a veritable Garden of Eden, offering a peaceful respite from the bustling city.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: Multiple locations in New York City

## 7. Ralph’s Coffee

Located in the Upper East Side, Ralph’s Coffee exudes opulence and exquisitely captures a charming, retro atmosphere. This café ranks among the most endearing in New York City, as evidenced by the perennially long lines. It’s easy to understand why both locals and visitors are drawn to this café. Between the sophisticated decor and exceptional coffee (crafted with La Colombe beans), you’ll feel like a million bucks. While there are a few outdoor tables for lounging, don’t expect to find an empty seat easily; they tend to fill up quickly. Feel free to pair a delectable baked good with your coffee and take a few unhurried moments to watch the world go by. This is one of the most charming cafés in NYC, especially on a brisk autumn day.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 888 Madison Ave, New York, NY 10021

## 8. Citizens Coffee

One of the cutest cafés in NYC is Citizens Coffee. This Australian-influenced café prides itself on fostering a sense of community by creating a safe space to savor a delectable cup of coffee. Whenever I visit Citizens Coffee, I’m met with a warm welcome from a staff member who consistently goes above and beyond. The affable staff, scrumptious fare, and the café’s overall charm make it a place I keep returning to. The interior is vibrant and well-lit, adorned with verdant plants and playful tiled floors. Citizens Coffee has truly mastered the art of crafting a welcoming environment.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: Multiple locations

## 9. Sweet Moment

If you ever find yourself in Chinatown with a hankering for dessert, be sure to swing by Sweet Moment. This is one of the most endearing cafés in NYC, and the treats here are unlike anything I’ve ever had before. I initially came here for the matcha latte after spotting their latte art on Instagram. However, when I stepped inside and saw the Bingsoo (milk shaved ice), I promptly changed my order to indulge in dessert instead. Bingsoo, a beloved South Korean snack, features shaved ice crowned with fruit and ice cream. If your mouth isn’t watering at the mere thought of it, I’m not sure what to tell you (only half-kidding). The café offers ample seating and a penchant for K-Pop. During my visit, I was pleasantly surprised to see both younger and older generations congregating at this delightful café in New York City. But once I sampled the Bingsoo, it all made perfect sense.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 106 Mott St, New York, NY 10013

## 10. Urban Backyard

If you’re a fan of succulent plants and cupcakes, Urban Backyard is the place to be. This small oasis in the heart of Little Italy is one of the most enchanting cafes in New York City. Famous for their lifelike mini cupcakes with frosting sculpted into the shape of succulents, they’re almost too adorable to eat. Offering a range of unique coffees and teas, Urban Backyard is my go-to spot when I’m in the area and need a mid-day pick-me-up.Urban Backyard strives to be a sustainable business and sells natural, reusable products. They also prepare all their sauces and syrups in-house, so drinks are made with fresh ingredients. The space may be small, but they’ve managed to transform a concrete room into a cozy, rustic escape from the city. Size doesn’t hinder this coffee shop from being one of the most delightful cafes in NYC. You’ll find greenery sprinkled all over this cafe, and the employees are always eager to give suggestions, so don’t hesitate to ask for help.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 180 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10012

## 11. Davelle

Davelle is a Japanese-style café, serving delectable food, including Instagram-worthy toast. The café is on the cozier side, accommodating perhaps ten people inside, along with a few tables outside. Given that this is one of the most charming cafés in NYC, almost everything you order perfectly matches the aesthetic. Offering an array of toast flavors, you can opt for something savory like ham and egg or something sweet like berry and cream cheese. Alongside the famous toasts, their menu boasts a selection of Japanese dishes and drinks (the matcha is exquisite).


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 102 Suffolk St, New York, NY 10002

## 12. Ladurée

Laduree offers five locations to choose from, making it easier than ever to find one of the most charming cafés in New York City. Renowned for their macarons, Laduree has garnered a dedicated following for good reason—these are some of the finest in the city. The ambiance is quintessentially Parisian, creating a perfect space to unwind in the midst of the city’s hustle and bustle. Laduree’s hot chocolate strikes a delightful balance for those who prefer a taste of genuine chocolate in their drink without overwhelming richness. Regardless of your reason for stopping by, you’re in for a treat at one of the most charming cafés in NYC.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: Multiple locations

## 13. Café Flor

Café Flor is a roomy café that’s ideal for enjoying coffee and tackling work during the day, or for gathering with friends and unwinding with a glass of wine in the evening. This lovely café in NYC is part coffee shop, part retail shop, selling floral arrangements and home decor. The moment you step inside Cafe Flor, you’re greeted with an intoxicating blend of coffee and flowers, so if you’re sensitive to scents, this may not be the spot for you. The café is adorned with blooms, and the art on the walls is exceptional. There’s an abundance of seating, so finding a table to savor a bite or drink shouldn’t pose a problem. You’ll discover bistro chairs and verdant leather booths that enhance the charm of this one of the most charming cafés in New York City. Cafe Flor is laptop-friendly, and outlets are readily accessible, so expect to find New Yorkers hard at work with a superb cup of coffee close by.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 218 8th Ave, New York, NY 10011

## 14. Devoción

Devoción delivers some of the best coffee in one of the most delightful cafés in NYC. After meticulously selecting coffee plantations in Colombia, the team at Devoción mills their coffee at their Bogotá warehouse. Through overnight shipping, it reaches Brooklyn for in-house roasting. From there, it’s prepared to order and finds its way into your cup, all within roughly 10 days. With several locations around NYC, I tend to frequent the Williamsburg location most, as it exudes a cozy ambiance with exposed brick and warm lighting. A word of caution, though—since this is one of the cutest cafés in NYC, finding seating (at times) can be a challenge.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: Multiple locations

## 15. Milk + Roses

Nestled in the heart of Greenpoint, Brooklyn, you’ll find the enchanting Milk + Roses—a place that feels straight out of a storybook. While it transforms into a bustling restaurant by night, its daytime atmosphere is decidedly more relaxed and inviting.


View this post on Instagram


**Location**: 1110 Manhattan Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11222

## Map of The Cutest Cafés in NYC

As promised, find here a map to some of the cutest cafés in NYC. Any new recommendations to my list? Let me know in the comments below. Happy exploring!

title: 25 Most Instagrammable Cafes In New York City (From A Local!)
author: Charlotte Dow

text:
# 25 Of The Most Instagrammable Cafes in NYC

This post contains affiliate links, including Amazon affiliate links. If you purchase through these links, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. As an Amazon Associate, I earn from qualifying purchases. Thank you for your support!

**Instagrammable cafes in NYC** abound, especially ones that serve a delicious cup of coffee, as well.

Because here’s the thing:

While the show *Friends* may not have been the most accurate portrayal of life in New York City, they got one thing right: New Yorkers love a good cafe.

You’ll find coffee shops, tea rooms, and general caffeination stations on almost every corner in the five boroughs.

Aside from serving great beverages and pastries, some of these cool cafes in NYC make great spots for Instagram grid-worthy photos that will make every major coffee chain devotee jealous.

To help you explore some of the most beautiful cafes in NYC, check out the following list — created by a local New York influencer and photographer.

You can also grab my free **Ultimate Travel Planning Kit** — which also includes a Google Map of this Instagrammable NYC cafes itinerary. Add the map to your phone to have it ready to go!

📸 **Want to capture your time in New York through photography?** I offer **Professional NYC Photoshoots** and **NYC Influencer Shoots** through my company, NYC Photo Journeys. With both, you’ll get a customized private photoshoot and 100+ images to keep.

🥘 **NYC Food Tours:** One of the best ways to taste — and photograph — a bunch of great local NYC food spots is to book a tour, like a:

–**Brooklyn Pizza Walk**

–**Chelsea Market & High Line Food Tour**

–**Chinatown & Little Italy Food Fest**

➡️ **Click here for a full list of food and drink tours in NYC**!

## Instagrammable Cafes In NYC: Manhattan

### 1. Felix Roasting Co.

*450 Park Avenue South / NoMad*

No guide to New York would be complete without mentioning a few of the fun cafes in NYC.

This new addition to NoMad — designed by famed interior designer Ken Fulk — gives off a classic vibe while remaining a little quirky.

Distinct pink and blue walls blend with classic wooden bookcases and museum-worthy portraits to make you feel like you’re in the library of a slightly eccentric millionaire, and not just one of the best cafes in Manhattan.

You also won’t find any cumbersome milk carafes here; Felix keeps several milk selections — including almond milk — on tap for self-service.

Visiting NYC in winter or in search of rainy day activities?

You could easily spend a few hours warming up in this beautiful space with a hot beverage and a book (or your smartphone!).

### 2. Two Hands

*251 Church St / Tribeca *

Looking for an Australian-inspired cafe in NYC?

Two Hands is a bright and airy cafe with smoothies, coffee, and Instagrammable brunch fare.

Grab one of their breakfast dishes — served all day — or sandwiches to fuel up for your next round of adventures.

Along with their Tribeca location, you can also visit them in NoHo, Manhattan, and Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

### 3. The Butcher’s Daugher

*19 Kenmare Street / Nolita*

Another Instagrammable Manhattan cafe is The Butcher’s Daughter. This restaurant serves healthy and delicious vegan and vegetarian fare for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

In addition to their mouth-watering menu, they have a wide selection of coffee, juices, and smoothies.

The Butcher’s Daughter also has locations in the West Village and Williamsburg.

They are all among New York’s most Instagrammable cafes!

### 4. Chillhouse

*149 Essex Street / Lower East Side*

Pioneers in the self-care industry, Chillhouse is probably most well-known for their millennial-friendly massages and manicures.

The spa is also home to a very Instagramable cafe serving lattes with adaptogenic powders and healthy snacks for maximum chill. Between the spa and the menu, Chillhouse is one of the most unique cafes in NYC.

Get some photos with their signature neon signs and browse the shop for unique self-care products while you’re there.

### 5. Jack’s Wife Freda

*226 Lafayette Street / SoHo*

Jack’s Wife Freda is a cute and colorful all-day cafe in SoHo, with additional locations that have opened in the West Village, Chelsea, and Williamsburg. It’s one of the most popular cute coffee shops in NYC, though they serve up so much more than just coffee.

Their menu ranges from typical brunch classics to sandwiches to inventive Mediterranean-inspired fare. This is one of the best unique restaurants in New York that serves something for everyone.

It’s a great place for brunch with friends, but an equally good spot for a cozy and intimate dinner.

### 6. Urban Backyard

*180 Mulberry Street / Lower East Side*

Committed to environmental and social responsibility, Urban Backyard brings the outdoors inside for weary New Yorkers and tourists alike. In our opinion, it’s one of the coolest cafes in NYC.

Sip on their sustainably-sourced coffee while snapping photos on their tiny front patio, complete with plants and vintage furnishings.

Bonus: This is a great spot if you’re looking for places to go by yourself in NYC without feeling awkward.

### 7. Variety Coffee Roasters

*261 Seventh Avenue / Chelsea*

One of five locations throughout Manhattan and Brooklyn, this cafe feels like an updated version of a classic New York coffee shop, from its vintage neon sign out front to its minimalist interior design.

Grab some of their signature beans to keep your buzz going at home.

### 8. Matchaful

*359 Canal Street / SoHo*

One cafe trend gaining steam (pun intended) in New York City is the rise of matcha, a finely ground powder of specially grown green tea leaves that contain tons of antioxidants.

One of the cutest places to get your matcha on in Manhattan is Matchaful, a new addition to SoHo NYC that features lush green interiors to match their signature drinks.

Sip your latte and snap some photos in their adorable corner lounge.

### 9. Cha Cha Matcha

*1158 Broadway / NoMad*

Another major player on the New York matcha scene is Cha Cha Matcha, with three locations in Manhattan.

The NoMad location features their signature pink and green interiors with a good helping of neon and vintage travel posters. We think it’s one of the best cute cafes in Manhattan!

Their matcha frozen yogurt doubles as a unique way to cool off in the warmer months and a cute Instagram prop.


Need help capturing amazing memories in NYC — with you in the photos? Book a private NYC Photo Journeys a walking tour that includes photos of your group to keep. Or upgrade your Instagram feed with an NYC Influencer Shoot or a Professional New York City Shoot. Email [email protected] with inquiries.

### 10. Slate Cafe

*121 Madison Avenue / NoMad *

This Instagrammable spot in NYC features cozy-chic vibes, soft natural light, and aesthetic details like mint-green accents, exposed brick, and tufted leather seating.

And the menu is just as photogenic. You’ll find colorful breakfast plates like avocado toast topped with radish, sweet toast layered with coconut almond butter and fresh strawberries, and s’mores-style treats.

For drinks, expect the regular coffee beverages alongside matcha lattes, rose lattes, and iced drinks served in mason jars.

### 11. Pietro NoLita

*174 Elizabeth Street / Nolita*

Stepping inside Pietro Nolita is a bit like walking into a Barbie Dreamhouse. It’s no wonder it’s one of the most loved cute coffee shops in Manhattan!

This all-pink-everything cafe features a menu of updated Italian classics, unique cocktails, and, of course, coffee.

The pink benches and graffitied door outside the cafe’s entrance are particularly popular spots for Instagram photoshoots.

### 12. Ralph’s Coffee

*888 Madison Avenue / Upper East Side*

Conveniently attached to the Ralph Lauren Women’s Store and across from their Men’s Flagship Store, the brand’s cafe is worth a visit on its own.

You’ll feel as if you’re sipping your coffee in the dining room of an Upper East Side penthouse inside this swanky cafe that mirrors the brand’s preppy style.

The quality of the drinks and snacks available proves that this spot isn’t just a gimmick, though.

### 13. McNally Jackson

*52 Prince Street / SoHo*

This expansive independent bookstore and hub for all things literary is already a must-visit for book lovers visiting New York City, but the shop’s attached cafe is definitely worth a stop.

The cafe is a tribute to books, with pages lining the walls and novels hanging from the ceiling among the lights.

Fold down one of the little book-like tables for a photoshoot that will make all your fellow word nerds jealous.

### 14. Citizens of Chelsea

*401 W 25th Street / Chelsea*

This Australian-owned coffee shop and cafe in Chelsea has a bright, light-filled interior with hanging plants, making it a very Instagrammable spot.

On the menu is all-day breakfast, sandwiches and bowls for lunch, and an extensive coffee menu.

This cute cafe in New York is the perfect place to fuel up before walking the Chelsea High Line or popping into the many art galleries throughout the neighborhood.

## Beautiful Cafes In NYC: Brooklyn

### 15. Gertie

*357 Grand Street / Williamsburg*

If you’re looking for cute cafes in Brooklyn, make Gertie your first stop. This light and airy Williamsburg cafe offers a great selection of food served all day alongside colorful 50s and 60s-inspired art.

Feeling particularly retro? Grab a classic egg cream and pose for photos with the cafe’s signature mural. Gertie is absolutely one of the most Instagram-worthy restaurants in NYC!

### 16. Devocion USA

*69 Grand Street / Williamsburg*

On those dreary winter days when spring feels too far away and you’re just dying to see something green, Devocion has got you covered, as one of the best cute coffee shops in New York City.

This light-filled shop specializing in Colombian coffee brings the garden inside with a huge green wall and plants sprinkled throughout the main floor.

Bonus: They offer a discount if you bring your own cup.

By the way, this neighborhood is a popular spot for Brooklyn food tours if you’re also feeling hungry.

### 17. Milk & Roses

*35 Box Street / Greenpoint*

This cozy cafe feels a bit like eating in an old library, without anyone there to shush you for chewing too loud.

The expansive outdoor garden is perfect for rustic shots and chill drinks during the warmer months. They also offer one of the best NYC bottomless brunch options at just $17 for an hour of unlimited mimosas. They even offer weekday brunch deals!

Also, the bistro is a popular spot for Brooklyn weddings, so you know it’s photo-ready. It may just be one of the prettiest cafes in NYC!

### 18. Butler Bake Shop

*40 Water Street / DUMBO*

Tucked away in the shadow of the Brooklyn Bridge, this industrial-style cafe offers beautiful pastries—the olive oil muffins with seasonal toppings are a favorite— alongside delicious coffees and teas and a space filled with natural light and lots of plants.

Their windowside booths offer your best chance at a shot with the iconic New York landmark. If you can snag an outdoor table, you can get a great shot of the Brooklyn Bridge behind you while sipping your latte.

Their DUMBO location isn’t the only place to pair a delicious matcha latte with gorgeous photos. Also visit Butler in South Williamsburg and North Williamsburg in Brooklyn and SoHo in Manhattan.


Want to explore the city while getting some gorgeous shots for your Instagram grid? Sign up for a private NYC Photo Journey, or take it to the next level with an NYC Influencer Shoot or Professional New York Photoshoot!Email [email protected] with inquiries.

### 19. Brooklyn Roasting Company

*543 Metropolitan Ave / Williamsburg*

Brooklyn Roasting Company’s Williamsburg café is the kind of spot where great coffee meets great design.

The space is bright, colorful, and unmistakably photogenic—with its striped counter, hanging retro lights, and shelves of bold, pop-art coffee tins that practically beg to be photographed.

Alongside classics like lattes and cappuccinos, you’ll also find fun menu highlights like the “Maple Shay” espresso drink featuring a hint of sweet maple, plus a yummy selection of pastries and light bites.

Beyond the aesthetics, the company is deeply committed to sustainability, fair-trade sourcing, and ethically roasted beans, so your latte tastes good and does good.

With plenty of seating and a welcoming neighborhood vibe, it’s an easy place to settle in with a cappuccino, snap a few pics, and enjoy one of NYC’s best homegrown cafés.

Along with their Williamsburg location, you can also find Brooklyn Roasting Company in Brooklyn Heights and near the Brooklyn Navy Yard, as well as at an outpost in Manhattan’s Strand Book Store.

### 20. Upstate Stock

*2 Berry Street / Williamsburg*

Spending a few hours at Upstate Stock is one of my favorite things to do in Williamsburg.

The space has an industrial vibe and showcases a cafe and a shop offering handmade local goods like candles, perfumes, soaps, jewelry, clothing, and even outdoorsy field guides.

Plus, they offer creative java drinks. One fan favorite is the “Campfire Latte” laced with smoked maple syrup.

Pair it with a locally-made maple donut for the ultimate foodie flatlay.

### 21. Five Leaves

*18 Bedford Avenue / Greenpoint*

Five Leaves is a hip bistro and cafe in Brooklyn’s Greenpoint neighborhood.

On the menu, you’ll find casual international-inspired brunch fare, while dinner is more on an upscale affair. This restaurant is great for any time of the day.

## Instagrammable New York: Beautiful Cafes In Queens

### 22. White Noise Coffee Co.

*41-02 162nd Street / Flushing*

Talk about unique NYC cafes!

White Noise has made its mark on Flushing with its neon artwork, minimalist interiors, and Instagram grid-worthy drinks and dishes.

Make sure to grab a photo of your latte art before you dig in!

### 23. Sweetleaf Coffee Roasters

*10-93 Jackson Avenue / Long Island City*

Featuring coffee locally roasted in Queens, Sweetleaf is a great place to stop in the up-and-coming Long Island City neighborhood.

Stop by for great drinks and pastries as well as a peek at their quirky antique-inspired decor.

### 24. Cafe Bench

*194-07 Northern Boulevard / Flushing *

This whimsical cafe and creperie in Flushing dazzles with tiny gardens, fairy lights, and extremely grid-worthy crepes. It’s definitely one of the cutest cafes in NYC!

Cafe Bench regularly updates its displays for each season, so it’s definitely worth repeat visits to see what they have in store.

## Cute Cafes In NYC: The Bronx

### 25. Prince Coffee House

*2306 Arthur Avenue / Arthur Avenue*

Located in “The Little Italy of the Bronx,” Prince Coffee House offers a quality java experience in a beautiful space, with floor-to-ceiling windows illuminating your java drinks and pastries in natural light.

Introduce your Instagram followers to classic New York through a “Bialy Egg Sandwich.”

If you’re unfamiliar with bialys, they’re often described as a “bagel with no hole,” though there are many other differences, such as that a bagel is boiled and a bialy is baked.

The cute cafe in NYC offers a delectable bread menu — semolina rosemary, anyone? — and a mix of serious and unique drinks.

Try a Thai Mocha or opt for the Turkish coffee served with on a gorgeous bronze tray with traditional long-handled pot (*cezve*).

Another visual highlight:

The hundreds of tin cups dangling over the bar. This is really one of the best places to visit in The Bronx!

## Most Instagrammable Hotels In NYC

Looking to stay overnight in NYC?

There are so many photo-worthy hotels, like **NoMo SoHo**, **The Ludlow**, and **1 Hotel Brooklyn**.

title: Lattes and no laptops: Unplugged cafes in NYC
author: Sasha DuBose; Jasmine Venet
text:
# Lattes and no laptops: Unplugged cafes in NYC

The best coffee shops in the city where you can unplug and chill out with friends — plus a coffee and a treat.


October 13, 2022

I can’t remember the last time I went to a coffee shop without my laptop in tow. At first, going out for coffee was a relaxing outing that allowed me to enjoy an overpriced iced latte alone or with friends. But as the semester drones on and assignments pile up, I find myself only going to coffee shops to work. Even when I go with friends, we spend hours in one place silently sipping on, and not enjoying, our $6 drinks. Constantly caught up in my laptop screen — which is a reminder of all the assignments I have left to complete — I’ve forgotten what it’s like to go to a coffee shop just to grab a drink and relax. So here is a list of a few coffee shops around campus that offer everything including coffee, tea, croissants, no laptops — and most importantly, an opportunity to unplug from day-to-day tasks.

**Ad Hoc Collective Coffee + Shoppe**

*13 Christopher St.*

I have trekked up and down Christopher Street for months on end, so I am shocked that I recently discovered Ad Hoc Collective Coffee + Shop. It’s easy to miss if you don’t know it’s there. But if you look closely, a small sign points you toward a narrow staircase that descends below the sidewalk and leads straight into what feels like someone’s living room. The space is filled with antiques I’d find in my grandma’s attic, from framed paintings and photographs to leather-bound books and gold candlesticks. They offer most of your classic drinks, as well as some of their own specialties, like the Honey Lavender Latte, and a large selection of food from their kitchen. Laptops aren’t allowed inside the shop, but if you desperately need to finish some work and the weather’s nice — or you brought a thick jacket — you can sit on the chairs lined along the sidewalk. 


**Kobrick Coffee Co. **

*24 Ninth Ave.*

This is the place to go if you’re just looking to grab a drink and a pastry with some friends. Located in the Meatpacking District, Kobrick Coffee Co. can be a bit pricier than most of the coffee shops on this list. Their drinks are averagely priced, ranging from $3.50 to $6.50 for classic coffees and teas, and their food can average from $10 to $15. If you’re feeling fancy, you can even entertain yourself with a $22 charcuterie board to share with friends. They also offer a wide selection of specialty cocktails; their rotating cocktails are the highlight of their menu. The brick walls and hanging vines create a chill atmosphere and there’s a lot of seating to choose from, including a hanging rattan chair that I still need to try out. Although laptops are allowed, you can only use them for an hour if you sit inside.

**Maman — Multiple Locations**

*67 University Pl.*

Walking into Maman is like walking into a charming garden in the countryside. The cafe has a rustic feel with imperfect wooden tables, ceiling greenery and blue accents everywhere. Open seven days a week at multiple locations across New York City, Montreal and Toronto, the café chain markets itself as a laptop-free environment. Their closest location to campus is on University Place with a 10% NYU discount, but some larger locations close to other campus dorms include Centre Street, Hudson at King and Nomad. Their breakfast- and lunch-focused menu features everything from $9 quiches to salads, which range from $14 to $16, that compete with the quality ingredients of Sweetgreen. For a quick bite and sip, try their $5 almond croissant paired with a $5 honey lavender latte.

**Book Club**

*197 E 3rd St.*

This place is always packed no matter what time of day you go, but the ambiance and late hours are worth the crowds. Open until midnight daily, Book Club is a blend between a bookish cafe and a bar, offering coffee, alcohol and pastries. Coffees and teas are $4 to $5 and glasses of beer or wine range from $6 to $16. Bring your own book, or grab one from the shelves, and find a comfy armchair to fall into and read alongside others doing the same. Laptops aren’t allowed after 7 p.m., but most people barely use them throughout the day. Don’t forget to check out their bathroom downstairs — the walls are covered in pages from books like “Pride and Prejudice” and “Harry Potter.”

**Café Kitsuné**

*550 Hudson St.*

With its big windows and ample amount of seating, this cafe is worth visiting on a rainy day. Connected to the Maison Kitsuné store in the heart of West Village, Café Kitsuné offers $4 pastries, drinks priced between $4 to $7, pricier food options ranging from $14 to $19, and a relatively large selection of wines. Like every coffee shop on this list, this one has a strict no-laptop policy. This makes it a great spot to come and talk with friends over tea or to sit and people-watch with a latte and croissant.

*Contact Jasmine Venet at [email protected]*

Plus, unlike at home where students might be tempted to watch TV, do chores, or take prolonged breaks, coffee shops provide a setting with fewer personal distractions. And what’s really important, being surrounded by other people working or reading can create a collective sense of productivity. Witnessing others focused on their tasks can motivate students to concentrate on their own work.

While coffee shops provide the perfect ambiance and environment for studying and brainstorming, sometimes the academic pressure becomes too much to handle. In such instances, students often look for alternative solutions. Fortunately, with the rise of online resources, students can now quickly and easily find professional assistance. By simply searching write my essay online, they can connect with experienced writers. This online aid proves invaluable for many students. Especially when deadlines are tight or when they’re juggling multiple assignments. Just as coffee shops offer a haven for focused studying, online writing services offer a lifeline for academic challenges.
