title: Study Spots with Food in New York City: Complete Guide for Students
author: SethAmazon
text:
You’ve found the perfect study spot. The wifi is strong, there are outlets nearby, the atmosphere is just right. Three hours later, your stomach is growling, but you’re finally in a productive flow. Do you pack up everything, lose your seat, and go find food? Or do you try to power through on an empty stomach and watch your concentration dissolve?

Here’s where NYC shines. Unlike smaller college towns where your options are limited to whatever’s near campus, New York has developed an entire ecosystem of study spots that understand students need more than just coffee. We’re talking cafes with full lunch menus, all-day breakfast options, healthy bowls and salads, and actually satisfying food that keeps you going through marathon study sessions.

The best part? You don’t have to choose between a great study environment and good food. NYC has places that deliver both. Cafes where you can order a proper meal, eat at your table, and keep studying without the guilt of occupying space while just nursing a cold coffee.

This guide breaks down the absolute best study spots in New York City where food is actually part of the equation. Whether you’re looking for healthy options, comfort food, quick bites, or full meals, we’ve got you covered. Let’s find places where you can feed both your brain and your stomach.

## Why Food Access Matters for Serious Study Sessions

Before we dive into specific locations, let’s talk about why having food options at your study spot is actually crucial for productivity.

### The Brain Fuel Reality

Your brain uses about 20% of your body’s energy, and during intense concentration that percentage increases. When you’re learning new material, solving complex problems, or writing papers, your brain burns through calories fast. Running on empty isn’t just uncomfortable; it actively undermines your cognitive performance.

Having access to real food means you can maintain steady energy levels throughout your study session instead of hitting that mid-afternoon crash that kills productivity.

### The Momentum Problem

Breaking your study flow to hunt for food is productivity death. You pack up your laptop, lose your seat (this is NYC, someone will take it), walk to a restaurant, wait for food, eat, and then try to find another study spot. By the time you’re settled again, you’ve lost an hour plus whatever momentum you had built up.

Study spots with good food let you stay put, maintain your flow state, and keep your productive streak going.

### The NYC Time Factor

In New York, everything takes longer than it should. A “quick” food run can easily become 45 minutes between crowds, lines, and distance. If you’re juggling classes, work, internships, and studying, that time matters. Being able to order food where you’re already studying is a genuine time-saver.

## The Best NYC Study Cafes with Excellent Food Menus

### Think Coffee (Multiple Manhattan Locations)

Think Coffee has achieved legendary status among NYC students, and while the wifi and atmosphere get most of the attention, their food menu deserves serious credit.

Food highlights:

- **Beyond basic pastries**– Full breakfast and lunch options available
- **Oat milk availability**– Great for dairy-free students
- **Healthy options alongside comfort food**– Something for every craving
- **Reasonably priced**– Won’t destroy a student budget
- **You can eat at your table**– No need to pack up

With 11 locations throughout the city (10 in Lower Manhattan, one in Brooklyn), Think Coffee understands that students need sustenance for long sessions. The menu includes sandwiches, salads, and substantial breakfast items that actually fill you up.

Student strategy: Order food when you arrive for your study session, then you’re covered for hours. Most locations are open until 7pm, giving you extended access to food and study space.

### Bluestone Lane (Multiple Locations)

This Australian-inspired cafe chain has brought Melbourne’s cafe culture to NYC, and that includes serious food alongside excellent coffee.

Menu standouts:

- **Avocado smash**– Their signature dish, perfect study fuel
- **Healthy options focus**– Bowls, salads, grain dishes
- **All-day breakfast**– Because sometimes you need eggs at 3pm
- **Quality ingredients**– Fresh, well-prepared food
- **Locations near major campuses**– Rice Village (near Rice University equivalent in NYC context) and other student-heavy areas

Bluestone Lane locations in Manhattan typically have good seating, wifi, and a welcoming atmosphere for students. The food is on the pricier side but the quality justifies the cost, especially when you’re fueling a serious study session.

### Black Cat LES (Lower East Side)

Black Cat isn’t just a cafe; it’s a student-focused space created by a criminology professor specifically to bring together students and intellectuals. The food reflects this mission.

What makes it special:

- **Full menu designed for extended stays**– They understand students need real food
- **Comfortable seating for eating and studying**– Couches, upholstered chairs, wooden tables
- **Great vibes**– Cozy atmosphere that welcomes long study sessions
- **Late-night hours**– Food available during evening study sessions
- **Event calendar**– Academic lectures and tutoring when you need a study break

The cafe was literally designed by someone who understands student needs, and that shows in every aspect including the food offerings. You can settle in with a meal and know you’re welcome to stay.

### Variety Coffee Roasters (Multiple Locations)

With locations ranging from Morningside Heights to Park Slope, Variety Coffee has developed a loyal student following thanks to their quality coffee and substantial food menu.

Food features:

- **Seasonal menu**– Changes to reflect what’s fresh and available
- **Selection of pastries plus more substantial options**– Not just croissants
- **Free vanilla and simple syrup at self-serve counter**– Small perk that matters when coffee prices are high
- **Accommodates long study sessions**– You’ll see students posted up for hours

The diverse customer base (everyone from collage-makers to exam-cramming college students) creates an accepting atmosphere where studying with food is completely normal.

### Kona Coffee Roasters (Near NYU)

Popular with NYU students, Kona Coffee Roasters combines excellent coffee with a food menu that goes beyond the typical cafe offerings.

Why students love it:

- **Scrumptious food options**– Actual meals, not just snacks
- **Ample seating**– Room to spread out while eating and studying
- **Welcoming staff**– They understand students need to stay awhile
- **Pre-order through app**– Saves time on busy days
- **Relaxed vibe**– Comfortable environment for long sessions

The convenience of app ordering means you can stay focused on your work and have food delivered to your table without interrupting your flow.

### Ground Support Cafe (Multiple Locations)

Ground Support has built its reputation on being a serious study spot, and their food menu supports that mission.

Food advantages:

- **Delicious coffee paired with quality food**– Both aspects get attention
- **Cozy atmosphere**– Makes eating and studying feel natural
- **Airy space**– Comfortable seating for extended sessions
- **Friendly staff ready to serve**– Quick service when you need food

## Cafes with Exceptional Breakfast and Brunch Options

### Matto Espresso (Near NYU)

Affordability meets quality at Matto Espresso, where the food menu is as carefully curated as their coffee selection.

Breakfast highlights:

- **Robust espressos paired with delicate pastries**– Perfect morning fuel
- **Prices consistently lower than larger chains**– Student-budget friendly
- **Sweet treats and rich coffee**– Satisfying without breaking the bank
- **Friendly service**– Personal, welcoming atmosphere

For morning study sessions, Matto delivers on both coffee and food without the premium pricing of trendier spots.

### Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar (SoHo)

Butler pairs stylish aesthetics with a food menu that leans healthier, perfect for students who care about what they’re putting in their bodies during long study sessions.

Menu features:

- **Healthier food options**– Salads, grain bowls, fresh ingredients
- **Good coffee to complement the food**– Both aspects are quality
- **Free wifi**– Study-friendly infrastructure
- **Welcoming to laptop users**– Explicitly student and remote worker friendly

The SoHo location makes it convenient for students at nearby schools, and the healthier menu helps you avoid the afternoon crash that comes from heavy cafe food.

## Study Spots with Full Lunch and Dinner Menus

### Barnes & Noble Union Square Cafe (Third Floor)

Here’s an unconventional pick that actually works brilliantly for students who need food access during study sessions.

Why it works:

- **Serves Starbucks products**– Full Starbucks food and drink menu
- **No purchase required**– Part of the bookstore, tables open to all
- **Massive seating capacity**– Giant tables perfect for spreading out materials
- **Can order food and eat while studying**– No guilt about occupying space
- **Extended bookstore hours**– More time than typical cafes

The fact that you can use the space without buying anything removes pressure, but the full Starbucks menu means food options when you need them.

### Capital One Cafe (Multiple Locations)

This might seem like an odd inclusion, but Capital One Cafes have become study havens for NYC students, partly because of their food options.

Food and study features:

- **Decent coffee and food options**– Better than expected for a bank cafe
- **No purchase required**– Can use space for free
- **Wide variety of seating**– Booths, desks, armchairs for eating comfortably
- **Multiple floors**– Space to spread out with your meal
- **Complimentary wifi**– Free study infrastructure

Note: Best for weekday studying as they limit wifi on weekends. But during the week, you get free space with food available and zero pressure to buy.

### THE ELK (East Village)

This hidden gem combines cozy, rustic charm with a food menu that goes beyond typical cafe offerings.

Food highlights:

- **Delicious coffee and mouthwatering pastries**– Quality on both fronts
- **Peaceful ambiance**– Perfect for eating while studying
- **Cozy atmosphere**– Makes long sessions comfortable
- **Student-friendly vibe**– Welcome to settle in with food

## Brooklyn Study Spots with Great Food

Brooklyn’s cafe scene has developed its own identity when it comes to combining study spaces with quality food options.

### OST Cafe (Grand Street, Brooklyn)

This Brooklyn favorite pairs exposed brick ambiance with quality food perfect for study sessions.

What makes it work:

- **Good espresso and pastries**– Quality basics done right
- **Welcoming atmosphere for solo work**– Comfortable for eating alone while studying
- **Simple outdoor seating**– Weather-permitting study and dining combo
- **Cozy spot for couple-hour sessions**– Perfect for focused bursts with food

The compact nature means it’s best for shorter sessions, but the food quality makes those hours productive.

### Sweetleaf (Queens/Brooklyn)

Consistently mentioned as a top pick for students and remote workers, Sweetleaf delivers on both coffee and food.

Student advantages:

- **Menu that keeps you going through long work blocks**– Substantial food options
- **Good for before or after commutes**– Convenient location
- **Wi-Fi and outlets**– Study infrastructure covered
- **Popular with laptop users**– Atmosphere accommodates studying with meals

Part of StudyNearby’s directory of 113 verified Brooklyn study places, Sweetleaf has earned its reputation among students who need both workspace and food access.

## SoHo Study Cafes with Quality Food Options

### Bibliotheque (SoHo)

This unique bookstore, cafe, and wine bar combination offers a completely different study and dining experience.

Food and atmosphere:

- **Cozy seating perfect for eating while working**– Comfortable stools and couches
- **Food and social interaction after 5pm**– Transforms into dining focused space
- **Wine bar component**– For 21+ students doing evening sessions
- **Study until 5pm**– Then enjoy the transition to social dining

The rule is strict: laptops only until 5pm, then it becomes a work-free zone. But for daytime studying with food access, it’s a beautiful option.

### The Lost Draft (SoHo)

Popular with students, creatives, and remote workers, The Lost Draft combines study infrastructure with quality food.

Why it works:

- **Variety of artisanal coffee blends**– Quality drinks to pair with food
- **Free wifi and comfortable nooks**– Study-friendly setup
- **Quiet space on second floor**– Perfect for eating and studying without distractions
- **Good vibes and stress-free atmosphere**– Welcome to stay with your meal

### Argo Tea Cafe (Multiple Locations)

For students who prefer tea to coffee, Argo Tea offers an extensive menu plus food options for extended sessions.

Food features:

- **Healthy snacks alongside tea selection**– Light but satisfying options
- **Variety of teas**– Hundreds of options from around the world
- **Comfortable seating**– Good for settling in with food and books
- **Calm, peaceful atmosphere**– Serene environment for focused study

The emphasis on tea creates a different energy than coffee-focused cafes, and the healthy snacks support sustained concentration without the coffee jitters.

## What to Look For in Study Spots with Food

### Menu Substance

Not all cafe food is created equal. Look for places that offer:

- Actual meals, not just pastries
- Options beyond baked goods (sandwiches, salads, bowls)
- Protein options to sustain energy
- Healthy choices alongside comfort food
- Dietary accommodation (vegan, gluten-free, etc.)

### Eating Logistics

Can you actually eat comfortably while studying?

- Tables large enough for laptop plus food
- Napkins and utensils easily accessible
- No weird rules about eating at tables
- Staff attitude toward people eating and working

### Timing and Availability

When can you get food?

- All-day breakfast options
- Lunch menu hours
- Snack availability throughout the day
- Whether kitchen closes before the cafe

### Pricing Reality

Can you afford to eat here regularly?

- Menu prices relative to your budget
- Portion sizes (do you actually get full?)
- Whether one meal can sustain a long session
- Any student discounts available

## Budget Strategies for Studying with Food Access

### Smart Ordering

Make your money go further:

- Order one substantial meal instead of multiple snacks
- Look for combo deals (coffee plus food bundles)
- Bring supplemental snacks to complement a smaller cafe purchase
- Use apps that offer loyalty rewards
- Take advantage of happy hour or off-peak specials

### Mix Free and Paid Spots

You don’t need to buy food every study session:

- Use free libraries when you bring your own food
- Hit cafes with food when you specifically need a meal
- Alternate between packed lunches at libraries and cafe meals
- Save cafe food for days when you need the atmosphere boost

### Maximize Each Purchase

Get the most value:

- Choose filling, protein-rich options that sustain energy
- Order water with your meal (free refills)
- Make one meal stretch through a 3-4 hour session
- Bring healthy snacks to supplement the cafe meal

## Using StudyNearby to Find Food-Friendly Study Spots

StudyNearby is specifically designed for finding study-friendly locations, and the platform includes information about amenities that matter to students. With 378 verified study places across New York, you can discover cafes and spaces that accommodate both studying and eating.

Browse by borough to find options near you. Check out Manhattan study spots, explore Brooklyn locations, or discover Queens options. Reviews from other students often mention food quality and menu options, helping you choose spots that work for study sessions with meals.

## Study Cafe Etiquette When Eating

### Be Considerate of the Space

When eating at study cafes:

- Clean up after yourself completely
- Dispose of food waste properly
- Wipe down tables if you make a mess
- Don’t bring smelly outside food (disrespectful to the business)
- Keep food noise to a minimum (crunchy snacks can be disruptive)

### Support the Business

If you’re using their space:

- Buy your food from them, not outside sources
- Make purchases proportional to time spent
- Tip appropriately for table service
- Don’t take up large tables solo during meal rushes
- Respect any posted policies about outside food

### Balance Eating and Studying

Find the right approach:

- Don’t spread food across your entire workspace
- Finish eating before tackling messy or important materials
- Position food so spills won’t damage electronics
- Take actual meal breaks rather than mindlessly eating while working

## Building Your Food-Enabled Study Rotation

Create a system that works for your needs and budget:

- **The Full Menu Cafe**– Where you go for serious meals during long sessions (Think Coffee, Black Cat LES)
- **The Healthy Option**– When you need nutritious fuel (Bluestone Lane, Butler Bakeshop)
- **The Budget-Friendly Spot**– Good food without premium prices (Matto Espresso, Variety Coffee)
- **The Free Space with Bring-Your-Own**– Libraries when you pack lunch
- **The Special Occasion Splurge**– Premium food for when you need extra motivation

This rotation ensures you always have appropriate options based on your hunger level, budget, and study needs for the day.

## The Bottom Line on NYC Study Spots with Food

The reality of serious studying is that it requires time, and time requires food. Trying to maintain focus on an empty stomach or constantly breaking your flow to hunt for meals is productivity death. The good news is that New York City has evolved beyond the traditional model of “cafes have coffee, restaurants have food, and never the two shall properly meet.”

From Think Coffee’s substantial menu across 11 locations to Black Cat LES’s academic-focused food offerings, from Bluestone Lane’s healthy Australian-inspired fare to the surprising quality at Capital One Cafe, NYC has options where food is a genuine part of the study experience, not an afterthought.

The key is being strategic. Use resources like StudyNearby to discover which spots have the food options you need. Build your rotation based on different types of study sessions and hunger levels. Understand the menu before you commit to a spot for a long session.

Don’t sacrifice your productivity by choosing between food and a good study environment. Don’t waste time and momentum hunting for meals when you could stay focused. Don’t try to survive on coffee and hope when your brain needs actual fuel.

You’re a student in New York City. You deserve study spots that understand marathon sessions require sustenance, that feed your body while you feed your mind, and that let you stay in your productive flow without hunger derailing your concentration.

Now you know where to find them. Fuel up and get to work.

## Quick Reference Guide for NYC Study Spots with Food

| Location | Area | Food Type | Best For | Price | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Think Coffee | Multiple Manhattan | Full breakfast & lunch menu | All-day study sessions | $-$$ | 
| Bluestone Lane | Multiple locations | Healthy Australian-inspired | Nutritious fuel | $$ | 
| Black Cat LES | Lower East Side | Full menu, late hours | Evening study sessions | $$ | 
| Variety Coffee | Multiple (Morningside, Park Slope, etc.) | Seasonal menu | Quality food & coffee combo | $-$$ | 
| Matto Espresso | Near NYU | Pastries & coffee | Budget-conscious students | $ | 
| Barnes & Noble Cafe | Union Square | Starbucks full menu | No-purchase-required studying | $-$$ | 
| Capital One Cafe | Multiple locations | Coffee & light food | Free space with food available | $ (optional) | 
| Argo Tea | Multiple locations | Tea & healthy snacks | Tea lovers, calm atmosphere | $-$$ | 

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I eat my own food at NYC study cafes?

Generally no. Most cafes prohibit outside food as a business policy. If you need to bring your own food, use public libraries where it’s typically allowed in designated areas. Respect cafe policies by purchasing their food if you’re using their space. Some cafes may allow discrete snacks, but bringing full meals from elsewhere is considered disrespectful.

### Which NYC study spots have the best food for long sessions?

Think Coffee offers full breakfast and lunch menus perfect for extended studying. Black Cat LES has substantial options with late hours. Bluestone Lane provides healthy, filling Australian-inspired meals. Variety Coffee has seasonal offerings. All these spots understand students need real food for marathon sessions.

### Are there study cafes in NYC with vegan or vegetarian food?

Yes! Bluestone Lane emphasizes healthy options including many vegan choices. Think Coffee has dairy-free milk options and vegetarian items. Many Brooklyn cafes cater to plant-based diets. Check individual menus, but NYC’s diversity means vegan and vegetarian options are widely available at student-friendly cafes.

### What should I order at a study cafe to stay focused?

Choose protein-rich options that provide sustained energy: eggs, grain bowls, sandwiches with protein, salads with chickpeas or nuts. Avoid heavy, greasy foods that cause crashes. Stay hydrated with water. If ordering coffee, pair it with food to avoid jitters. Complex carbs and healthy fats support concentration better than simple sugars.

### Can I study at NYC cafes without buying food?

Some spots like Capital One Cafe and Barnes & Noble Cafe don’t require purchases. At regular cafes, etiquette expects buying something. You don’t need to order food immediately, but make purchases proportional to time spent (every 2-3 hours). If you can’t afford regular cafe purchases, use free library options instead.

### Which study spots are open late with food available?

Black Cat LES has late-night hours with food. Think Coffee locations generally stay open until 7pm with full menus available. Check specific locations as hours vary. Most cafes close their food service before closing entirely, so confirm kitchen hours if you’re planning evening study sessions with meals.

### How much should I budget for studying with food in NYC?

Budget $10-20 per study session for one substantial meal or multiple smaller items. Cheaper options like Matto Espresso run $5-10. Premium spots like Bluestone Lane cost $12-18 for meals. Use free libraries and bring food 3-4 days a week, splurge on cafes with food 1-2 days for variety without breaking the bank.

### Do Brooklyn study cafes have better food than Manhattan?

Not necessarily better, but often more diverse and sometimes more affordable. Brooklyn cafes tend toward health-conscious, creative menus. Manhattan has more variety including high-end and budget options. Check StudyNearby’s Brooklyn directory and Manhattan listings to compare specific spots.

### Can I order delivery to study spots?

Generally no. Bringing outside food to a cafe is disrespectful to their business. If you’re at a library, delivery is usually fine to designated eating areas. At cafes, order from their menu or go elsewhere. Some coworking spaces allow delivery, but verify policies first.

### What are the healthiest study cafes with food in NYC?

Bluestone Lane specializes in healthy Australian-inspired options. Butler Bakeshop leans toward healthier choices. Argo Tea offers healthy snacks and teas. Many cafes now include grain bowls, salads, and plant-based options. Look for menus emphasizing whole grains, vegetables, lean proteins, and minimally processed ingredients for sustained study energy.

title: Categories
text:
It’s been said that you can find a coffee shop on every single corner in New York City. While I may not have been there myself to know if this really is true, it seems undeniable that communal caffeine intake is a huge part of the city’s culture. 


However, no matter how many cafés you may come across, it can be difficult for freelancers to find one with the right amount of space and plug sockets, that doesn’t want you to leave the second you’ve collected your drink, let alone one that is happy for you to plop down your laptop for a few hours! 

## CREATIVE DIFFERENCES

In the UK, freelancers tend to choose their remote working locations based on recommendations from other freelancers and the amenities the place has to offer. In New York, this culture is very different. Freelancers in New York tend to choose local coffee shops that are near to their home, sometimes even moving apartments based on proximity to these locations. 


As the city is so large, it’s divided into five boroughs, each with several neighborhoods of their own. Thanks to each neighbourhood’s distinctive scenery and atmosphere, each one has a very unique creative fingerprint that provides creatives with different kinds of inspiration. This often leads like-minded creatives to move to the same areas so they can collaborate and bounce off each other.


The coffee shops in these neighborhoods often mirror the creative vibes of their community, so it’s important to find one that gives you inspiration if you’re planning to spend your time there working. 

# Brooklyn

Creatives used to be found mostly in the traditionally hipster friendly areas of Brooklyn like Willamsburg or Greenwich Village. However, as these areas become increasingly more expensive thanks to rising rent costs, freelancers are finding themselves priced out of these areas and moving to cheaper alternatives like Bushwick instead.


Bushwick is filled with former warehouses and garages that have been converted into shops, galleries and restaurants. The exteriors are home to a thriving street art scene that is annually repainted by the Bushwick Collective, giving the whole neighborhood a vibrant and evolving landscape that is very popular with professionals from the film, art and fashion industries.


If you’re looking for coffee shops to work from in Bushwick, then check out:

## The Cobra Club

The Cobra Club on Wyckoff Avenue started its life as a yoga studio and craft cocktail bar, the first of its kind in the city. They made a point to listen to the needs of their community and 8 years later their coffee shop is considered a home away from home for most of the local creatives. They have free wi-fi, plenty of tables with outlets and outdoor seating; the bar even works great as a standing desk if that’s something you’re into.

## Molasses Books

If you’ve ever dreamt of settling down to work amongst piles of books with a nice glass of wine, then look no further than Molasses Books, a used bookstore and café on Hart Street. There’s a bar for you to ply yourself with coffee while you work, you can even get alcoholic drinks if you work better that way. It’s open until midnight, seven days a week, although they do require you to put your laptop away after 8pm.

## Dweebs

Popular coffee shop, Dweebs, on Dekalb Avenue is known as one of the great places to study or get work done in Bushwick. Its spacious interior is light and airy with plenty of coffee available allowing you to focus fully on your to-do list. 


If you happen to take a liking to any of the local art being displayed on the walls, every piece is up for sale with all proceeds going to the artist. Their art collection changes every month, so there’ll always be something new and interesting to inspire you whilst you work.

# Manhattan

The island of Manhattan is one of the more expensive places to live and work in New York City but affordable apartments can still be found in the traditionally working class neighborhood of Hell’s Kitchen. While its name and reputation may conjure up some terrifying imagery, the area is actually very welcoming and boasts a thriving community of creatives involved in the theatre scene thanks to its close proximity to the stages of both Broadway and Off-Broadway.


Some of the best coffee shops for creatives to work in here are:

## Ground Central

Located in the heart of the theatre district, Ground Central is very popular with remote workers thanks to its large communal tables, comfy sofas and free wi-fi. It has a laidback and vintage library vibe, with tons of books and interesting furniture. While there are plenty of outlets, it can get a little busy so if you need to quiet to focus, make sure to hole up in one of the little nooks tucked out of the way in the back of the store.

## Paper Coffee

If you’re seeking a nice, quiet place to work with good wi-fi and friendly staff, then make sure to try out Paper Coffee in the lobby of the Made Hotel on West 29th Street. They have a range of high quality coffee, tea and baked goods available but a limited supply of outlets so it’s better for a few hours of work than for staying all day. The Made Hotel also has several other bars, restaurants and patios if Paper is a little too full when you get there.

# Queens

There are many big movie studios, television networks and countless opportunities to be found amongst the streets of Astoria, having been an entertainment production hub since the days of silent movies. The area is filled with affordable apartments, Greek restaurants and beautiful views of Manhattan, famed for helping the web-slinging photographer Spider-Man pay his bills.


While there might be a lot of really great coffee shops in Astoria, make sure to swing by:

## Kinship Coffee

After the recent COVID-19 lockdowns, lots of freelancers were looking for a place to spend time outside of their homes. Kinship Coffee has provided an answer for their local entrepreneurs by welcoming long stay visitors in each of their locations in Astoria. Their many tables are often filled with remote workers taking advantage of the free wi-fi, affordable menu and on-site roasting facility. 


Thanks to its popularity, it can be tricky to find an available outlet. However, the locations are all open until 9pm so sometimes it’s better to come down later in the evening for a few hours, than be stuck in a bad spot all day.

## Madame SouSou

Though Madame SouSou is on the smaller side, it still has ample seating, free wi-fi and a peacefully decorated interior that makes you want to spend more time on your latest project. During the warmer weather, they have a large variety of outdoor seating options for you to enjoy. They are well-known in the local area for their great coffee, tasty baked goods and friendly staff.

# Staten Island

A piece of New York that feels strangely out of place, Staten Island seems to have more parks than it does people. It’s well-known for its abundance of green spaces, historic buildings and museums as well as the Staten Island Ferry with its beautiful views of the Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island and the Lower Manhattan skyline. 


There’s nothing like working with a view, so be sure to try out:

## The Mustard Seed

Loved by the locals for its great ambience and food, The Mustard Seed is a charming little place where you can work for the entire day without needing to worry about buying another coffee. While their indoor seating can often fill up quickly, there are plenty of seats in their new outdoor seating area with padded chairs and sofa seats.

## Every Thing Goes Book

The only large used bookstore on the island, Every Thing Goes Book is located near the ferry to the main city for easy commuting. The store collects donations of used books and also doubles as a community center with a neighbourhood stage for performances and local art displayed on the walls, giving the store a real homely feel. They have great coffee, free wi-fi and plenty of seating both indoors and outdoors on their garden patio.

# The Bronx

The Bronx has had a difficult evolution throughout its history. Since the area has largely been populated by migrants from Europe and the Caribbean, it has long suffered from high levels of poverty and crime thanks to the attitudes of those in power. This has resulted in a predominantly negative reputation that tends to keep visitors away.


For the majority, the Bronx is either about the local baseball team, the New York Yankees, or hip-hop. The borough has a flourishing music and art scene that focuses on local experiences and culture, reflected in the street murals and graffiti seen throughout the neighborhood.


For an inspiring environment and great coffee, be sure to check out:

## La Casa Del Caffè

Revered as one of the best places to work in the neighbourhood, La Casa Del Caffè, is run by the locals for the locals. It’s on the smaller side, so you’ll need to come early if you want a table for more than a few hours at a time. Their menu has been lovingly created by the owner, Anna, and is very reasonably priced, although it is cash only so make sure to stop by the ATM on your way there.

## Prince Coffee House

Tucked away in a corner of Little Italy, the Prince Coffee House is a great place to focus on your work. Its spacious interior has a bright and airy atmosphere and ample seating, even during its busiest hours. If you’re feeling stuck for inspiration, take a look at the stunning copper coffee pot installation hanging from the ceiling or the many patterns adorning the counters around you. Their homemade desserts and range of hot drinks will give you the energy to tackle those emails or edit endless numbers of photos until closing at 11pm - ideal for late night work or study sessions.

# Recommendations From Our Members

Since I have not yet had the chance to visit the Big Apple for myself, I was keen to find out what the locals thought, so I asked Jorge Aragon, a photographer from New York and one of our new American members, to share his favourites with me:

“Even though I don't usually work much away from home, NYC has many interesting places to accompany work with a coffee, or some dessert. My favorite area is the one near Washington Square park, where I find places like Irving farm or The Commons, Maman or Lena Greenwich Village, because I always let myself be tempted by a waffle or a tiramisu, or some croissant or seasonal delicacy.”


“In any case, the city has many spaces where you can go out simply for a moment of inspiration or to connect in other ways, such as in the markets and walks of the city (Chelsea, Essex, Fulton or Industry City to name a few) or even some parks with large tables and even free internet connection.”

## TRIAL AND ERROR

While both traditional and home offices have a lot of benefits, there’s definitely something to be said for working in public surrounded by the bustle of life. By trying out different spots around the city, you’re sure to keep finding new sources of inspiration and new, like-minded creatives to collaborate and share ideas with. At very least, you’ll probably find some good coffee.

title: Best Bookstores with Cafés in New York City
author: Devorah Lev-Tov
text:
With plummeting temps, and even some snowfall in New York City, finding cosy spots to snuggle up in with a good __book to combat the winter blues__ is more important than ever. And recently, NYC has been experiencing a bit of a bookstore boom. Instead of a sea of Barnes & Nobles, the last 15 years have seen book superstores closing and __independent__ shops blooming. Some of our favourite bookstores also happen to be the cosiest in the city, so read on for where to read and buy books right now. 

**The Ripped Bodice, Park Slope** 

Sisters Leah Koch and Bea Hodges-Koch first opened The Ripped Bodice, a bookstore dedicated to romance fiction, in Los Angeles in 2016. In 2023, it opened a second location in Park Slope, Brooklyn, behind a bubble gum-pink store front with a graphic tiled floor and ceiling art with floating books. The store carries romance sub-genres, including contemporary, LGBTQ+, science fiction, historical, erotica, and young adult. Aside from daytime shopping, the store hosts events nearly every night – from author readings to live podcast recordings. It also has three different book clubs that meet monthly.

__therippedbodice.com/brooklyn__ 

                            ###### 218 5th Ave, NY 11215

**Liz's Book Bar, Brooklyn** 

Opened last year in Carroll Gardens by Black author Maura Cheeks, Liz’s Book Bar is named after her grandmother. The inviting mahogany bar at the front serves coffee from Black Acres Roastery, tea from SerendipiTea, pastries from Bien Cuit, charcuterie and cheese boards, French and Italian wines, and local beers. In the back are the bookcases carrying about 4,000 titles, a worn-in leather couch, and a handful of tables. Events often combine reading, writing, and wine or beer tasting, with several writing and book publishing workshops.

__lizsbookbar.com__ 

                            ###### 315 Smith St, NY 11231

**McNally Jackson, Seaport** 

McNally Jackson is the city’s premier independent bookstore, known for its dark wood shelves and snug reading nooks. While the local mini-chain now has five locations, the Seaport one is our favourite for maximum cosy vibes. It spans two floors of a historic brick building from 1811 and has tons of charming details – and thousands of books. Windows overlook the cobblestone street outside and armchairs await in each room. There’s a bar and café on the ground floor, and this location currently hosts the most events and author readings.

__www.mcnallyjackson.com__ 

                            ###### 4 Fulton St, NY 10038

**Book Club Bar, East Village** 

If your living room was a bookstore that also served wine, cocktails, and coffee, it might feel like Book Club Bar, an intimate space in the East Village that opened in 2019. Books are carefully chosen, the coffee is locally roasted, and the beers are all from New York State. And yes, the store does host a book club, which meets once a month in the back garden. There are also game nights, live music shows, author readings, lectures, and more.

__bookclubbar.com__ 

                            ###### 197 E 3rd St, NY 10009

**Archestratus, Greenpoint** 

Food and book lovers unite at this charming Greenpoint shop. The books here all focus on cookbooks and other food-related tomes, both fiction and non-fiction, including hard-to-find and out-of-print volumes. The back of the store is a full café, serving Sicilian-accented dishes and drinks both alcoholic and non. There’s also a bakery section with freshly made bread from She Wolf and a grocery area with artisanal items ranging from raw bamboo honey to fresh ricotta. A space in the back is set aside for cooking classes, tastings, dinner parties, screenings, readings, potluck cookbook clubs, and more.

__archestrat.us__ 

                            ###### 164 Huron St, NY 11222

**Albertine, Upper East Side** 

Often cited as the __most beautiful shops__ in NYC, Albertine is a French and English bookstore supported by Cultural Services of the French Embassy. It’s located across the street from the Met on the Upper East Side, inside the historic Payne Whitney mansion. The gorgeous interior features a cobalt blue ceiling hand-painted with constellations, stars, and planets; parquet wood floors; comfy brown leather chairs; and handsome wooden bookcases lining the walls. The store hosts various talks and panels, plus a monthly book club that discusses French books with English translations available.  

__albertine.com__ 

                            ###### 972 5th Ave, NY 10075

**Books Are Magic, Cobble Hill** 

When author Emma Straub opened the original Books Are Magic shop with her husband in Cobble Hill, it felt like a salve for Brooklyn and independent bookstores everywhere. In fact, it opened inside her beloved BookCourt, a longtime neighbourhood standby where Straub had once been an employee. Today, Books Are Magic is famous in NYC and beyond, known for its welcoming space, excellent curation, and spectacular author events. A second location in Downtown Brooklyn opened at the end of 2022, but it doesn’t have quite as many inviting nooks as the original.

title: 20 of the best Bookstore Cafés in New York City
author: Claudio Ciardi
text:
# 20 of the best Bookstore Cafés in New York City

Claudio Ciardi

• Updated: 2024-10-08Bookstore Cafés in NYC offer a unique experience for book lovers and coffee enthusiasts alike. These cozy havens combine the love of literature with the enjoyment of a good cup of coffee, creating a perfect spot to relax, read, work, or socialize. With a variety of locations throughout the city, Bookstore Cafés in NYC provide a unique atmosphere that blends intellectual stimulation and caffeinated satisfaction.

Table of Contents

- 1. Every Thing Goes Book Cafe and Neighborhood Stage
- 2. Shakespeare & Co
- 3. Sister's Uptown Bookstore
- 4. Bookafé
- 5. Cafe con Libros
- 6. Molasses Books
- 7. Book Club
- 8. The Center for Fiction
- 9. McNally Jackson Books SoHo
- 10. Yu & Me Books
- 11. Milk & Roses
- 12. The Drama Book Shop
- 13. The Lit. Bar
- 14. Cups and Books
- 15. Bluestockings Cooperative Bookstore
- 16. Topos Bookstore Cafe
- 17. Housing Works Bookstore
- 18. Archestratus Books + Foods
- 19. Dear friend books
- 20. P&T Knitwear Bookstore, Coffee, & Podcast Studio

## 1.Every Thing Goes Book Cafe and Neighborhood Stage

A hub for creativity and community connection.

The staff goes above and beyond to create a welcoming environment, fostering a sense of belonging and camaraderie among patrons. Their commitment to quality and service is evident in every interaction, making this a truly exceptional place to visit. Whether you're looking for a place to work, catch up with friends, or simply enjoy a great cup of coffee, this establishment is sure to exceed your expectations.

## 2.Shakespeare & Co

A literary haven with a bustling cafe

The bookstore itself is situated a short flight of stairs above the café, though it is unfortunate that this layout may pose challenges for those with mobility limitations. That being said, Shakespeare and Company's book collection is truly impressive, featuring a diverse range of titles and genres that cater to all tastes. The staff members are consistently friendly and approachable, ready to offer recommendations or assist in locating a specific title. Overall, the bookstore provides a warm and welcoming environment for book lovers and café-goers alike, as long as the latter group keeps their visits to a reasonable length.

## 3.Sister's Uptown Bookstore

Knowledge is key

In addition to a wide selection of books, Sister's Uptown also offers food and beverages, providing a comfortable and welcoming space for visitors to spend time and connect with others. The business has been serving the Harlem community for 24 years, and its warm and inviting atmosphere has made it a beloved institution in the area. Whether you're looking to expand your knowledge of Black history, connect with others in the community, or simply enjoy a good book, Sister's Uptown Bookstore and Cultural Center is the perfect place to be.

## 4.Bookafé

## 5.Cafe con Libros

Empowering voices, one book and coffee at a time

The café was recommended by the LitSociety podcast and has a well-curated selection of books from various cultures. The latin diaspora is particularly well-represented in the collection, which was a delightful discovery for this reviewer. Additionally, works from Asian, African, and Caribbean authors can also be found in the library. The café's matcha drinks are highly recommended and add to the overall enjoyable experience of the establishment.

## 6.Molasses Books

A unique blend of bookstore and bar.

As a fan of cozy and relaxed environments, Molasses has quickly become my go-to spot for daytime work in Bushwick. The café offers a variety of drinks, including filter coffee, beer, and wine, making it a versatile destination for different times of the day. With the added bonus of second-hand books available for purchase, customers can enjoy reading, working, or simply relaxing in this charming space.

## 7.Book Club

Independent bookstore and bar in the heart of East Village.

The café aspect of Book Club is equally commendable, serving top-notch coffee and a variety of delicious drinks. Whether you're in the mood for a cappuccino or a chai latte, the knowledgeable baristas will craft a beverage that will delight your taste buds. The combination of great books, delicious drinks, and a cozy ambiance makes Book Club a must-visit destination for book lovers and coffee aficionados alike. Overall, it's a fantastic spot that truly embodies the joy of losing oneself in a good book while savoring a tasty drink.

## 8.The Center for Fiction

A haven for fiction lovers and writers in Brooklyn.

The bookstore café at The Center for Fiction is a must-visit for book lovers. With a wide selection of books and top-quality coffee, it offers a haven for those seeking a tranquil environment to indulge in their love of reading. The comfortable setting and serene atmosphere make it a perfect place to escape the hustle and bustle of the outside world. Whether you're looking for a new book to read or a quiet place to enjoy a good cup of coffee, this bookstore café is highly recommended.

## 9.McNally Jackson Books SoHo

Independent bookstore with a unique charm and community focus.

The café serves an excellent latté, making it an ideal location to take a break from shopping or sightseeing. Whether you're looking for a place to grab a quick drink or a comfortable spot to sit and read, McNally Jackson has got you covered. Their cozy café provides the perfect ambiance to slowly sip your coffee as you dive into a new book or catch up on some reading.

## 10.Yu & Me Books

A home for immigrant stories and diverse voices

This adorable bookstore has a vast array of Asian literature, showcasing not only East Asian literature but also South Asian and Arab literature. It also features a charming selection of stickers, providing customers with a variety of options to personalize their belongings. Despite its small size, which is common for small independent bookstores in the neighborhood, Yu&Me manages to create an inviting atmosphere that makes it easy for customers to lose track of time while browsing its offerings.

## 11.Milk & Roses

A magical garden setting perfect for any event.

As the weather turns cold, the restaurant transforms into a cozy and intimate space. The decorations are tastefully done, with a festive touch that adds to the warm and inviting atmosphere. Guests often rave about the phenomenal ambiance, describing it as magical, awesome, and the perfect setting for any event.

## 12.The Drama Book Shop

A cultural hub for theatre lovers since 1917.

In addition to its extensive collection of plays, musicals, and acting texts, the Drama Book Shop frequently hosts events, workshops, and author signings, making it a vibrant and engaging community hub for theater lovers. Its cozy and intimate atmosphere, combined with its knowledgeable and friendly staff, make it an ideal place for customers to discover new works, expand their knowledge, and connect with other like-minded individuals. Overall, the Drama Book Shop is a highly recommended destination for anyone interested in theater and the performing arts.

## 13.The Lit. Bar

The only indie bookstore in the Bronx.

The cozy and inviting atmosphere at The Lit. Bar makes it the ideal place to spend an afternoon. The café area serves up a variety of delicious drinks and snacks, making it easy to settle in with a good book for a few hours. The Lit. Bar also hosts a variety of events, including book clubs, author talks, and writing workshops, making it a true hub for the literary community in the Bronx. Overall, it's a must-visit destination for anyone who loves books and enjoys a great cup of coffee. Highly recommended!

## 14.Cups and Books

Bringing people together through shared stories

John and Tricia, the knowledgeable and passionate owners, have created a space that not only celebrates Black literature but also fosters a sense of community. The bookstore regularly hosts events, such as author talks and book clubs, that bring people together to engage in meaningful conversation and learn from one another. It is clear that the bookstore is a beloved institution in the PLG community, and it is certain to continue providing a valuable resource for those seeking to expand their understanding of Black culture and history.

## 15.Bluestockings Cooperative Bookstore

NYC's only queer, trans, sex-worker run bookstore.

The staff members are known for their kindness and eagerness to assist. They are highly knowledgeable about the products and literature they carry, making it easy for shoppers to find exactly what they're looking for. Whether you're a seasoned feminist or just starting to explore the movement, this bookstore is sure to have something for you.

## 16.Topos Bookstore Cafe

A perfect blend of literary and culinary delights.

The knowledgeable and friendly staff at Topos Bookstore Cafe further enhance the experience in this haven for book lovers. Their selection of books caters to a wide range of tastes, providing ample opportunity for patrons to uncover new favorites. Pairing this with a delightful cup of coffee, the café section offers a perfect setting to immerse oneself in a captivating read or enjoy engaging conversations with friends. Topos Bookstore Cafe is, indeed, a gem for those looking for a cozy retreat to enjoy the pleasures of both books and beverages.

## 17.Housing Works Bookstore

100% of profits fund lifesaving services for those in need.

In addition to its extensive collection of used books, Housingworks Bookstore also features a café that serves food and coffee. Customers can relax and enjoy a cup of coffee while browsing through the books. The café's cozy atmosphere makes it an ideal spot for reading or meeting up with friends. Moreover, the shop's profits support local initiatives aimed at ending AIDS and homelessness, making every purchase meaningful and impactful.

## 18.Archestratus Books + Foods

A haven for food lovers and book enthusiasts.

Archestratus Books & Foods is not your typical bookstore. This Brooklyn-based establishment offers an extensive collection of books on food, cooking, and culinary culture, hailing from every corner of the globe. Patrons can enjoy a diverse selection of beverages and bites while immersing themselves in the vast culinary literature. The bookstore's events, such as cooking demonstrations, author talks, and themed dinners, create a vibrant community atmosphere, making Archestratus a must-visit destination for food lovers and bookworms alike.

## 19.Dear friend books

A haven for book lovers in the heart of Brooklyn

This cozy sanctuary is ideal for those seeking a peaceful environment to spend a quiet afternoon. The combination of an extensive book collection and delicious coffee creates a haven for bookworms and café connoisseurs alike. Its charming ambiance and delightful offerings make Dear Friend Books a must-visit destination for anyone seeking a refreshing escape.

## 20.P&T Knitwear Bookstore, Coffee, & Podcast Studio

A hub for stories, creativity, and community.

In the heart of the community, P&T Knitwear bookstore stands as a welcoming space for book enthusiasts and café regulars alike. The combination of a thoughtfully selected book collection and a charming café creates an environment that is both inspiring and soothing. Ideal for those seeking a break from their daily routines, the bookstore and café invite patrons to unwind, indulge in their literary passions, and connect with others who share a similar love for stories and tranquil settings. At P&T Knitwear, visitors will find a haven for quiet afternoons and a celebration of the boundless joys of reading and community.

# Top 5 Most Cozy Bookstore Cafés in NYC that Readers Love

Nothing soothes a chilly **NYC** winter like curling up with a warm cup and a great book. **NYC cozy bookstore cafés** offer the perfect escape, blending inviting interiors, excellent drinks, and reading-friendly spaces.

Here’s a quick snapshot of NYC’s most cozy bookstore cafés before you dive in.

**✨ Fast Facts: NYC Bookstore Cafés**

| Bookstore | Best For | 
| Book Club Bar | Chill reading + social vibes | 
| Housing Works Bookstore Café | Budget treasures + social mission | 
| Topos Bookstore Cafe | Local favorite, comfy seats | 
| Cafe con Libros | Inclusive, intersectional space | 
| McNally Jackson Books Café | Classic NYC reading nook | 


ADVERTISEMENT

**1. Book Club Bar — Literary Lounge for Coffee & Community**

This **East Village staple, ****Book Club Bar** pairs a bookstore with a bar-café for readers who love atmosphere as much as their espresso. Visitors praise the space’s comfy chairs, strong coffee, and lively vibe, perfect for long afternoons of page-turning.

- **📚 Vibe:**Bookish but social. Ideal for post-work reading with coffee or wine.

**2. Housing Works Bookstore — Classic Cozy Bookstore Café**

A longtime NYC favorite, this SoHo bookstore doubles as a **laid-back café** and **community hub**. **Housing Works** sells secondhand books and serves coffee, craft beer, wine, and light bites. Reviewers love its “homey feel” and the charm of browsing used books with a warm drink in hand.

- ☕ **Best for:**Warm drip coffee or latte with a quiet read
- 📚 **Perks:**All profits fund homelessness and HIV services
- 📍 **Location:****SoHo**


“One of my favorite spots to sit, sip coffee, and flip through books for hours.”— authentic comment from reviews

**3. Topos Bookstore Cafe — Ridgewood’s Charming Book & Brew Spot**

Nestled in Queens, **Topos** is where high-quality used books meet a serious coffee program. While it’s more of a “grab-a-latte-and-browse” spot than a long-stay lounge, this **Time Out** feature remains a local favorite for its perfectly curated shelves. Snag a spot on their famous outdoor benches or a small indoor nook to flip through a rare find.

- ☕ **Drink & Read:**A meticulously pulled espresso + a rare vintage find
- 📚 **Why it’s great:**Best for discovering “deep cut” titles you won’t find elsewhere
- 📍 **Location:****Ridgewood (Queens)**

“The quintessential neighborhood bookstore. Small, quiet, and always has a hidden gem waiting for you.” —

Local regular

**4. Cafe con Libros — Warm, Inclusive Vibes in Crown Heights**

This intersectional, feminist bookstore is a vibrant pillar of the Brooklyn community. Though the space is intimate and seating is limited to a few cozy stools, the warmth is unmatched. **Cafe con Libros** is the perfect “slow-down” spot to grab a signature latte, chat with the incredibly welcoming staff, and pick up a book that challenges your perspective.

- ☕ **Try:**A signature seasonal latte while chatting with the community
- 📚 **Atmosphere:**Intimate, empowering, and deeply personal
- 📍 **Location: Crown Heights (BK)**


“Perfect for long reading sessions with a latte in winter.”— verified review

**5. McNally Jackson Books — SoHo’s Classic Indie Bookstore Café**

**McNally Jackson** is **one of NYC’s** **most respected independent bookstores** and includes an attached café space widely praised by visitors. The café is a **cozy nook** amidst shelves of fiction and nonfiction, ideal for whiling away winter hours.

- 📚 **Highlight:**Serene reading-friendly space in SoHo
- 📍 **Location: Find your nearest store! (SoHo / Seaport)**


“Great coffee and a relaxed reading atmosphere right in the bookshop.”— actual review snippet

NYC’s bookstore cafés offer more than just coffee, they’re winter sanctuaries for readers seeking warmth, community, and a good book. From downtown classics to Brooklyn favorites, each spot brings its own vibe and charm, backed by real love from local reviewers.

title: 20 All-Time Best New York City Book Cafés - Magazine
author: Migz
text:
Travel across Manhattan, Staten Island, and more to discover the 20 best book cafés and book bars in New York City.

New York is a city that runs on coffee; that’s why we’ve picked out the 20 best book cafés and book bars, from the Upper West Side to Staten Island.

**McNally Jackson Books Seaport**

McNally Jackson is an independent bookstore chain with multiple locations across the Big Apple, each with their own unique appeal.

Its Seaport branch, for example, invites visitors to grab a book and stay all day. The first floor is home to the store’s café and wine bar, with movie theater-esque carpeting and cozy booths and tables. Upstairs has an elegant but still inviting feel, with wooden floors, Persian rugs, and rows of bookshelves in between comfy lounge areas.

**Topos Bookstore Cafe**

Need a friendly face in the big city? Turn to Topos in Ridgewood, Queens, for a dose of old-fashioned warmth and laid-back hipster vibe. The inside is bright and welcoming, with mismatched furniture, eclectic wall art, and the kind of this-and-that décor that gives a place personality. Though its selection is mainly secondhand, you can find a few new titles as well.

On the café side, many reviewers talked about its reasonably priced drinks and tasty treats. They offer both indoor and outdoor seating—perfect for relaxing with one or two newly bought books.

**Cafe con Libros**

With a shopfront declaring Black, Feminist & Bookish (half-hidden behind some lovely hanging plant life), Cafe con Libros makes no secret about where it’s coming from. It spotlights women writers, particularly diverse writers, but doesn’t fuss about sticking to a particular genre.

While it doesn’t have a ton of seating, the café offers friendly service alongside some great coffees and lattes.

**Bluestockings Cooperative Bookstore**

Named after an informal society of English women intellectuals in the mid-18th century, this shop was designed from its conception in 1999 to be a radical feminist bookstore. Since 2020-2021, it has changed locations and began running as a full-worker co-op (i.e., “employee-owned” rather than run by a specific manager or owner).

Regulars love the sense of community and the creative menu, which often includes fun names like Lavender Menace (for coffee with lavender syrup) and London Fog Latte (Earl Grey with vanilla).

**Book Club Bar**

Coffee is hardly the beverage of choice for every bookworm out there. If you’d much rather have a cocktail with your favorite read, try Book Club Bar. With a bare brick wall, natural wooden shelving, and a candle-bearing fireplace, this book bar offers a cozy, intimate vibe.

Book Club Bar has a great selection of books and comic books and a literary-themed menu with cocktails and coffee. And, as a little Easter egg, you can find the first chapter of the comic book Persepolis plastered on the bathroom wall.

**The Center for Fiction**

This spot is big on aesthetics, creating a calming, open atmosphere for visitors. The main feature is the massive bookshelf lining the wall, facing out into the natural light let in by floor-to-ceiling windows. It’s a simple but striking design.

Behind the front-facing shop and café, however, is an exclusive club. Members get special access to upstairs working spaces and an outdoor patio.

**Barnes and Noble Café**

Head to Manhattan’s 5th Avenue for Barnes and Noble Café, which has a checkerboard floor and the perfect fix for a sweet tooth. It’s actually just a run-of-the-mill Starbucks on the second floor of a Barnes and Noble, but sometimes the familiarity of a well-known franchise can offer a spot of comfort in an often crazy world.

Like most Barnes and Noble, it offers a broad selection of books across a wide variety of genres for people of all ages. So, it makes for a nice stop with a group who have varying interests.

**Shakespeare & Co. Broadway**

Shakespeare & Co. has been independently owned since 1983 and has two locations: one on Lexington Ave next to Hunter College, and a more recent store that opened on Broadway. While its Lexington location shut down its coffee shop, Broadway’s café is thriving, with a wide selection of teas, coffee, wine, and beer alongside a decent selection of pastries and sandwiches.

Its book selection caters to a broad array of tastes, so it’s sure to have a few to grab anyone’s interest.

**New York Public Library Café (The Library Shop & Café by Amy’s Bread)**

Any tourist who pops into the New York Public Library’s Stephen A. Schwarzman Building is bound to want to pick up a volume themselves. For that, there’s no place better for that than the Library Shop. Its collection includes classics and newer titles from a variety of genres.

Meanwhile, the café is a branch of the ever-popular Amy’s Bread, and has plenty of delicious items on sale, from pastries to salads. The service provides that signature, grumpy New York charm, which will no doubt be a delight to tourists hoping to get the full Big Apple experience.

**Molasses Books**

Molasses Books is an all-in-one bookstore, café, and bar. It has a very cool, hipster vibe that attracts many creative types. Its atmosphere is friendly and laid back, and to many, is a home away from home where they can relax in one of many hidden nooks or mingle with like-minded people.

This place serves up some quality espresso in addition to its alcohol selection. Books-wise, its collection has a mix of new and used titles that prop up the hip, artsy vibe.

**P&T Knitwear Bookstore, Coffee & Podcast Studio**

This place is one of a kind; a mash of bookshop, coffee shop, event space, and podcast studio, all crowded into a concrete floor warehouse kind of interior. The bold orange and yellow signboard give it a pop art cinema vibe, something only helped along by occasional movie screenings and amphitheater-style seating.

As odd as it might all sound, it comes together into a perfect hangout spot. The book selection includes both mainstream and indie publishers, and covers an impressive range: academic, fiction, children’s, young adult, and more.

**Bibliotheque**

Bibliotheque is a book café and bar in the heart of SoHo. The walls of the dining area are lined with books and art, and the room comes with plenty of sofas and comfy chairs to relax in. And while the dim lighting in the evening is hardly ideal for reading, it certainly completes the “Bookstore and Café by Day/Wine Bar by Night” Batman transformation they’re aiming for.

From the food side of things, they offer plenty of fresh baked goods and a nice charcuterie board. They also have a decent wine selection, and quite a few praises for their daytime coffee as well.

**Every Thing Goes Book Cafe**

This is the largest used bookstore on Staten Island, offering a diverse collection of secondhand books, vinyl records, and CDs. Basically, they meant it when they named this place “Everything Goes.”

The café specializes in organic and fair-trade coffee, plus fresh fruit and sweet treats. It provides a cozy atmosphere, filled with a pleasant sort of clutter and a lively hustle and bustle. The shop also hosts various performances including live music, poetry readings, and more.

**The Drama Bookshop**

The Drama Bookshop always makes a dramatic entrance—how can it not, with such a stunning art display tunneling through the air? This shop has more to offer than just stunning aesthetics, though. It specializes in all film and theater-related literature, including plays, scripts, and books on cinema.

It has a small section for coffee and seating, but really, that’s all a sideshow to the main event: the pure love of cinema embodied in this store.

**The Lit. Bar**

The Lit. Bar isn’t just a great book bar; it’s the only independent bookstore in the Bronx. It was opened in 2019 by Noëlle Santos, a Bronx native, who wanted to bring literature back to the neighborhood after the closing of the only local bookseller.

It offers a wine bar and a curated selection of books, with a focus on local and diverse authors, including black feminist writers and Bronx-based authors. It also has a fresh and unique interior design, with an indoor tree growing out of the corner and art painted on the walls.

**Yu & Me**

Located in Manhattan’s Chinatown, Yu & Me is an independent bookstore in NYC owned by Lucy Yu, an Asian American woman. The bookstore’s initials, YM, are the same as her mother’s, and its collection is curated to highlight immigrant stories, particularly those that speak to the Asian American experience.

Its interior design is eclectic, but homey and welcoming, brimming with personality. It hosts regular events like open mic night and serves coffee and beer for a more relaxed atmosphere.

**Housing Works Bookstore**

This SoHo charity shop is entirely staffed by volunteers, and all profits go towards supporting people with HIV or AIDS who are homeless. Its stock is filled with donated books, clothes, CDs, and household goods, creating a diverse mix of items that’s always full of surprises.

The café side serves various drinks, including coffee and beer. Overall, it has a very elegant, polished interior that’s easy to relax in.

**Bungee Space**

Bungee Space is another fusion, located in Manhattan’s Lower East Side and combining art bookstore, fashion boutique, and café into a single, artistic space. It specializes in art books, zines, and photo books, often featuring works by emerging artists and independent publishers.

Alongside art books, the store showcases fashion-forward clothing meant to draw artists’ eye. Many visitors also praised the coffee and tea, which are made by a Japanese tea master.

**Dear Friend Books**

If you need a bit of calm in Brooklyn, duck into dear friend books—a name which, in itself, promises a peaceful and welcoming escape from the city. The simple, natural wooden shelving and spacious arrangement make it easy to relax at the bar with a drink of your choice. The menu is very broad, including wine, sake, tea, and kombucha, among others.

The book selection, while relatively small, is varied, and bound to pique the interest.

**Strand Book Store**

The Strand Book Store is one of the oldest and largest bookstores in the Big Apple, located in Manhattan’s East Village. It boasts over 2.5 million volumes that it touts as “18 miles of books,” covering a wide range of genres from philosophy to finance. Here, you can find both classics and a dedicated section to banned books.

The café is small, but it offers a decent coffee and a few tasty treats to give you fuel for more book-hunting.

title: 10 Best New York City Cafe Bookshops to Cozy Up Inside this Winter - The Creative Adventurer
author: The Creative Adventurer
