text:
**I may be compensated if you purchase through any affiliate links on this site. Thank you for supporting the Creative Adventurer**

Cold winter days in **New York City** can be pretty chilly even for the most prepared traveller. And there is no better way to escape the cold than to duck into a charming bookstore, especially those serving a hot cup of coffee! Coffeeshop bookstores have become one of the trendiest little treasures in a bustling city like New York. These little reading nooks are the best place to get warmed up and relax inside, away from the hustle and bustle of the big city. Grab a cup of your favourite warm beverage, snuggle up into a well-worn leather armchair with a new book, and the cold will simply melt away. So come with me as I bring you on a guided tour of the **Best Cafe Bookshops in New York City**! 

Whether you love science fiction, mystery novels or just chilling with the classics (or anything in between), these 10 bookshops in NYC will have something unique to offer everyone who loves a good read. I’ve been sure throughout this guide to include only cafe bookshops with space to sit and read. While some popular bookstores in New York have their own coffee counters, many only offer them to go, and we are looking for spots on this tour where you can really hunker down for the afternoon.

## Cafe con Libros

**Cafe con Libros** is literally translated into “coffee with books,” so you know you’ve come to the right place. This cozy little bookshop is hidden in Brooklyn’s Crown Heights neighbourhood. The bookshop is best known for being a black-owned feminist store featuring healing, empowering and enriching books. What could sound more comforting than that?

Their little window seats are the perfect place to get cozy and watch the world go by. The coffee is rich and delicious, and their freshly made pastries are the ideal accompaniment to nosh on while you read. Every Sunday, there is a book club meet-up, and the sense of community in this space is unrivalled.

## McNally Jackson Books

**Nolita** is New York’s “North of Little Italy” neighbourhood best known for its charming buildings, upscale designers and trendy boutiques. **Prince Street** is known for its popup jewelry and artwork vendors that swarm the street on weekends. Also along Prince Street is the **McNally Jackson Books**. **McNally Jackson Books** is a New York independent bookseller with four locations across the city. And while their location on Prince Street is far from the largest, it is indeed the most adorable.

This shop is known for its unique curated collection of recommended books. Its “*New York Reads*” section is incredible for tourists. You can pick up a book that is set or inspired by the city that never sleeps. Be sure to look up when visiting! Books hung from the ceiling, like paper airplanes flying across the store.

The cafe towards the back of the shop is serving up some incredible brews and delicious baked goods. The french toast bagel is just one example of their amazing creations! This place always has me coming back to see what’s new. Park yourself in the cafe seating area to savour the smells and sounds of this endearing bookshop.

## The Center for Fiction

In the centre of Brooklyn, you’ll find this monolith of literature; the **Center for Fiction**! The walls are toweringly high, with a huge ladder required to access the books on the tallest shelves. Like a modern-day version of *Beauty and the Beast’s* baroque library. The Center for Fiction opened its brick-and-mortar bookshop in 2019. The shop features floor-to-ceiling windows, allowing light to stream inside in the most heavenly way. Compared to some of the other bookstores on this list which are more *dark academia*, this place is *contemporary chic*!

In addition to their incredible selection of books, they also frequently hold panels, lectures, seminars, reading groups, and conversations. Often led by some of the nation’s most beloved writers. Their cozy cafe and bar is a fantastic spot to come and grab a bite to eat while enjoying your newest book purchase. There are so many people here writing away on notepads and computer screens. Like you can feel the next big novel written right in the room! The vibes here are unrivalled, and it is one of the most peaceful places in the city to come, shop and relax with a cup of coffee.

## The Drama Book Shop

As New York City is home to **Broadway** and one of, if not the BEST, places to see live theatre! And visiting the **Drama Book Shop** feels like a truly New Yorkian outing! Open since 1917, the **Drama Book Shop** has been a mainstay of the New York theatre scene and a cultural institution. One of my favourite parts of going inside is admiring the decor. They always go all out with the store’s styling, and I’m sure they get some set decorators to help them create these fantastical displays. The most impressive is the “book tornado” that spirals throughout the store. Whirling you into a dizzying book-buying frenzy!

Historic posters from Broadway’s past line the walls. If you are a thespian book lover, you’ll be in heaven. But it’s not just playbooks and musical scores that you’ll find here. There are many books about acting, non-fiction about theatre and history books all about Broadway past and present. There is also a fantastic collection of biographies from renowned actors and writers. If you ever wanted to know the secrets of the stage, you’ll find them in the books here.

Although the shop has been open for over 100 years, it only recently moved to this new location. The new shop was designed by ** Hamilton **set designer 

**David Korins**. It was created to pay homage to twentieth-century European reading room cafes. So, in addition to all 8,000 playbooks, they also have a full-service cafe! I love sitting in here, because as a musical lover, they really do have the BEST playlist!

## Molasses Books

If you’re looking for a cute used bookstore in the middle of the trendy **Bushwick** neighbourhood, look no further than **Molasses Books**. **Molasses Books** is a small, independent publishing house focusing on poetry, contemporary writers, and out-of-print or public domain works. Their brick-and-mortar shop in Bushwick, Brooklyn, is home to a varied collection of used books. You’ll never know what you’ll find here, but you can always expect it to be good.

The great thing about Molasses Books is that they are open from 11 am to midnight. If you’re a night owl, this is the spot for you to come to get some late-night reading done. In addition to coffee and tea, they are a fully licensed bar. So if you’re craving something a little stronger than cold brew.

## New York Public Library Cafe

One of the most incredible interiors in all of New York City has got to the awe-inspiring New York Public Library. Inside the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building. The NYC Public Library’s main branch was built in the late 1890s. The interiors were constructed in the Beaux-Arts style and featured one of the most beautiful reading rooms in the entire world. The reading room was meant to improve the morale of readers during the Great Depression. The room was meant to imbue visitors with a sense of wonder as they walked in. And even a hundred years later, I always get goosebumps walking inside.

Whether you’re a visitor or a local, you can enter this pantheon of reading and browse their collection. Tourists can’t check out books, but you’re welcome to explore. And if you’re looking to sit and enjoy a warm cup of coffee, then **Amy’s Bread** has you covered. Recently, Amy’s Bread opened a new location inside the **Library Shop**. Here, all visitors can come and grab an espresso and one of their incredible handmade pastries. Amy’s has been open in New York for over thirty years in Hell’s Kitchen. And now they have seven different shops open across the city! 

The best part of a visit to the library is that entrance to the building is free. So other than your coffee and sweet treat, the experience won’t cost you a dime! No need to buy any books. You can simply browse the shelves, find something that perks your interest and sit down to enjoy.

## Shakespeare & Co

**Shakespeare & Co** is a well-known name in the literary game, opening their flagship store in **Paris **(of all places for a shop named after the English playwright.) But in 1983, they opened their New York City location along Lexington Avenue, on the Upper East Side.

Recently, the bookshop introduced a small but top-notch cafe among the hundreds of books inside. The baristas here are friendly, and the quaint little area where you can sit and enjoy your coffee while reading is the perfect size to feel nice and cozy. The cafe also features a daily selection of **Dough donuts**. If you know *Dough*, you’ll learn how delicious these sweet pastries really are! And what’s better than doughnuts and coffee…and books?! 

## Barnes & Noble

Although visiting a **Barnes & Noble** might sound like a boring and basic thing to do when visiting the Big Apple, the Barnes & Noble on Union Square is actually the **biggest bookstore in Manhattan!** This Barnes & Noble is also located inside the old headquarters of the Century Publishing Company. And the building it now resides in was built in 1881. The stunning brick and copper engravings are still the beacon of literacy that draw many into it today. Walking inside, look at the old iron columns, wooden bookshelves and library ladders. It always makes me feel like I’ve stepped back in time. And I love the store’s effort to preserve this slice of New York architectural history.

On the 3rd floor, you’ll find their coffee shop. Their cafe is vast, and there is lots and lots of space to spread out! The windows that face south also feature a gorgeous view across Union Square park, the Flatiron building and the south Manhattan skyline! Sure the coffee might be Starbucks, but the environment is so friendly and open, and you can almost always find a spot to sit! Plus, public bathrooms are a key essential any visitor knows comes in clutch. One of the other advantages of visiting such a big brand in this iconic location is often it is where authors come to have signing events. So check their schedule to see who’s in town. But hundreds of signed books are also spread out throughout the store, like hidden treasure waiting to be found.

## Housing Works Bookstore

People celebrated on the streets across the city when it was announced that the **Housing Works Bookstore** cafe had reopened after the pandemic. Ok, well, not literally, but when this literary touchstone was finally reopened, it was definitely a cause for celebration. The **Housing Works Bookstore** is another historic building transformed into a chic bookshop. It is so popular that it is often booked out on the weekends as a fashionable venue for weddings. It was even featured in **Taylor Swift’s** music video for her smash hit *All Too Well*.

The Housing Works Bookstore has been open downtown in New York for over a decade. Unlike any other shop on this list, 100% of the profits from the book sales go to fund Housing Works’ lifesaving services. Their cafe is the perfect place to immerse yourself in their cozy atmosphere. In addition to beverages and food, you can also pick up a cocktail at the bar.

## Book Club

Located in the heart of the East Village is the aptly named **Book Club**, one of the best independent bookstores and bars in town. Whether it’s coffee, NY state craft beer, wine, romance novels, mystery books or autobiographies that you’re looking for, you’re bound to find that here! The owners who started the Book Club wanted to create a space in the city’s centre where you could feel nice and cozy while surrounded by the most lovingly curated collection of books.

One of the shop’s most exciting aspects is that it is open till midnight but is** laptop free ***after 7pm*! This is meant to encourage people to chat with each other, make friends and take book recommendations in the evening when the wine is flowing. This a great reminder to turn off the computer or put down your phone and enjoy a bit of screen-free time with new friends. Plus, this place has some great music too! The vibes here are immaculate.

I hope you enjoyed this little literary jaunt around the city and found spots along the way to snuggle up inside on a cold winter’s day. Let me know your favourite bookshops in the comments where you love to sit and drink a cup of coffee in your hometown! Maybe I’ll be visiting there next!

title: Top Bookstore Cafes in New York City for Book Lovers [2024]
author: Priyanka
text:
Exploring the fusion of literature and culinary delights in one place would be an ideal weekend plan for any book lover.

Amidst New York City’s bustling energy, bookstore cafes can offer a tranquil escape, where the aroma of coffee blends with the scent of books. These cozy corners are perfect for getting lost in a book while enjoying the aroma of freshly brewed coffee.

New York City has a lot to offer, and I believe these gems are one of them. Here are some of the best book cafes in NYC that the bookworms swear by.

### Best Bookstore Cafes in NYC

## Housing Works Bookstore

*Address: 126 Crosby St, New York, NY 10012*

The Housing Works Bookstore is located in Soho, a trendy neighborhood in Manhattan. 100% of their profits go to fund Housing Works’ lifesaving services. With a cozy café, a diverse selection of books, and a range of events, it’s a perfect Bookstore Cafe in New York City to spend your time in.

## Book Club Bar

*Address: 197 E 3rd St, New York, NY 10009*

Book Club Bar is a charming independent bookstore located in East Village. Its cozy interior exudes a warm living room ambiance and they have a curated selection of adult fiction, non-fiction, and children’s books.

In addition to the bookstore, they offer locally roasted coffee, a variety of craft beers from New York State, and a selection of wines and cocktails.

Whether you’re in search of a good read or a relaxing place to enjoy a beverage, Book Club has something for everyone in the heart of the East Village.

## Cafe Con Libros

*724 Prospect Pl, Brooklyn, NY 11216*

Cafe con Libros, an Intersectional Feminist community bookstore and coffee shop, is a truly unique gem. A perfect place for book lovers who love to add a side of coffee to their reading ritual. They aim to create a community of readers and thinkers who feel loved and accepted.

With a wide selection of books and a cute sitting area outside, it’s a fantastic book cafe in NYC to spend your time at, either alone or with your friend.

## Topos Bookstore Care

*788 Woodward Ave, Ridgewood, NY 11385*

Topos Bookstore Cafe, nestled in Ridgewood, Queens, has been a beloved neighborhood store since 2014. This small yet cozy establishment offers a delightful blend of used and new books, making it a haven for book lovers seeking diverse literary treasures.

With the added bonus of serving Variety Coffee, it’s a charming spot where you can enjoy a cup of joe while exploring your latest literary find.

## The Center for Fiction

*15 Lafayette Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11217*

The Center for Fiction, a unique literary nonprofit based in the heart of Downtown Brooklyn, stands as a dedicated haven for all things fiction.

You’ll discover a dynamic blend of amenities, including a Bookstore, Café & Bar, Library, and Writers Studio, making it a multifaceted space for those who cherish the written word.

The Center for Fiction actively fosters a sense of community by offering a rich variety of programs throughout the year, designed to unite diverse communities in their shared passion for storytelling. Whether you’re a passionate reader or an aspiring writer, this book cafe in NYC provides a welcoming space for literary enthusiasts

## The Drama Book Shop

*266 W 39th St, New York, NY 10018*

If you love dramas and theatres, as much as you love books, The Drama Book Shop is a must-visit. In the midst of the theatrical scenes in New York, this book cafe has been the birthplace of a lot of theatrical works.

Rounding all of that up with a cafe, this makes a wholesome place for all the book lovers. Choose from a wide selection of coffees, teas, pastries and other snacks and lounge on any of the comfy chairs and read your book.

## Barnes & Noble

*33 E 17th St, New York, NY 10003*

I am sure no one has never not heard of Barnes and Noble.

And this bookstore in Union Square is one of the best B&N stores. It’s a huge book shop with four floors and a cafe on the third, with a big seating space.

The store is well-stocked and you have a lot of genres to explore like Romance, Science Fiction and more. There are a lot of events – virtual and offline that you can attend at this B&N.

Be sure to explore this one when you’re in NYC.

## McNally Jackson Books

*134 Prince St, New York, NY 10012*

McNally Jackson is one of the best independent bookstores in NYC.

With a fantastic layout, you’ll spend hours picking from the best selection of books from different genres like arts, fiction, films and more. Apart from books, you’ll also find a good collection of journals, cards, and other stationary items.

This NYC Bookstore also offers fine coffees and wine, making it a perfect haven for book lovers who are also a coffee or wine aficionado.

## Molasses Books

*770 Hart St, Brooklyn, NY 11237*

Molasses Books is an eclectic mix of a bookstore, cafe, and bar. It’s a charming book cafe and bar with a cozy atmosphere. You can stay up till midnight with your choice of beverage and book (what more can we ask for haha)

There is a good selection of books both used and new from a wide range of genres. One of the unique things about this place is you can barter your copies for coffee, beer, or more books. The coffee is to go for and you can also get beer – all affordable.

## The Lit. Bar

*131 Alexander Ave, Bronx, NY 10454*

The Lit. Bar is the only brick-and-mortar store currently in the Boogie Down Bronx. They have a wide selection of books especially by people of color, making it a safe space for everyone.

The bar menu has an extensive range of wines, and also snacks for you to munch on as you read your book. The book cafe has a pleasant and unique atmosphere, perfect to spend your reading time.

## Every Thing Goes Book Cafe and Neighborhood Stage

*208 Bay St, Staten Island, NY 10301*

ETG Book Cafe is located in Staten Island, the largest bookstore in the area, with a wide variety of used and new books.

The cafe has a lot to offer – coffees, supplied by Equal Exchange, are organic and Fairtrade. They have bagels, vegan-friendly options, and other light snacks to munch on as you read your book. Along with being a quirky, vintage bookstore, there are also live performances happening.

A perfect place with a cozy atmosphere and friendly faces.

## Shakespeare & Co

*2020 Broadway, New York, NY 10023*

Shakespeare and Co offers a diverse and extensive selection of books that caters to every taste. From bestsellers to classics, fiction to non-fiction, and poetry to philosophy, their collection is a literary treasure trove.

The store features a charming cafe where you can savor a cup of coffee and pastries while immersing yourself in your latest literary find. Beyond just a bookstore, Shakespeare and Co. embodies a community of like-minded readers and writers who share a deep passion for literature.

These are some of the highly recommended Bookstore Cafes in New York City.

Add them to your list for your next bookstore hop, and experience the best of books and snacks and wine/beer/coffee!

Let me know if you have visited any of them!

*Looking for book recs? Here are some that I have reviewed: *

- Beautiful Disaster by Jamie McGuire (New Adult Romance)
- Deviant King by Rina Kent (Dark Bully Romance)
- Brutal Prince by Sophie Lark (Mafia Romance)
- Bared to You by Sylvia Day (Billionaire Romance)

title: Exploring Unique Coffee Shop Bookstores in Lower Manhattan
author: Ashley
text:
# Exploring Unique Coffee Shop Bookstores in Lower Manhattan

Imagine you’re strolling through Lower Manhattan, overwhelmed by cars honking, the mysterious puddle you just accidentally stepped in, and avoiding running into people at every step. Suddenly, a magical combination catches your attention — local bookstore coffee shops. Yes, you heard that right! These hidden gems blend the love for books with the aroma of freshly brewed coffee, creating an epic experience that’s anything but ordinary. Get ready for a fun, caffeinated ride as we dive into the three hippest coffee shop bookstores in Lower Manhattan.

### Book Club: East Village’s Ultimate Hangout Spot

Book Club is where it’s at in the East Village. This unique bookstore serves up some great coffee during the day and morphs into a wicked bar at night. As you step into Book Club, you’ll be transported to a world of dark wood academia vibes that will make you feel like an intellectual rockstar. The seating here is limited because the space is not crazy big, but it’s certainly cozy. They have areas with stools and tables, the bar top, and even plush couch seating. The environment is quite conducive to socializing or getting some work done. So grab a book, sip your java, and read something fabulous!

### P&T Knitwear: Lower East Side’s Hidden Gem

Prepare to be blown away by P&T Knitwear, the ultimate place to chill during a busy NYC day in the Lower East Side. This bookstore has all the most up-to-date recommendations and features a variety of newer creative works. I loved the books that they were showcasing and, through browsing their selection, added some books to my reading list.

Now, let’s talk aesthetics — this place has a simple, sleek modern design and GREAT lighting. Of course, P&T Knitwear is a solid bookstore, but we can’t forget about the coffee shop built into the store too! They have the usual essential selection of caffeinated drinks and a small bar top to sit at too. They have lots of seating on a giant staircase or a few tables with chairs too. So grab a cup and enjoy a book or get some work done in this fantastic bookstore!

### Housing Works: SoHo’s Literary Hideaway

Housing Works is a coffee shop bookstore in SoHo, and it’s quite extensive. With its vast space and books galore, you’ll feel you’ve discovered a hidden cave within the chaos of the big city as soon as you walk in. There’s room for everyone here, with a lot of seating in the back of its store where their cafe is. It really feels like you’re in a regular full-sized coffee shop, plopped in the middle of a bunch of bookshelves. This place’s vibes are also very cozy, with its bookstore cave feel and warm wood accents.

## Satisfy your literary and caffeination cravings!

Lower Manhattan’s local bookstore coffeeshops offer a delightful blend of literary exploration and coffee culture. Whether you seek the cozy charm of Book Club, the modern aesthetics of P&T Knitwear, or the vast literary paradise of Housing Works, each unique establishment provides a haven for book lovers and coffee enthusiasts alike.

There are many more that I didn’t include in this list, too, and so many I’ve yet to explore. Let me know if you know of any others that I should visit. And next time you crave a literary escape or a caffeine fix, try venturing into one of these coffee shop bookstores and discover the perfect blend of words and beverages. You won’t be disappointed.

title: NYC's Prettiest Bookstores: 9 Spots For Books and Aesthetics
author: Theworkingline; The Working Line
text:
*A guide to NYC’s prettiest bookstores from Midtown to Brooklyn and the Upper East Side – the most beautiful bookstores (some are must-visit book cafes!)!*

Whether you visit New York City at Christmas, during spring or in the dead of fall, the city is a treasure trove of gorgeous, unique bookstores anchored in the community that offer an immersive experience into the literary world.

From Books Are Magic in quaint Brooklyn to Broadway’s Rizzoli Bookstore and the charming Corner Bookstore on the Upper East Side, the places you’ll see today offer more than just books – they also offer looks.

*Plenty of, actually.*

Whether you’re looking for a romance fiction or an inspiring biography, these are the prettiest bookstores in New York City, and make for must-visit spots for whoever would like to treat their close ones… or themselves.

## NYC’s Prettiest Bookstores: 9 Spots For Books and Aesthetics

Before we get started, I have to admit to loving *anything* related to the book world.

If you ever decide to visit other cities in the world, like Paris or London, you’ll find out, for instance, that London boasts lots of bookish locations, which also include quirky sculptures and spots celebrating Shakespeare.

Paris also offers some of the prettiest bookstores in the world, like famous Shakespeare & Company, close to the Quartier Latin’s floral spots and other cute coffee shops.

When it comes to other cities I’ve lived in or visited, I’ve found that many of Rome’s bookshops, in Italy, are more on the antique and rare book side – another kind of charm from the old world.

Anyhoo; if you’re into rustic, old and aesthetic bookstores, let’s get started with this new travel guide to New York City!

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: The Corner Bookstore, Upper East Side

Tucked away in Manhattan’s sophisticated Upper East Side, The Corner Bookstore is an independent and unique store with a warm, inviting interior and a carefully-curated selection of New York-centric titles, fiction, and children’s books.

Established in 1978, this gorgeous bookstore draws in visitors who would like to lose themselves in books and find hidden literary gems, only a few blocks from Central Park.

Beyond the old-world charm The Corner Bookstore boasts, it’s also a community place where the friendly staff will help you and advise titles you’d never have thought of – and a bookstore historically famous for its book signings.

Once you’re done wandering around the fully-stacked bookshelves and enjoying the gorgeous bookstore’s inviting atmosphere, stroll down Madison Avenue to admire Christmas lights, or make your way for the world-famous Guggenheim Museum.

Or, walk to Central Park to discover the Burnett Fountain, another must-visit literary location in NYC, since it revolves around Burnett’s The Secret Garden, and particularly beautiful during the fall and the spring.

Read: 9 Cozy Spots For Desserts in London

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: Albertine Bookstore

Nestled inside the French Embassy on Fifth Avenue, Albertine Bookstore features an ornate interior that reflects the Beaux-Arts architecture of the mansion it’s established in, the historic Payne Whitney mansion built in 1906.

What makes Albertine one of the prettiest bookstores in NYC, beyond its heavy, glossy wooden furniture and floors, is none other than the starry ceiling in the upstairs reading room.

Inspired by Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel and reimagined with zodiac constellations, the painted ceiling adds an artistic layer to an otherwise quite intellectual atmosphere.

Not only can you walk around and browse for your next read, but Albertine Bookstore also hosts events, signings, and located only minutes away from Bergdorf Goodman.

If you’d like to do some shopping in NYC, this upscale spot is perfect for gifts and treats after a visit to both Francophiles and book lovers alike!

Read: London’s Best Christmas Markets to Visit for Festive Fun

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: The Ripped Bodice, Brooklyn

The Ripped Bodice in Brooklyn, located on 5th Avenue, is not only a family-run business, but also the ultimate store to visit if you’re into romance and fiction.

A colorful addition to New York’s indie bookstore scene, The Ripped Bodice is famous for their unparalleled selection of romance novels and inclusive collections.

Inside the pretty bookstore, beyond books, you’ll find plenty of cute little photo spots and cozy reading nooks – and if you’re into meeting new people, why not attend a workshop, a book signing, or one of the many events The Ripped Bodice hosts?

When you’re done shopping, you’ll find plenty of free things to do in Brooklyn; Prospect Park for a serene walk in nature, or, on select days, the Brooklyn Museum and the Brooklyn Botanic Garden – great if you’re tight on budget!

Read: 9 Pretty Cafes in London With Dazzling Christmas Decor

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: The Drama Bookshop, Midtown

Originally founded by the Drama League in 1917, the Drama Bookshop in the Theater District in Midtown Manhattan became an independent bookstore in 1923, and is an it-spot for theater enthusiasts.

Inside, you’ll find everything from posters of Broadway classics to rare books, and thousands of plays – but it’s really the 140-foot bookworm sculpture that makes Pinterest, Instagram, and locals talk.

Made of 2,400 recycled materials, the bookstore’s interior, designed by David Korins of Hamilton fame, makes it one of NYC’s most unique stores, and even has an on-site cafe to sip and nibble while you’re reading.

When you’re done admiring this Midtown gem, why not discover other places nearby, like Bryant Park (a must-visit if you’re visiting NYC around Christmas!), Times Square for glowing lights, or the New York Public Library with its iconic architecture and interiors?

Read: The Most Colorful Cities in the World

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: Rizzoli, Broadway

Located in the heart of Manhattan’s NoMad district, Rizzoli Bookstore on Broadway, first opened in Midtown in 1964, is a must-visit place for anyone into books, architecture, and history.

Elegant columns, striking Fornasetti murals, the Saint James Building in which Rizzoli Bookstore is nestled feels glamorous, almost overwhelming, as does the impressive collection of books Rizzoli offers.

Specializing in architecture, art, photography and culinary literary, Rizzoli Bookstore also boasts a curated selection of French, Italian and Spanish books – great if you’re trying to learn a new language!

When you’re done browsing, it’s time to enjoy some of NYC’s landmarks; just a short walk away, you’ll find the Flatiron Building and Madison Square Park.

Should you want to spend some time in Flatiron, one spot to visit absolutely, especially if you’re very hungry, is Eataly Flatiron.

With its tasty Italian specialties and its food market downstairs, Eataly is *very* pretty restaurant to visit during the fall in NYC, but also at Christmas and spring for striking decor that follows the seasons.

Read: The Best Cafes to Work in Manhattan

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: Sweet Pickle Books

Now, with Sweet Pickle Books on the Lower East Side, we have one of the quirkiest bookstores in New York City – opened in 2020, Sweet Pickle Books embodies a lovely fusion of the literary and culinary worlds.

Embracing the area’s rich history as a hub for Jewish pickle vendors, and combining it with her lifelong passion for books, Leigh Altshuler decided to take a community-focused approach, accepting book donations in exchange for jars of pickles.

Unique reads, handwritten signs, and a playful layout: Sweet Pickle Books definitely is one of the *prettiest* bookstores you could visit while in town.

It’s also great to treat yourself to a new read before visiting the Tenement Museum, the Essex Market or, if you’re hungry, the Katz’ Delicatessen for its famous pastrami sandwiches.

Read: The Most Instagrammable Places in NYC

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: Housing Works Bookstore, SoHo

Located in the lively SoHo neighborhood, Housing Works Bookstore is one of the most interesting places to visit in NYC because it’s not just a bookstore.

Established in 1996, this bookstore is indeed part of the Housing Works nonprofit initiative aimed at combating homelessness and supporting people living with HIV/AIDS – the books are entirely donated, and the staff are mostly volunteers.

Over two stories, the Housing Works Bookstore offers charming views; floor-to-ceiling shelves, wooden staircases, a cute on-site cafe, and everything from rare books to fiction can be found there.

If you’d like to meet new people, you’ll find that community-based Housing Works Bookstore is also a vibrant cultural hub: live music, storytelling series and book launches also take place there, in addition to the odd charity gala and wedding.

When you’re done enjoying the lovely vibe, make your way to the New Museum on Bowery for avant-garden exhibitions, take in the charm of the Little Italy area around Mulberry Street, or why not take a walk around Soho’s cast-iron buildings?

Read: A Local’s Fashion in London Itinerary from Museums to Shops

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: Lit. Bar, Bronx

Opened in 2019 by African American and Puerto Rico Noëlle Santos, the Lit. Bar on Alexander Avenue in the Bronx is one of the area’s only independent bookstores, and one that champions Black and Latino voices.

The diverse selection of titles highlights locals authors, bridging the Bronx’s past with its evolving present – the mission, here, is to celebrate literature and the Bronx’s culture.

When you’re done browsing the curated selection of Afro and Latino books, make your way to the Bronx Museum of the Arts for another layer of arty to your way, or visit the New York Botanical Garden for its incredible miniatures and manicured gardens.

And, if you’re a sports fan, consider visiting the Yankee Stadium, home of the Bronx Bombers, to anchor yourself into NYC life a bit more!

Read: The Most Instagrammable Cafes in NYC

### Prettiest Bookstores in NYC: Books Are Magic, Brooklyn

Books Are Magic in Cobble Hill, Brooklyn, might be more famous for its vibrant pink mural outside, but it’s a beloved neighborhood staple at this point, with shelves packed with bestsellers, hidden gem books and children’s books.

The store is known for hosting regular events that help anchor reading a bit more in the community, including author readings, panels, and kids’ story time.

If you’re visiting NYC with kids, why not take part in an event to further take in the city’s creative atmosphere?

When you’re done at Books Are Magic, explore Cobble Hill’s quaint streets and make your way to the Brooklyn Bridge Park, perfect to get free views of NYC, or the New York Transit Museum, located in an impressive decommissioned subway station.

Read: 15 Themed London Itinerary Ideas Off the Beaten Path

## NYC’s Prettiest Bookstores: 9 Spots For Books and Aesthetics

Thus finishes this guide to the prettiest bookstores in New York City: exploring them is like diving into the city’s very core; creative, unique, diverse, and always unexpected.

Whether you pop by the Drama Bookshop close to Broadway or want to discover the neighborhood warmth of Books Are Magic (and take a picture in front of the famous mural!), you’ll hopefully have found new spots you can’t wait to visit.

Across every borough, from the Lower East Side to Midtown, these bookstores aren’t just for book lovers.

They’re for history and architecture lovers, for dreamers, and for anyone looking to discover the true NYC off the beaten path.

title: The 12 Best NYC Restaurants, Coffee Shops, And Bars For Book Lovers - Tasting Table
author: Nikki Vargas
text:
# The 12 Best NYC Restaurants, Coffee Shops, And Bars For Book Lovers

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

New York has a lot to offer, but quiet places to settle in with a book are not one of them. Sure, you can find a bench in Central Park, but chances are the sounds of honking cabs and idle chatter will punctuate your reading. Thankfully, the city has seen a rise in bookish places that offer respite from the crowded streets — and a chance to grab a quick bite, a cocktail, or even a full sit-down dinner. If you're unsure of where to settle in with a good read, I've done some of the legwork for you. Not only have I lived in New York City for over 15 years and experienced some its best spots, but I am a two-time published author and professional writer — which is to say I spend *a lot* of time writing in cafés and, especially, bookstores that double as coffee shops.

Many of the following places are hybrid bookstores and cafés — places where one can read a book, buy a book, and enjoy a small bite and drink alongside a novel. A few of the places are restaurants that manage to capture the magic of books through thoughtful decor. A lot of these places are neighborhood gems that act as community hubs where book lovers can gather and, in some cases, help those in need. Whether you're searching for a bookstore to relax or a cozy restaurant that feels like you've stepped into an old library, here's where book lovers should go in New York City.

## Biblotheque in SoHo

Bibliotheque opened back in 2022 and was founded by celebrity plastic surgeon-turned-entrepreneur Dr. Andrew Jacono, who worked with notable patients — including fashion designer Marc Jacobs**.** When you step into Bibliotheque, you'll be greeted by a long bar room that leads into an open space lined with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves and a mix of lounge chairs and tables. This all-day, all-night SoHo spot has since become a haven for book lovers and remote workers who can perch up with a book (and their laptop) while nibbling on a food menu from Daniel Boulud's Epicerie Boulud. Once happy hour hits, this bookstore-meets-wine spot enforces a no-computer policy, which is honestly for the best, as Bibliotheque curates a fantastic events calendar that includes everything from monthly book clubs and cinema nights to wine-fueled writing retreats. 

Bibliotheque also takes its books-meets-wine hybrid to the next level. Its wine list is formatted to resemble a novel and is divided into "chapters." Wines by the glass are "short stories," while tasting notes correspond to bookish genres like romance, art history, and fantasy. Bibliotheque is an ideal spot for book lovers to enjoy a glass of wine and a good read; its collection comprises over 3,000 curated wine bottles with a focus on French and Italian vintages.

(646) 410-0143

54 Mercer St, New York, NY 10013

## Book Club Bar in the East Village

If SoHo's Bibliotheque is the place to enjoy a book and a glass of wine, then Book Club Bar is the place for book lovers to enjoy literary-themed cocktails. Longtime East Village residents Erin Neary and Nat Esten — who met at a book club in 2011— are the founders of Book Club Bar, which opened in 2019. Like Bibliotheque, Book Club Bar features a wooden bar where patrons can sip on coffee or cocktails while enjoying a good book or writing the next great American novel. The back of Book Club Bar opens onto a cozy bookstore with wooden shelves sagging beneath the weight of books. The open space is filled with rugs, leather armchairs, and wooden tables lining an exposed brick wall.

During the warmer months, Book Club Bar opens its backyard for some al fresco reading, too. But back to the book-themed bar, which offers a full literary-themed cocktail menu with creatively named libations like Feminine Mezcal Mystique (a mix of mezcal, maple syrup, lemon, and cardamom bitters) or the Murder on the Orient Espresso (Book Club Bar's take on a classic espresso martini). Like Bibliotheque, Book Club Bar also enforces a no-laptop policy once happy hour hits, which encourages its patrons to be present for the fantastic events that take place at this beloved neighborhood gem.

(646) 678-4160

197 E 3rd St, New York, NY 10009

## Sullaluna in the West Village

If books and pasta are more your speed, look no further than Sullaluna. Its original location is in Venice, but the Italian bistro eventually opened an NYC outpost in Manhattan's West Village on Carmine Street. Founded by Francesca Rizzi and her husband Rodolfo, Sullaluna combines Italian fare (and flair) with beautifully illustrated children's books and art books displayed on shelves lining the walls. While most of the books at Sullaluna are for children, adults will also find interesting books to peruse, including titles on design, illustration, and storytelling.

Book lovers with a deep appreciation for aesthetic appeal will appreciate how Sullaluna's founders have lovingly curated their collection of books. It was in part inspired by Francesca's upbringing in an art-loving family, as well as the selections she collected during her travels. Her appreciation for illustration infuses all of the books on Sullaluna's shelves.

Sullaluna is cozy, albeit small, so it's recommended to make a reservation ahead of time if you're planning to dine in and enjoy your reading alongside a bowl of cacio e pepe or gnocchi.

sullalunavenezia.it/category/ny

(212) 352-3182

41 Carmine St, New York, NY 10014

## The Lit Bar in the Bronx

The Lit Bar is the only independent bookstore in the Bronx and, as such, has become a beloved cultural hub in the Mott Haven neighborhood since opening in 2019. The Lit Bar was founded by Bronx native Noëlle Santos when the neighborhood's only bookstore — a Barnes & Noble — shuttered its doors in 2016. When one door closes, another one opens, and so with the closure of Barnes & Noble came the opening of the neighborhood's new and only bookstore-meets-wine bar, which offers a curated selection of books tailored to the Bronx community, including "where black women and feminism intersect" or hip hop blends with poetry.

For book lovers, The Lit Bar is a special place infused with a deep Bronx pride that places special emphasis on uplifting diverse voices and BIPOC authors through organizing community events, poetry nights, and author events. You can come to The Lit Bar to enjoy a glass of wine or graze on one of its cheese or charcuterie boards or, better yet, pair books with brunch by ordering one of Lit Bar's brunch boards, featuring either Belgian waffles or cinnamon sugar French toast –served with fresh berries, whipped cream, and syrup.

(347) 955-3610

131 Alexander Ave, Bronx, NY 10454

## Cafe con Libros in Brooklyn

Another community bookshop is Cafe con Libros in Brooklyn, which doubles as a coffee shop. Founded by Kalima Desuze in 2017, this intersectional feminist community bookstore was created with a mission to center the narratives of BIPOC women through a curated collection of feminist-leaning literature.

"I wanted to build a space that is completely and unapologetically dedicated to feminist texts, narratives, and authors," Kalima Desuze said in an interview with Black-Owned Brooklyn. She refers to books by icons like Toni Morrison and Zora Neale Hurston and explains how women's voices — and especially the voices of diverse women — were essential to her own upbringing.

"They gave me a vision of myself. They gave me roots. They affirmed me. So I'm trying to center stories by women, about women, for women, particularly women across the diaspora and women of color who we don't typically hear from in the mainstream," she says.

Walk into Cafe con Libros (which translates from Spanish as "coffee with books"), and you'll discover a glossy coffee bar and cozy seating alongside white shelves adorned with an eye-catching rainbow of titles. It's the sort of place that is ideal for spending an afternoon sipping on tea, enjoying a latte (whipped up by Desuze's co-founder, husband, and barista, Ryan Cameron), and diving into a good book.

(929) 327-9373

724 Prospect Pl, Brooklyn, NY 11216

## Liz's Book Bar in Brooklyn

From books and pasta to books and coffee to books and cocktails, bibliophiles have their pick of the litter when choosing how they'd like to read in NYC. But what about book lovers who with a sweet tooth? Enter Liz's Book Bar, a Brooklyn gem that serves a menu with tantalizing baked goods such as a za'atar and preserved lemon scone or a cranberry and coconut oatmeal cookie.

Founded by novelist Maura Cheeks (the author of "Acts of Forgiveness"), this spot is named for Cheeks' grandmother, who inspired her own writing. Expect an airy, cool, and light-filled space with wood shelving lined with over 4,000 titles, including the latest releases. Pair that with a chill R&B playlist and its baked goods, and you'll see why Liz's Book Bar is well worth the subway ride to Brooklyn.

(718) 210-2222

315 Smith St, Brooklyn, NY 11231

## Milk & Roses in Brooklyn

Brooklyn's Milk and Roses isn't a bookstore — but don't let that deter you. Stepping into this shop is like entering a dreamy library, complete with soft lighting, red booths, and wooden shelves lined with antique books. Inside this Greenpoint restaurant, which serves an Italian-focused menu, you'll feel as though you're moving through the old and deeply loved home of a dear friend who happens to be a book collector or, perhaps, an eclectic writer.

Enter the lush garden patio, and a magical haven of fairy lights, ivy-draped walls, and rustic furniture will greet you. Milk and Roses was opened by husband and wife team Tommaso Mazzoni and Helena Yelovich, who met on the Subway. The pair transformed what was once a rustic kitchenette into this bookish nirvana that feels like it's worlds away from the streets of Brooklyn.

(718) 389-0160

35 Box St, Brooklyn, NY 11222

## Yu & Me Bookstore in Chinatown

Founded by Lucy Yu in December 2021, Yu & Me Books became NYC's first Asian-American woman-owned independent bookstore. Its mission is simple: to highlight diverse voices, spotlight immigrant stories, and celebrate books by BIPOC authors. Since opening, Yu & Me has become a neighborhood gem, serving as a gathering place for readers, writers, and creatives.

Despite facing a devastating fire back in 2023, Yu & Me rose like a phoenix from the ashes and — with the help of crowdfunding efforts and community support — reopened its doors. The resilience of Yu & Me (much like the diverse stories that it shares) makes this place a special spot for book lovers to spend time and enjoy the cozy ambiance of its in-store café, serving locally-roasted coffees, teas, wine, beer, and snacks. If headed to Yu & Me, make sure to check out its events calendar, which shares upcoming book launches, author meet-and-greets, book clubs, and more.

(646) 559-1165

44 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10013

## The Algonquin Hotel's Blue Bar in Midtown

On a list spotlighting the best NYC places for book lovers, it's impossible not to honor the city's literary history. The Algonquin Hotel has a storied past thanks largely to its iconic Round Table, where an informal group of writers, critics, and editors regularly met back in the 1920s to discuss everything from prose to politics. Nicknamed the "Vicious Circle," these creatives — which included Dorothy Parker and Edna Ferber — left an indelible mark on The Algonquin Hotel that still resonates today.

There are a lot of places in NYC where you can enjoy a good book alongside a well-made cocktail, but there are few places where you can do so in the very place where the most celebrated literary circle once sat; this is what makes The Algonquin Hotel's Blue Bar such a special place. Here, you'll find a menu divided into "chapters," with chapter one sharing literary-themed cocktails, chapter two dedicated to grapes and hops, and chapters three through five dedicated to eats, dessert, and breakfast.

In the words of Parker, "Three be the things I shall never attain: envy, content, and sufficient Champagne." I'd suggest ordering a French 75 (Hendrick's gin, lemon, and Champagne), making your way to the very Round Table where Parker once sat, and sipping Champagne in the company of these great literary ghosts. While there, keep an eye out for Hamlet, the hotel cat who has his very own Instagram.

algonquinhotel.com/the-blue-bar

(212) 840-6800

59 W 44th St, New York, NY 10036

## Bluestockings Cooperative in the Lower East Side

Originally founded by Kathryn Welsh as a feminist bookstore, Bluestockings has evolved over the years, transitioning into a worker-owned cooperative in 2021. Today, this collectively-owned bookstore, café, and activist center sits inside a light-drenched space on Manhattan's Lower East Side. Bluestockings boasts a diverse selection of books that range in genre from feminism, queer, and gender studies to race and political theory. Like other spots on this list, the in-store café helps create a haven for book lovers to enjoy a read alongside a latte, but what sets Bluestockings apart is its commitment to serving Fairtrade coffee and organic tea alongside a rotating selection of snacks.

Coffee and snacks aside, Bluestockings is doing incredible work in the local community, actively supporting New Yorkers through initiatives like an opioid overdose prevention program, offering free resources like Fentanyl test strips, and even operating a free store where individuals in need can access essential items. This dedication to the community makes Bluestockings so much more than a retail space; it is a vital hub for education, aid, and activism in New York City and a place that any book lover will feel good supporting.

(917) 409-0440

116 Suffolk St, New York, NY 10002

## Archestratus in Brooklyn

This cozy culinary bookstore and café, located in Brooklyn's Greenpoint neighborhood, blends food, books, and community within an inviting space. This is the place to find cookbooks — both new and old — as well as a slew of other food-focused titles ranging from non-fiction to cuisine from other cultures. You can enter Archestratus with an insatiable appetite for knowledge and end up satiating both your curiosity and hunger. Not only does Archestratus curate a selection of food and beverages, but its backroom is frequently used for cookbook launches, author readings, and community dinners.

Founded by local Brooklynite Paige Lipari, Archestratus Books creates a delicious experience both on and off the page. The front of the house is filled with food-focused books, while the back of the house is packed with Mediterranean-inspired sweet and savory baked goods. Like many of the other places on this list, Archestratus is a neighborhood gem that doubles as a lovely hangout for locals and visitors alike.

164 Huron St, Brooklyn, NY 11222

## McNally Jackson Books in the Seaport District

Chances are you may have heard of McNally Jackson, a beloved independent bookstore founded by Sarah McNally in 2004. Its original SoHo location has expanded throughout the city, and it now has stores in Williamsburg, downtown Brooklyn, Rockefeller Center, and the Seaport District. But we're here to focus on the latter. Housed within Manhattan's historic Schermerhorn Row building (built in 1811), this particular McNally Jackson is incredible both for its size and its in-store café and bar.

Spanning two floors and 7,500 square feet, this particular McNally Jackson location is like an oasis for book lovers in New York, providing ample space to read a book in cozy armchairs while enjoying the natural light pouring in from the large windows that overlook this historic neighborhood. This store is also home to a café and bar on its ground floor, making this another stellar spot for book lovers to transition from day to night, coffee to happy hour.

(646) 964-4232

4 Fulton St, New York, NY 10038

## Methodology

When it came to identifying the best places in New York for book lovers, I focused on a mix of spots that combined a bookstore experience with a food and beverage element (such as a coffee shop, bistro, wine, or cocktail bar) alongside restaurants like Milk & Roses, which offers a bookish ambiance, or historic literary haunts like The Algonquin's Blue Bar.

Some of the places listed — like Book Club Bar or Bibliotheque — tend to be included on most NYC book bar lists, while others, like Sullaluna or Lit Bar, often fly under the radar. In compiling this list, it was important for me to include not only known favorites, but also places like Bluestockings Cooperative that are important community hubs as well as a great spot for book lovers.

Some of the places on this list are ones I regularly visit, such as Bibliotheque, while others hold a special place in my heart, such as Book Club Bar, which hosted me for an author event to celebrate the release of my travel memoir "Call You When I Land." In the end, all of the places on this list had to check off one essential box: They had to offer a cozy place for readers to sit, relax, and enjoy a story alongside something wonderful to drink or delicious to eat.

title: Top 8 Literary-Themed Cafes, Lounges, and Bookstores in NYC
author: Author Shanea Patterson
text:
# Top 8 Literary-Themed Cafes, Lounges, and Bookstores in NYC

Some little known and some well-known…

New York City is a haven for those who love to get lost in a good book and sip on a warm cup of coffee. In this concrete jungle, there are plenty of literary-themed cafes and bookstores waiting to be explored.

From hidden gems in the city’s neighborhoods to historic institutions, we’ve scoured the streets to bring you the top 10 literary-themed cafes and bookstores in NYC.

So grab a book, order a latte (or some tea!), and let’s dive into the literary scene of the Big Apple.

## 1. Shakespeare & Co. Booksellers Cafe

Located on the Upper East Side, this cafe is named after the famous bookstore in Paris and offers a cozy atmosphere with plenty of books to peruse.

Shakespeare & Co. is an iconic independent bookstore and cafe located in the heart of New York City, just a few blocks away from Central Park.

The bookstore was founded in 1981 and has been a beloved destination for book lovers ever since.

The space is filled with books from floor to ceiling, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere for readers and writers alike.

The cafe, located on the second floor, offers a selection of delicious snacks, coffee, tea, and other beverages.

It’s a perfect spot to grab a drink and a bite to eat while browsing the bookstore’s extensive collection of books, which range from the latest bestsellers to rare and out-of-print editions.

Shakespeare & Co. is more than just a bookstore and cafe — it’s a cultural institution that hosts a variety of literary events and workshops, including author readings, book clubs, and writing workshops.

The owners are passionate about promoting literature and the arts, and strive to create a space that fosters creativity, community, and intellectual curiosity.

Overall, Shakespeare & Co. is a must-visit destination for anyone who loves books and literature.

It’s a place where you can lose yourself for hours, discovering new authors, meeting fellow book lovers, and enjoying the cozy atmosphere of one of the most iconic bookstores in New York City.

## 2. Housing Works Bookstore Cafe

Housing Works Bookstore Cafe is a unique and charming bookstore and cafe located in the heart of downtown New York City.

The bookstore is housed in a beautiful and historic building and is staffed by volunteers, many of whom are people living with and affected by HIV/AIDS.

The bookstore offers a wide range of books, including rare and out-of-print editions, as well as more recent releases.

The cafe serves a selection of delicious snacks, coffee, tea, and other beverages, and is a popular spot for locals and tourists alike.

What sets Housing Works Bookstore Cafe apart is its mission.

All of the proceeds from book sales and cafe purchases go towards Housing Works, an organization dedicated to ending the twin crises of AIDS and homelessness.

The organization provides a range of services, including healthcare, housing, and advocacy, to people living with and affected by HIV/AIDS.

In addition to its mission, Housing Works Bookstore Cafe is known for its vibrant literary events, which include author readings, book launches, and panel discussions.

The space is also used for community events, including open mic nights, art shows, and fundraisers.

This place is a unique and inspiring destination that combines a love of literature with a commitment to social justice.

It’s a place where you can discover new books, meet like-minded people, and support a worthy cause.

## 3. The Library at the Public

This cafe in the Public Theater serves light bites and cocktails, and offers a literary-themed atmosphere with bookshelves lining the walls and a cozy fireplace.

It’s a sophisticated and stylish cocktail bar located inside the Public Theater in New York City. The space is designed to evoke a classic library, with towering bookshelves, vintage decor, and plenty of cozy nooks and seating areas for patrons to relax and enjoy a drink.

The bar offers a selection of classic cocktails, as well as unique and inventive creations inspired by literary figures and works. For example, the Hemingway Daiquiri is a nod to the famous author.

In addition to its drinks, The Library at the Public also offers a range of small plates and snacks, including artisanal cheeses, charcuterie, and other seasonal treats.

What sets The Library at the Public apart is its location within the iconic Public Theater, which has a long history of supporting the arts and fostering creative expression.

The bar is usually frequented by actors, writers, and other artists, creating a lively and dynamic atmosphere.

This place is a unique and sophisticated destination that combines great drinks, delicious food, and a love of literature and the arts.

It’s the perfect spot to unwind after a show or enjoy a night out with friends.

## 4. Ground Central Coffee Company

With several locations throughout the city, Ground Central Coffee Company offers a comfortable atmosphere with plenty of seating and a selection of books available for purchase.

The company is dedicated to providing high-quality coffee and a welcoming atmosphere for its customers.

The shop’s decor features exposed brick walls, wooden accents, and plenty of comfortable seating, creating a warm and inviting ambiance.

The menu at Ground Central Coffee Company includes a wide variety of coffee drinks, including classic favorites like lattes, cappuccinos, and Americanos, as well as specialty drinks like the Honey Lavender Latte and the Nutella Mocha.

The shop also serves a selection of teas, pastries, and light bites.

One of the standout features of Ground Central Coffee Company is its commitment to sustainability.

The company sources its coffee from small, independent farmers who use sustainable and ethical farming practices, and the shop uses eco-friendly cups, utensils, and packaging.

Ground Central Coffee Company has become a popular spot for coffee lovers and remote workers looking for a cozy and comfortable place to get some work done.

The shop offers free Wi-Fi and ample seating, making it a convenient spot for a coffee meeting or a solo work session.

Overall, Ground Central Coffee Company is a must-visit destination for anyone looking for high-quality coffee and a welcoming atmosphere in New York City.

## 5. Bookmarks Lounge

Located on the rooftop of the Library Hotel, Bookmarks Lounge offers a stunning view of the city skyline as well as literary-themed cocktails and small bites.

The bar’s decor is inspired by classic literature, with bookshelves lining the walls and a cozy fireplace area for guests to relax in.

The outdoor seating area offers stunning views of the city skyline, making it a popular destination for both tourists and locals.

The menu at Bookmarks Lounge includes a variety of classic cocktails as well as specialty drinks inspired by famous literary works.

Some popular options include The Great Gatsby, a refreshing gin and champagne cocktail, and the Hemingway Daiquiri, a rum-based drink with grapefruit juice and lime.

In addition to its impressive drink menu, Bookmarks Lounge also serves a selection of small plates and snacks, including cheese and charcuterie boards, flat breads, and sliders.

The bar is known for its attentive and friendly staff, who are happy to make recommendations and help guests find the perfect drink to suit their tastes.

Overall, Bookmarks Lounge offers a unique and memorable rooftop bar experience in the heart of Manhattan.

Whether you’re a literature lover or simply looking for a great view and delicious drinks, this bar is definitely worth a visit.

## 6. Cafe con Libros

This feminist bookstore and cafe in Brooklyn offers a selection of books focused on social justice issues and intersectionality, as well as coffee, tea, and baked goods located in the Crown Heights neighborhood.

The space is designed to be a welcoming and inclusive community hub, with a focus on amplifying the voices of women, queer and trans people, and people of color.

The bookstore carries a diverse selection of books, including works by both established and emerging feminist authors.

The space is also used for community events, such as book clubs, readings, and workshops on social justice issues.

The coffee shop at Cafe con Libros serves a range of espresso drinks, teas, and pastries, all of which are sourced from local and independent vendors.

The cozy interior is decorated with colorful murals and artwork, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere for customers to relax and enjoy their drinks.

One unique feature of Cafe con Libros is its “Pay It Forward” program, which allows customers to purchase a beverage or snack for someone who may not be able to afford it.

This program reflects the cafe’s commitment to creating a more equitable and just community for all.

Overall, Cafe con Libros is a vibrant and socially conscious space that offers both great books and delicious coffee.

It’s a must-visit for anyone who’s passionate about intersectional feminism and supporting small, independent businesses.

## 7. The Book Club

The Book Club is a charming independent bookstore and cafe located in the heart of the East Village in New York City.

As soon as you walk through the door, you’re greeted with a cozy, inviting atmosphere filled with books, art, and comfortable seating.

The bookstore offers a wide selection of new and used books, as well as rare and out-of-print titles, catering to both casual readers and serious book collectors.

In addition to the extensive book collection, the cafe serves a variety of delicious drinks and snacks, including coffee, tea, wine, and pastries.

The cozy seating areas, including a reading nook and outdoor garden seating, make it the perfect place to relax with a good book or catch up with friends over a cup of coffee.

But The Book Club is more than just a place to buy books and grab a drink. It also hosts a range of literary events and workshops, including book clubs, author readings, writing classes, and poetry readings.

It’s a true community hub for book lovers and writers alike, and a must-visit destination for anyone looking for a cozy, welcoming bookstore and cafe experience in NYC.

## 8. Cups & Books

A black-owned bookstore cafe in Prospect Lefferts Gardens, Cups and Books is a beloved black-owned bookstore and cafe located in the Bronx, New York City.

The shop is known for its warm, welcoming atmosphere and commitment to promoting literacy and education within the community.

The shop boasts a diverse collection of books, covering a wide range of genres and topics, from African-American history to contemporary fiction.

The cafe serves a variety of delicious drinks and snacks, including coffee, tea, smoothies, and pastries, making it the perfect place to relax with a book or catch up with friends.

The cozy seating areas and vibrant decor make it a great place to hang out, study, or attend one of the many events hosted by the shop, including book clubs, poetry readings, and writing workshops.

Cups and Books is more than just a bookstore and cafe, it’s a community space that fosters a love of reading and education.

The owners are passionate about promoting diversity and representation in literature, and they strive to create a welcoming and inclusive space for all.

If you’re in the Bronx and looking for a great book and a cozy spot to read, Cups and Books is definitely worth a visit.

## BONUS: The Lit Bar

The Lit Bar is a unique and vibrant independent bookstore and wine bar located in the Bronx, New York City.

It was founded by Bronx native and entrepreneur Noëlle Santos, who saw a need for a bookstore in her community after the last bookstore in the borough closed down.

The Lit Bar is a warm and welcoming space that celebrates literature and culture, while also serving as a hub for the local community.

As soon as you walk through the doors, you’ll be struck by the beauty of the space.

The bookstore features a wide selection of books, including bestsellers, classics, and works by local authors and writers of color.

The wine bar offers a carefully curated selection of wines, craft beers, and small plates, making it a perfect place to unwind and enjoy a drink while browsing for books.

The Lit Bar also serves as a community space, hosting a variety of literary events, author readings, and workshops.

The owners are passionate about promoting diversity and inclusivity in literature, and strive to create a space that reflects the vibrant culture of the Bronx.

The bookstore also offers a variety of educational programs, including a book club and a literacy program for young readers.

Bottom line: this place is more than just a bookstore or a wine bar — it’s a community hub and cultural center that celebrates literature, diversity, and the power of community.

It’s a must-visit destination for anyone looking for a unique and welcoming bookstore experience in New York City.

Have you been to any of these places? What’s been your experience? I’d love to hear about it in the comments so I can plan my trips accordingly.

Thanks for reading and feel free to share this if you enjoyed reading it or found it helpful.

title: Best NYC bookstores that double as cafés and bars
author: Joaquin B
text:
# Best NYC bookstores that double as cafés and bars

## This article is part of a series where I give my top 5 NYC bookstores for different occasions

Sometimes, when you find yourself in a bookstore with a small stack of books in your hand, you’ll just want to sit down and have a nice drink while you sort through your pile. Often though, bookstores lack seating and most don’t double as cafés or bars. If you often find yourself in need of a drink while you read, this article is for you.

## Housing Works

A guilty secret of mine with this bookstore- it’s the only one I’ve frequented and *don’t* buy books at. First thing you’ll notice once you enter is how beautiful and wooden everything is. It’s definitely a contender for a hypothetical “most comfy bookstores in NYC” article (new idea maybe?). Let’s also not forget to mention that the Housing Works bookstore is only one part of a non-profit with the important mission of fighting AIDS and homelessness in NYC. You can read more about that here.

For me, the main draw has always been the bar area at the back. The seating is also fun because they leave journals and pens on the tables for anyone to write with. It’s always interesting to flip through the journals and see what hundreds of people have written or drawn in them. Maybe you can add your touch? For those who are interested, it also doubles/triples as a thrift shop on the second floor!

**Address:** *126 Crosby St, New York, NY 10012*

## Book Club

Book Club is one of the few bookstores in the city that is open past 10pm; on Sunday to Wednesday, they close at midnight, and on Thursday to Saturday, they close at 1am! Being that it’s located in the nightlife neighborhood of East Village, it only makes sense that it closes so late. The book selection is pretty new and up to date. As for the drinks, Book Club serves a range of beer, wine, and cocktails + coffee. It’s definitely the most strongest “bar” vibe of all of the bookstores on this list. Seating is comfy but space is limited! Great place to catch up with some friends who love bar-hopping *and* bookstore hopping.

**Address:** *197 East 3rd Street, New York, NY 10009*

## Molasses Books

This is kind of the opposite of Book Club. Whereas Book Club is for extroverts and has a tad bit more of a nightlife atmosphere, Molasses is a more mellow and introverted experience. Also unlike Book Club, Molasses is a smaller used bookstore with a single small counter and more of a café vibe to it. There’s sufficient seating both inside and outside! Located in Bushwick, it is a bit out of the way and more of a neighbourhood-focused bookstore but that only makes it an even cosier place to hang out at. Lastly, and probably to the great benefit of my fellow night owls, Molasses closes at midnight every day!

**Address: **

*770 Hart St, Brooklyn, NY 11237*

## McNally Jackson – Seaport

If you’re not already familiar with McNally Jackson, it’s probably New York’s biggest indie bookstore chain (the others include Book Culture, Shakespeare & Company, and Greenlight). Don’t let that label fool you though. McNally Jackson locations are often in some of the nicest locales with pretty interiors.

The Seaport location is perhaps one of my favourite bookstores in the city. Upstairs there is tons of comfy seating and shelves upon shelves of books. One thing that McNally Jackson does that is unique is that it separates fiction by region of the world. So if you’re in the mood to sample literature from other countries or continents such as Russia, France, South Asia, Africa, Japan, etc, there is a section for you. In this location’s case, it has a wonderful bar downstairs with a really sweet cushioned corner booth if you can get it.

**Address:** *4 Fulton St, New York, NY 10038*

## Topos Bookstore Cafe

I wrote about this place in my first article detailing my opinion on the best NYC bookstores per borough and choose it as my pick for Queens. Surprise, surprise, it still holds up. While it may be a little out of the way (near one of the last stations on the M), it’s still worth a visit if you expect to come and stay for a couple hours.

The book selection is great with a impressive collection of used classics if that’s your thing (it’s definitely mine). The café is just as good with seating both inside and outside. The bookstore and the cafe actually share the same counter so you can order a coffee and buy your book at the same time, or do one before the other!

**Address:** *788 Woodward Ave, Queens, NY 11385*

### Honourable Mentions

Every Thing Goes Book Cafe, Shakespeare & Company, Bluestocking Cooperative, Kinokuniya
