title: 6 of the best places to work remotely in Brooklyn
author: Charlotte Deprez
text:
# 6 of the best places to work remotely in Brooklyn

Tired of working alone from home in New York? Are you looking for a nice working atmosphere while having the opportunity to sip coffee or eat delicious cookies? These work friendly quiet places with good WiFi are not always easy to find… To make it easier for you, we’ve put together a short list of the best cafes where you can work in Brooklyn.

Here are our 6 favorite spots to relocate your office during the day.

### Our best places to work remotely in Brooklyn

### Stumptown Coffee Roasters, Cobble Hill

All over New York, Stumptown Coffee Roasters are known for their great coffee. But not all of their locations are that laptop friendly! The Cobble Hill address has a very original layout, with a covered patio followed by a first room where you order coffee and wait for it, then another beautiful room where you can actually sit and enjoy the wifi, coffee and pastries.

That’s right, in addition to their full espresso bar, drip coffee and different (cold) brews, Stumptown has kombucha from Big Easy Bucha, and pastries from Ovenly and Supermoon Bakehouse!

Stumptown Coffee Roasters, 212b Pacific St, Brooklyn, NY 11201.

Info on stumptowncoffee.com.

### 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge

If you need high ceilings, a hip decor and plants everywhere, you’ll feel at home here! To us, this hotel lobby is one of the most welcoming spaces in Brooklyn. Located in the waterfront community of DUMBO, this design hotel opened at the beginning of 2017 and won the Best Urban Hotel AHEAD Hospitality Award the year after. With its raw yet sophisticated design, zen atmosphere, and the Neighbors Café conveniently located nearby, the lounge area of 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge is one of our favorites. Oh and you’ll be on one of New York’s most amazing rooftops in just an elevator ride’s time!

1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge, 60 Furman St, Brooklyn, NY 11201.

Info on 1hotels.com

### Kos Kaffe Roasting House, Park Slope

Den of Park Slope freelancers, Kos Kaffe is always packed with cool people working on their MacBooks. One of the things we like about this place is the fact that you can actually eat on the spot, and not only pastries, but also salads and sandwiches (the BLT is delicious). The place is also really big, which makes it fairly easy to find a spot. Obviously, where there are cool entrepreneurs, there’s good coffee. Kos Kaffe sources high-quality green beans and roasts them in-house.

Just beware of one thing though: Kos’ success has turned against them, so they had to put restrictions in place. During rush hours (Monday to Friday 12pm-3pm and Saturday/Sunday 10am-4pm), laptop use is only permitted in certain areas of the cafe.

### Sey Coffee House

Sey is a micro roaster based in the heart of Brooklyn with an ideal ambiance for remote working. This wide open cafe has been carefully designed and provides a beautiful space, delicious coffee, and open air. Complete with a skylight, this plant-filled oasis is a fantastic getaway if you’re craving a bit more peace and calm while working.

### Devoción, Williamsburg

Ever wondered what lies behind Devoción’s very recognizable black facade? This coffee shop is located in the trendy Williamsburg neighborhood, and the decor couldn’t be more Brooklyn! Exposed brick walls and pipes, plants, leather sofas, a skylight… Everything here makes it easy to focus on your work. Oh, and did we mention they have the best brew around? That’s because Devoción actually roasts their own coffee, imported straight from Colombia.

### Manhattanville Coffee, Crown Heights

Manhattanville Coffee is one of Crown Heights freelancers’ favorites (and closest to our coliving space in Crown Heights). Whether it’s on the big leather sofa or on the coffee tables, there are power outlets everywhere. The decor is also gorgeous, making it a great spot for work meetings in the neighborhood.

The baristas are always nice, the coffee is very good, and the food is exactly what you need during a hard work day. Also good to mention, everything here is kosher!

If the idea of remote work from home with daily pay sounds appealing to you, then New York is the perfect backdrop for working wherever you want. Explore the city as well as all the cafes that are perfect for digital nomads and remote workers!

## How to Spot a High-Quality Coffee Shop in Midtown NYC

Finding a high-quality coffee shop in Midtown NYC can be tricky since the area is filled with both tourist traps and hidden gems. Here are some key signs to look for when searching for the best spot:

**1. The Coffee Itself**

- **Beans & Roasting**: Look for shops that highlight their coffee sourcing, such as single-origin beans or partnerships with reputable roasters (e.g., Stumptown, Counter Culture, or Intelligentsia).
- **Brewing Methods**: High-end cafes often offer pour-over, Chemex, or siphon brewing in addition to standard espresso drinks.
- **Barista Skill**: A good shop takes pride in well-prepared espresso shots—smooth, not overly bitter, and properly extracted.

**2. Atmosphere & Ambience**

- **No Corporate Vibes**: If it looks like a generic chain, it’s probably not a top-tier specialty coffee shop.
- **Seating & Vibe**: Cozy but not overcrowded, with a mix of people working, chatting, or reading—often a sign of a quality local favorite.
- **Music & Noise Level**: A balance between lively and relaxing, not too loud or chaotic.

**3. Milk & Alternative Options**

- **Dairy Quality**: Good cafes often use high-quality whole milk (sometimes organic) and alternatives like oat, almond, and macadamia milk.
- **Proper Steaming**: A good barista steams milk to a creamy microfoam, not overly bubbly or scalding hot.

**4. Food & Pastries**

- **House-made or Local Bakery Partnerships**: Many quality coffee spots partner with local bakeries or make their own pastries.
- **Limited But Thoughtful Menu**: A smaller menu with fresh, high-quality offerings is better than an overly broad one with mass-produced items.

**5. Reviews & Reputation**

- **Google & Yelp Ratings**: Look for places with consistently high ratings (above 4.5 stars) and detailed positive reviews.
- **Word of Mouth**: If locals or coffee aficionados recommend it, it’s a good sign.
- **Instagram Presence**: Many good spots have a strong social media following showcasing their drinks and space.

## Tips for Enjoying the Perfect Cup at Midtown NYC’s Best Cafes

Midtown NYC is a vibrant hub, home to some of the best cafés in the city, offering everything from perfectly brewed espressos to creative seasonal drinks. Whether you’re looking for a cozy spot to relax, a place to work, or just a great cup of coffee, Midtown has something for everyone. Here’s how to make the most of your coffee experience in the heart of New York City.

- Choose Specialty Cafés – Visit spots like Culture Espresso, Blue Bottle, or Birch Coffee for top-quality brews.
- Try Different Brew Methods – Explore pour-over, Chemex, or siphon for unique flavors.
- Avoid Peak Hours – Best times are 10 AM to 12 PM or after 3 PM for a relaxed vibe.
- Pair Coffee with a Treat – Try a croissant at Dominique Ansel Workshop or a mochi donut at Matchaful.
- Chat with Baristas – Ask for recommendations to find your perfect cup.
- Pick the Right Ambiance – Cozy at Felix Roasting Co. or modern at Arabica.
- Try Seasonal Specials – Limited-time lattes and unique flavors are worth a taste.
- Savor the Moment – Midtown is fast-paced, but take time to enjoy every sip.

Midtown Manhattan is filled with coffee shops that not only serve exceptional coffee but also provide the perfect ambience for students to relax, study, or socialise. Each of the spots mentioned in this guide offers something unique – from quiet spaces perfect for reading and working to vibrant cafes ideal for catching up with friends. As someone on a hybrid work schedule, I, like many others in New York City, love to seek inspiration outside the walls of my tiny apartment.

When I’m not in the office, I find myself exploring coffee shops with welcoming atmospheres and communal energy. Here are a few of my favorite places to work remotely, sip great-tasting coffee, and gain a bit of creativity while I’m at it.

**Buunni Coffee, **4961 Broadway, New York, NY 10034 

Buunni Coffee is an independent Ethiopian coffee shop that crafts its own small-batch roasted coffee beans. They have four locations across Washington Heights and Inwood and their coffee boasts a high-quality flavor, sourced from smallholder farms and farmers’ cooperatives.

They locally roast their beans once a week in micro batches to maintain peak freshness and deliver full, nuanced flavors. I have visited their Inwood location a handful of times and have always been greeted with a smile. Their Wi-Fi is strong and their food selection will have you coming back for more.

**Devoción, **69 Grand St. (at Wythe), Brooklyn, NY 11249

Devocion is a coffee shop launched by Colombian-born Steven Sutton. With five locations across the city, Sutton’s goal was to produce the freshest coffee imaginable. They are one of the only coffee companies in the world that roasts true farm-fresh coffee only 10 days after leaving origin, quicker than the industry norm of 6-12 months.

Their Williamsburg location serves as a testament to their work since 2006. This cozy industrial-chic venue is actually housed in a former warehouse. It is spacious, boasts amazing interior decor, and is definitely the place to spark some creativity. The leather couches add a nice touch, and the strong WiFi never fails me.

**787 Coffee**, 159 2nd Ave, New York, NY 10003

This Puerto Rican coffee chain has made a name for itself in the city with 18 locations to date. Their coffee is grown and roasted in the town of Maricao, Puerto Rico and their beans have delicious notes of dark chocolate, butter and citrus.

I love this Greenwich Village location because of it has an attached co-work space for customers. I think this bonus area really sets the tone for those who want to get work done but also allows for that community connection. The overall vibe is relaxed and the baristas have great knowledge on what they are preparing.

One of my favorite drinks is their coquito latte. It’s a variation of the traditional coquito that is blended with espresso to create a creamy and rich beverage that is the perfect combination of coffee and holiday flavors.

title: Five Amazing Coffee Shops in the Flatiron District
author: Emily
text:
For a relatively small piece of Manhattan, the Flatiron District has an impressive density of coffee shops. And not just chains (though they have those, too) — the area is rich with coffee shops with unique ties to NYC. This list includes local family-owned businesses, shops that roast beans in Brooklyn, and one you’ve probably heard of that was first conceived right here in NYC.

The only thing I love more than a challenge is a coffee crawl, so I set out to on a mission to caffeinate my way around the Flatiron District. If you find yourself in the neighborhood and in need of a pick-me-up, check out one of these amazing coffee shops.

If your favorite didn’t make this list, let me know in the comments so I can check it out!

## Gotham Coffee Roasters

- **Location**: 23 W 19th St, New York, NY 10011
- **Seating**: 4 small indoor tables, plus a few more outside when the weather is nice
- **Food**: Light pastry selection, plus seasonal offerings (breakfast tacos during my visit)
- **Menu Highlight**: Espresso Tonic

Gotham Coffee Roasters is a cozy and unassuming coffee shop. It’s a small cafe with a walk-up counter and just a handful of tables. The coffee menu is straightforward, printed in vinyl letters on the back wall, with a few specials on a letter board beside the register. I knew I was in for a treat when I saw they had an Espresso Tonic on the menu, my personal favorite.

What stood out immediately was the service. The baristas were warm and welcoming, treating each customer as if they were a regular. They were knowledgeable, kindly talking patrons through the menu items, without being condescending.

I took one sip of my coffee and knew I had found a good one. This was one of the best Espresso Tonic’s I’ve ever had, with a sharp hit of espresso followed by the citrusy zip from the tonic. Don’t just trust my taste in coffee, though. Upon further research, I realized that this coffee shop is about as legit as it gets.

The founder, Chris Calkins, was mentored by Alfred Peet (founder of Peet’s Coffee) and was part of the original team that opened the very first Starbucks store in Seattle’s Pike’s Place Market. After an impressive career in coffee and then wine, he moved to NYC and opened Gotham Coffee Roasters in 2017. They source coffee from around the world and roast it in Red Hook, Brooklyn.

I’ll go right out and say it: Gotham Coffee Roasters was my favorite coffee shop in the Flatiron District.

## :3Coffee

- **Location**: 29 W 21st St, New York, NY 10010
- **Seating**: 3 small indoor tables
- **Food**: Light selection of homemade, Colombian pastries
- **Menu Highlight**: Dulce de leche Pionono

:3Coffee is a family-owned coffee shop with Colombian flare. They source all of their beans from Colombia and showcase Colombian flavors in their homemade baked goods. It’s a no-frills cafe that focuses on providing quality coffee and sincere customer service.

The coffee menu was short and sweet, printed out on a paper sign near the register. There was no fancy concoctions or flavors combinations, just the basics. I leaned into that and ordered a cappuccino. If I’ve learned anything from watching hours of baking shows, it’s that if you’re going to do something simple, you have to do it really well. They accomplished that.

The highlight at this coffee shop though, was actually not the coffee — it was their pastries. The pastry case was simple, but stocked with interesting South American flavors you won’t find at every other coffee shop. During my visit, the options included guava-filled Cambray (Colombian empanadas), fresh yellow corn arepas, and dulce de leche Piononos (a Colombian cake roll). I opted for the later and it was phenomenal.

I really enjoyed my coffee and pastry here, the barista’s were delightful, but it just wasn’t my favorite vibe inside. I’m not sure if it was dull wooden cabinetry or just the lack of twinkle lights. This coffee shop is a great pick to grab a coffee to take with you as you shop your way through the rest of the Flatiron District.

## Foreigner NYC

- **Location**: 64 W 21st St, New York, NY 10010
- **Seating**: Two mall tables inside, plus nice tiered seating outside during warmer months
- **Food**: Small selection (but great quality) of pastries
- **Menu Highlight**: Cardamom bun (are you even surprised?)

One of the most ascetically pleasing coffee shops on this journey was Foreigner NYC. That shouldn’t be surprising, given they share the space with a photo studio. The vibe is sleek and modern, with gray stone walls and minimalist decor.

The menu was posted just inside the door and was split between coffee and tea. They had a selection of specialty drinks at the bottom, though it didn’t list any details or ingredient information. (Which is unfortunate because I would love to know what a Hanoi Aroma is, but was far too intimidated by the cool barista to ask.)

As noted earlier in this post, I almost always order an espresso tonic when I see it. Here though, it was the espresso spritz that piqued my interest. I wish I could tell you exactly what was in it. It seemed like just regular sparkling water, though I’m not sure why that made it $2 more than the tonic. It was good, but was not sparkling at all.

The pastry case was small, but mighty. I ordered a cardamom bun — something I grew very fond of during recent trips to Scandinavia — and it came out perfectly warm and bursting with spicy sweetness. I kid you not, it was one of the most delicious things I’ve ever eaten. This cardamom bun was life-giving and I cannot recommend it enough!

I did find this coffee shop to be a bit intimidating. I love good coffee as much as anyone, but I don’t like when good coffee shops come off as elitist. It was one of those places that felt like I had to somehow prove that I belonged there. I get the same feeling when I walk into a craft beer bar and order anything other than an IPA.

I’m willing to let that go though, because that cardamom bun was so dang good!

## Devoción

- **Location**: 25 E 20th St, New York, NY 10003
- **Seating**: Lots of indoor seating available (does fill up though)
- **Food**: Small selection of pastries
- **Menu Highlight**: Something black, like an espresso, americano or drip coffee.

The most impressive thing about Devoción is their commitment to serving the freshest coffee imaginable. They work with farmers in Colombia, ship the beans directly to their roasting facility in Brooklyn, and then serve the coffee in their stores as soon as possible. The coffee in your cup at Devoción left the farm as little as 10 days ago, compared to the industry norm of 6 months to 1 year!

Honestly, my palate is not that sophisticated, but it was darn good coffee.

The other thing that makes Devoción stand out is their cafe space, which is stunning and homey and oh-so-very NYC. The focal point is a hanging chandelier of live plants, meant to evoke the jungles of Colombia. That is set in contrast to the industrial vibes from the original exposed brick and wood floors.

It is also the largest of the cafes on this list. There was a lot of seating, both tables and a leather sofa, but not quite enough for how popular the place was. Not a lot of coffee shops around here have this much seating, so it was a popular destination for remote workers. No bother, I took my farm-fresh coffee with me to go.

Overall, this place was a delight in terms of both coffee and ambiance.

## Ralph’s Coffee

- **Location**: 160 5th Ave, New York, NY 10010
- **Seating**: No indoor seating, but there are a few tables outside.
- **Food**: Selection of pastries and sandwiches
- **Menu Highlight**: Sea salt dark chocolate bar (expensive, but worth it!)

Okay, I’m sure I’ve got some people rolling their eyes at this one, so I made sure to put it last. I stand by it, though!

Ralph’s Coffee is the coffee shop founded by the clothing retailer, Ralph Lauren. It’s now a chain, but it originated right here in NYC. Their flagship location is on the Upper East Side and is immensely popular, particularly during Christmastime. After the success of that location, they continued to open Ralph’s Coffee locations around NYC and the world, including one in the Flatiron District.

The Ralph’s Coffee in Flatiron is small, and takeout only. It’s got that Ralph Lauren-y Americana aesthetic inside that makes you question if you’re at a coffee shop or a tennis match. The queue leads patrons past a wall of merch (including specialty chocolates made in Brooklyn) and then right to the register to order. The pickup bar is right back by the door.

The Ralph’s Coffee menu features their classic Ralph’s Roast coffee, a collection of espresso-based beverages and tea, plus a few unique items like draft oat latte, espresso tonic (so many espresso tonics in Flatiron!) and matcha lemonade. They had a gingerbread latte as a special during December, and it was one of the best I’ve had all season.

The important thing to know about Ralph’s Coffee is that they brew La Colombe coffee. They roast a special blend for Ralph’s, but it’s the same quality that you’ll find at a La Colombe cafe. I happen to love La Colombe, so I naturally loved Ralph’s, too.

The Ralph’s Coffee in Flatiron is much smaller and doesn’t offer the full experience of the flagship location, but that also makes it much less crowded. If you want to try Ralph’s but don’t want to commit a full morning to the experience, the Flatiron location is the way to go.

## Interested in more coffee content?

We wrote this Coffee Around the World post while we were backpacking around the world for 18 months. During that trip, we also took a really cool coffee farm tour in Medellin, Colombia, which we documented in this video.

## ☕️ Introduction: Your Ultimate Flatiron Coffee Guide

Whether you’re chasing an expertly pulled cortado, need WiFi and outlets for a few hours, or want a quiet moment with a maple cruller, **this guide has your next cup covered**.

I spent years sipping through the area — from sleek Aussie imports to Latin-owned roasters and under-the-radar mom-and-pop shops. These are **10 of the best coffee shops in Flatiron NYC**, in a curated, purposeful order. ☕👇

## 3. Devoción – The Brooklyn Import with Major Jungle Vibes

**Why Go:**

This **Colombian coffee powerhouse** roasts some of the freshest beans in the city (shipped direct from Bogotá weekly). The café itself feels like a *greenhouse meets coffee temple*. Perfect for a recharge between meetings.

## 4. Copper Mug Coffee – Low-Key, Locally Loved

###### Flatiron Coffee Guide

## 5. Patent Coffee – Sleek Speakeasy Energy

- **📍 Address:**49 W 27th St
- **🎯 Vibe:**Tiny, stylish, secret-feeling
- **✨ Must-Try:**Iced espresso with orange zest
- **💡 Tip:**Check out the hidden cocktail bar in the back after hours 👀

**Why Go:**

Tucked inside an old elevator shaft, this spot **feels like a downtown cocktail bar serving third-wave espresso**. Great for a fast, flavor-forward coffee hit. It’s small but mighty — and the vibe is everything.

## 6. Yanni’s Coffee – The Under-the-Radar Classic

- **📍 Address:**96 7th Ave (nearby flatiron)
- **🎯 Vibe:**Unfussy, old-school, local crowd
- **✨ Must-Try:**Regular drip or classic latte
- **💡 Tip:**No frills, but they move fast — great for your first cup of the day

**Why Go:**

Yanni’s is a **Flatiron mainstay that feels like your neighborhood café from the ’90s**. No reclaimed wood or house-made syrups — just good coffee, quickly, and at a price that still feels fair. Keep it simple.

## 7. Ralph’s Coffee – Polished and Surprisingly Great

- **🎯 Vibe:**Luxe, preppy, chill
- **✨ Must-Try:**Cappuccino + chocolate chip cookie

**Why Go:**

Yes, it’s fashion-adjacent, but **Ralph’s Coffee is the real deal**. The space is gorgeous, the drinks are dialed in, and it’s one of the quietest mid-afternoon coffee escapes in the area.

###### Flatiron Coffee Guide

## 8. Maman – French-Inspired, Always Cozy

- **📍 Address:**22 W 25th St
- **🎯 Vibe:**Rustic, floral, Instagram-ready
- **✨ Must-Try:**Lavender latte or nutty chocolate chip cookie

**Why Go:****Maman is mood.** The pastries are fantastic, the floral cups iconic, and the energy is always warm and social. You’re not rushing here — you’re staying, chatting, vibing.

787 brings the **warmth and boldness of Puerto Rico to Flatiron**. Every drink is strong, sweet, and full of personality. Their mission-driven approach (farm-to-cup, literally) adds meaning to every sip.

## ☕ Why Flatiron Is Packed With NYC’s Best Cafes

If you are on the hunt for the best cafes Flatiron, you have landed in the right place. This neighborhood blends energy, history, and architecture perfectly.

And that is not counting on the foot traffic from Madison Square Park, Eataly, and NYC’s tech offices, which makes the neighborhood a magnet for excellent coffee, delicious pastries, and cozy corners.

I’ve lived here for over 8 years and this year alone I’ve visited more than 30 cafes across the Flatiron District.

This article has the top five best cafes in Flatiron NYC! They are the ones I keep going back to for drinks, atmosphere, and other little things that make a café go from good to great.

Whether you’re looking for a place to do some work, unplug from the world outside, read, or catch up with a friend, here’s where to go.

## 🔥 Best Cafes Flatiron — Top 5 Picks

### 🥇 1. Ralph’s Coffee — A Quiet, Luxurious Coffee Lounge

📍 **109 5th Ave, New York, NY 10003**

🗺️ **Cross streets:** 5th Ave & E 18th St (Inside Ralph Lauren Flagship)

✨ **Vibe:** Quiet elegance, old-world charm, jazz playing softly in the background

☕ **Must-Try:** Classic Americano + chocolate chip cookie

💬 **Local Tip:** Arrive before 10:30AM for a great window seat

🏆 **Highlights:** Featured in NYT, Eater, Vogue; designed by Ralph Lauren

**Why Go:**

Ralph’s feels like a high-end study in calm. Set inside the Ralph Lauren flagship store, it’s all green leather, white tile, and vintage lighting. 

There’s no WiFi or plugs, and that’s the charm. Come here to disconnect and sip high-quality coffee in peace. A local favorite for quiet breaks or impressing out-of-towners.

### 🥈 2. Daily Provisions — Cruller Heaven and Local Favorite

📍 **103 E 19th St, New York, NY 10003**

🗺️ **Cross streets:** E 19th St between Park Ave South & Broadway

✨ **Vibe:** Buzzy, counter seating, fast-paced mornings

☕ **Must-Try:** Maple cruller + cortado

💬 **Local Tip:** Get there by 8:45AM to beat the pastry rush

🏆 **Highlights:** Created by Danny Meyer; featured in Eater, Grub Street

**Why Go:**

This is where Flatiron locals actually grab breakfast. The coffee is consistent, but the **pastries, especially the maple cruller**, are next-level. 

It’s a small space, mostly standing-room, but it’s packed with regulars for a reason. Come early, grab your pastry, and start your day like a Flatiron pro.

### 🥉 3. Devoción — Colombian Coffee in a High-Design Space

📍 **25 E 20th St, New York, NY 10003**

🗺️ **Cross streets:** E 20th St between Broadway & Park Ave South

✨ **Vibe:** Bright, open, greenery-filled with good seating

☕ **Must-Try:** Cascara spritz or iced latte

💬 **Local Tip:** Grab the corner table near the front window for max natural light

🏆 **Highlights:** Direct-sourced beans from Colombia; featured in Architectural Digest

**Why Go:**

Devoción is one of the best spaces in Flatiron to both work and relax. The bright, plant-filled interior is matched by ultra-fresh beans and rotating seasonal drinks. 

The vibe is polished but not pretentious. And it’s one of the few cafés in the area with plenty of tables and good WiFi.

### 🏅 4. Caffè Lavazza at Eataly — Italian Espresso with Plenty of Space

📍 **200 5th Ave, New York, NY 10010** *(inside Eataly Flatiron)*

🗺️ **Cross streets:** 5th Ave & W 23rd St

✨ **Vibe:** Sleek marketplace environment with extensive table seating

# Remote work cafés, marked

### 36 aesthetic cafés across NYC where you can open a laptop, stay awhile, and actually get something done.

New York has a lot of great coffee. What it doesn’t always have is cafés that are happy to see you open a laptop and stay for a while.

These are the spots I return to when I want to work outside my apartment: good light, enough space to settle in for a few hours, and specialty drinks & treats that make it worthwhile to stay. Some are quiet neighborhood cafés, some are beautiful hotel lobbies, and a few are slightly unconventional places to work that just happen to be perfect during the day.

I keep a running Google Map of them – and **paid subscribers can access the full map with every café pinned** so you always have a good place to work nearby.

**Brooklyn**

**Dumbo & Brooklyn Bridge Park**

**fontainhas + (/du.kaan/)** (Dumbo) – An Indian-inspired café connected to a /du.kaan/ shop, serving coffee and pastries alongside shelves of ceramics and pantry goods. A great place to order a chai.

**usagi** (Dumbo) – A minimalist café and concept shop serving coffee, matcha, and Japanese pastries inside a calm space filled with books, stationery, and design goods. Wide open space with plenty of seating.

**Brooklyn Heights, Cobble Hill, Boerum Hill & Carroll Gardens**

**Nako** (Brooklyn Heights) – A calm café on a beautiful tree-lined street. Just a few blocks from the waterfront if you want to take a walk between work sessions.

Located at 180 Mulberry St, Urban Backyard offers more than just coffee; it provides a vibrant atmosphere filled with live music and events that captivate both locals and visitors. This café stands out for its commitment to creating a welcoming community space. With a rating of 4.8/5 from numerous reviews, patrons particularly enjoy the Fried Chicken Sandwich and the Brisket Bun along with their aromatic coffees.

The outdoor seating area, spacious and inviting, is perfect for enjoying warm, sunny days. Despite being a bit pricey and having limited vegetarian options, the lively vibe and quality offerings make Urban Backyard a must-visit.

Just a short walk from Urban Backyard, Brewlita at 227 Mulberry St is the epitome of cozy. This coffee shop is renowned for its intimate ambiance and knowledgeable staff who are always ready to recommend the perfect brew. With stylish decor and an extensive beer selection, Brewlita also caters to late afternoon and evening crowds.

Popular items include Beer Flights and Truffle Fries, perfect accompaniments to their specialty coffees. The small plates might be on the pricier side, but the quality and service are well worth it.

#### Café Integral: Sustainable Excellence

Sustainability is at the heart of Café Integral’s ethos. Located at 149 Elizabeth St, this coffee shop is dedicated to ethical sourcing and roasts its specialty beans in-house. The sleek, modern design of the café attracts a crowd that appreciates great coffee and a stylish environment.

Known for its Cortado and Avocado Toast, Café Integral is a favorite among those who value sustainability and quality. The café can get crowded, and seating is limited, but the exceptional service and delightful menu options make it a standout spot in Nolita.

#### Yours Truly Coffee: Modern Minimalism

Yours Truly Coffee at 8 Spring St embodies modern minimalism with a twist of classic New York charm. This café is particularly famed for its iced matcha latte, which, along with a selection of premium coffee brews, attracts a discerning clientele. The interior is bright and airy, providing a serene escape from the bustling city streets.

Although there is a desire for more unsweetened milk alternatives, the quality of the beverages keeps customers returning. The staff’s efficiency and the overall clean, inviting environment make Yours Truly Coffee a standout spot for those seeking a quick caffeine fix in a stylish setting.

#### Café Lyria: European Flair

Nestled at 166 Crosby St, Café Lyria offers a slice of European café culture right in the heart of Nolita. With its cozy atmosphere and a selection of exquisite coffees and teas, it is a popular destination for those looking to unwind. The café also features a range of bakery items and light lunch options, making it ideal for a midday treat. Although it can get crowded and seating is limited, the welcoming service and quality offerings like the Chai Latte and Avocado Toast ensure a delightful experience for all visitors.

#### Ground Support Cafe: Eco-Friendly Innovation

Ground Support Cafe, located at 399 W Broadway, stands out for its sustainable practices and eco-friendly approach. This café not only offers vegetarian and vegan options but also serves a variety of coffees and brunch items in a trendy, modern setting. With communal seating and free Wifi, it’s an ideal spot for both casual meetings and solo work sessions.

The café’s ambiance, combined with its commitment to sustainability, attracts a diverse crowd, from students to professionals. Notable menu items include the Avocado Toast and Matcha Latte, making Ground Support Cafe a key player in Nolita’s coffee scene.

#### The Lost Draft: Artistic Inspirations

The Lost Draft at 398 Broome St captures the artistic spirit of Nolita with its old New York-style décor and an inspiring atmosphere. It’s a favorite among local artists and creatives looking for a space that fuels their imagination. The café rates highly for its diverse coffee selection and the quality of its service. The Lost Draft is particularly appreciated for its location, allowing customers to enjoy a quiet coffee break or a lively discussion without straying far from the cultural heartbeat of the city. title: The 13 Best Restaurants In Hudson Yards - New York - The Infatuation
author: Will Hartman; Willa Moore; Carlo Mantuano; Kenny Yang; Molly Fitzpatrick
text:
#### Will Hartman

Staff Writer, NYC

Will is passionate about bagels and being disappointed by The Mets. He has been writing for The Infatuation since 2023.

NYCGuide

photo credit: Kate Previte

Hudson Yards is a massive real estate development that calls itself a neighborhood, and feels like it was created for particularly rich Sims. There’s a big luxury mall with an NFT store, an Equinox, and shiny glass office buildings with sweeping views of the big luxury mall and Equinox. (Penn Station is also nearby.)

When the mall opened in 2019, the only reason to go there involved a paycheck. But our reasons have improved, along with the restaurants. Here’s where to go in Hudson Yards for everything from elegant __temaki__ and Spanish tapas to live-fire Mediterranean cooking and one of our favorite __Italian restaurants__ in the city.

Walking into Ci Siamo is like checking into a nice hotel at the start of a vacation in Milan, while in reality, you still have that 8:15am meeting tomorrow to discuss “team dynamics.” The menu centers around live-fire cooking, although your focus should really be on the breads and pastas. Get the cavatelli with crab and chilis, and the caramelized onion torta. Despite the massive space, it can be tough to secure a table, so make a reservation in advance.

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

David A. Lee

The second location of Tribeca institution __Locanda Verde__ adheres to the formula pioneered by the original: Open a spacious restaurant with impeccable service and crowd-pleasing Italian food, and the people will come. Factor in all the offices around here, and you’ve got yourself a post-work, corporate-card destination. But we also like the bar for a solo martini, if you leave your desk early and need some alone time before you get on the train. 

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Quentin Bacon

For a work lunch sans the same old little gem salads, Papa San is our top choice. It’s the first foray into the world of business lunches for the __Llama Inn__ people, and it’s a refreshing setting for a midday business meal if you've just spent an alarming number of hours in a conference room. (Thank the restaurant's big windows and living plants for that.) Always order one of the rotating ceviches.

Dane Tashima

The P.J. Clarke’s at Hudson Yards is about 50% bar, because this place knows its audience. The workers who flock from surrounding office buildings at 5pm on the dot definitely don’t want a table, and they’re out by 7pm at the latest. For those two hours, Monday through Thursday, P.J. Clarke’s is a scene for a very specific post-work crowd, plus a few tourists who stumble in after a visit to the Vessel. Whether you're here for lunch or dinner, the burger is as safe a bet as it’s always been, complete with the classic combination of american cheese, lettuce, onion, and a not-quite-ripe-enough tomato.

Willa Moore

This flashy Mexican restaurant—from the same people as __Zou Zou's__ around the corner—gets packed with groups of colleagues on weekday evenings, and with good reason. The big, moodily lit space is ideal for after-work drinks that feel a lot more glamorous than the office you just escaped from. The food menu here is hit or miss, so stick to drinks and snacks: the guacamole, maybe a machete quesadilla for the table, and yet another round of blood-orange margaritas.

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Christian Harder

This food hall from José Andrés is like a Spanish version of Eataly, with a bunch of different grab-and-go tapas kiosks specializing in things like empanadas, flatbreads, and cured meats. There are two solid sit-down restaurants to choose from within the hall. While __La Barra__ has an extensive menu of regional tapas in the center of the market, __Txula Steak__ serves a slightly more formal dinner that involves live-fire cooking and beautiful cuts of red meat. 

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Mercado Little Spain

Oyamel, which replaced __Spanish Diner__, is the latest addition to the Little Spain universe, but it reads much more like its own Mexican restaurant than an extension of the food hall. And it's generally a pleasant post-work move if you earn a living in the area. Come for warm chips, smoky salsa, and $17 cocktails that are (unfortunately) reasonably priced for the neighborhood. You can feel good about bringing a bunch of people, too: there’s enough space for your whole team at the stretched-out dining room and bar where people in blazers shout over mezcal.

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Nitzan Keynan

At this upscale spot from the team behind __Don Angie__ and __Quality Eats__, the portions are big and there’s no real distinction between entrées and appetizers. That’s why it works well for a group who wants to share some merguez tartare, smoky lamb chops, and a refreshing fattoush. The dining room has a socialites-in-evening-wear grandness, but you won’t feel out of place at a casual get-together. Given that Zou Zou’s is perpetually packed, we can’t help but think that people who live and work near Hudson Yards have been thirsting for a restaurant they can finally brag about to the rest of the city.  

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Greywind is an understated, elegant neighborhood restaurant from the people behind __Loring Place__, in a neighborhood that is anything but elegant or understated. Like at Loring Place, the menu is seasonal, so you may find things like carrot hummus with orange molasses, or a rigatoni with acorn squash. They also have a bakery around the corner where you can try the same high-quality ingredients in sandwiches, salads, and baked goods.

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Kate Previte

If a restaurant connected to a high-end gym franchise isn’t your first choice for a night out, Electric Lemon, the rooftop hotspot perched atop the Equinox Hotel, might make you reconsider. The food here is marketed as healthy-ish, and it sort of is, but it’s also just solid New American fare. Will it blow your mind? Probably not, but everything tastes better than what you'd get at your average influencer haunt.


Team Infatuation

The wall of sky you see in front of you at Peak is truly something. If you’re looking for one of the city’s best views, this New American restaurant is worth the elevated prices. You’ll get your usual corporate card fare here—foie gras, duck, lobster. The cooking isn’t particularly imaginative, but opulent seafood towers and a signature egg-shaped dessert covered in edible gold match the luxe environment.

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Alex Staniloff

Like its other location in Midtown, this Greek spot is very fancy, with most tables occupied by dressed-up groups eating lobster or jumbo prawns that cost over $100 per pound (fresh fish is flown in daily from around the world, duh). It’s expensive, but if you're entertaining clients on the company’s dime, you’ll eat some good food here, like perfectly cooked octopus with a rich fava bean puree. The dining room with big round tables and floor-to-ceiling windows works for groups, and there’s also the walk-in-only __Milos Wine Bar__.

RESERVE A TABLE WITH

Francis Dzikowski

Butter chicken chops and hype salmon bowls just north of Madison Square Park.

Korean handrolls, brick-oven pizza, exceptional Thai food, and more.

Where to eat when you find yourself in the land of office buildings and Broadway shows.
